and publish/display authority remain valid:

> **Make this Giving page public?**
>
> This web address becomes permanent when you publish. You can rename the page
> later, but this address will not change. If you need another address, Core
> will create a new one and keep this address protected.

After success, the screen says **Public · cannot be assigned to another Core
Giving page**. Full URL display, **Copy link**, **Test as donor**, **Download QR
code**, export, and accessible full-value text require current need-to-know
display capability and retention/use basis; otherwise Core uses the source-
owned safe/redacted label plus opaque reference and suppresses revealing
actions. **Review places to share** and **Create a new web address** remain
role-appropriate. The screen never shows **Edit address** for an issued value.

Ordinary Page UI and Giving may reuse an accessible field component but use
different language: **Website page URL** follows the separately proved Page
continuity contract; **Giving page address · cannot be reused after
publication** never implies a Giving redirect. Errors preserve input and use
inline text, associated help,
and polite status. Failed submission moves focus once to the error summary;
its first link targets the Giving-address field, while advisory checks never
move focus. The split visual control exposes the complete pre-issuance candidate
URL, including fixed origin/prefix and editable segment, as one programmatically
associated accessible value/description; it avoids per-keystroke chatter and
offers a concise authorized announcement during availability review and final
confirmation. Post-issuance accessibility uses the authorized complete value
or correctly named safe/redacted label plus opaque reference, and actions never
copy/reveal hidden text. Keyboard, screen reader, 320-pixel, 200%/400% zoom,
forced-color, RTL/native-script, no-JS, and weak-network behavior are release
gates.

### Adversarial result

The review found material concerns in all 22 requested categories when Option
3 is left unqualified. None requires abandoning the readable default. They
require a bounded route model, one source of truth, atomic issuance, a
non-enumerating collision UX, privacy-safe suggestions, immutable post-issue
behavior, and adverse-first rollout.

The highest risks are:

- the current host-blind `/give` redirect and generic query checkout are not a
  safe foundation;
- current CMS slugs are non-unique and ambiguous lookup chooses the newest row;
- current Page generation strips non-ASCII text and silently adds an internal
  ID suffix, contrary to this founder choice;
- separate CMS/Giving/router registries would drift;
- cross-Tenant collision detail and permanent sensitive URL text can leak;
- stale availability, concurrent publish, response loss, and mixed-version
  routers can create duplicate or ambiguous outcomes;
- ordinary Page redirect behavior must not leak into Giving; and
- at D11 close, a replacement's effect on another exact-entry address remained
  D12; D12 now resolves it as eligible direct continuity plus separate terminal
  Stop.

The permanent answer is deliberately simple for staff but strict underneath:
one fixed route family, one editable segment, one opaque Giving identity, one
atomic claim, one shared address authority, and no silent suffix or reassignment.

### Affected contracts and required reconciliation

- Root glossary now defines **Giving Address Slug** separately from **Issued
  Giving Address**.
- Accepted ADR-0026 supports the `/give` route family; ADR-0029 keeps CMS
  presentation as reference-not-copy; Phase 10 keeps sensitive data out of
  URL egress; D9/D10 govern absence and permanent address identity.
- Phase 5 A12 must give Giving an explicit carve-out from broad CMS slug/
  redirect ownership.
- Phase 13 D14b must make `/give/<staff-slug>?sc=...` the issued Giving seam,
  keep Source Code in the query, and make every issued `/s/<token>` destination
  immutable. Any destination change—even to a new preferred address for the
  same Giving entry—requires a newly issued token and QR.
- Proposed Phase 22 Page routes remain separate from Page Giving Bindings.
- Proposed Phase 23 same-Page continuity applies only to ordinary Pages and
  cannot authorize Giving redirects.
- Open PR #1323 and PR #1340 are proposed evidence until merged or explicitly
  superseded.

### Required evidence

The linked D11 adversarial review specifies 26 outcome criteria covering the
staff/donor flow, canonical and international boundaries, exact-origin
collisions, reserved route kinds, cross-Tenant non-enumeration, grants/RLS and
privileged writers, concurrent claims, semantic idempotency, partial failure,
legacy migration, mixed versions and rollback, accessibility/low bandwidth,
staff comprehension, and production-shaped load.

Named production monitors include zero-tolerance reassignment, positive route
conflict, cross-Tenant leak, prohibited-sensitive-slug, and unreconciled-outcome
signals; measured collision, abandonment, early replacement, race, error,
latency, issuance-burst, locale-profile, and support-case thresholds each have
a named owner and response.

### Documentation status

The complete evidence is in
`phase-24-d11-human-readable-giving-slug-adversarial-review.md`. D11 qualifies
as an ADR candidate, but an accepted ADR and OpenSpec change wait for the
separately invoked `/to-prd` workflow and explicit reconciliation of the open
Phase 22/23 route work. This blocks implementation-ready status, not the
completed founder decision.

## D12 — Behavior of an older live address after exact-entry replacement

### Plain-language context and impact

D11 lets staff create a new address because an issued one cannot be edited.
Now Core needs one safe default for the old link when **nothing about the gift
meaning changed**.

Example: Hope Missions changes its preferred sharing link from:

```text
https://give.hope.org/give/water-project
```

to:

```text
https://give.hope.org/give/clean-water
```

Both addresses still represent the same immutable public-entry meaning:
Tenant, originating environment, original Site attribution, locale route,
Giving entry, Designation/donor task, and route kind. Each retains its own
distinct immutable address allocation. Old email, bookmarks, and printed QR
codes may remain in use. The question is whether the old address keeps opening
that same Giving page or immediately becomes **Page not found**. On every
request, Core revalidates route, Site, safety, and presentation eligibility.
Financial owners revalidate Legal Entity, Stripe, Settlement Account Binding,
bank, currency, and accounting facts only at their CTA, checkout-admission,
payment, or mutation boundary; those facts never select or remap either URL.

This is not a redirect decision. Under D9/D10, the old address may never move
to a different Site, gift, Designation, donor task, route kind, or “closest
match.” A proved different meaning, terminal disposition, or completed **Stop
old address** command receives D9's neutral `404`. Authority that is timed out,
corrupt, divergent, or outcome-unknown receives D10's neutral no-store `503`;
Core never guesses either continuity or terminality. A lawful prospective
financial/provider change alone does not reinterpret the route, although every
new checkout still must pass its owners' current checks.

### Options

1. **Keep the old address working for the same immutable public-entry meaning —
   recommended.** Both addresses resolve directly through their original route
   allocations to that same meaning; there is no redirect. Old bookmarks and
   QR codes keep working, while the new address is clearly **Preferred for
   sharing**. Staff can later use a separate, irreversible **Stop old address**
   action when privacy, safety, or obsolete public wording requires it. That
   Giving-owned, capability-gated terminal command revalidates expected heads,
   commits by compare-and-set with a durable audit receipt, clears preference
   if needed, and has no effect on existing gifts or recurring commitments.
   This is the least donor friction, but staff may accumulate several active
   links and must see a clear inventory.
2. **Stop the old address immediately.** Publishing the replacement makes the
   old address privacy-safe **Page not found**. Staff see the cleanest active
   inventory and obsolete wording disappears, but donors using old messages or
   printed materials fail even though the gift did not change.
3. **Ask staff during every replacement.** The review explains both results
   and requires staff to choose each time. This is flexible, but it makes a
   routine correction carry a consequential technical choice, creates
   inconsistent tenant behavior, and still needs a default for automation,
   retry, and accessibility.

### Recommendation

Choose option 1. Keep an older address serving only the same eligible immutable
public-entry meaning, mark the newer issued/current address **Preferred for
sharing**, and provide the capability-gated, audited, irreversible **Stop old
address** command above. This protects old donors without redirecting or moving
intent. If the route would represent a different Tenant, Site attribution,
originating environment, locale route, Giving entry, Designation/donor task, or
route kind, continuity is forbidden. If a current route, safety, host, Site, or
presentation check fails, public rendering follows that owner's fail-closed
contract; an unknown authority result is not mislabeled `404`. A financial
check gates only its owning CTA, checkout, payment, or mutation and may present
Giving as unavailable; it never suppresses otherwise eligible Site
presentation or repoints the URL.

### Exact question

When staff create a new preferred URL for the same Site and the same Giving
purpose, should the old URL keep opening that same Giving page by default, with
a separate audited and irreversible **Stop old address** action?

### Founder answer

Founder chose **Option 1** and required the complete staff journey to be clear,
beautiful, highly intuitive, and grounded in current UX evidence.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

The donor-protective default stands: when replacement B is issued for the same
eligible immutable public-entry meaning, older address A continues serving
that meaning directly through A's own allocation. B becomes **Preferred for
sharing**. A does not redirect, rewrite, traverse B, silently fall back, or
change Site attribution, Giving purpose, Designation/donor task, or financial
identity.

The required amendments make this safe and understandable:

- **Preferred for sharing** guides new Copy, Share, QR, and new generated-link
  actions only. It is never routing or authorization authority.
- A separate capability-gated **Make preferred for sharing** command may select
  only a same-scope issued/current address. It derives scope and actor on the
  server, compare-and-sets expected heads, and atomically records a semantic
  receipt, audit, and outbox; stale, cross-scope, unavailable, terminal, or
  unauthorized attempts have zero effect.
- Replacement atomically creates B, makes B preferred, and leaves A working as
  **Other address · Page opens**. Failure changes nothing; a response-lost
  retry returns the same durable B receipt.
- Every address independently revalidates allocation, host, Site, route,
  lifecycle, safety, and Giving-entry presentation eligibility before
  rendering. Designation and financial owners revalidate their facts only at
  the CTA, checkout-admission, payment, or mutation they own. A failed money
  check may disable new Giving but never remaps the address or suppresses
  otherwise eligible Site presentation.
- **Stop this address** is a separate, capability-gated, audited, irreversible
  terminal command. The ordinary command can target only one nonpreferred
  address while another eligible current preferred address
  survives. It never changes gifts or recurring commitments. Privacy/safety,
  Site retirement, and emergency containment retain separate owner paths.
- A stop atomically closes the canonical allocation and co-located router-
  equivalent address heads or none. It durably records dependent identities
  and downstream effect intents. QR files, CMS/email placements, embeds,
  search, and analytics are non-authoritative references that may still carry
  the terminal URL and reconcile later; stop never claims to rewrite them or
  repoints anything to the preferred address. Signed provider callbacks,
  Donor Portal routes, reconciliation, and the scoped checkout-result route for
  already-admitted work remain independent. The result route can report only
  one admitted operation and can never start/repeat a gift or revive the
  address.
- Activity and known-placement evidence are advisory, freshness-labeled, and
  honest about external, printed, forwarded, and bookmarked copies. Core never
  labels an address **Unused** or **Safe to stop**.
- Serving lifecycle and sharing preference remain separate. Terminal addresses
  stay permanently reserved and cannot resume, transfer, or be reused.
- Existing Core-managed placement convergence is not a hidden D12 side effect;
  it is the next founder decision, D13.

### Required staff UX/UI journey

1. The Giving-entry header presents one calm primary card:
   **Preferred for sharing · Page opens**, and—only for an authorized address
   manager under the current display/retention basis—the complete URL plus
   **Copy link**, **Test as donor**, and **Download QR**. One quiet line says how
   many other addresses open the page; **Manage addresses** opens inventory.
2. **Create new web address** first explains: this publication will not stop
   the current Core address; direct emails, bookmarks, and QR codes continue
   opening the same page after this change; the new address becomes preferred;
   gifts and recurring commitments do not change; and other safety,
   availability, and domain controls still apply.
3. Staff enter only the editable words beside the fixed, fully visible origin
   and prefix. Collision errors preserve input and offer a few public-safe
   alternatives; Core never reveals another Tenant or adds a surprise suffix.
4. A single before/after review shows the complete old/new addresses when
   current display authority permits, otherwise the source-owned safe/redacted
   labels and opaque references, plus Site, locale, Giving purpose, donor
   preview, and impact on known Core placements.
5. Success is a persistent receipt—not a disappearing toast—with the message
   **New preferred address published** and the reassurance **Your previous
   preferred address still opens the page**. The next best action, **Copy
   preferred link**, is visually primary.
6. The address inventory uses plain route statuses: **Preferred for sharing ·
   Page opens**, **Other address · Page opens**, **Temporarily unavailable in
   Core**, and **Stopped permanently in Core**. An unavailable or stopped
   address reports the observed public result only with fresh Core-routing
   proof; otherwise it says **Current public result not controlled by Core**
   and offers the domain action. New-gift readiness is a separate source-owned
   state such as **New gifts unavailable**, never folded into address status.
   The UI avoids ambiguous labels such as active, canonical, legacy, archived,
   or redirected.
7. A nonpreferred address detail page shows its exact purpose, immutable Site/locale
   attribution, known Core placements, aggregate activity with freshness, and
   explicit coverage limits. The exceptional action is **Stop this address**.
8. Permanent stop uses a dedicated review page focused at its heading. It shows
   the complete URL only when the stopper also has current need-to-know display
   authority and retention basis; otherwise it uses the source-owned safe/
   redacted label and opaque stable reference. It also shows real current state,
   the surviving preferred address under the same display rule, authoritative
   route effect, an inspectable grouped list of known Core placements, honest
   activity, the consequence for loaded-but-not-admitted donors, the separate
   checkout-result path for admitted donors, a distinct **Known external/
   provider links · Not controlled by this action** group, a closed reason,
   Core-versus-external-hosting control limit, and explicit admitted-work/
   history non-effects. **Do not stop this address** is the safe action;
   **Stop address permanently** validates missing reasons with an inline error
   and focused error summary. **Other serious reason** requires a bounded,
   server-validated plain-text explanation or safe evidence reference.
9. Success creates a durable terminal receipt explaining what stopped, which
   pages/addresses remain available, what did not change, and what staff should
   update next. Actor, reason/why, evidence, and full host/path appear only in
   their separately capability-filtered fields. The receipt separates Core's
   terminal record from a currently
   observed public `404`; external or unknown routing never receives a false
   Core-control claim. Its opaque URL is private/no-store; every read
   reauthorizes active Tenant membership and field capabilities, so copied URLs
   or revoked access reveal nothing extra. There is no Undo; an erroneous
   address needs a newly issued URL.
10. Viewers see state, address managers can replace or change preference,
    authorized stoppers can stop, and lower-privileged staff see **Request
    address stop**. An assistant may prepare the review but never performs the
    irreversible effect.

The interface follows Core's Maia/Zinc and shared Base UI patterns: spacious
hierarchy, one primary action, restrained status color, warning treatment only
at the final consequential step, no novelty animation, and full keyboard,
screen-reader, forced-color, reduced-motion, 320-pixel, 400%-zoom, RTL/native-
script, no-JavaScript, and weak-network support. Authorized complete URLs—and
required safe/redacted labels and opaque references when full display is not
permitted—remain readable, correctly named, wrapping, bidirectionally isolated,
and excluded from translation. Copy actions never reveal a value the viewer
cannot display.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories contain a material concern if Option 1 is left as
the sentence “keep the old URL working.” None requires rejecting direct
continuity. The permanent corrections above narrow it to the same structural
meaning, keep preference non-authoritative, make invalid and cross-Tenant
states impossible at the database/command boundary, serialize preference and
terminal transitions, fence stale checkout effects, make partial outcomes
reconcilable, preserve terminal allocation, minimize sensitive analytics, and
require accessible production-shaped proof.

The complete category-by-category review records severity, likelihood,
evidence, decision effect, permanent fix, exact normative clauses, 44 required
acceptance criteria, and named operational monitors in
`phase-24-d12-direct-giving-address-continuity-adversarial-review.md`.

### Affected contracts and required reconciliation

- Root glossary now separates **Preferred Giving Address** and **Stopped Giving
  Address** from address serving state.
- D9's privacy-safe absence and no-Giving-redirect invariant, D10's permanent
  allocation/lifecycle, and D11's immutable readable address remain governing.
- D9-R7's route-purpose registry must distinguish two Giving/payment-owned
  admitted-operation routes from the stopped Site address: an exact-target
  provider handoff after durable admission/session proof, and a read-only,
  nonredirectable result reader. Neither is a successor/fallback or has new-
  admission authority.
- Guest access uses the transport/security floor from
  [ADR-0025: Producer-owned protected actions](../../adr/0025-producer-owned-protected-actions.md)
  and
  [ADR-0037: Scanner-resistant exact-artifact access](../../adr/0037-scanner-safe-exact-artifact-access.md):
  inert selector, independent 256-bit fragment verifier, deliberate same-origin
  exchange at one code-owned allowlisted Asym doorway per environment/provider
  mode, purpose session, and exact no-store/no-referrer behavior—never a caller-
  selected host, bearer result URL, cross-origin cookie bootstrap, or revealing
  provider `GET`.
- Those ADRs do not authorize an anonymous subject. Phase 13/D12 must separately
  ratify one Tenant-scoped admitted-operation result authority whose subject is
  the exact opaque operation/session and whose issuance, scope, disclosure,
  expiry, revocation, recovery, and audit are explicit. Direct Protected Actions
  ADR authority requires its exact Party/contact; Core never infers one.
- D10-R4/R6 must be reconciled with D7-R17 and D12: route/presentation
  availability remains separate from Giving, Designation, and financial
  admission. A payment-owner failure may disable new gifts without hiding an
  otherwise eligible Site page or changing address state.
- D7 Site Serving Suspension suppresses Site presentation only. It never
  intercepts the fixed-Asym admitted-operation handoff/result; a legacy Site-
  qualified return requires the exact admitted-only carve-out or the same
  migration/expiry fence before website-offline activation for that scope.
- Accepted ADR-0029 keeps CMS/reference projections subordinate to operational
  Giving and route owners.
- Phase 5/13 and proposed Phase 22/23 route/reference work must be reconciled;
  ordinary Page redirects cannot authorize Giving redirects, and terminal stop
  cannot activate until checkout/payment owns a scoped admitted-operation
  result route independent of the Site address. Phase 13's optional account
  offer remains allowed only after the truthful result, under the separate
  Identity/Donor Portal owner, never as a confirmation gate or new-gift action.
- Every address-terminal writer—including Site retirement and safety owners—
  remains behind a per-scope cutover fence until pre-seam operations and still-
  replayable old return paths are source-proved migrated or safely expired;
  ambiguity blocks terminalization and rollback preserves result access.
- Open PR #1323 and PR #1340 remain proposed evidence until merged or
  superseded. Current `develop` behavior is migration evidence, not authority.

### Required evidence and documentation status

The D12 appendix is the durable adversarial and UX evidence. D12 is an ADR
candidate because direct continuity, non-routing preference, and irreversible
terminal stop are consequential and hard to reverse. An accepted ADR,
OpenSpec delta, PRD, implementation plan, tickets, migration, or runtime change
requires the separately invoked `/to-prd` workflow and contract
reconciliation. The founder decision itself is complete.

## D13 — Convergence of existing Core-managed Giving placements

### Plain-language context and impact

D12 already makes new Copy/Share/QR actions and future links generated from a
stable Giving reference use the preferred address. D13 covers only Core-
managed output that was already published or materialized with the earlier
address when preference changed.

Example: Hope Missions has a published Donate button on its Home Page, another
on the published Water Project Page, a prospective newsletter placement whose
source adapter is not yet available, and a downloaded QR file. Staff replace
`/give/water-project` with preferred `/give/clean-water`.

- A sent email, printed/downloaded QR, external website, or bookmark cannot and
  must not be silently rewritten.
- A URL staff deliberately pasted as literal text remains literal and is shown
  for review.
- An eligible reference-backed Page button may enter one dependency-only
  private website publication candidate using the stable Giving reference and
  new address generation. It does not edit the button or authored Page. A
  separately qualified editable source may create its own new version. An
  unsupported source and every approved, frozen, or immutable message/artifact
  remain **Not changed by Core**.
- Replacement itself does not stop the prior URL. A delayed update is nonurgent
  while that address remains current and opens its page; if another owner makes
  it unavailable or terminal, Core shows one cause-owned repair and never
  falls back.

The impact preview is capability-filtered and non-enumerating. A user-initiated
Prepare action uses only the human actor port. A separately ratified
noninteractive source occurrence may use its purpose-specific service-command
port, which cannot serve a user request or accept requester-selected scope.
Every source independently reauthorizes Tenant/scope, current source version,
placement, capability, and required review at each effect.

Without actor authority, Core creates no Page/source version. It creates a
source-owned attention state and deep link; one privacy-minimized owner request
exists only where an accepted typed source collaboration contract and verified
owner queue exist. Current generic Mission Control tasks, Giving workers,
outbox, and service role never bypass source-owner commands or RLS.

Example: a Giving manager may prepare one private website update covering the
Home Page and Water Project Page placements they are allowed to prepare. Page
copy and the public generation remain unchanged until the Website owner
publishes. The prospective newsletter shows **Source not available · Not
changed by Core**. Staff see **Ready to prepare**, **Needs an authorized
owner**, **Not changed by Core**, or **Could not be checked**.

Every proposed version binds target address ID/generation and expected
Preferred-head revision. If A→B prepares editable/unapproved work and C becomes
preferred first, the proposal stales/supersedes idempotently and presents C;
it never publishes B merely because B remains current. Approved/frozen output
never mutates and keeps its owner-approved address snapshot with review status.

Whichever option is selected, a Core-managed page/message owner must recheck
target lifecycle and the owner-approved/frozen preference snapshot appropriate
to the artifact when its new version publishes/sends. If publication wins
before a later Stop, its literal link points to the terminal allocation and
appears for cleanup; while the domain routes through Core it receives the
neutral `404`, and external routing remains outside Core's control. If Stop
wins, publication refreshes/rejects and never emits the stopped address.
Placement changes are advisory and never block Stop.

### Options

1. **Prepare authorized updates and route the rest to their owners after one
   impact preview — recommended.** Core prepares private source work only where
   the actor and an accepted source contract authorize it. Reference-backed
   Pages get a dependency-only publication candidate, not edited content.
   Other supported items show **Needs an authorized owner**; unsupported,
   approved/frozen, sent, downloaded, printed, external, and literal items show
   **Not changed by Core**. Editable proposals track/refresh the expected
   preference before approval/publish. Replacement does not stop the prior
   address, so delay is nonurgent while its page remains current; another owner
   state creates one repair with no fallback.
2. **Ask each authorized owner about every place.** Each Page/communications
   owner chooses their eligible button or editable draft. This gives maximum
   local control but adds repeated decisions, creates inconsistent links, and
   turns a simple address improvement into a migration checklist.
3. **Keep all existing Core-managed places unchanged.** Preferred affects new
   Copy/Share/QR actions and newly generated links only. This avoids automated
   updates but leaves avoidable nonpreferred addresses in current Core-managed
   output and creates continuing manual cleanup.

### Recommendation

Choose option 1. Give staff one capability-filtered preview; prepare only the
private source outcomes currently authorized, show the exact owner/source need
for the rest, route a grouped request only through an accepted verified queue,
and revalidate target lifecycle plus expected preference at every later source
effect. Never rewrite authored Page content for a reference-only change,
history, approved/frozen artifacts, sent messages, external copies,
printed/downloaded artifacts, or literal URLs.

### Exact question

After showing staff only the typed Core-managed places they may see, should Core
prepare authorized private source outcomes for the preferred Giving address,
show or route supported remaining work to its exact source owner, and leave
unsupported, approved/frozen, sent, downloaded, printed, external, and literal
artifacts **Not changed by Core**?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — Prepare authorized updates and route the rest to their owners.**

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

Option 1 remains the best staff experience only as private, source-owned
preparation—not a global URL replacement or hidden publish/send. `Giving` owns
the preference-change occurrence and never writes Page or Communications
content. Only a registered source owner may create its ordinary successor,
attention/review request, release, or send after reauthorizing the exact actor,
Tenant, environment, Site, locale, Giving entry, resource/version, placement,
capability, authorization epoch, lifecycle, and expected heads. A human
**Prepare** action uses only that actor's source port. A separately ratified
noninteractive source occurrence may use a purpose-specific service-command
port that cannot serve user requests or accept requester-selected scope.

Automatic preparation is limited to a typed **Core-managed Giving placement**
with stable source-owned identity and provenance. Raw URL equality, rich-text/
HTML/JSON search, provider results, analytics, and deliberate literal links
never authorize a write. Approved/frozen, scheduled, prepared, sent,
downloaded, printed, external, and otherwise immutable output never mutates.

The D13 button is **Prepare authorized updates**. It creates private source work
only; Page publication remains its accepted separate action, and
Communications approval/send exists only after that exact source family is
accepted and activated. For reference-backed Page/Navigation placements, authored
content and Working Revisions do not change: Core prepares a private
publication candidate that reuses the stable Giving reference, pins the new
address generation, and closes the exact actor/source-authorized placement
work package into one complete Site-locale Public Site Generation and serving-
head CAS. Out-of-scope placements remain structurally unchanged and receive
only their own non-enumerating source attention. Existing human work, active
editor leases, candidates, reviews, schedules, and approvals are preserved. A
Page's later private draft is visibly excluded from the dependency-only
candidate; a source that would require an authored patch uses **Content changed
· Review latest**, never overwrite or branch.

Every managed placement structurally references the exact Giving entry,
directly or through a same-scope binding. Giving entry is never inferred from
Designation, title, Page, URL text, Preferred address, or similarity.
Newsletter/marketing Communications remain **Source not available · Not
changed by Core** until their own accepted authoring/version/freeze/send contract
ships; Phase 17 System Messages cannot be stretched into that authority. A
scheduled publication never rebases: changing it requires an unscheduled
successor or an explicit source-owner replace/cancel plus repeated review.

Each proposal pins the source head/version, placement, old/target address
generation, expected Preferred revision, semantic dependency-delta or content-
patch digest as applicable, actor/authority path, and idempotency identity. A→B
editable/unapproved work stales
or is superseded when C becomes preferred. Approved/frozen B remains immutable
but can newly release/send only while B is still issued/current. Stop-first
blocks new emission; publish/send-first preserves history and a later Stop
creates one source-owned repair. Stop never waits for convergence and no path
falls back.

Cross-owner preparation is itemized, resumable, and non-atomic. Staff see only
currently permitted evidence grouped as **Ready to prepare**, **Needs an
authorized owner**, **Not changed by Core**, or **Could not be checked**.
Hidden resources contribute no count or existence signal. Source routing
derives a source-owned attention state and exact deep link. It creates at most
one privacy-minimized request only where an accepted source collaboration
contract exists, and never lets the initiator select or invent an approver.
Current generic Mission Control task infrastructure is not D13 authority.

### Required staff UX/UI journey

1. D12's success receipt keeps **Copy preferred address** primary and offers
   **Review places to update** secondarily, explaining that the earlier Core
   address still works and this cleanup is nonurgent.
2. One capability-filtered review shows Site, locale, Giving purpose,
   authorized old/new display, and four plain outcome groups. With ready work,
   **Prepare N authorized updates** is primary and adjacent text names any
   owner reviews it also requests. With zero ready items but a verified owner
   queue, the action is **Request N owner reviews**. With neither effect, no
   disabled/zero button appears; retry/checklist/copy/Done leads. **Not now** is
   safe.
3. Responsive source cards say what content is affected, which source owns it,
   what visitors/recipients get now, what private change is proposed, who acts
   next, and the exact next action. They do not expose provider/version jargon.
4. Preparation creates only private source publication candidates/versions and
   owner-routed attention. There are no per-item checkboxes, hidden
   auto-publication, warning theater, or cross-source transaction.
5. A durable receipt reports, for example, **1 website update covering 3
   placements prepared · 1 owner review requested · 4 not changed by Core**,
   with itemized source receipts and safe residual retry.
6. Page owners land on the exact publication candidate and stable-reference
   dependency diff, then use accepted source-owned review/publish actions. Only
   after an exact Communications family has an accepted and activated adapter
   do its owners land on an editable source version and use its source-owned
   approval/schedule/send path; otherwise it stays **Source not available · Not
   changed by Core**.
7. Immutable/external evidence is labelled **Not changed by Core** and may
   receive **Copy preferred address** or an honest generated-at checklist.
8. Core Maia/Zinc/Base UI, one primary action, status text plus icon, 320-pixel
   reflow, 400% zoom, keyboard/touch/screen-reader support, forced colors,
   RTL/native script, bidirectional URL isolation, weak-network resume, and
   reduced motion are release gates.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories contain a material concern if Option 1 remains the
informal phrase “update authorized links.” None invalidates the selected
direction. The permanent corrections above prevent search-and-replace,
confused-deputy service writes, draft loss, hidden publication, dual ownership,
cross-Tenant enumeration, stale/terminal link emission, false global success,
task/notification spam, unsafe backfill, and vendor-driven coupling.

The complete review records what could go wrong, why it matters, severity,
likelihood, evidence, decision effect, permanent prevention, exact normative
clauses, 44 acceptance criteria, and 14 named monitors in
[`phase-24-d13-authorized-giving-placement-convergence-adversarial-review.md`](./phase-24-d13-authorized-giving-placement-convergence-adversarial-review.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Root glossary now defines **Core-managed Giving placement** without giving it
  Page, Communications, Giving, or financial authority.
- Accepted ADR-0029 remains controlling: CMS stores stable operational
  references plus presentation; Giving remains operational truth; there is no
  cross-schema FK/sync engine.
- Accepted ADR-0032 remains controlling for prepared/sent communication:
  frozen message bytes/identity do not rerender or change under recovery.
- D9–D12's privacy-safe absence, no redirect/fallback, permanent allocation,
  immutable slug, direct continuity, nonrouting preference, and terminal Stop
  remain unchanged.
- Open PR #1323's Page version/review/release model and PR #1340's Working
  Revision/Content Health model are proposed evidence until merged or
  superseded. D13 activation waits for the exact source contract's accepted
  final form.
- Current broad Payload staff access, raw href/merge-tag values, logger audit,
  and generic finance-oriented tasks are migration evidence, not D13 authority.
- Proposed Phase 23's complete Site-locale Public Site Generation and separate
  actor/service ports must be reconciled in their accepted final form. A Page
  preference-only change must not copy the URL into authored content.
- Newsletter/marketing Communications need their separately owned future
  source contract; current System Messages and **Coming soon** email scheduling
  are not implementation proof.
- D13 is an ADR candidate. Accepted ADR/OpenSpec/PRD/design/tickets/runtime work
  requires the separately invoked specification workflow; this founder
  decision and adversarial evidence are complete.

## D14 — Locale identity of a Giving address

### Plain-language context and impact

D13 makes every placement update exact to its source locale but deliberately
leaves target-address compatibility to D14. D14 decides whether the public
Giving address itself is locale-specific on a multilingual Site.

A locale is a language-and-formatting context such as `en-US` or `fr-CA`; it
is not a country, currency, Site, Legal Entity, Stripe account, settlement, or
bank identity.

Example: Hope Missions publishes Clean Water Giving in English and French.
Should it have stable English and French addresses such as
`hope.org/lang/en-us/give/clean-water` and
`hope.org/lang/fr-ca/give/eau-potable`, or should one URL silently change language
based on browser settings? The prefixes are illustrative; D14 does not choose
their final placement. D11's base-relative `/give/` root remains literal.

The choice affects donor confidence, bookmarks, staff sharing, D13 placement
scope, translation readiness, search, caching, analytics, and language
switching. It never selects currency or financial identity.

Current official evidence favors explicit identities:
[Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/managing-multi-regional-sites)
recommends different URLs per language and warns against automatic language
redirects; [W3C](https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-when-lang-neg)
explains that automatic language negotiation is imperfect and recommends a
clear user override; and
[Next.js](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/internationalization) supports
multiple routing patterns without choosing the product rule for Core.

### Options

1. **When Site-level Giving is enabled and an exact locale presentation is
   ready, let authorized staff deliberately issue one independent address for
   it — recommended.** Each
   issued address has immutable exact-locale meaning and its own staff-approved
   readable slug. Publishing/enabling a Site locale never issues an address or
   enables Giving. A visible language switch appears only when both locale
   presentations and addresses are independently published/issued, current,
   compatible, and eligible. Browser language may suggest a choice but never
   silently redirects. Missing French remains honestly unavailable instead of
   showing English at a French URL. Staff manage an additional address only
   where that exact presentation is ready; D14 adds no second admission toggle.
2. **One locale-neutral address that negotiates language.** The URL is short,
   but the same link can show different content based on browser/cookie,
   weakening reproducibility, cache/search behavior, staff preview, printed
   material, and exact-locale attribution.
3. **Only the Site default locale gets a Giving address.** Additional-locale
   Pages explicitly hand donors to the default-language Giving page. This is
   operationally simplest but creates a mixed-language donor journey and makes
   multilingual Giving incomplete.

### Recommendation

Choose Option 1. Where Site-level Giving is enabled and exact locale
presentation is ready, it gives each language a stable, honest public identity
while keeping the donor in control through a visible language switch.
Site-locale publication alone never auto-enables Giving or issues an address.
An English placement can update only to an independently issued address with
the same exact stable Site Locale and Giving-entry meaning; it never drifts to
French or infers language from the browser.

### Exact question

When Site-level Giving is enabled and one published Site-locale presentation is
ready, should authorized staff deliberately issue that locale its own stable
Giving address, with a language switch only to another independently current
locale address and no automatic language redirect?

### Founder answer

**Independent address per Giving-enabled locale.**

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

The selected direction is permanent: every newly issued Giving address belongs
to one exact stable Site Locale and one Giving-entry meaning. A literal English
address always presents English; a literal French address always presents
French. Browser settings, cookies, IP/geolocation, current Site default,
provider settings, currency, and authenticated preference never redirect,
negotiate, or replace the language at that address.

“Giving-enabled locale” is staff language, not a new god Boolean or second
financial-admission toggle. Core derives readiness from the separately owned
Site-locale release, exact-locale Giving presentation, Site-level Giving
capability, current Giving-entry/safety facts, and address lifecycle. D7
admission remains a separate Site-wide checkout gate. Publishing a Site locale
never enables Giving or issues an address; changing D7 admission never creates
locale content or an address. Authorized staff issue the exact address
deliberately after current readiness proof.

An exact locale may have zero or several issued/current addresses for one
Giving entry because D12 replacements continue directly. At most one is
Preferred for sharing per exact Tenant × environment × Site × stable Site
Locale × Giving entry. Issuing/replacing French changes no English address or
preference.

### Accepted decision

- **Site Locale** is a stable Site-owned public presentation context identified
  by one canonical BCP 47 locale under a versioned IANA/Unicode profile. It is
  not a country, currency, Site, Legal Entity, Stripe account, settlement,
  bank, or accounting identity.
- Every Issued Giving Address immutably pins one Tenant, originating
  environment, Site, stable Site Locale/catalog generation, Giving entry, and
  D10/D11 route-allocation manifest. Similar language, region, script, title,
  slug, or browser preference never proves equivalence.
- Only standards-profile canonical equivalents or deprecated-tag preferred
  values may share one Site Locale identity. `fr`/`fr-CA`, `pt-BR`/`pt-PT`,
  `zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant`, and `sr-Latn`/`sr-Cyrl` remain distinct; no Tenant or
  owner policy may alias materially different language/script/region
  presentations.
- A Site default-locale, locale display-name, canonical-alias/profile, browser,
  provider, or title change never relabels, reassigns, redirects, or mutates an
  issued address. A replacement locale identity gets separately issued
  addresses.
- D14 adds no `locale_giving_enabled` financial switch. The UI may summarize
  **French Giving page ready** only as a projection over Site-level Giving
  capability and exact French presentation/Giving facts. D7 **New gifts from
  this Site** is a separate Site-wide status.
- Site-level Giving capability not yet enabled blocks new address issuance.
  After an address exists, ordinary reversible containment uses D7. A later
  capability disabled/needs-attention outcome alone never mutates, hides,
  stops, unprefers, or reassigns an issued address; presentation and route
  effects remain with their existing source owners.
- “Ready to publish address” requires the exact actor capability, verified
  Site/public base, current complete Site-locale and Giving-entry
  presentations, Site-level Giving authority, route support, rendering/
  accessibility capability, and no adverse safety/lifecycle block. It does not
  require every Site Page, message, receipt, provider surface, or language to
  be complete. D7 pause, Designation/financial admission, and provider
  checkout-language support do not block or stale issuance; they govern the
  CTA/checkout outcome. A paused Site may publish the exact-locale address, and
  the page shows **New gifts unavailable**.
- D11's shape remains
  `{verified-site-public-base}/give/{staff-chosen-slug}`. The locale owner may
  contribute a later-ratified literal segment to the public base, but `/give/`
  is not translated or tenant-configured. Staff edit only the final public-safe
  words.
- Core proposes the final words from approved exact-locale public copy. It
  never silently translates, transliterates, suffixes, claims, or replaces
  staff input. Collision identity is the complete canonical address; different
  admitted locale public bases may reuse the same final words.
- Suggestions, availability hints, drafts, autosave, preview, Site/locale/
  Giving setup, QR preview, and background work consume no route. One explicit
  locale-named issue action reauthorizes/re-proves current heads and atomically
  commits allocation, locale binding, exact-locale preference effect, business
  audit, durable result receipt, and projection outbox—or nothing.
- The Site-locale owner owns locale identity/public presentation/public-base
  facts; CMS/Page owners own localized content/release; Giving/route owners own
  Giving meaning/address/preference/Stop; D7 owns Site public-Gift admission;
  finance owners alone own Designation, Legal Entity, Tenant Stripe account,
  settlement, currency, bank, receipt, and accounting facts.
- Disabling new Site gifts leaves an otherwise current exact-locale page and
  address available with **New gifts unavailable**. Withdrawing the exact
  locale presentation makes its route/alternative unfavorable without
  rendering another language, releasing allocation, or fabricating Stop.
  Recovery can restore only the same identity/meaning.
- A direct issued URL never negotiates or auto-redirects. Browser language may
  support only a dismissible user-activated suggestion to an independently
  current exact alternative. Missing/unknown/terminal targets use their
  privacy-safe adverse contract, never a locale homepage or default Giving
  page.
- A language switch is a server-rendered semantic link derived from a trusted
  same-Site/same-Giving-entry relation to another independently
  issued/current/preferred, current-presentation, safe, eligible address. Core
  never builds it by translating/replacing URL text. D7 pause does not hide a
  current language link; it changes only the target page's new-gift CTA.
- Donor labels use native language name plus optional script/region with
  correct `lang`, direction, and bidi isolation; flags never identify
  languages. The control works without JavaScript and under keyboard,
  screen-reader, touch, long/CJK/RTL, forced-colors, reduced-motion, 320-pixel,
  and 400%-zoom conditions.
- A switch drops arbitrary query/fragment, amount, cadence, currency, personal,
  payment, session, provider, token, and cart state. Only a separately accepted
  attribution owner may preserve sanitized non-authoritative Source Code. An
  admitted checkout can change display language only under its owner without
  navigating addresses or changing frozen facts.
- D13 compatibility is exact stable Site Locale plus exact Giving-entry
  meaning. An English placement never converges to French. No compatible
  preferred target means no prepared public/source effect.
- QR/share artifacts encode and visibly label the exact immutable locale URL
  only after issuance and cannot repoint. D14 does not mandate indexing. If
  search admits the pages, a preferred locale address self-canonicalizes, an
  eligible nonpreferred address may use D12's same-locale canonical to the
  preferred address but emits no `hreflang` cluster or sitemap membership of
  its own. Only preferred canonical locale pages participate in reciprocal
  self-inclusive `hreflang` and localized sitemaps using current preferred
  addresses from one exact-equivalence manifest. Visible donor language links
  remain ordinary navigation. No French → English canonical, donor redirect,
  or Giving `x-default` fallback is allowed.
- Structural same-scope relationships, canonical address uniqueness,
  at-most-one exact-locale preferred head, immutable history, restricted
  deletion, explicit grants, operation-correct RLS `USING`/`WITH CHECK`,
  hardened views/functions, and service/owner/Payload/worker/import/support
  poison tests enforce the same boundary.
- Issuance pins expected locale catalog, Site-locale/public release,
  Site-level Giving capability, Giving-entry, host/route, authorization,
  address, and preference heads. D7 admission does not participate in, lock,
  CAS, or stale issuance. Races use a bounded transaction and one durable
  receipt; unknown outcomes read it back rather than claiming another address.
- Migration leaves external/unissued literal URLs external, binds a proved
  fixed-locale Core route exactly once, and never infers from current default,
  URL/title/content, country/currency, browser traffic, provider settings, or
  majority use. Every negotiated, ambiguous, or unproved Core route remains
  reserved/nonissuable, nonpreferred, quarantined, and privacy-safe absent. D14
  authorizes no legacy chooser or redirect; a real census-proved continuity
  need requires a separate founder decision. Readers and negative occupancy
  precede writers; rollback retains every allocation/locale fact.

### Required staff and donor UX/UI

Staff enter one Giving-owned **Giving page addresses** view. Single-locale
Sites keep one quiet card. Multi-locale Sites use a responsive vertical list,
not a matrix:

```text
English (United States)
Website ready · Giving page ready · Preferred address ready
hope.org/lang/en-us/give/clean-water                [ Copy address ]

Français (Canada) · French (Canada)
Website ready · Giving page ready · Address not created
                                          [ Create French Giving address ]

العربية · Arabic
Website needs review                         [ Review Arabic website ]
```

D7 **New gifts from this Site** appears once above the locale list, never as a
per-locale toggle. During a pause it says language pages/addresses still open
while donors cannot start a new gift.

Creation shows the fixed full base plus `/give/`, one editable final segment,
exact language and purpose, current blockers, and **Preview as donor**. The
final action is **Publish French Giving address** and explains that the address
is permanent while English, currency, Stripe, settlement, and existing gifts
do not change. Success persists with **Copy address**, **Test as donor**,
**Download French (Canada) QR code**, and optional D13 placement review.

A donor opening `hope.org/lang/fr-ca/give/eau-potable` always receives French
Canadian presentation. **English (United States)** appears only as a deliberate
link while that exact sibling remains independently current. Core never sends
the donor there automatically.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories contain a material concern if the founder answer
remains informal. None invalidates independent exact-locale addresses. The
permanent corrections prevent a second Giving toggle, default/browser/provider
fallback, wrong-locale D13 convergence, locale-selected finance, cross-Tenant
enumeration, provider-owned identity, address/QR mutation, destructive legacy
inference, and mixed-version route drift.

The complete review records every failure, impact, severity, likelihood,
evidence, decision effect, permanent prevention, exact clause, 55 acceptance
criteria, and 17 named monitors in
[`phase-24-d14-independent-locale-giving-address-adversarial-review.md`](./phase-24-d14-independent-locale-giving-address-adversarial-review.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Root glossary now defines **Site Locale** and **Exact-locale Giving Address**
  and narrows Issued/Preferred address and Core-managed placement to exact
  locale scope.
- D14 explicitly narrows Phase 2's generic locale fallback for issued Giving
  addresses and resolves the compatibility seam D13 left open.
- D11's fixed `/give/` family, human-readable final segment, atomic issue, and
  permanent reservation remain unchanged. D12 direct continuity and terminal
  Stop remain per exact locale.
- PR #1323/#1340 exact-locale/public-generation material is proposed evidence
  until merged/superseded and must be reconciled before implementation-ready
  status. Current hard-coded English/null Site/raw checkout links are migration
  facts, not D14 authority.
- D14 is an ADR candidate. Accepted ADR/PRD/OpenSpec/design/tickets/schema/
  migration/runtime work requires the separately invoked specification flow.

## D15 — Explicit Site-locale public base for locale-bearing content

### Plain-language context and impact

D14 freezes each address to one exact Site Locale. D11 places locale inside the
Site-locale public base before Giving appends fixed `/give/{slug}`. D15 must
therefore choose one base strategy used consistently by locale-bearing Pages,
Navigation, Giving, canonical/`hreflang`/sitemap, cache identity, and public
generations—not a Giving-only prefix and not a blanket rule for APIs, callbacks,
or protocol files.

If the default stays unprefixed, `hope.org/about` and
`hope.org/give/clean-water` are shorter but must remain English forever when a
later Site default changes. If every locale is explicit, the whole public Site
gets one stable route rule. The adversarial pass found that direct
`/{locale}` collides with real `api`, `app`, and `dev` IANA language tags and
Core root control routes, so the corrected examples use a fixed namespace:

```text
hope.org/lang/en-us/about
hope.org/lang/en-us/give/clean-water
hope.org/lang/fr-ca/a-propos
hope.org/lang/fr-ca/give/eau-potable
```

Current `develop` has no D10/D11 Issued Giving Address cohort. If such an older
unprefixed cohort is later discovered, only an address with authoritative
exact-locale binding and continuing D12 eligibility keeps that meaning and
works directly. Negotiated/ambiguous/unproved routes remain reserved,
quarantined, and privacy-safe absent under D14. Ordinary Pages keep their
owner-specific continuity. Nothing redirects, chooses a language, or is
relabelled.

### Options

1. **Every Site Locale gets an explicit segment across locale-bearing public
   content — recommended.** This creates one stable invariant; the cost is a
   slightly longer default-language URL. A fixed namespace or permanent
   separation from root control routes still requires adversarial proof.
2. **The default Site Locale is unprefixed; additional locales get a segment
   across all public routes.** This keeps the common routes shortest but
   requires permanent default-route pins plus extra alias, collision,
   migration, cache, and source-owner continuity cases.
3. **Each Site Locale uses its own domain or subdomain across all public
   routes.** This supports deliberate regional brand separation, but as a
   default adds DNS, verification, certificates, canonical/search, incident,
   migration, and staff burden.

### Recommendation

Choose Option 1. A public Site and its permanent Giving links benefit more from
one visible, predictable invariant than from saving one path segment. Staff
complexity stays low because every source owner supplies the fixed locale base;
staff edit only meaningful Page/Giving words.

### Exact question

Should every Site Locale—including the default—use an explicit locale segment
in one public base consumed consistently by Pages, Navigation, Giving, search,
cache, and public generations, or should the default locale remain unprefixed?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — explicit locale for every language.**

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

The founder direction is permanent: every exact Site Locale—including the
current default and the only locale on a single-locale Site—uses one explicit
locale identity across every locale-bearing human public content route. The
canonical wording is **Site Locale**, not merely language, because language,
script, region, and variant may distinguish public presentation.

The answer does not literally apply to every endpoint. Root `/robots.txt`,
root sitemap/index, `/.well-known/*`, framework assets, APIs, webhooks, auth/
preview callbacks, checkout/payment continuation/result routes, and
authenticated product routes remain in a finite source-owned nonlocalized
route-class registry.

Direct `/{locale}` is rejected after primary-source review. IANA currently
assigns `api` (Apiaká), `app` (Apma), and `dev` (Domung), while Core already
uses root control namespaces. To support every legitimate language without
blacklists, suffixes, route-order accidents, or a costly control-origin move,
the permanent launch grammar is:

```text
{verified-site-public-base}/lang/{lowercase-exact-locale}/{owner-path}
```

Examples:

```text
hope.org/lang/en-us/about
hope.org/lang/fr-ca/a-propos
hope.org/lang/fr-ca/give/eau-potable
hope.org/lang/api/about
hope.org/api/donate
```

This is a Core stability/equity decision, not an SEO-ranking claim. Google
accepts several locale URL structures and does not require a prefixed default.

### Accepted decision

- Every favorable locale-bearing public homepage, ordinary Page/Article,
  specialized ministry Page, update, localized public form/document, and
  Giving entry consumes one exact Site Locale Public Base. No favorable new
  default/primary/only-locale content route is unprefixed.
- The base order is trusted verified Site origin → optional permanent shared-
  host Site handle → fixed `/lang/` namespace → immutable lowercase exact-
  locale segment. Giving then appends fixed `/give/{slug}`.
- `/lang/` is code-owned and permanently reserved. Pages, CMS catch-alls,
  Navigation, plugins, redirects, imports, tenants, and middleware cannot claim,
  translate, or override it.
- That reservation outranks generic Page continuity. `/lang`, malformed,
  ambiguous, and nonconforming legacy namespace routes remain reserved/privacy-
  safe absent with no redirect and receive a Page-owner successor. A conforming
  `/lang/{exact-Site-Locale}/{owner-path}` ordinary Page may continue directly—
  never by redirect/alias—only after atomic proof of the same Tenant,
  environment, Site, verified origin, stable exact locale, immutable Page/
  resource, route kind, meaning, and collision-free address and migration into
  the new authority. Giving uses D10–D14 only. Staff see exact impact; an
  unacceptable proved pre-allocation cost reopens D15, never route precedence.
- The stable Site Locale ID and pinned canonical BCP 47 profile own locale
  meaning. Core generates the segment once by serializing the exact canonical
  tag in lowercase ASCII with hyphens. Staff do not type it.
- Core preserves every justified language/script/region/variant distinction
  and never forces a country. Generic `fr` remains `fr`; `fr-CA`, `zh-Hant`,
  and `sr-Cyrl` remain distinct when their public content needs that precision.
- Tenant address, domain, browser, IP, traffic, currency, Stripe country, and
  provider settings never infer locale specificity.
- Private locale setup, copy, draft, autosave, import, preview, and advisory
  availability consume no public route. First favorable activation atomically
  commits allocation, stable locale binding, base/public generation, business
  audit, durable receipt, and outbox—or nothing.
- After first public use, the segment is immutable and non-reusable. Changing
  default locale, display name, latest standards profile, Page title, branding,
  host, currency, or provider does not rewrite it. A material correction uses
  a governed successor.
- A direct `/en-us/...`, missing `/lang`, unknown/malformed segment, or
  unavailable locale never aliases, negotiates, redirects, or renders another
  locale/Site/Tenant. Explicit routes ignore browser, cookie, IP, profile,
  default, currency, query, referrer, provider, and device.
- D15 itself supplies no locale-neutral root content, redirect, chooser,
  negotiation, or `x-default` and never redirects Giving intent. D16 later
  governs the distinct Site Root Entry without changing any D15 explicit base.
- One finite typed route registry classifies content, Giving, specialized and
  ordinary Pages, infrastructure, API/control, preview, authenticated, and
  transaction routes before positive release. Catch-alls/framework defaults
  never infer the class.
- Root `/robots.txt`, sitemap/index, `/.well-known/*`, assets, API/webhook/
  health, auth/protected action, Preview enablement, checkout/provider return,
  and authenticated portals retain source ownership. They may carry a locale
  under their own contract but are not Site-locale public content identity.
- Site Locale owns stable locale meaning/lifecycle; shared route authority owns
  literal allocation/occupancy; Domain/Site owns verified base/handle; Page and
  specialized owners own their relative paths/continuity; Giving owns
  `/give/{slug}`/preference/Stop; Navigation owns membership/labels; search,
  cache, QR, preview, support, and analytics derive.
- Editable managed candidates/current projections store stable source
  references and resolve only while compiling a new compatible immutable
  generation/effect. Frozen publications, schedules, messages, documents,
  downloads/exports, QR/printed/share artifacts pin their exact absolute URL
  and generation forever; a new destination creates a new owner-authorized
  artifact/effect. External literals stay literal or quarantine. Language
  alternatives use exact semantic relations, never string replacement.
- The globally unique key is canonical external origin plus normalized path
  across all Sites, Tenants, environments, host departure/return, route kinds,
  owners, and history. Tenant, environment, Site, host generation, handle,
  owner, allocation, and canonicalizer/profile are immutable provenance and
  never partition uniqueness. Canonical comparison includes case, IDNA/
  effective port, encoding, Unicode, separators, dot/slash/trailing-slash
  rules, and router-equivalent forms.
- One complete public generation pins exact base, locale release, shell,
  Navigation, route/content/Giving references, search inputs, cache identity,
  renderer, and dependencies. Expected-head activation cannot mix generations.
- Eligible canonical ordinary/specialized locale Pages self-canonicalize.
  Giving preserves D14: preferred exact-locale addresses self-canonicalize;
  eligible nonpreferred addresses may canonicalize only to the same-locale
  preferred address and never redirect. Reciprocal self-inclusive `hreflang`
  contains only exact current equivalents. Provider-unsupported locale values
  are mapped only by separately proved compatibility or omitted; route identity
  never changes for a search provider.
- Sitemaps list eligible canonical locale URLs and split before 50,000 URLs or
  50MB uncompressed. Root crawler artifacts remain guidance, not access
  control. D16 later permits the Site Root Entry as `x-default` only in an
  eligible homepage cluster; deep Pages and Giving remain excluded.
- Structural same-scope keys, unique canonical occupancy, restrictive delete,
  explicit grants, operation-correct RLS `USING`/`WITH CHECK`, hardened
  service/worker/Payload/import/support/RPC paths, and poison tests prevent
  cross-Tenant/Site/locale mutation, disclosure, transfer, or reuse.
- Commands pin current authority/route/generation heads, use bounded lock
  order and one durable business idempotency key, perform no external call
  under lock, return the original receipt on retry, and reconcile unknown
  outcomes before another effect.
- Cache keys include Tenant, environment, Site, trusted host, stable Site
  Locale ID, public-base generation, owner/resource, audience, public
  generation, and renderer. Tags invalidate only and never isolate.
- Negative route/collision/cache/error/log/support behavior reveals no other
  Tenant, unpublished/restricted locale, sensitive ministry/location, actor,
  title, financial fact, or lifecycle.
- Site Locale and URL never select Giving entry, Designation, Legal Entity,
  Tenant Stripe account, currency, settlement, bank, tax/receipt legal facts,
  or accounting identity. Site Locale may provide a validated presentation-
  locale request; checkout/message/receipt owners independently resolve and
  record the actual rendered locale. Financial operations resolve/freeze their
  facts through their own owners after admission.
- Migration inventories and evidence-classifies every current route/owner/
  exact-locale fact. It never infers locale from today's default, path/copy,
  country, currency, traffic, browser, or provider. Ordinary Page continuity
  remains Page-owned; specialized routes remain source-owned; Giving never
  redirects or falls back.
- For legacy `/lang*`, the namespace rule above is decisive: only a proved
  conforming same-resource ordinary Page may migrate and continue directly;
  `/lang`, malformed/ambiguous/nonconforming sources never serve or redirect
  after cohort activation and receive a reviewed successor with staff-visible
  old/new-link impact. Giving receives no Page continuity.
- Typed route classification/reservation/negative readers precede writers;
  Sites activate by cohort; host-blind `/give`/`/donate` redirects, generic
  catch-all, static canonical/default assumptions, and null-Site seams are
  removed or fenced first. Post-public rollback retains allocation/history and
  recovers forward or serves privacy-safe absence.
- Accepted ADR-0026 must later be explicitly amended: locale-bearing families
  become base-relative below `/lang/{segment}` while ADR-0026's public root
  `/checkout` and bare/root legacy/control forms stay with their source owners.
  Open PRs #1323/#1340 remain proposed evidence until merged or superseded.

### Required staff and visitor UX/UI

Staff use **Site → Languages**. One locale is a quiet row; several locales use
a responsive vertical list, not a matrix. Adding a language searches native
and staff-language names, asks for region/script only when meaningful, and uses
no flags.

Core shows the generated result before staff continue:

```text
French (Canada)

Website address prefix                         Not public yet
hope.org/lang/fr-ca

Core adds this automatically to every French (Canada) website address.
Changing the default language later will not change it.

Planned Page      hope.org/lang/fr-ca/a-propos
Planned Giving    hope.org/lang/fr-ca/give/eau-potable
```

Page editing exposes `hope.org/lang/fr-ca/ [ a-propos ]`. Giving exposes
`hope.org/lang/fr-ca/give/ [ eau-potable ]`. Staff never type the domain,
Site handle, `/lang/`, locale code, `/give/`, or complete URL.

First publication shows the exact language, Site, prefix, route count,
blockers, continuity, permanent consequence, and unchanged default/finance
facts. One primary action publishes; success returns a durable receipt plus
**Open website**, **Copy website address**, and **Manage French (Canada) content**.

A visitor opening `hope.org/lang/fr-ca/a-propos` always receives French
(Canada), correct HTML language/direction, same-locale managed Navigation, and
an exact corresponding language link only when that target is current. A donor
opening `hope.org/lang/fr-ca/give/eau-potable` never changes language or
financial identity through hidden signals.

The flows must pass keyboard, screen-reader, visible-focus, touch, forced-
color, reduced-motion, long/CJK/RTL, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 400% zoom, no-
JavaScript public navigation, and weak-network recovery requirements in the
shared Maia/Base UI system.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories contain a material concern if the founder answer
remains informal. None invalidates explicit locale identity. The corrected
decision closes direct-locale/control collisions, default-route mutation,
wrong-locale fallback, copied URL drift, CMS/framework/provider ownership,
cross-Tenant cache/RLS leakage, partial activation, destructive migration,
Giving redirects, and locale-selected finance without building a customizable
routing or translation platform.

The complete review records every failure, impact, severity, likelihood,
evidence, decision effect, permanent prevention, exact clause, 74 acceptance
criteria, and named production monitors in
[`phase-24-d15-explicit-site-locale-public-base-adversarial-review.md`](./phase-24-d15-explicit-site-locale-public-base-adversarial-review.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Root glossary now defines **Site Locale Public Base**.
- D15 narrows Phase 2's generic fallback and current unprefixed/default behavior
  for favorable public reads. It preserves D14's exact locale and D9–D14
  Giving no-redirect contract.
- D11's fixed `/give/` family remains unchanged relative to the Site Locale
  Public Base. `/lang/` is fixed, code-owned, nonlocalized, and noneditable.
- Accepted ADR-0026 needs an explicit later amendment; D15 is itself an ADR
  candidate because public URL shape is hard to reverse, surprising, and a
  real trade-off.
- PR #1323/#1340 exact-locale/public-generation material is proposed evidence
  until merged/superseded. Current unprefixed English/null-Site/static redirect
  behavior is migration fact, not D15 authority.
- Accepted ADR/PRD/OpenSpec/design/tickets/schema/migration/runtime work requires
  the separately invoked specification flow.

## D16 — Locale-neutral Site root behavior

### Plain-language context and impact

D15 makes every real language homepage explicit, such as
`hope.org/lang/en-us` and `hope.org/lang/fr-ca`. Bare `hope.org/` is therefore
neutral and contains no Giving intent. D16 must decide what a visitor sees when
they open only the domain. The answer cannot change or redirect any explicit
Page or Giving address.

### Options

1. **Temporarily redirect the neutral root to the current default Site Locale —
   recommended.** The destination is deterministic; browser language, IP, and
   cookies are ignored. Visitors reach a real homepage in one step and retain a
   visible language control. A later default change affects only the neutral
   root destination.
2. **Temporarily redirect a single-locale neutral root to its sole explicit
   locale URL; show a neutral chooser only on multi-locale Sites.** Localized
   content remains at `/lang/{locale}`, never directly at `/`. This is the
   strongest explicit `x-default` experience and adds no choice on a single-
   locale Site, but adds one for new multi-locale root visitors who expect a
   homepage.
3. **Redirect using browser or remembered language, with default fallback.**
   This often personalizes the first page, but is nondeterministic, harder to
   cache/test/support, and can surprise shared-device visitors.

### Recommendation

Choose Option 1. It is the lowest-friction deterministic visitor journey and
keeps hidden signals out of explicit route identity. Root uses a temporary
response because the current default may legitimately change; it never carries
or redirects Giving intent.

### Concrete example

If Hope Missions makes French (Canada) default, `hope.org/` temporarily opens
`hope.org/lang/fr-ca`. Existing `hope.org/lang/en-us/about` and
`hope.org/lang/en-us/give/clean-water` remain exactly unchanged.

### Exact question

When a visitor opens only the Site domain, should the locale-neutral root
temporarily route to the current default Site Locale, show a neutral language
chooser, or use browser/remembered language detection?

### Founder answer

**Option 1.** If French (Canada) becomes default, `hope.org/` temporarily opens
`/lang/fr-ca`. Existing `/lang/en-us/about` and
`/lang/en-us/give/clean-water` remain unchanged.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

The permanent corrected decision is:

- The **Site Root Entry** is the exact locale-neutral canonical Site public
  base, including any permanent shared-host Site handle. It is not a Page,
  locale fallback, Giving address, generic redirect, or financial identity.
- Public `GET` and `HEAD` receive one server-side `307 Temporary Redirect` to
  the same Site's current, public-ready Default Site Locale homepage. `HEAD`
  has identical headers and no body. `OPTIONS` returns a bodyless, `no-store`
  capability response with `Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`. Other methods never
  redirect: known unsupported methods return `405` with that complete `Allow`,
  and unrecognized/unimplemented methods may return `501`; both use `no-store`.
- The target is compiled from trusted stable Site/default/verified-base/
  homepage/route/Public Site Generation facts and reaches a final explicit
  `200` homepage in one Core-controlled hop. It can never be caller supplied,
  external, alias, deep Page, Giving, checkout, authentication, API, callback,
  protected-action, provider-return, sibling-Site, or cross-Tenant.
- Browser language, `Accept-Language`, IP, cookies, device, profile, referrer,
  currency, Stripe/provider state, and traffic never select or vary the root
  target. Root emits no `Vary: Accept-Language`.
- Changing the default advances only the one current immutable Default Site
  Locale Version/head and its derived root/search effects. Every explicit
  Page/Giving address and frozen QR/message/document/share artifact remains
  unchanged. Site/default/root never selects Giving, Designation, currency,
  Legal Entity, Tenant Stripe account, settlement, bank, receipt, tax, ledger,
  or accounting identity.
- Query values are dropped by default. Only a separately authoritative,
  versioned attribution-ingress manifest may admit a fixed, bounded, sanitized
  non-authoritative parameter under its own policy. D16 freezes no names: the
  current Source Code owner must explicitly classify canonical `sc` and any
  successor; historical Phase 2 `t`/`c`/UTM examples are not D16 authority.
  Parameters never select locale or target. Unknown, unowned, personal,
  Giving, payment, auth/session, return, and control parameters are dropped.
- The `Location` contains an explicit empty fragment component and browser
  conformance proof, preventing RFC 9110 source-fragment inheritance.
- Every default change is privately reviewed, but it changes public truth only
  through one authorized, idempotent, expected-head activation of the sole
  Default Site Locale head after the exact homepage, shell, same-locale
  Navigation, visible language switch, verified base, route, serving policy,
  and locale-exact Public Site Generation are current and compatible. The
  prior default remains current until that activation commits; D17 separately
  decides whether an unready choice may stay saved as planned work.
- Optional Giving, messaging, other Pages, and additional locales do not block
  a safe website-default activation. Missing/unready/adverse/unknown target
  truth never falls back to another locale/Page/Site/Tenant/Giving destination.
- Launch redirect responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`. Trusted internal
  resolver caching follows ADR-0030 with complete scope/generation arguments,
  exact invalidation, immediate adverse-state bypass, and a hard `300`-second
  maximum favorable age; a missed invalidation self-heals within that ceiling.
  Tags never isolate, and the ceiling is a provisional maximum to tighten—not
  permission to delay routine activation.
- Eligible explicit locale homepages self-canonicalize and emit one reciprocal
  self-inclusive `hreflang` cluster. Root may appear as `x-default` only in
  that homepage cluster and is never a sitemap `<loc>`. Deep Pages and Giving
  never use root `x-default`.
- Locale-owned Home/logo/Navigation/breadcrumb/not-found links point directly
  to the current explicit locale homepage, not back through root. Auth,
  checkout, protected-action, operation-result, provider-return, PWA, document,
  message, QR, and share destinations remain owner-specific. An intentionally
  installed explicit-locale PWA remains in that locale after the Site default
  changes; only neutral-root override or manifest-locale disagreement is an
  error.
- One source chain owns truth: Site locale policy owns immutable Default Site
  Locale Versions and their sole current head; Page owns exact homepage
  release; Domain/Site owns verified base; shared route authority owns
  allocation; and each locale-exact Public Site Generation owns its serving
  truth. Root/search/cache effects derive from those current authorities and
  have no independently current head. Runtime, Payload, Next, analytics, and
  providers cannot write back. There is no Site-global generation, parallel
  current root table/head, mutable URL, redirect DSL, language-negotiation
  service, or provider authority.
- Composite same-scope relationships, one-current-head constraints, immutable
  retained history, restrictive deletion, operation-correct RLS
  `USING`/`WITH CHECK`, trusted server-derived actor/scope/target, narrow
  privileged commands, compare-and-swap, semantic idempotency, receipts,
  durable outbox, and poison tests apply.
- Migration inventories and source-proves current root content, `/home`, static
  metadata/canonicals, hard-coded root links, PWA/service workers,
  unprefixed/catch-all routes, `/give`/`/donate`, auth/checkout/return paths,
  null-Site/host/cache seams, analytics, and search. It activates one Site
  cohort only after D15 and full mixed-version proof. New Core-controlled
  `/home` requests do not chain through root; post-activation recovery is
  forward and retains history.

### Required staff and visitor UX/UI

Mission Control uses **Site → Languages** and one focused Maia/Base UI review:

```text
Make French (Canada) the default website language?

Current
hope.org/ opens English (United States)
hope.org/lang/en-us

After publish
hope.org/ will open French (Canada)
hope.org/lang/fr-ca

Unchanged
✓ hope.org/lang/en-us/about
✓ hope.org/lang/en-us/give/clean-water
✓ Existing Page, Giving, QR, and shared links
✓ Currency, Stripe, bank, settlement, and accounting settings
```

Persistent copy says:

> What opens when someone types only the domain changes to French (Canada).
> Existing Page and Giving addresses and existing content stay unchanged.

Readiness groups **Ready**, **Needs another owner**, and **Does not block this
change**. A missing French Page-publication action routes to its authorized
owner; missing French Giving is informational. Staff preview the real private
