candidate, then use one outcome-labelled publish action. Unknown outcomes
reconcile without resubmission. Success returns a durable receipt with **Open
website**, **View change record**, and **Change website default**.

Visitors experience one no-JavaScript `307 → 200` hop, correct final
`lang`/direction, same-locale Navigation, and a visible accessible language
control. Internal Home links remain explicit, so a later default change does
not switch a visitor's active locale journey.

Production proof measures the complete visitor journey, not only resolver
time: privacy-safe RUM and synthetic checks capture redirect duration and
navigation-start-to-final-homepage LCP, with a provisional launch requirement
of `2500 ms` or less at p75 for mobile and desktop separately.

The staff/public flows must pass keyboard, screen-reader, visible-focus,
text-plus-icon, touch, forced-color, reduced-motion, long/CJK/RTL,
320-CSS-pixel reflow, 400% zoom, no-JavaScript, and weak-network recovery
requirements in the existing `base-maia` system.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories contain a material concern if Option 1 remains
informal. None invalidates the deterministic root behavior. The corrected
decision closes unsafe-method replay, open/cross-Tenant redirects, query and
fragment disclosure, hidden negotiation, wrong/default fallback, explicit
Giving mutation, copied root truth, stale cache/search output, partial
activation, destructive migration, inaccessible staff workflow, and technical
overreach.

The full review records every failure, impact, severity, likelihood, evidence,
decision effect, permanent prevention, exact clause, 78 acceptance criteria,
and named production monitors in
[phase-24-d16-locale-neutral-site-root-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d16-locale-neutral-site-root-adversarial-review.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Root glossary now defines **Default Site Locale**, **Default Site Locale
  Version**, and **Site Root Entry**.
- D16 supersedes generic Phase 2 fallback only for public Site route
  resolution: explicit public routes never fallback, while Site Root Entry
  uses the current Default Site Locale. Message, document, checkout, provider,
  and other presentation fallback remains under its accepted source-owner
  contract and never selects a public route, Giving, or financial identity.
- D14's Giving `x-default` prohibition remains: D16 permits root
  `x-default` only for the non-Giving homepage cluster.
- D15's historical “pending D16” reservation is resolved by this root-only
  contract; explicit locale bases remain unchanged.
- Accepted ADR-0026 and the eventual D15 URL/route ADR require amendment in the
  later spec flow. D16 does not require a standalone ADR because its temporary
  behavior was selected to remain reversible.
- PRs #1323/#1340 remain proposed evidence until merged or superseded.
- Accepted ADR/PRD/OpenSpec/design/tickets/schema/migration/runtime work requires
  the separately invoked specification flow.

## D17 — Preparing a future default before it is public-ready

### Plain-language context and impact

D16 says an unready French homepage cannot take over `hope.org/`. The next
choice is whether staff can save their intent and route the missing work before
French is ready, or must return and choose it again later.

### Options

1. **Save one private planned default; keep the current root unchanged until
   reviewed activation — recommended.** Staff choose French, see the exact
   blockers, prepare what they are authorized to change, and route the rest to
   the correct owners. “Planned” is workflow intent only; it never becomes a
   second current default.
2. **Do not save the choice until the target is ready.** Show the checklist,
   send staff to fix it, and require them to return and choose French again.
   This has the smallest state model but creates re-entry and coordination
   work.
3. **Switch immediately and show unavailable or a chooser until ready.** This
   knowingly degrades the public root, creates a second temporary behavior, and
   conflicts with D6/D16.

### Recommendation

Choose Option 1. It is the clearest, lowest-effort staff journey without
weakening public truth. Reuse the private candidate and owner-routing model
specified in D16 rather than inventing a second default or generic task engine.

### Concrete example

For this serving-Site example, Maria chooses French (Canada), but the French
homepage needs publisher approval:

> **Planned: French (Canada)**  
> `hope.org/` still opens English (United States). Nothing changes
> automatically.  
> **Needs Website publisher:** Publish the French homepage.

Visitors continue receiving English (United States). After the publisher's
source work is complete, currently authorized locale-policy staff must still
perform the fresh reviewed D16 activation. Only then does `hope.org/` change to
French (Canada); all explicit English (United States) Page and Giving links
remain unchanged.

### Exact question

When a future default is not ready, should Core save one private planned
default and route its blockers while keeping the current root unchanged,
refuse to save the choice until everything is ready, or switch immediately?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — Save one private planned default.**

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

The permanent corrected decision is:

- A **Default Site Locale Plan** is one private, Site-owned workflow intent
  naming one existing stable same-Site Site Locale. It is not the current
  default, a Page draft, public release, approval, task, schedule, or public
  truth.
- At most one active Plan exists per exact Tenant/environment/Site. Selecting
  the current default is an idempotent no-op. Changing target requires an
  explicit review that creates a successor and marks the prior Plan
  **Superseded**.
- D17 applies only after a Site has a current Default Site Locale Version. D6
  Site Setup/**Go live** owns the first default/public activation. Suspended
  Sites may retain permitted private work but cannot activate; terminal Sites
  cannot plan or activate.
- Saving, viewing, routing, cancelling, replacing, or superseding a Plan
  changes zero current-default, root, Page, Navigation, route, generation,
  canonical, `hreflang`, sitemap, search, public cache, explicit URL, Giving,
  currency, provider, settlement, bank, receipt, ledger, or accounting truth.
  Public readers cannot depend on Plan state. The Plan/readiness projection
  does not query or reveal Giving enablement; staff receive only the invariant
  assurance that Giving links and settings are separate and unchanged.
- The Plan preserves stable target intent and source-reference evidence only.
  Current Page, Navigation, locale, verified-base, generation, publication,
  permission, and safety owners remain authoritative. **Ready to review** is a
  rebuildable, permission-filtered projection with `checked_at`, not stored
  truth.
- Saving a Plan never creates, clones, translates, edits, publishes,
  unpublishes, schedules, approves, rejects, or deletes source-owned content.
  ADR-0029 stable soft references remain controlling; D17 creates no
  cross-schema foreign key or sync engine.
- Each blocker shows the source-owned action, current user's permitted action,
  safely visible owning role/queue, and whether one qualifying request exists.
  The initiator cannot choose an arbitrary assignee, approver, prior editor,
  email, role, or queue. Assignment grants no record access or business
  authority.
- A future qualified adapter may project exact, deduplicated follow-up into the
  shared Mission Control task model. At most one active attention lineage
  exists per stable Plan lineage/owner/semantic cause/stable source object or
  placement, plus target only when work meaning changes. Plan/source revisions
  fence and update that lineage; they never partition uniqueness or duplicate
  notice. Task completion/comment/dismissal never proves readiness. Today's finance/
  contribution-only helper is not D17 authority and cannot be reused without
  source types, same-scope links, semantic dedupe, queues, permissions, and
  lifecycle proof.
- Plan save and source routing are itemized, resumable effects—not a fictional
  distributed transaction. If routing fails after save, the Plan remains and
  the receipt retries only unresolved effects with the same semantic identity.
- Capabilities independently govern Plan read/create/replace/cancel, every
  source edit/review, Preview, locale-policy change, and D16 activation. Every
  read/effect reauthorizes current server-resolved scope and authority. AI stays
  within the initiating human's scope and stops before activation.
- Clearing the last blocker changes only private display to **Ready to
  review**. Time, tasks, publication, providers, workers, caches, or
  notifications never activate. D17 adds no scheduler or “activate when ready”
  flag.
- Final activation compiles a fresh immutable D16 candidate and repeats
  current/after/unchanged impact plus Preview. It rechecks the active Plan,
  expected current default head, current sources, Site lifecycle, actor
  authority, and dependency digest. Changed facts require explicit review and
  never silently rebase. When activation originates from the Plan, advancing
  the default head, recording the D16 receipt, and terminalizing the Plan as
  **Activated** are one operational transaction; downstream convergence stays
  outbox-owned. If another locale became current, **Review changed default**
  appends a zero-effect immutable review revision in the same Plan lineage,
  preserves the target, pins the new current head/impact, and supersedes the
  old basis before another candidate. If the target is already current, the
  Plan becomes **Satisfied elsewhere**.
- Cancelling changes only private intent and qualifying Plan-specific
  coordination. Every terminal outcome idempotently closes/supersedes only its
  Plan-specific active requests and pending notifications, reports cleanup in
  its receipt, and safely retries unresolved cleanup. It never deletes or rolls
  back French content, reviews, schedules, releases, or other source work.
  Terminal Plan history never reopens.
- Durable states are **Active**, **Cancelled**, **Superseded**,
  **Activated**, **Satisfied elsewhere**, and **No longer applicable**.
  **Needs attention**, **Waiting for owner**, **Ready to review**, **Changed
  since review**, **Could not be checked**, and **Confirming outcome** are
  derived UI states.
- Create/replace/cancel/activate use same-meaning idempotency, expected
  revisions, bounded lock order, CAS, authoritative receipt reconciliation,
  and one race winner. Another default stales the Plan; the target becoming
  current elsewhere closes it honestly without false attribution.
- Later schema structurally enforces one active Plan, same-scope target/
  expected-head relationships, immutable provenance/terminal outcomes,
  restrictive deletion, append-only history, source-request dedupe, trusted
  server attribution, operation-correct grants/RLS, and hostile privileged-path
  tests. A mutable `planned_locale_id` beside `default_locale_id` is forbidden.
- Every private cached function keys exact Tenant, environment, Site, Plan
  lineage/revision, source scope/revisions, and projection version; IDs or
  epochs alone never isolate. Authorization-neutral facts are filtered after
  read. Any cached filtered projection additionally uses the complete principal
  or proved-equivalent authorization partition, membership/authorization
  epochs, role/subrole, and capability/field/restricted-resource policy;
  nominal role never isolates. Every render reauthorizes. Public caches are
  excluded, **Ready** evidence older than the provisional `300`-second maximum
  is suppressed, and hidden resources disclose no count, label, owner, timing,
  or existence.
- Migration starts empty. Existing locales, defaults, drafts, tasks,
  translations, traffic, or docs never fabricate staff intent. D15/D16 land
  first; readers/constraints precede writers; readiness shadows before cohort
  activation; source adapters enable one at a time; rollback preserves inert
  private history.
- D17 remains small: no generic stages, Plan-owned or Plan-derived priorities,
  comments, dates, arbitrary assignments, recurrence, rules, calendar,
  scheduler, workflow builder, automatic translation, second approval system,
  or second public activation path. Source-workflow dates/schedules remain
  source-owned; Mission Control owns shared-task due dates/reminders. Neither
  can propagate into Plan/default truth.

### Required staff UX/UI

Mission Control uses **Site → Languages**:

```text
Plan French (Canada) as the website default?

Current website
hope.org still opens English (United States)

Planned
French (Canada)

Nothing public changes when you save this plan.
It will not go live automatically.

You can do now
✓ Finish French navigation                         [Open navigation]

Needs another owner
○ French homepage needs Website publisher approval
  Review requested · 27 Aug                        [Open homepage]

Unchanged
Giving links and settings are separate and will not change.
```

The primary action discloses its effects: **Plan French (Canada) and request 1
review** when one qualified request will be created, otherwise **Plan French
(Canada)**. **Not now** is safe. There are no item checkboxes or arbitrary
assignee picker.

Success says:

> **French (Canada) is planned**  
> `hope.org` still opens English (United States).  
> The planned change is private and will not go live automatically.

When ready:

> **French (Canada) is ready to review**  
> `hope.org` still opens English (United States).  
> **Preview French website** · **Review and make default**

These examples show a serving Site. While suspended, the row instead says
**English (United States) remains default · Site suspended · Not currently
public · Nothing changes automatically**, shows **Needs attention**, and exposes
no **Ready to review** or activation action.

Cancel/replace screens say the Plan and its Plan-specific follow-ups close and
move to history, the current default/serving state stays unchanged, and French
(Canada) content plus source-owned review/approval records stay unchanged.
Receipts itemize closed follow-ups. The responsive journey uses one reading
order, text-plus-icon states, native/Base UI semantics, associated labels/
errors, visible unobscured focus, WCAG 2.2 AA, `24 × 24` targets or its spacing
exception, Core `44 × 44` important mobile controls, status announcements,
320px reflow, 400% zoom, forced colors, reduced motion, long/CJK/RTL text, and
weak-network reconciliation. Core Plan read/create/replace/cancel remains
server-rendered/server-backed when client JavaScript fails; Preview is optional
enhancement.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories contain a material concern if “save a planned
default” remains informal. None invalidates Option 1. The corrected decision
prevents a shadow default, stale readiness activation, accidental public or
financial effects, content fabrication, task-as-authority, arbitrary
assignment, cross-Tenant enumeration, duplicate requests, source-work
deletion, automatic scheduling, concurrent Plan corruption, fabricated
migration history, and a bespoke workflow engine.

The complete review records every failure, impact, severity, likelihood,
evidence, decision effect, permanent prevention, exact normative clauses, 72
acceptance criteria, and 17 named monitors in
[phase-24-d17-private-default-site-locale-plan-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d17-private-default-site-locale-plan-adversarial-review.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Root glossary now defines **Default Site Locale Plan**.
- D16's open persistence question is resolved: an unready target may remain as
  one private Plan while the current default/root stays unchanged.
- D6 first activation, D13 source-owner routing, D15 exact locale identity,
  D16 sole current head/activation, ADR-0029 reference-not-copy, tenant
  publication boundaries, and the shared-task direction remain controlling.
- PRs #1323/#1340 remain proposed evidence until merged or superseded.
- D17 does not independently require a standalone ADR. The later spec flow
  incorporates it into the Site/default workflow ADR and updates OpenSpec/PRD
  together.
- Accepted ADR/PRD/OpenSpec/design/tickets/schema/migration/runtime work requires
  the separately invoked specification workflow.

## D18 — Optional coordination date on a Default Site Locale Plan

### Plain-language context and impact

D17 preserves one private Plan. Staff may also want to record “we aim to launch
French by 15 October” so source owners understand timing.

That date can improve coordination, but it can also look like a promise or
scheduled switch. D17 forbids automatic activation. The date question must
therefore decide planning context separately from public scheduling. No
representative Core staff evidence currently proves Phase 24 needs date
metadata.

### Options

1. **Store no target date in Phase 24 — recommended.** The Plan remains until
   activated, replaced, cancelled, or no longer applicable. This is the
   smallest honest model and avoids false promises, reminder/time-zone policy,
   and metadata no known Core user has requested.
2. **Allow one optional Plan-only coordination date.** If representative
   evidence proves the need, store one editable/clearable ISO civil date
   labelled **Target date—not scheduled**. It never copies into source/task due
   dates, appears publicly, becomes a relative deadline, or triggers reminder,
   escalation, expiry, automation, or activation.
3. **Schedule automatic activation at a precise date/time.** Recheck and switch
   at that instant if ready. This reduces a click but introduces deferred
   authority, time-zone, permission, stale-proof, missed-schedule, and recovery
   risk and conflicts with D17's reviewed activation.

### Recommendation

Choose Option 1. Sanity/Contentful/HubSpot prove that dates are possible, not
that Core ministries need them. D17 already preserves visible intent and routes
current work. Adding date semantics now would freeze speculative state and
invite scheduling expectations; Option 2 remains the bounded evidence-led
amendment.

### Concrete example

```text
French (Canada) is planned

hope.org still opens English (United States).
French will not become default automatically.
```

The Plan stays visible until staff finish or cancel it. Visitors receive English
unless an authorized person completes the fresh D16 review.

### Exact question

Should a Default Site Locale Plan store no target date, allow one optional
Plan-only civil date that never schedules activation, or schedule an automatic
default change?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — Store no target date.**

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

The permanent corrected decision is:

- A Default Site Locale Plan has no target date, launch date, due date,
  planned/scheduled activation time, expiry time, deadline, relative duration,
  Plan priority, Plan urgency, Plan reminder, or release-type concept in Phase 24. Its target Site Locale and actual event/terminal timestamps remain
  required. Absence is product meaning—not `NULL`, an empty setting, generic
  metadata, or a dormant future seam.
- Created/revised/reviewed/checked/receipt/terminal timestamps remain exact,
  trusted historical and reconciliation evidence. They never become a Plan
  deadline, sorting promise, urgency input, lifecycle condition, source-
  workflow schedule, Mission Control task date, or public schedule.
- An Active Plan persists regardless of age until D17’s authorized Activated,
  Cancelled, Superseded, Satisfied elsewhere, or No longer applicable outcome.
  Time alone never changes authoritative state/readiness, Plan visibility,
  ownership, priority, activation, expiry, or public behavior. D17 freshness
  may only revoke reuse/display of cached favorable readiness proof and require
  recheck; it never grants readiness or changes Plan/source truth.
- Page, Navigation, and publication workflows may retain their independently
  authorized source-owned dates/schedules. Mission Control owns shared-task due
  dates, reminders, and urgency. D18 copies nothing in either direction; none
  becomes Plan/Site/default truth.
- A future D17 Plan-specific Mission Control request starts with
  `due_at = NULL`, creates no reminder row, and receives explicit code-owned
  `normal` urgency under the current enum. The available generic helper can
  calculate higher urgency at 24/48
  hours when given an older `firstSeenAt`; the current create path supplies the
  current instant and does not prove later automatic escalation. The Site
  adapter must not adopt Plan/request age. An authorized actor may later manage
  Mission Control timing under that contract without revising or advancing the
  Plan.
- D18 creates no timer, cron, delayed event, age scan, countdown, recurrence,
  inactivity reminder, escalation, SLA, archive/expiry job, scheduled
  publication, or automatic activation. D19 separately decides state-driven
  attention; it cannot turn Plan age into authority.
- Every permitted Languages view keeps the active Plan on its target locale
  row. The later Phase 24 authorized Sites management surface may filter
  **Planned default**. Lists group by actionable meaning, then stable Site/
  locale labels and stable identity; time never implies urgency or ordering
  priority.
- Staff see **Planned**, current blockers/readiness, current default/serving
  state, the non-automatic consequence, and one next action. The Plan summary
  never shows an empty date, **Unscheduled**, **No deadline**, calendar,
  countdown, **Late**, **Overdue**, **Stale**, or red age. Separately authorized
  source/task rows may show their own status without roll-up.
- A visible Mission Control task due date is explicitly subordinate—for example
  **Review task
  due 15 October** plus **This task date does not schedule hope.org** where
  ambiguity exists. It is never **French launch: 15 October** and never rolls
  up.
- Strict Plan-schema/command/import validation rejects date/schedule/priority
  aliases recursively within Plan envelopes before any Plan revision, receipt,
  task, notification, event, outbox, cache, or public effect. Separately typed
  Mission Control mutations remain valid under their own contract. Plan APIs
  and exports omit the property rather than returning a blank.
- Event sequence, immutable revisions, current heads, expected revisions, and
  CAS determine Plan lifecycle/concurrency. Source-workflow schedules and
  Mission Control task dates resolve under their own owners and remain Plan-
  inert. Client/server clock, time zone, DST, leap day, provider timing, and
  delayed/out-of-order delivery cannot choose a Plan/default winner.
- Every read/effect reauthorizes exact Tenant/environment/Site/capability/source
  scope. Hidden dates, age, activity, owners, reminders, and schedules leak no
  count, label, ordering, cache, timing, or existence signal.
- Migration starts empty and infers neither Plan nor date from locales, Sites,
  Pages, publications, tasks, reminders, audits, calendars, campaigns,
  analytics, files, comments, documents, messages, imports, or free text.
- D16 fresh human review remains the only Plan-originated path to changing the
  current default/root. No Plan time/age or D18/source-workflow/Mission Control
  timing event advances the default head or creates Plan-originated public,
  Giving, or finance truth. Source publication, Giving, recurring, settlement,
  and accounting owners retain independently authorized behavior under their
  own contracts.
- Any future Plan date requires representative user evidence and a separately
  accepted, versioned amendment covering ownership, semantics, authorization,
  UX, migration, concurrency, accessibility, operations, and compatibility.

### Required staff UX/UI

```text
French (Canada)
Planned · Waiting for Website publisher

hope.org still opens English (United States).
Nothing changes automatically.

[Continue setup]
```

If an authorized source row has its own timing:

```text
French homepage approval
Website publisher · Review task due 15 October
This task date does not schedule hope.org.

[Open homepage]
```

When current sources prove readiness:

```text
French (Canada)
Ready to review

hope.org still opens English (United States).
Nothing changes automatically.

[Preview French website]  [Review and make default]
```

The one-column mobile/no-JavaScript/weak-network journey retains target locale,
current default/serving state, Plan state, and next action. A suspended Site
says **English (United States) remains default · This Site is suspended and is
not currently public · Nothing changes automatically**; it never claims English
is live. The journey inherits D17’s WCAG 2.2 AA, focus, status, reflow, zoom,
target-size, forced-color, reduced-motion, long/CJK/RTL, authorization, and
idempotent-reconciliation gates.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories contain a material concern if “no date” remains a
UI-only convention. None invalidates Option 1. The corrected decision prevents
hidden nullable/metadata dates, copied task schedules, age-driven urgency,
false overdue/launch promises, automatic switching, Tenant timing leaks,
clock-dependent lifecycle, timer failure, inferred migration history, scheduler
debt, and forgotten Plans.

The complete review records each failure, impact, severity, likelihood,
evidence, decision effect, permanent prevention, exact normative clause, 60
falsifiable acceptance criteria, and 13 named monitors in
[phase-24-d18-undated-default-site-locale-plan-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d18-undated-default-site-locale-plan-adversarial-review.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Root glossary now states that the Plan owns no target date/deadline/Plan
  reminder/planned activation time, while source-workflow schedules and Mission
  Control task timing retain their separate owners.
- D17 now carries a later-D18 clarification and narrows “no dates” to
  Plan-owned/Plan-derived timing, preserving accepted ADR-0054 task ownership.
- D15/D16/D17, ADR-0029 reference-not-copy, ADR-0054 shared-task ownership, and
  [ADR-0027: One notification presentation and engagement model](../../adr/0027-one-notification-presentation-and-engagement-model.md)
  remain controlling.
- ADR/PRD/OpenSpec/design/schema/migration/runtime/tickets remain unchanged and
  require the separately invoked specification workflow.

## D19 — Bringing staff back when an undated Plan becomes actionable

### Plain-language context and impact

No target date avoids false deadlines and noisy reminders. The next UX question
is how Maria learns that work owned by someone else is now complete and her
French Plan is **Ready to review**.

This would react to a real state change—not elapsed time. Reading an in-product
item would never complete the Plan, and the website would never change
automatically.

### Options

1. **Create one state-driven in-product Needs attention item — recommended.**
   A meaningful transition such as **Ready to review** or **Changed since
   review** creates one deduplicated producer occurrence. [ADR-0027: One
   notification presentation and engagement model](../../adr/0027-one-notification-presentation-and-engagement-model.md)
   presents it only to the exact currently authorized recipient(s) who can
   perform the displayed next action under a code-owned route—never the creator
   by default, every editor, or an arbitrary assignee. Reading clears only the
   unread indicator; the item remains in **Needs attention** and cannot be
   archived while actionable. It leaves **Needs attention** when the producer-
   owned actionable condition ends, then preserves authorized recent history
   under `presentation.source_actionable_then_recent_90d@1`. It sends no
   recurring reminder or email by default. With no qualified recipient, Core
   creates no guessed item; the Plan remains discoverable in **Site →
   Languages** and the later Phase 24 authorized Sites management surface.
2. **Use Site → Languages and the later Phase 24 Sites filter only.** This adds
   no notification and is the smallest model, but staff managing several Sites
   are more likely to miss newly actionable work.
3. **Send periodic inactivity reminders.** Core nudges staff after elapsed
   time. This adds arbitrary cadence, time-zone, snooze, preference, escalation,
   and notification-fatigue policy. It would require an explicit decision
   superseding D18's no-age-reminder contract and is not recommended.

### Recommendation

Choose Option 1. It responds once to work becoming actionable, reuses the
accepted role-safe notification model, and never turns age into urgency. Source
owners continue receiving only their qualified Mission Control follow-up;
Maria does not receive repeated “still waiting” noise.

### Concrete example

```text
Needs attention

hope.org · French (Canada)
Ready to review

French (Canada) became ready for final review.
This Plan does not change the website automatically.

[Review planned change]
```

No item appears merely because 30 days passed or someone refreshed a page. A
suspended Site emits no **Ready to review** occurrence; **Site → Languages**
shows **English (United States) remains default · Site suspended · Not currently
public**. Core re-evaluates and may emit only after serving becomes favorable
and a fresh readiness check succeeds.

### Exact question

When an undated Default Site Locale Plan becomes actionable, should Core create
one state-driven in-product **Needs attention** item, rely only on **Site →
Languages** and the later Phase 24 Sites filter, or explicitly supersede D18 to
send periodic inactivity reminders?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — One state-driven Needs attention item.**

Create one deduplicated in-product item only for currently authorized people
who can perform the next action. Reading clears **unread**, but the item remains
actionable until the underlying condition ends. Send no recurring reminder or
email by default.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

The permanent corrected decision is:

- **One** means one immutable semantically idempotent producer occurrence for
  one exact actionable source episode, not one shared Tenant row. The canonical
  Phase 6/17 compiler creates one recipient- and role-specific item for each
  exact member of the complete bounded recipient set. Each qualified person
  experiences one item and has independent engagement.
- The Site locale-policy/readiness producer alone owns the actionable predicate
  and end. Refresh, polling, retry, cache recovery, Plan/source timestamps,
  elapsed time, task state, and revisions that do not change registered meaning
  create no occurrence. A genuine later recurrence creates new items; old ones
  never revive.
- Every recipient must currently be able both to see the private Plan/source
  context and perform the displayed typed action. Creator, prior editor,
  assignee, nominal staff/admin, support, service role, historical authority, or
  item possession does not qualify. The caller cannot choose recipient/scope/
  role/action.
- Resolver output is complete, all-or-none, and uses Phase 17's inherited
  provisional bounds: at most 50 staff recipients and 200 total members per
  occurrence. A proved zero-recipient result releases a zero-member occurrence
  and guesses nobody. Partial/ambiguous/timeout/overflow creates no visible
  partial fan-out and enters same-identity reconciliation.
- Every item uses
  `presentation.source_actionable_then_recent_90d@1`, code-owned **Attention**,
  an exact source-end rule, a minimal privacy-safe preview, and a server-resolved
  typed destination. It is not a task, workflow, permission, readiness owner,
  source completion, or activation command.
- Deliberately opening item detail or explicit **Mark as read** changes only
  that exact recipient+role engagement. Listing, prefetch, viewport, hydration,
  background refresh, realtime, source end, or another recipient does not mark
  it read. Read clears unread/badge only; the row stays in **Needs attention**
  and **All** while the source remains actionable.
- Active archive/dismiss is omitted and rejected. Source end once-sets
  presentation end; unseen items create no unread debt/fabricated read; the same
  authorized viewer receives non-unread recent presentation for exactly 90 days
  before query-time exclusion. Access loss hides active and recent immediately.
- Every list/count/search/detail/render/cursor/cache/engagement/realtime/support/
  destination/action operation reauthorizes current Tenant, Party, role,
  capability and source/privacy state. Later authority never revives/transfers
  an old item or its engagement and requires a new producer-authorized occurrence
  if a later decision admits a handoff.
- The bell's accessible badge counts unread groups. The notification page
  separately labels active groups so `0 unread` never means `0 work`. The calm
  row names Site, target locale, exact state, unchanged current default/serving
  consequence, **Nothing changes automatically**, one navigation action, and a
  stay-here explanation. It has no dismiss `X`, direct activation, red urgency,
  date, countdown, sound, or technical/private details.
- The destination reauthorizes and opens current private review; it performs no
  GET/HEAD mutation. D16 activation remains a separate explicit POST with fresh
  actor/Plan/source/Site/default-head/safety/dependency proof.
- D19 uses the future canonical Phase 6/17 occurrence/item/group/engagement
  runtime and creates no Site notification table. It MUST NOT reuse or dual-
  write `notification_queue`, `mission_control_attention_items`, contribution
  notification storage, or the static demo dropdown.
- **No recurring reminder or email by default** is structural: the contract has
  no task/due date/recurrence/email/digest/push/SMS/sound/provider/age-urgency
  step or dormant toggle. Any later channel requires a separately accepted
  contract.
- Occurrence creation, recipient fan-out, item/engagement/source end, retention,
  failure, and reconciliation have zero Plan/source/public/default/Page/Giving/
  currency/Legal Entity/Stripe/settlement/bank/receipt/ledger/accounting effect.
- Rollout is future-only with schema/readers/constraints/RLS and shadow recipient
  comparison before one cohort writer. Historical Plans/tasks/notifications/
  emails/opens/audits create no unread item or inferred engagement.
- D19 does not authorize one generic `plan_actionable` key. D20 chooses the
  initial exact trigger registry; materially different actions require separate
  stable keys unless one closed union is proved.

### Required staff UX/UI

```text
Notifications · 1 unread

Needs attention · 1 active

Unread
hope.org · French (Canada)
Ready to review

French (Canada) became ready for final review.
This Plan does not change the website automatically.

[Review planned change]

Reading this does not complete the work.
It stays in Needs attention until this review is no longer required.
```

After Maria opens the item, her unread label/badge clears and **Needs attention
· 1 active** remains. Joel's sibling item/read state is independent. The action
only opens current review; another actor completing the source action ends the
item safely and Maria's stale action cannot duplicate the public effect.

Mobile uses one text-first reading order with the same Site, locale, source
state, current-public consequence, active/unread distinction, and one 44px
important action. Keyboard/screen-reader/non-color/focus/forced-color/reduced-
motion/long/CJK/RTL/320px/400%-zoom requirements, polite non-focus-stealing
updates, and complete loading/empty/error/offline/access-loss states are release
gates.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories contain a material concern if the answer remains an
informal “one item.” None invalidates Option 1. The corrected decision prevents
shared read state, broad/stale recipients, cross-Tenant badge/cache/cursor leaks,
duplicate storms, missed recurrences, partial fan-out, resolver failure treated
as zero, source/read races, fabricated unread/read history, active dismissal,
direct activation, private-preview disclosure, arbitrary destinations,
age/reminder/channel creep, legacy dual truth, historical unread floods,
inaccessible/mobile-hostile UI, and hidden public/Giving/finance effects.

The complete review records every concern's failure, impact, severity,
likelihood, evidence, decision effect, permanent prevention, exact normative
clause, 70 falsifiable acceptance criteria, and 22 named monitors in
[phase-24-d19-state-driven-plan-attention-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d19-state-driven-plan-attention-adversarial-review.md).
The dated primary-source evidence and the explicit resolution of the external
“shared logical item” analogy against ADR-0027 live in
[phase-24-d19-state-driven-attention-primary-research.md](./phase-24-d19-state-driven-attention-primary-research.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Existing glossary terms for in-product availability, item, attention group,
  engagement, and source status remain controlling; no new glossary term is
  needed.
- D19 adopts accepted ADR-0027 and the Phase 17 manifest/OpenSpec model; no new
  ADR is required.
- Phase 17 runtime and D15–D18 are hard implementation dependencies; current
  generic notification/task seams remain explicitly non-authoritative.
- PRD/OpenSpec/design/schema/migration/runtime/tickets/commit/staging remain
  unchanged and require separately invoked workflows.

## D20 — Which Plan changes should notify staff?

> **Question wording revised 2026-08-28:** Expanded with plain-language terms,
> impact, staff journeys, benefits, costs, and examples at the founder's
> request. No D19 decision changed.

### The decision in plain English

D19 decided **how** a Plan notification must behave: one quiet in-product item
for each exact authorized recipient, read state separate from unfinished work,
and no email, reminder, deadline, or automatic website change.

D20 decides **when** that item is valuable enough to create.

A notification deliberately asks a staff member to stop what they are doing and
look at something. If Core creates too few, important review work can sit
unnoticed. If Core creates too many, the bell becomes another crowded task list
and staff learn to ignore it. This decision therefore controls the signal-to-
noise ratio of the future staff experience.

### The terms mentioned below

- **Ready to review** means current checks show that the planned language can
  enter final review. It does **not** mean the language is live or that Core will
  change it automatically.
- **Changed since review** means source facts used in an earlier review changed,
  such as the reviewed Page, Navigation, generation, or safety evidence. Staff
  must review the changed facts before activation can be allowed.
- **Current default changed** means another locale—not the planned target—became
  the Site's current default while this Plan remained active. Staff must perform
  the separate zero-public-effect **Review changed default** action before the
  Plan can return to final review. If the planned target itself became current,
  the Plan becomes **Satisfied elsewhere** instead and needs no action item.
- A **registered direct staff action** means the product has one specifically
  defined action that this recipient is authorized and able to perform now,
  such as **Open navigation**. It is not a vague warning or a problem owned by
  someone else.

### What this decision does—and does not—change

Whichever option is chosen:

- refreshes, retries, background checks, and elapsed time create no item;
- **Waiting for another owner**, ownerless work, and operator-only failures
  create no item for ordinary staff;
- a suspended Site creates no review/activation item unless a later contract
  proves a different safe direct action;
- the recipient must be currently authorized to see the Plan and perform the
  displayed action;
- opening or reading the item changes nothing public; and
- there is still no email, recurring reminder, task deadline, or automatic
  default-language change.

D20 does not yet decide which one of several qualified people should receive an
item. We will make that recipient-routing decision after deciding which moments
should create items.

### Option 1 — Notify for every review-required episode

**Recommended.** These are treated as three distinct, carefully defined review
moments:

1. The Plan newly becomes **Ready to review**, so a qualified staff member can
   begin final review.
2. An earlier review becomes unsafe to rely on and the Plan truthfully becomes
   **Changed since review**, so a qualified staff member can immediately
   perform **Review changes**.
3. Another locale becomes the current default and the Plan truthfully becomes
   **Current default changed**, so a qualified staff member can immediately
   perform the zero-public-effect **Review changed default** action.

**Staff experience:** Maria is notified when French (Canada) is finally ready
for her review. If she reviews it and a material review fact later changes, she
gets one new, clearly different item telling her that the review must be done
again. If another locale becomes the current default, she receives a different
item explaining that the current-versus-planned impact must be reviewed again.
She does not receive Plan notifications for every ordinary Page, Navigation, or
owner-work update along the way.

**Benefits:**

- catches both the moment staff can finish and the moment an earlier review is
  no longer trustworthy;
- keeps the bell focused on high-value decisions rather than setup progress;
- gives each item one obvious review action; and
- preserves Page, Navigation, and other source-owned work queues as the place
  for ordinary blocker work.

**Costs and consequences:**

- staff must still use **Site → Languages**, the Sites view, and source-owner
  queues for ordinary setup/blocker progress; and
- **Ready to review**, **Changed since review**, and **Current default changed**
  need separate stable message meanings, end rules, copy, tests, and audit
  evidence. That is small deliberate complexity that prevents one vague,
  brittle “Plan changed” notification.

**Tenant example:**

```text
Ready to review
hope.org · French (Canada)

French (Canada) became ready for final review.
This Plan does not change the website automatically.

[Review planned change]
```

Later, only if the earlier review becomes outdated:

```text
Changed since review
hope.org · French (Canada)

Information used by a previous review changed.
Review the current version before continuing.
This Plan does not change the website automatically.

[Review changes]
```

If a different locale becomes the current default while the Plan remains
active:

```text
Current default changed
hope.org · French (Canada)

The website's default changed while this Plan was active.
Compare the current website with this planned change.
This Plan does not change the website automatically.

[Review changed default]
```

### Option 2 — Notify for Ready-to-review episodes only

Core creates a Plan item whenever the Plan genuinely enters **Ready to review**.
That includes a later real Ready → not ready → Ready recurrence, which creates a
fresh episode and item. This option does not create the separate **Changed since
review** or **Current default changed** items.

**Staff experience:** Maria receives one clear “ready” item. She reads it and
reviews the Plan. If that review later becomes outdated, she discovers that
only when she returns to Languages or another authorized Site-management view.
If staff resolve that state and the Plan later genuinely becomes Ready again,
Maria receives a new Ready item.

**Benefits:**

- quietest notification experience;
- only one message meaning, action, and end rule to implement; and
- lowest chance of notification fatigue.

**Costs and risks:**

- an earlier review can become outdated without bringing the responsible staff
  member back;
- staff may reasonably assume their prior review is still current; and
- long-lived or multi-Site Plans depend more heavily on people routinely
  revisiting the source surfaces.

**Tenant example:**

```text
Ready to review
hope.org · French (Canada)
[Review planned change]
```

If the review later becomes outdated:

```text
Site → Languages
French (Canada) · Changed since review
[Review changes]

No new bell item is created.
```

If staff later review/repair the changed facts and the Plan genuinely re-enters
Ready:

```text
Ready to review
hope.org · French (Canada)
[Review planned change]

A fresh Ready episode creates a fresh item.
```

### Option 3 — Notify for every registered state with a direct staff action

Core can create a distinct item for **Ready to review**, **Changed since
review**, and any other Plan state where the current recipient can immediately
perform one registered action. Every added state needs its own exact meaning,
recipient rule, action, end rule, privacy-safe copy, and tests.

This option still excludes ownerless work, waiting for someone else, vague
warnings, ordinary progress, suspension without an admitted safe action, and
operator-only failures.

**Staff experience:** Maria may see Plan items not only for final review, but
also for work she can do immediately—for example, **Navigation needs your
update** with an **Open navigation** action.

**Benefits:**

- gives staff one broader place to find actionable Plan work across several
  Sites;
- can reduce the need to revisit each Languages page; and
- makes more cross-team handoffs discoverable when the action genuinely belongs
  to the recipient.

**Costs and risks:**

- the same Page or Navigation work may appear in both its source-owned queue and
  the Plan notification center;
- more item types, recipient resolvers, end rules, and permission combinations
  increase implementation and testing cost;
- staff may struggle to understand which surface owns completion; and
- higher volume makes the two most important review items easier to overlook.

**Tenant example:**

```text
Navigation needs your update
hope.org · French (Canada)

French navigation is incomplete, and you can update it now.

[Open navigation]
```

Reading the item never completes the Navigation work. It stays in **Needs
attention** until Navigation-owned truth says the action is complete.

### Comparison

| Option                                       | What reaches the bell                                    | Main staff benefit                 | Main tradeoff                                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| 1. Every review-required episode             | Ready, Changed since review, and Current default changed | important reviews are hard to miss | three precise message contracts                  |
| 2. Ready episodes only                       | every genuine entry or re-entry into Ready to review     | quietest and simplest              | review-invalidating states may go unnoticed      |
| 3. Every registered state with direct action | review plus other immediately actionable Plan work       | broader cross-Site work discovery  | more noise, duplication, permissions, and upkeep |

### Recommendation

Choose **Option 1 — every review-required episode**.

It gives staff the best balance: Core brings Maria back when she can finish the
change, when source facts invalidate her earlier review, and when a different
current default changes the impact she must review. Ordinary Page, Navigation,
and owner work stays in the surfaces that actually own it. This is the clearest
UX, keeps notification volume low, and avoids turning the bell into a second
task system.

### Exact question

Which option should Core use for the first Plan notifications: **Option 1 —
every review-required episode**, **Option 2 — Ready-to-review episodes only**,
or **Option 3 — every registered state with a direct staff action**? You may
also amend an option.

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — every review-required episode.** Verify that it is best practice,
then perform the complete adversarial review.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

The evidence supports renewed review after material reviewed facts change. It
does not justify one alert per edit. The permanent decision is:

- D20 admits exactly three separate meanings: **Ready to review**, **Changed
  since review**, and **Current default changed**. The strings proposed in the
  D20 report are non-executable trace handles; Phase 17 stable keys are not
  minted until D21 and every source/recipient contract closes.
- One Site-owned selector evaluates complete current truth and chooses at most
  one meaning. Terminal/target-current wins, then proved source/action
  unavailability, then unknown, Current-default, Changed, Ready, or none.
  Current-default excludes that fact from generic Changed.
- One review-required episode is one maximal interval in which one selected
  review action remains required. Repeated edits, revisions, retries, refresh,
  cache recovery, default observations, and elapsed time inside that interval
  create no peer occurrence or unread pulse. A genuine recurrence after source
  end creates a new item; an old item is never mutated/re-unread.
- Changed requires explicit source-owned immutable review evidence and a closed
  material dependency registry. Candidate existence, compilation, Preview,
  page load, task state, item open/read, or engagement never proves review.
- Current-default compares with the latest acknowledged expected head or the
  Plan's initial expected head. If the planned target itself became current,
  the Plan becomes **Satisfied elsewhere** and creates no D20 item.
- Suspension always suppresses Ready/activation. Changed or Current-default may
  remain only if their exact zero-public review command, required facts, and
  safety are independently proved available while suspended.
- Unknown proof suppresses unsafe presentation without ending the source
  episode or re-alerting on same-fact recovery. An apparent reversion after a
  proved material invalidation never silently revives old review.
- The card uses durable past-event copy such as **French (Canada) became ready
  for final review** and **This Plan does not change the website
  automatically**. Current mutable default/readiness/diff facts appear only at
  the reauthorized destination.
- Re-review and final review remain distinct but continuous. A chained Ready
  step appears inline with **Continue to final review**; rendering it changes
  no engagement. Only a deliberate item open/mark-read may mark that exact
  recipient's item read.
- Notification actions are native navigation links. Review/activation commands
  are separate native buttons on the destination. **Make French (Canada)
  default** is consequence-led UI copy for D17's single **Review and make
  default** command, not another authority.
- One D20 producer episode/outbox transaction records occurrence identity after
  observing source truth. It never joins, rolls back, or rewrites independent
  Page, Navigation, default, review, or safety transactions. Phase 6/17 fan-out
  replays the same semantic token.
- D19 remains controlling: current exact authorization, recipient-specific
  items/read state, zero-member occurrences, all-before-any bounded fan-out,
  source-owned end, access-loss removal, fixed **Attention**, in-product-only,
  no task/reminder/email/time behavior, and zero public/Giving/financial effect.
- All three future contracts are minted as Reserved in one generation or none
  are; historical rows infer no review/item/engagement, and any missing D21,
  source, RLS, usability, migration, or proof binding keeps them unminted or
  Reserved.

### Required staff UX/UI

```text
Ready to review
hope.org · French (Canada)

French (Canada) became ready for final review.
This Plan does not change the website automatically.

[Review planned change]
```

The review link opens the full current impact screen. It shows **Current
website**, **If you make French (Canada) the default**, **Unchanged**, optional
private Preview, and one separate **Make French (Canada) default** button. It
does not add a redundant Continue step to the initial Ready journey.

For a renewed review:

```text
Changed since review
hope.org · French (Canada)

Information used by a previous review changed.
Review the current version before continuing.
This Plan does not change the website automatically.

[Review changes]
```

The notification stays truthful in active and Recent history because mutable
current-default names and change details remain on the destination.

### Adversarial result

All 22 requested categories have a material concern if “every episode” stays
informal. None invalidates the direction. The corrected contract prevents
every-edit storms, overlapping states, missing/forged review basis, stale card
copy, source/event-order races, auto-read chaining, cross-Tenant disclosure,
client/privileged authorization bypass, legacy dual writers, hidden provider/
task/time behavior, and public/Giving/financial effects.

The complete finished review contains D20-R1–R22, the full staff journey,
source/invariant/lifecycle maps, all concern fields, 80 falsifiable acceptance
criteria, named signals/thresholds/owners/responses, implementation order, and
primary-source reconciliation in
[phase-24-d20-every-review-required-episode-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d20-every-review-required-episode-adversarial-review.md).
The external evidence and its limits remain in
[phase-24-d20-review-required-attention-primary-research.md](./phase-24-d20-review-required-attention-primary-research.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Root `CONTEXT.md` defines **Plan review-required episode**.
- D20 conforms to ADR-0027; no new ADR is required.
- D15/D16, D17, D18, D19, and canonical Phase 17 are hard dependencies.
- D20 does not yet mint or activate a key. D21 recipient routing is required
  before the later PRD/OpenSpec/design/manifest workflow.
- PRD/OpenSpec/schema/migration/runtime/tickets/commit/staging remain unchanged.

## D21 — When several people can review, who should receive the item?

> **Question wording revised 2026-08-28:** The recommendation and its practical
> reasons now appear inside the exact question at the founder's request. No D20
> decision changed.

### The decision in plain English

D20 decided **when** review attention appears. D21 decides **whose bell it
appears in** when several people have permission to do the review.

Two different ideas must stay separate:

- **Authorized** means a person is currently allowed to see this private Plan
  and perform the exact review action.
- **Responsible** means the ministry expects that person to handle review
  notifications for this Site.

Permission should not automatically make someone responsible for every Site,
and naming someone responsible must never give them permission. This choice
controls notification noise, accountability, absence coverage, and how much
setup a small ministry must do.

### What this decision does—and does not change

Whichever option is chosen:

- every selected person still needs current exact view+action authorization;
- each receives an independent D19 item/read state—never one shared team row;
- one successful source review ends applicable sibling items because the source
  condition ended, not because someone read a card;
- the Plan creator cannot choose arbitrary recipients for one episode;
- Core never falls back to the creator, prior reviewer, last editor, all admins,
  support, service role, AI, or a legacy queue;
- no route grants capability, Site membership, or source access; and
- with no valid recipient, the review remains discoverable in **Site →
  Languages** and notification absence never blocks/completes review.

### Option 1 — Notify every currently authorized reviewer

Core sends a personal item to everyone who can currently open and perform the
review.

**Staff experience:** Twelve website-capable staff receive **French (Canada) —
Ready to review**. Maria completes it; the other eleven items safely end.

**Benefits:** no responsibility setup and strong coverage when someone is away.

**Costs/risks:** permission becomes responsibility, people are interrupted for
Sites they do not manage, ownership is unclear, and Phase 17's safety ceiling
is mistaken for a good UX target.

### Option 2 — Notify one explicitly named Site reviewer only

Each Site names exactly one accountable reviewer. The item appears only if that
person is still currently authorized.

**Staff experience:** Maria alone owns hope.org reviews. Staff always know who
is responsible.

**Benefits:** clearest accountability and lowest notification volume.

**Costs/risks:** leave, departure, deactivation, or permission change can leave
no notification route. Every Site also needs a safe assignment/inheritance
story, and Core cannot infer that Maria is away while she remains authorized.

### Option 3 — Explicit Site/Tenant reviewer routes with one visible fallback

**Recommended.** A Tenant configures **Website reviewers** once. Ordinary Sites
inherit that route. A Site with genuinely different ownership may explicitly
name its own reviewer(s) and visibly declare the Tenant route as fallback. At
episode time, Core intersects the first applicable route with current exact
authorization. It never widens to every capability holder.

**Staff experience:** Hope Ministries sets Maria and Joel as Tenant Website
reviewers. Most Sites inherit them. Its Spanish Site names Ana and shows
**Fallback: Tenant Website reviewers**. Spanish review goes to Ana; if Ana can
no longer open it, the explicitly shown fallback is considered. If neither
route has a qualified member, no item is created and authorized Site settings
say **Review notifications aren't assigned** with the safe setup path.

**Benefits:** one-time setup for small ministries, clear multi-Site ownership,
deliberate absence coverage, low noise, and no hidden broadcast.

**Costs/risks:** Core needs one small audited responsibility-route concept,
exact precedence/handoff/no-route behavior, and clear UI. A broad “reviewer
team” could recreate Option 1, so any final size/default needs evidence rather
than using the 50-recipient execution ceiling as UX guidance.

### Option 4 — Let Core auto-select one reviewer

Core chooses by round robin, recent workload, availability, or a claimable
queue.

**Staff experience:** only one person is notified, but staff may not understand
why Core chose them or who takes over.

**Benefits:** low fan-out without manually selecting someone each time.

**Costs/risks:** Core has no accepted workload, presence, availability,
fairness, or queue-claim authority. This creates another state machine and can
route private ministry work using telemetry that was never responsibility
evidence.

### Comparison

| Option                                  | Setup effort              | Accountability | Absence coverage    | Noise       | Main risk                               |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------- |
| 1. Every authorized reviewer            | none                      | weak           | high                | highest     | capability-wide broadcast               |
| 2. One named Site reviewer              | per-Site                  | strongest      | brittle             | lowest      | work can strand                         |
| 3. Explicit Site/Tenant routes+fallback | one default+rare override | strong         | deliberate/visible  | low/bounded | small new route contract                |
| 4. Core auto-selects                    | low                       | opaque         | algorithm-dependent | low         | unapproved workload/availability engine |

### Recommendation

Choose **Option 3**. Primary evidence from GitHub/GitLab and CMS/approval tools
supports explicit responsibility separated from current eligibility; Blackbaud
provides nonprofit-specific evidence for designated routes and explicit absence
coverage. The Tenant default makes the simple case easy, while a visible Site
override/fallback handles real multi-Site ownership without broadcasting to
everyone or inventing automatic workload management.

This is a product judgment, not a universal vendor rule. The supporting current
primary research, evidence limits, staff journeys, edge cases, proof ideas, and
monitors are in
[phase-24-d21-review-recipient-routing-primary-research.md](./phase-24-d21-review-recipient-routing-primary-research.md).

### Exact question

**My recommendation is Option 3 — explicit Site/Tenant reviewer routes with one
visible fallback.** It gives a small ministry one simple Tenant-level Website
reviewer setup, lets a larger ministry override only Sites with genuinely
different ownership, keeps responsibility separate from permission, and avoids
both noisy capability-wide broadcasts and a brittle single-person route. The
fallback is always visible and deliberate; Core never secretly widens to all
staff or admins.

For example, Hope Ministries can configure Maria and Joel once as its Tenant
Website reviewers. Its Spanish Site may name Ana and visibly use those Tenant
reviewers as fallback. If nobody in either explicit route is currently allowed
to perform the review, Core guesses nobody and **Site → Languages** shows the
safe setup path.

When several people are currently authorized to perform a D20 review, do you
choose my recommended **Option 3**, or do you prefer **Option 1 — every
authorized reviewer**, **Option 2 — one named Site reviewer**, or **Option 4 —
Core auto-selects one reviewer**? You may amend any option.

### Founder answer

**Option 3.** Think through edge cases and provide the best staff and Tenant UX
consistent with the repository, then complete the full 22-category adversarial
review.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

Option 3 is the best permanent direction, but “Site/Tenant routes with
fallback” was not precise enough to implement. The corrected decision is:

- **Default Site Locale Plan review responsibility route** is one private,
  versioned, D20-specific coordination policy—not a role, permission group,
  task, generic workflow, approval quorum, or public Site fact.
- Ordinary Sites use the Tenant **Website reviewers** route. An authorized
  manager may choose **Site reviewers** and visibly save either **Use Tenant
  Website reviewers if no Site reviewer can currently act** (recommended) or
  **Send no review notification**. No hidden or chained fallback exists.
- Responsibility never grants authorization; authorization never creates
  responsibility. The server intersects the first applicable explicit route
  with current exact Plan-view and review-action authorization.
- A partially qualified Site route wins with its qualified members. Only proved
  zero can consider the saved Tenant fallback. Unknown, stale, partial,
  timed-out, contradictory, corrupt, or over-limit resolution releases nobody
  and never widens the audience.
- The winning route/recipient set is stable for its current routing leg. If
  fallback wins, primary recovery alone does not bounce the same open review
  back; the next genuine D20 episode evaluates current Site-first precedence.
- Route settings affect future episodes by default. Changing current reviews
  requires a separate authorized, impact-previewed action. Proved loss of all
  selected recipients may invoke the already declared fallback automatically.
- Explicit current handoff is differential: unchanged people retain their item
  and engagement with no new unread; newly selected people receive one
  successor item; responsibility-only removal leaves Needs attention and may
  show non-unread **Reassigned** Recent history; access loss removes all private
  presentation. Nothing transfers or revives.
- A proved no-recipient result creates no item and never blocks/completes review.
  **Site → Languages** remains the persistent review path and shows distinct
  configured-zero, no-route, and verification-unavailable states according to
  current permission.
- Site clone/import/transfer does not copy named reviewers or engagement;
  destination Sites inherit only their destination Tenant policy unless later
  explicitly configured.
- D21 has zero Page, Communications, public, Giving, Legal Entity, Stripe,
  settlement, bank, currency, or accounting effect and adds no email, reminder,
  due date, schedule, availability, workload, round-robin, queue, or provider.

### Required staff UX/UI

Tenant staff configure one calm **Review notifications** card. D26 and D29 later
converge it into **Settings → Websites → Reviews**, where its card label is
**Review notifications** beside—but never merged with—**External review
follow-up**. It covers D20's ready, changed-since-review, and current-default-
changed meanings. Sites clearly show **Uses Tenant Website reviewers** by default and
reveal the Site picker plus the single fallback choice only when staff choose an
override. Every editor says assignment changes notifications only and gives no
access.

Ordinary route saves are one step and prospective. If open reviews exist, Core
says they still use their current reviewers and offers **Review current
assignments**. That separate screen shows privacy-filtered newly notified,
removed, and unchanged people; unchanged staff are explicitly not notified
again. No typed phrase or per-Site busywork is required.

The no-route state says:

```text
Review notifications need setup

No selected reviewer can currently receive this Site's review notifications.
Authorized staff can still review the Plan in Languages.

[Set up reviewers]
```

The complete Base Maia/mobile/keyboard/screen-reader/zoom/RTL/long-name/weak-
network journey, lifecycle and source maps, database/RLS constraints, all 22
material concerns with every requested field, 69 acceptance criteria, 25 named
monitors, rollout/rollback order, exact synthesis, and current primary sources
are in
[phase-24-d21-explicit-review-responsibility-routing-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d21-explicit-review-responsibility-routing-adversarial-review.md).
The supporting evidence appendices are
[phase-24-d21-review-recipient-routing-primary-research.md](./phase-24-d21-review-recipient-routing-primary-research.md)
and
[phase-24-d21-responsibility-routing-adversarial-primary-research.md](./phase-24-d21-responsibility-routing-adversarial-primary-research.md).

### Affected contracts and documentation status

- Root `CONTEXT.md` defines **Default Site Locale Plan review responsibility
  route**.
- D21 conforms to ADR-0027; no new ADR is required.
- D19/D20 source-episode language must admit immutable successor routing
  occurrences without creating another D20 episode or appending recipients to
  a released Phase 17 occurrence.
- D21 does not yet mint a key. D22 must close route cardinality/completion and
  the later Phase 12/17 workflow must close exact identifiers and proof.
- PRD/OpenSpec/schema/migration/runtime/tickets/commit/staging remain unchanged.

## D22 — What should it mean when one review route names several people?

### The decision in plain English

D21 decided **where reviewers come from**. D22 decides whether a route is one
person, a small group where any one may act, an ordered primary/backup list, or
a group where everyone must approve.

This directly changes staff experience. More recipients improve human coverage
but add notifications and can weaken “who owns this?” clarity. Requiring every
person creates a new multi-approval workflow; ordered backups create another
handoff state machine. No current vendor or Core contract proves a universal
team size, so the exact small product limit must be validated before Live
rather than borrowing Phase 17's 50-person execution ceiling.

### Option 1 — exactly one reviewer per route

Maria alone receives the item. This is clearest and quietest, but one absence or
access loss immediately invokes fallback/no-route.

### Option 2 — one or a deliberately small co-responsible set; any one may act

**Recommended.** The picker begins with one person but permits a small,
intentional set. Every selected and currently authorized person receives a
personal item. The first valid source review ends the review for everyone;
personal read state remains separate.

**Example:** Hope Ministries normally chooses Maria alone. For a multilingual
Site it chooses Maria and Ana. Maria opens her item, clearing only her unread.
Ana completes the review first, so both actionable items end from source truth
without pretending Maria reviewed it.

**Impact:** best balance of simple ownership and real human coverage, with no
calendar, timer, presence, escalation, or quorum engine. The UI must say
**Either reviewer can complete this review** and discourage broad teams.

### Option 3 — one primary plus ordered backups

Maria receives the item first; Ana becomes responsible only after a deliberate
handoff/backup transition. This keeps one owner at a time, but does not solve
unreported absence and duplicates fallback state.

### Option 4 — every named person must review

Maria and Ana must both approve. This supports consensus, but changes D20 from
one source review into a new quorum workflow, adds delay, and is brittle when
anyone is unavailable.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 2 — one or a deliberately small co-responsible
set where any one authorized reviewer may complete the source review.** It
keeps the default simple for a small ministry, adds deliberate human coverage
when useful, and avoids both an escalation engine and a new all-of approval
workflow.

When a Tenant or Site review route names more than one person, do you choose my
recommended **Option 2**, or do you prefer **Option 1 — exactly one reviewer**,
**Option 3 — one primary plus ordered backups**, or **Option 4 — every named
person must review**? You may amend any option.

### Founder answer

> **Option 2 — one or a deliberately small co-responsible reviewer set where
> any one may act.**

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

D22 closes the route's cardinality and completion meaning as follows:

- A configured Tenant or Site route starts with one deliberately chosen person
  and admits at most three exact people. Core never auto-selects the creator,
  current user, an admin, a role, or a group.
- Members are unordered and co-responsible. There is no primary, backup,
  position, promotion, claim, round robin, quorum, or all-of progress. Display
  order has no responsibility meaning.
- The route selects private attention, not an action allowlist. Every configured
  member who currently passes the exact view-and-action authorization receives
  one personal Phase 17 item, but any actor independently authorized by the
  source may discover and complete the review from its owning surface whether
  or not that actor received an item.
- One current, CAS-valid source review completes the one source review
  requirement and ends applicable sibling attention. Reading, opening, or
  another recipient's engagement does not claim or complete work.
- Notification surfaces expose no peer delivery, open, read, unread,
  engagement, or implied review attribution. The source-owned review history
  retains only the actor evidence its own authorization and privacy contract
  permits.
- A partially qualified route still wins with only its qualified members;
  D21's explicit fallback is not joined while any selected member can act.
  Inactive or ineligible configured people remain honest responsibility status,
  gain no access, and receive no item.
- Add/remove changes remain prospective by default. D21's explicit current-
  review handoff preserves unchanged engagement, ends removed responsibility,
  and creates successor items only for newly admitted qualified people. There
  is no reordering interaction because members are equal.
- The three-person maximum is a code-owned v1 product bound, not Tenant
  configuration and not Phase 17's 50-person execution ceiling. A later increase
  requires a versioned contract and new usability, load, isolation, and rollout
  proof.
- D22 adds no task, assignment queue, due date, reminder, email, SMS, push,
  public Site/Page/Navigation mutation, Giving effect, Legal Entity, Stripe,
  settlement, bank, currency, contribution, receipt, ledger, or accounting
  effect.

The complete pressure test, UX journey, 22-category review, acceptance criteria,
data/RLS requirements, monitors, and synthesis are recorded in
[phase-24-d22-small-co-responsible-reviewers-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d22-small-co-responsible-reviewers-adversarial-review.md).
The supporting current primary-source evidence and evidence limits are recorded
separately in
[phase-24-d22-co-responsible-reviewers-primary-research.md](./phase-24-d22-co-responsible-reviewers-primary-research.md).

## D23 — May a person review work they helped prepare?

### Why this needs your decision

D22 decides who receives private review attention, but a notification route is
not permission and does not decide whether the person who planned or edited the
change may perform its source-owned review. D23 must close that self-review
boundary.

The choice affects both safety and whether a small ministry can operate. A rule
that always requires a second person looks simple but can strand a one-person
Website team and would add a universal approval gate that D16 currently rejects.
A rule that always permits self-review is equally simple but can bypass an
existing Page, Navigation, publication, safety, or Tenant policy that requires
independent review.

### Concrete Hope Ministries example

Maria creates Hope Ministries' French default-language Plan and helps prepare
the ordinary public copy. She is also one of the configured Website reviewers.
For an ordinary change, Hope's current publication policy may permit Maria to
complete review herself. If protected Navigation, safety-sensitive content, or
the governing publication policy requires a different human, Maria cannot
satisfy that exact review; Ana or another currently qualified independent person
must do it. If nobody qualifies, Core shows the honest blocker and never treats
Maria's route membership as a bypass.

### Option 1 — Always require a different person

The Plan creator and every material editor can receive context but can never
complete the review.

**Impact:** strongest universal separation and easiest rule to explain, but it
blocks small ministries even where the source owner and Tenant policy require no
second person. It invents a global gate rather than respecting Core's existing
proportional publication boundaries.

### Option 2 — Enforce the source-owned proportional independence floor

**Recommended.** The Page, Navigation, publication, safety, and default-change
owners declare which exact changes require another human. Core enforces the
strictest applicable current rule. Where no governing rule requires separation,
a routed creator/editor may review only if independently authorized for the
exact current source action.

**Impact:** preserves every real maker-checker requirement, keeps one-person
ministries operable for ordinary changes, and introduces no second review-policy
engine. The UI must plainly say either **You can complete this review** or
**Someone else must review this change**, name the safe reason, and route the
next step without exposing protected facts.

### Option 3 — Always permit self-review

Any routed and currently action-authorized creator/editor may complete review,
regardless of the source's ordinary independence policy.

**Impact:** least friction and simplest happy path, but route membership could
become a bypass around Page, publication, safety, or Tenant-required independent
review. This conflicts with source ownership and is not safe as a permanent
default.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 2 — enforce the source-owned proportional
independence floor.** It keeps the safety rule with the domain that understands
the change, never weakens an existing independent-review requirement, and does
not punish small ministries with a second-person gate where no accepted source
policy requires one.

Do you choose my recommended **Option 2**, or do you prefer **Option 1 — always
require a different person** or **Option 3 — always permit self-review**? You may
amend any option.

### Founder answer

**Option 2 — enforce the source-owned proportional independence floor.**

### Adversarial disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

D23 now records a source-owned **Plan review independence floor** for each exact
D20/D17 action. The server composes one immutable, versioned result over the
exact candidate and review epoch: **same human permitted**, **different human
required**, or **indeterminate**. Indeterminate always blocks.

The strictest applicable still-unsatisfied source obligation wins. A typed
source contract must explicitly bind the obligation to this exact action. D23
does not repeat an already satisfied Page, Navigation, or publication review,
and Plan review cannot satisfy or weaken another source's review.

Same-human eligibility never grants access. Every actor must still be currently
source-authorized through Phase 12. Different-human review additionally compares
the actor's stable human/Party identity with source-owned immutable material-
participation proof. Alternate accounts, roles, Assignments, shared/service
identities, AI, support, impersonation, View as, routing, notification state, or
administrator status cannot manufacture independence.

Tenant policy may strengthen only through a bounded, code-defined, versioned
source setting and can never weaken a source/platform floor. Tightening stales
weaker proof. Relaxation is successor-only and never downgrades an in-flight
candidate. Material edits, dependency/head changes, identity changes,
authorization loss, and incompatible evaluator generations stale review.

D21/D22 remains attention-only. Selected but ineligible people receive no
actionable item for the current episode and gain no authority; they remain
selected for future qualified work. Partial qualification notifies only the
qualified members and does not invoke fallback. Only a complete proved-zero
Site leg may invoke D21 fallback; unknown never widens. A current authorized and
independent non-route actor may act from **Site → Languages**.

The final source command re-proves candidate, source/default heads, policy and
evaluator versions, participant proof, stable human identity, current authority,
and semantic idempotency inside one expected-head/CAS transaction. One winner
records one attributable receipt. Zero-public re-review stays zero-public; only
D17's separately authorized **Review and make default** command may consume a
