occur near the limit and when crossing it. There is no HTML `maxlength` trap.
The empty error is **Describe what needs to change.** The length error is
**Shorten the explanation to 1,000 characters or fewer.** A stale anchor says
**That section is no longer available for this review. Remove the link or
refresh the review.** Errors remain inline, associated, and non-toast-only.

**Reference this section** appears only beside a safe anchor already in the
review projection. A source with no stable safe anchor omits the entire
optional row. Changing/removing a location preserves the body and focus. The
field supports CJK, RTL, bidi isolation, long localized labels, automatic
paragraph direction, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 400% zoom, forced colors, reduced
motion, keyboard/screen-reader use, Core's 44-by-44 important targets, mobile
keyboards, and low-bandwidth operation.

The unsent body and location stay only in page memory. Validation, offline,
rate-limit, stale-state, lost-response, or transient failure preserves them.
Leaving with a nonempty draft asks **Discard this explanation?**; D30 creates no
autosave, browser storage, cookie, generic form-recovery record, or server
draft. Submission is not optimistic. A lost response reconciles the exact
receipt before any re-keyed attempt.

Success says:

```text
Changes requested

Your feedback was recorded for Hope Ministries.
Your access to this version has ended. No Website or Giving change was made.
```

It never claims **Sent**, **Read**, **Assigned**, **Published**, or successor
creation. If another terminal transition won, the reviewer sees **This review
has already ended. Your explanation was not submitted.** and the authoritative
privacy-safe outcome while their local draft remains available.

### D30 authorized staff UX/UI

The exact source repair/history surface—not Mission Control list text—shows:

```text
Changes requested
The current Website and Giving are unchanged.

What needs to change
The Contact us link opens the English page.

Related section
Contact us link · French (Canada)                 [View original section]

A corrected version requires fresh review.
```

Reviewer safe identity and server time appear only when separately authorized.
The original body is escaped, read-only, wraps normally, and uses `dir="auto"`.
**View original section** re-proves current access and opens only the retained
review projection. The source may expose its one lawful correction/successor
action. D30 exposes no Reply, Edit, Delete, Resolve, Mark addressed, Assign,
Convert to task, or copy-to-successor control. Source state—not a feedback
checkbox—ends any later action condition.

### D30 data, authorization, failure, and rollout amendments

- The consequence-owning source is the authoritative result owner. A
  purpose-limited readable-body record supports retention/quarantine without
  making a notification, task, comment, CMS document, or read model a writer.
- The browser receives no direct result/body/anchor/redaction mutation grant.
  Trusted server context derives Tenant, environment, Site, source, candidate,
  review epoch, reviewer Party/human, context, result, actor, and time.
- Same-scope relational constraints, one-terminal-result uniqueness, typed
  result/body compatibility, zero-or-one anchor, immutable receipts, least
  grants, `ENABLE` plus `FORCE RLS`, correct `USING` and `WITH CHECK`, safe
  views/functions, and service/owner/support/worker/export/cache/realtime poison
  tests are mandatory. An allowed update cannot transform scope or result.
- Current broad staff capabilities, `post_comments`, Mission Control tasks,
  Phase 17's legacy `review_comment_count`, and Payload/CMS fields are unsafe
  precedents and must not be reused. Phase 17 terminology must be narrowed
  before activation so it does not imply a comment body or comment system.
- A readable body uses the source's existing or newly named review-feedback
  records class; D30 invents no retention duration or Tenant retention builder.
  Body-free audit retains minimum causal/result evidence. Quarantine,
  disposition, restore suppression, legal hold, identity pseudonymization, and
  exact authorized export require closed owner contracts before Live.
- Rollout is additive and readers precede the single fenced writer. Historical
  bare Request changes results remain visibly legacy; no migration invents a
  reason, actor, or anchor and no dual write targets comments/tasks/legacy rows.
  Rollback stops new writes while preserving valid committed history and never
  falls back to bare Request changes.
- The active Statement Operations OpenSpec deliberately allows an optional
  bounded note for its internal protected-run source. D30 does not silently
  overwrite that contract: it applies to D25 external candidate review because
  the reviewer loses access after a terminal repair result. Any cross-product
  wording reconciliation belongs in the dedicated `/to-spec` pass.
- The active Sitestacker outbound-communications delta still contains a
  latest-material-editor eligibility shortcut that conflicts with D24. It must
  be reconciled before implementation; D30 does not revive or excuse it.

All 22 requested adversarial categories have a material concern under the bare
answer or an unsafe implementation; none invalidates the amended direction.
The complete category-by-category concern records, 29 corrected rules, 136
canonical acceptance criteria, named signal/threshold/owner/response contracts,
rollout, rollback, evidence limits, and exact disposition are in
[phase-24-d30-required-request-changes-explanation-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d30-required-request-changes-explanation-adversarial-review.md).
The current primary evidence, 23 research rules, 125 research-only outcomes,
and evidence limits are in
[phase-24-d30-required-request-changes-explanation-primary-research.md](./phase-24-d30-required-request-changes-explanation-primary-research.md).
The architecture is amended in
[ADR-0181](../../adr/0181-source-authorized-candidate-scoped-external-review.md),
ADR-0182 records that D30 never enters D28/D29, and `CONTEXT.md` defines
**Request-changes explanation** and **Review source anchor**.

D30 is recorded but remains **Reserved**, not Live, until the later OpenSpec,
design, implementation, migration, authorization/RLS, accessibility, security,
production-shaped tests, canary, monitors, and release proof implement the same
contract. The broad verification suite remains intentionally deferred until
the end of this Grill session.

## D31 — Who receives private attention after Request changes?

### Why this needs your decision

D30 makes the returned work understandable, but it deliberately creates no
task, assignee, email, or D29 decline/expiry follow-up. Core still needs one
truthful way to help the right staff notice the correction without broadcasting
private feedback, mistaking provenance for responsibility, or granting a new
permission. This decision governs personal **Needs attention** only; the source
remains authoritative and current authorization controls every visible detail
and action.

### Hope Ministries example

Eli reports that the French **Contact us** link opens the English page. Maria
can revise Page content, while Joel alone can revise Navigation. Neither should
receive an item for an action they cannot perform, and Eli's explanation must
not be copied into several unrelated tasks. Who should see **Needs attention**
while a corrected successor is still needed?

### Option 1 — source-owned correction attention — recommended

The source opens one correction episode and projects a personal item only to
each current, authorized person who can perform at least one still-required
next source action. One person receives one deduplicated item for the episode
even if several permitted actions apply; the detail shows only feedback and
actions that person may see. Reading clears only that person's unread state.
One successful source correction/successor transition ends applicable sibling
items. Proved zero recipients creates nobody and guesses no fallback; the
source remains discoverable to independently authorized staff.

**End-user experience:** Maria and Joel see only relevant, permission-filtered
next actions. Neither is assigned or granted access by the item, and one repair
transition removes obsolete attention without a manual Resolve checkbox.

**Impact:** best alignment among private context, present permission, and real
work; reuses the accepted state-driven attention model without a new roster.
The spec must deduplicate one person's several actions, keep personal read state
separate, prevent partial authorization from widening detail, and handle proved
zero or indeterminate recipients without guessing.

### Option 2 — original candidate initiator coordinates

Only the person who started the candidate receives one correction item and
contacts any other source owners.

**End-user experience:** one quiet recipient, but that person may be away or no
longer able to edit Page/Navigation. They may have to copy private feedback
outside Core.

**Impact:** simple happy path but brittle because creation history is not
continuing responsibility; turnover and permission changes can strand work.

### Option 3 — Website Review coordinators coordinate

The one-to-three D29 Review coordinators receive the correction item and choose
who repairs the candidate.

**End-user experience:** staff recognize a configured group, but coordinators
may see private feedback they cannot act on and must manually route every
repair.

**Impact:** reuses visible configuration but broadens a route explicitly
created only for decline/expiry next-lane recovery, creates overlapping
responsibility meanings, and adds another step.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — source-owned correction attention.** It
aligns private context, current permission, and the next real action; avoids a
third roster or historical-owner fallback; and preserves personal read state
without turning feedback into a shared task.

Do you choose **Option 1 — source-owned correction attention**, **Option 2 —
original initiator coordinates**, or **Option 3 — Review coordinators
coordinate**? You may amend any option.

### D31 resolution

**Founder answer:** Option 1 — source-owned correction attention.

**Additional founder direction:** Many actionable assignments across Core
should eventually create work for their recipients in one shared Tasks Hub,
including Website/CMS and future Mobilize work. D31 must build toward that
cross-domain future without assuming that every record called an assignment is
a task or prematurely making Inngest the product authority.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

The bare answer was directionally correct but insufficient. It did not define
responsibility versus capability, the source/task/notification ownership
boundary, safe zero and indeterminate routing, protected-feedback handling,
durable projection identity, or what “assignments create tasks” means. The
corrected permanent decision is:

> One exact D30 `changes_requested` result opens at most one source-owned,
> state-driven **Correction attention episode** for the exact Tenant,
> environment, Site, source, candidate, review epoch, and result. A finite,
> code-owned, versioned source contract declares typed next actions,
> responsibility, current action and visibility authorization, safe list facts,
> protected detail, source destination, source end, retention, recipient
> ceiling, and projection policy. It never parses the reviewer explanation or
> optional anchor, uses AI, treats capability as responsibility, or routes by
> historical author, generic role, queue, task, notification, or workflow-
> provider state.
>
> One complete bounded routing generation selects only people who are both
> currently responsible for at least one still-required action and currently
> authorized to see and perform their permitted action subset. Capability
> alone never broadcasts to every editor or administrator; assignment grants no
> access. Proved zero creates no guessed fallback. Partial, stale,
> indeterminate, contradictory, timed-out, or over-ceiling resolution releases
> nobody, while independently authorized staff retain truthful source
> discoverability.
>
> Each selected recipient receives one deduplicated actionable presentation
> for the episode at the exact Party+role+surface grain, even when several
> compatible actions apply. Reading clears only that recipient's unread state.
> It never completes, dismisses, transfers, or hides work. Current authorization
> is re-proved for list, count, detail, deep link, and every source action;
> access loss removes protected presentation immediately and never transfers
> engagement history.
>
> The Website source alone owns whether correction work exists, its typed
> actionability, valid corrected successor, cancellation, supersession,
> recurrence, and source end. Notification, task, comment, click, timer,
> worker, analytics, or provider state cannot clear or mutate it. Source end
> always makes applicable projections inapplicable. D31 creates no default date,
> reminder, recurrence, email, SMS, push, urgency escalation, public effect,
> Giving effect, finance effect, or new permission.
>
> Core will build one cross-domain **Tasks Hub** through ADR-0183's
> provider-neutral **Source work projection contract**. One source work
> occurrence has one stable product identity and at most one shared source-
> backed task identity with recipient-specific assignment and engagement
> projections. Website/CMS, Mobilize, contribution operations, and later
> producers reuse the platform task vocabulary only after each registers and
> proves its own actionable predicate, permissions, safe projection, recipient
> resolver, source destination, and end. Active Tenant Assignments, Support
> Assignments, roles, memberships, owners, participants, pipeline positions,
> and capabilities create no task by convention.
>
> Notification and task remain separate projections over the same causal
> source-work identity. Task materialization creates no second bell event,
> assignment never grants access, and protected D30 feedback is referenced at
> the source rather than copied into task text, comments, search, analytics,
> AI, exports, caches, telemetry, or workflow history. One coherent **My tasks**
> row leads with the exact source action and explains why it exists, what
> remains unchanged, and how source truth differs from unread and task state.
>
> The source result and identifier-only projection intent commit atomically;
> task and notification projections may be eventual, independently retryable,
> and reconcilable. Product database uniqueness, semantic receipts, expected-
> head compare-and-swap, and current-state claims own durable idempotency and
> race safety. Inngest may execute short projection/reconciliation work behind
> Core's existing ledger only if a later production-shaped comparison proves
> it is the smallest qualified executor. It owns no source, recipient,
> authorization, task, protected content, completion, or permanent dedupe fact
> and never waits for the human lifecycle.

### D31 staff UX/UI

The future Tasks destination becomes one real server-authorized **Tasks Hub**,
not another CMS task list and not the current prototype **Mission Pipeline**
collection. It defaults ordinary staff to **My tasks**. One compact row answers
what needs action, where, why it remains, and what the person can do:

```text
Website
Prepare a corrected Website version
hope.org · French (Canada)
Changes were requested · Website and Giving are unchanged

[Open Website work]
```

The list and badge remain body-free. The route-addressable detail re-proves
authorization, loads the protected explanation from the Website source, says
**Assigned to you by the Website workflow** rather than attributing assignment
to the external reviewer, and keeps the exact source action primary. Wide
screens may use the existing Base Maia Drawer pattern; small screens use a
full-page composition. Browser Back preserves list/filter/scroll/focus; source
end announces its result and moves focus logically. Unread and Active use
separate text, counts, and semantics. The journey must work at 320 CSS pixels,
400% zoom, forced colors, keyboard and screen reader, touch, long
translations, CJK/RTL, low bandwidth, authorization loss, and ambiguous
network outcomes.

Current behavior remains explicitly different from the target: Phase 24 has no
D31 runtime; the real `mission_control_tasks` backend is contribution-shaped
and non-atomic for the required multi-row effect; admin `/tasks` is a separate
seed/in-memory prototype; missionary tasks are a different role surface; and
Mobilize has no approved durable source-work contract. None is silently reused
or backfilled. Readers, denial guards, constraints, shared task commands,
source adapters, shadow projection, reconciliation, and observability must
precede a single canary writer. Rollback stops projection and rolls forward
from source truth; it never reverses D30 or deletes durable work history.

All 22 requested adversarial categories contain a material concern in the bare
answer or an unsafe implementation. The corrected contract, 30 normative
rules, 132 sequential acceptance criteria, 26 named monitors, exact ownership
map, UX journeys, RLS/database requirements, failure matrix, rollout order,
and evidence limits are in
[phase-24-d31-source-owned-correction-attention-adversarial-review.md](./phase-24-d31-source-owned-correction-attention-adversarial-review.md).
The current primary research, product comparisons, executor analysis, 120
research outcomes, and 22 research monitors are in
[phase-24-d31-source-owned-correction-attention-primary-research.md](./phase-24-d31-source-owned-correction-attention-primary-research.md).
The architecture is recorded in [ADR-0183](../../adr/0183-source-owned-work-projects-into-one-shared-tasks-hub.md),
clarified in [ADR-0027](../../adr/0027-one-notification-presentation-and-engagement-model.md),
and added to [ADR-0181](../../adr/0181-source-authorized-candidate-scoped-external-review.md).

D31 is recorded but remains **Reserved**, not Live, until the later OpenSpec,
design, implementation, migration, authorization/RLS, accessibility, security,
production-shaped tests, canary, monitors, and release evidence implement the
same contract. Broad repository verification remains deferred until the end of
this Grill session as directed.

## D32 — What should **Complete task** mean for source-backed work?

### Why this needs your decision

D31 establishes that task state can never clear Website correction truth, but
it deliberately does not decide whether a recipient may finish only their
subordinate Tasks Hub assignment before the source condition ends. That choice
will shape staff trust across Website, Mobilize, contribution operations, and
every future source-backed task.

### Hope Ministries example

Maria fixes the French Page content she can edit, but Joel's Navigation change
is still outstanding and no corrected Website successor exists yet. Maria
expects **My tasks** to reflect her effort accurately. Hope Ministries also
cannot afford a green **Complete** state that suggests the Website correction
ended when it did not.

### Option 1 — source-controlled task closure only — recommended

There is no independent **Complete task** control. Staff act through the
source-led action such as **Open Website work**. The task remains active until
the source says the assigned action or correction is no longer required; the
source outcome then maps to truthful task history.

**Staff experience:** one unmistakable truth and no duplicate cleanup. Maria
may find it slightly inflexible while waiting for Joel's action, but the UI
cannot falsely claim the Website work is finished.

**Impact:** safest and clearest initial cross-domain policy, with the least
lifecycle and reporting debt. It can be relaxed later without transferring
source authority.

### Option 2 — independent completion with current-source recheck

Maria may complete only her subordinate task assignment after a fresh
authorization/source check and explicit copy that Website correction remains
separate. Source work stays discoverable and actionable; a later source
transition reconciles history without rewriting Maria's personal completion.

**Staff experience:** better personal agency and workload hygiene, but staff
and managers must understand two real states. Core also needs reactivation,
reassignment, reporting, and “everyone completed tasks while source remains
open” rules.

**Impact:** strongest alternative, but materially more UX, lifecycle,
analytics, and reconciliation complexity.

### Option 3 — task completion invokes the source command

**Complete task** invokes the exact registered source action and completes the
task only if that command succeeds.

**Staff experience:** one button looks convenient, but it can hide source-
specific confirmation and evidence and turn a generic task control into
publication, finance, Mobilize, or other domain authority.

**Impact:** reject as a general Tasks Hub rule. A later exact source may expose
the same deliberate source command only when the controls are genuinely
identical and all source authorization and consequences remain visible.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — source-controlled task closure only.** It is
the clearest initial model, protects source truth, and avoids asking staff to
interpret a green task beside unresolved ministry work. Option 2 is the
strongest alternative if future representative research proves that “my part
is done” is essential.

Do you choose **Option 1 — source-controlled task closure only**, **Option 2 —
independent completion with current-source recheck**, or **Option 3 — task
completion invokes the source command**? You may amend any option.

### D32 resolution

**Founder direction:** Choose Option 1 or Option 2 using the strongest evidence
and product judgment.

**Selected answer:** Option 1 — source-controlled task closure only, amended to
operate at the exact assigned source-action scope.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

The unamended Option 1 could have been inflexible if Maria had to wait for the
entire correction episode after finishing her Page work. Option 2 would fix
that symptom by creating a second completion truth, allowing every recipient to
hide the same work while Website still said it was required. The permanent
answer instead uses the source granularity D31 already requires:

> Every shared task contract declares one closed, code-owned **Completion
> authority**. A D31 Website **Source-backed task** uses source-controlled
> closure. Tasks Hub exposes no independent Complete, Reopen, Dismiss,
> Suppress, Delete, drag-to-Done, bulk-completion, keyboard, API, import, AI,
> support, worker, or direct-database transition for that task or recipient
> assignment. A Tenant, client, assignee, administrator, workflow, or provider
> cannot change its completion authority.
>
> Each recipient assignment references one or more exact typed **Source-action
> scopes** from the current D31 routing generation. The recipient's task stays
> active while at least one assigned scope remains required, assigned, visible,
> and authorized. When the source authoritatively satisfies or otherwise ends
> Maria's final Page scope, Maria's projection leaves **My tasks** even if
> Joel's Navigation work and the parent correction episode remain active. The
> shared task/episode ends only from its own complete source predicate.
>
> If a source cannot prove a narrower action-specific end, Core uses the
> smallest broader source-owned predicate it can prove and explains the scope
> honestly. It never adds a personal Done assertion, parses the D30 explanation
> or anchor, trusts a comment, or infers completion from changed content, read,
> time, notification, task activity, worker state, or provider state to conceal
> a weak source model.
>
> The task's primary action is the exact source-led imperative, such as **Open
> Website work**. Tasks Hub may present an exact source-owned action only when
> the source contract supplies the same current authorization, evidence,
> consequence UI, expected heads, and command. The control remains a source
> action—not generic task completion—and only an authoritative successful
> source receipt changes task applicability.
>
> Source outcomes project to typed task history. A satisfied assigned action is
> **Completed in Website**. If another authorized actor satisfied it, the
> recipient may see **Completed elsewhere** without actor identity unless
> separately authorized. Cancellation, supersession, withdrawal, and
> inapplicability are **No longer required**; responsibility handoff is
> **Reassigned**. Access loss removes protected presentation and is never
> completion. Later recurrence creates a successor source-work/task identity
> and never reopens the predecessor.
>
> An **Independent follow-up task** is a different contract whose human
> deliverable can truthfully finish while its linked source remains open. It may
> record **Done with my task** under current authorization and task policy, but
> it cannot clear, hide, approve, publish, pay, release, communicate, or
> otherwise mutate source truth. This preserves ADR-0054 finance follow-up,
> Support activities, and ordinary manual Tasks Hub work without weakening D31
> Website correction. Completion authority is not a Tenant-configurable task
> mode or generic workflow DSL.
>
> Source action/end reason/receipt and identifier-only projection intent commit
> through the authoritative source transaction. Product database uniqueness,
> expected-head compare-and-swap, semantic receipts, current-state reads, and
> monotonic reconciliation own correctness. Inngest may execute only short,
> replay-safe projection/reconciliation effects; it never waits for the human,
> accepts completion, chooses the reason, supplies permanent deduplication, or
> becomes source/task audit truth.

### D32 staff UX/UI

A source-backed Website row omits—not disables—the familiar checkbox:

```text
Website · Needs action
Prepare the French Page correction
hope.org · French (Canada)
Completes in Website                              [Open Website work]
```

Its route-addressable detail says:

```text
Complete this work in Website
This task updates automatically from Website state.
Marking a task cannot publish the Website or change Giving.

[Open Website work]
```

After Maria's authoritative Page action succeeds:

```text
Page correction prepared
Your Website task is complete.
Other correction work may still be required.
```

Joel's row remains **Needs action**. A source-backed row has no completion
checkbox, overflow action, drag/swipe completion, command-palette shortcut, or
bulk mutation. Mixed bulk operations exclude these rows and explain the count.
Manual and Independent follow-up tasks retain their own clearly labelled
controls rather than borrowing Website completion semantics.

Current behavior remains explicitly different from the permanent target. The
admin `/tasks` prototype lets the browser toggle generic completion and
deletion in a seed/in-memory collection; `mission_control_tasks` has one broad
mutable status enum without a completion-authority discriminant, source-action
scope, source receipt, or typed end reason; missionary tasks are a separate
personal system. Policy-aware denial guards and readers must precede any D31
writer so an old checkbox, API, worker, import, support tool, or AI path cannot
mutate a source-backed task.

The complete review found a material concern in every requested category under
the bare answer or an unsafe implementation. The
[D32 adversarial review](./phase-24-d32-source-backed-task-completion-adversarial-review.md)
contains 22 eight-field category records, 22 normative rules, 126 sequential
acceptance criteria, 24 named monitors, exact RLS/database/lifecycle/privacy/
failure requirements, rollout order, and evidence limits. The
[D32 primary research](./phase-24-d32-source-backed-task-completion-primary-research.md)
contains 130 research outcomes, 25 additional named monitors, current official
CMS/CRM/nonprofit/task comparisons, and the full two-policy Tasks Hub analysis.

ADR-0183 now owns the cross-domain completion-authority boundary; ADR-0181
owns Website source-action closure; ADR-0054 classifies accounting human work
as Independent follow-up only where its deliverable is separately testable;
`CONTEXT.md` defines Completion authority, Source-action scope, Source-backed
task, and Independent follow-up task. Phase 34 records that an eventual
Mobilize workflow task closes only through its authoritative Phase 34 source
command, not a generic Tasks Hub or Inngest state.

D32 is recorded but remains **Reserved**, not Live, until the later OpenSpec,
design, implementation, migration, authorization/RLS, accessibility, security,
production-shaped tests, canary, monitors, and release evidence implement the
same contract. Broad repository verification remains deferred until the end of
this Grill session as directed.

## D33 — How should a recipient return or hand off source-backed work?

### Why this needs your decision

Source-controlled closure prevents false Done states, but the task must not
become a trap when responsibility is wrong or circumstances change. Maria may
be authorized for the French Page yet know Amélie owns that translation; she
may be going on leave, lack the needed source context, or discover that the
work is actually Navigation. A generic assignee picker can leak protected
feedback or assign someone without source responsibility or access. Requiring
an administrator for every ordinary handoff creates avoidable ministry delay.

### Hope Ministries example

Maria opens **Prepare the French Page correction** and realizes the translation
belongs to Amélie. Amélie is currently eligible for that exact source-action
scope. What should Maria be able to do without making Tasks Hub a second
responsibility authority?

### Option 1 — source-validated return or handoff — recommended

Offer **This needs someone else** from task detail. The source contract returns
only currently eligible destinations, shows the exact effect, and commits an
expected-head successor responsibility generation. Assignment grants no
access; unchanged recipients retain engagement; Maria ends **Reassigned** only
after the source accepts the transition. Proved-zero or indeterminate
destinations return to a protected source-owned unassigned/recovery state and
never guess a queue or administrator.

**Staff experience:** flexible and direct without sending private context
outside Core. The task keeps Maria's place, explains what changes, and gives
Amélie one fresh task/unread state only after a truthful handoff.

**Impact:** best balance of staff agency, current authorization, audit, and
cross-domain reuse, with one deliberate source-controlled step.

### Option 2 — only source administrators can reassign

Maria sees who to contact but cannot return or hand off the task. An authorized
Website administrator changes responsibility from the source surface.

**Staff experience:** simple authorization model, but ordinary leave and
misrouting require another person and often outside communication.

**Impact:** safe but slow and operationally brittle for small ministries.

### Option 3 — arbitrary Tasks Hub reassignment

Anyone with generic task reassignment permission selects another staff member
or queue and Tasks Hub updates the assignee immediately.

**Staff experience:** familiar and fast, but the selected person may lack
source access and the source still records Maria as responsible.

**Impact:** rejects the D31/D32 ownership boundary and creates dual routing,
privacy, lifecycle, and repair debt.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — source-validated return or handoff.** It is
the important flexibility companion to source-controlled closure: staff are
never forced to lie with Done or wait helplessly, while the source still proves
who may receive and perform the work.

Do you choose **Option 1 — source-validated return or handoff**, **Option 2 —
administrator-only reassignment**, or **Option 3 — arbitrary Tasks Hub
reassignment**? You may amend any option.

### D33 resolution

**Founder direction:** Option 1 — source-validated return or handoff, with the
best possible staff UX and full adversarial review.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

The selected direction is the necessary flexibility companion to D32, but the
original option incorrectly allowed several unsafe readings. It conflated a
named handoff with a no-successor return, implied indeterminate candidate lookup
could itself return work, did not preserve co-responsible recipients, and could
be implemented as a mutable Tasks Hub or Payload assignee.

The corrected decision is:

> A source-backed task may show **This needs someone else** as a visible
> secondary action. It opens one responsive Base Maia source-led panel, not an
> inline generic assignee field or nested confirmation flow. The current
> recipient selects one or more exact still-active Source-action scopes and
> deliberately chooses either a named handoff or a return without naming a
> successor.
>
> Opening, loading, searching, paging, selecting, canceling, losing connection,
> or receiving zero/partial/indeterminate choices changes nothing. One short
> expected-head Website operational-source command derives the actor from
> trusted context and re-proves initiator authority, Tenant/environment/Site/
> source/action scope, current assignment, source/policy/authorization heads,
> and any named target's exact current Party+role eligibility before appending
> the complete immutable successor responsibility generation, receipt, and
> identifier-only projection intent.
>
> **Named handoff:** one currently eligible person is selected. The actor's
> selected memberships end as **Reassigned**. The named person is added or kept
> responsible; if already responsible, they receive no duplicate task or unread
> pulse. Continuing recipients preserve their assignment and engagement.
>
> **Return:** no successor is named. The actor's selected memberships end as
> **Returned** and every other current responsible recipient remains. Only if
> nobody remains does the source enter **Needs assignment** and show **Returned
> for reassignment**. The required work remains visible on the exact authorized
> source recovery surface and guesses no person, queue, administrator,
> coordinator, or fallback. D29 Review coordinators are a separate route
> purpose and are never reused by convention.
>
> Proved-zero candidate availability, Needs assignment, and indeterminate proof
> remain distinct. Indeterminate/partial/stale/timeout/overflow writes nothing.
> Return remains available during candidate-search failure only if its actor,
> scopes, source recovery, and expected heads can be independently re-proved.
>
> Assignment grants no access. Tasks Hub, Payload, notifications, browser/task
> state, comments, AI, service tooling, and Inngest never own or certify
> responsibility. Inngest may only execute short identifier-only task/
> notification materialization and reconciliation after the authoritative
> source transaction. No email, recurring reminder, target date, acceptance
> workflow, bulk reassignment, public Website, Giving, finance, permission, HR,
> or generic delegation/routing effect is created.

### D33 staff UX/UI

The active task keeps **Open Website work** primary and makes the recovery
action easy to find:

```text
Website · Needs action
Prepare the French Page correction
hope.org · French (Canada)

[Open Website work]
This needs someone else
```

The responsive source-led subview uses a constrained searchable person picker
and one consequence-led final action:

```text
Who should take this Website work?

Page correction
hope.org · French (Canada)

Only people who can currently access and perform this exact work are shown.
Choosing someone does not grant access or mark the correction done.

[Search eligible people]
○ Amélie Laurent — Translator
○ Joel Mensah — Website editor

I don't know who should take this
```

After Maria selects Amélie, the same surface previews exactly what moves, what
Maria keeps, what other recipients retain, and that Website/Giving do not
change. The final button is **Hand off to Amélie**. There is no second modal.

Return previews the exact current outcome:

```text
Return Page correction?

You will no longer be responsible. Other current responsible people will stay.
If nobody remains, Website will show Needs assignment. The correction stays
open and no email or reminder is sent.

[Return this work] [Keep assigned to me]
```

Candidate rows use full international display names and the smallest lawful
role/team/Site disambiguator; avatars are supplemental. The source returns only
enumerable current candidates, uses neutral deterministic ordering, and never
ranks by AI, inferred skill, workload, presence, hierarchy, or history. Large
sets use indexed server search/cursor paging rather than downloading the Tenant
directory. Zero says **No eligible people are available**; indeterminate says
**We couldn't verify who can take this. Nothing changed.**

Named success is **Handed off to Amélie**. Return is **Returned** when someone
else remains, or **Returned for reassignment — this work still needs an owner**
when nobody remains. Source receipts drive the persistent result and one polite
announcement; a toast is not the only evidence. Cancel, stale target, source
completion, competing handoff, lost response, authorization loss, offline,
low-bandwidth, mobile, keyboard, screen-reader, 320px/400% reflow, forced-color,
Unicode/CJK/RTL, duplicate-name, and no-avatar states have explicit behavior.

### Current versus permanent behavior

Current admin `/tasks` is a browser/in-memory prototype with an arbitrary staff
dropdown. Current `mission_control_tasks` has one nullable profile assignee,
generic statuses, broad service-role grants, no RLS policies, no exact source-
action scope, no Tenant-composite successor lineage, and no transition receipt.
The contribution assignment policy's actor/Finance-queue defaults and the
separate missionary tasks system are not D33 authority.

The permanent path is additive immutable source responsibility generations,
members, expected heads, typed handoff/return receipts, source recovery,
same-scope constraints, one guarded `packages/api` source command, policy-aware
Tasks Hub readers, and monotonic projections. Generic assignment denial lands
before any writer; no historic handoff is inferred; shadow/canary precede one
writer; rollback disables initiation and rolls projections forward rather than
rewriting source history.

The [D33 adversarial review](./phase-24-d33-source-validated-return-handoff-adversarial-review.md)
contains 22 eight-field material-concern records, 26 normative rules, 120
sequential acceptance criteria, 30 named signal/threshold/owner/response
monitors, exact UX/data/RLS/auth/privacy/concurrency/failure/migration/Inngest
requirements, and the final synthesis. The
[D33 primary research](./phase-24-d33-source-validated-return-handoff-primary-research.md)
contains 138 sequential research outcomes, 29 additional named monitors, and
current official CMS/CRM/nonprofit/work-management/security/accessibility
evidence.

ADR-0183 now owns the D31–D33 shared Tasks Hub responsibility boundary;
ADR-0181 owns the Website correction-source transition; ADR-0182 explicitly
keeps D29 Review coordinators separate; `CONTEXT.md` defines Source
responsibility transition and Needs assignment; Phase 34 records that future
Mobilize responsibility must use its own source command rather than Website
predicates or a generic Tasks Hub assignee.

D33 is recorded but remains **Reserved**, not Live, until later OpenSpec,
design, schema, source adapters, Phase 12 authorization, RLS/grants,
implementation, migration, accessibility, security, production-shaped tests,
canary, monitors, and release evidence implement the same contract. Broad
repository verification remains deferred until the end of this Grill session.

## D34 — What context should staff provide when returning or handing off work?

### Why this needs your decision

The source already records the actor, exact action scopes, current state, and a
named successor when one exists. Requiring prose for every ordinary handoff
adds friction and invites sensitive explanations about health, leave,
performance, or conflict. But a return that leaves work in **Needs assignment**
may be easier to triage if recovery staff know whether the task reached the
wrong person, needs a different role, or cannot currently be taken.

### Hope Ministries example

Maria can hand the French Page correction directly to Amélie with all relevant
Website context attached by source reference. No explanation may be needed. If
Maria instead returns it and no responsible person remains, should Core require
or invite context for whoever later assigns it?

### Option 1 — context only when it changes recovery — recommended

- Named eligible successor: no required reason or note.
- Return while another responsible person remains: no required reason.
- Return that creates **Needs assignment**: require one short code-owned reason
  choice such as **Not the right person**, **Needs a different role**, **Cannot
  take this work**, or **Another reason**.
- No generic free-text note is collected; source context remains reference-only.
  A later source-specific note would require separate evidence and governance.

**Staff experience:** the common handoff stays one decisive interaction;
recovery receives enough structured meaning to triage without demanding
personal prose or creating a comment system.

**Impact:** lowest routine effort, useful recovery data, bounded localization/
analytics, and lower privacy/retention risk than free text.

### Option 2 — require context for every transition

Every named handoff and return requires one structured reason, with an optional
concise private source-owned note.

**Staff experience:** uniform and auditable, but obvious handoffs gain a
mandatory step and staff may select meaningless reasons or disclose personal
details merely to proceed.

**Impact:** more reporting consistency at the cost of friction, privacy,
retention, moderation, and weak-quality data.

### Option 3 — collect no user-provided context

Every transition relies only on source scopes, predecessor, destination,
trusted actor, expected heads, and timestamps; no reason or note is collected.

**Staff experience:** fastest and most private, but ownerless returns offer no
structured clue for recovery and recurring routing problems are harder to
understand.

**Impact:** simplest data model, weakest recovery triage.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — context only when it changes recovery.** It
keeps named handoff as low-effort as modern work tools while asking for bounded
meaning only when the transition creates an actual source responsibility gap.

Do you choose **Option 1 — context only when it changes recovery**, **Option 2
— context for every transition**, or **Option 3 — no user-provided context**?
You may amend any option.

### D34 resolution

**Founder direction:** Option 1 — context only when it changes recovery, with
modern-practice, technical-debt, brittleness, and excellent UX/UI review.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

The conditional direction is the best permanent path, but the draft four-code
list is too overlapping. **Not the right person** and **Needs a different
role/kind of work** both initially tell authorized recovery staff to inspect
the responsibility/action model. Treating them as separate before
representative evidence would create arbitrary choices, localization,
analytics, and migration debt. The corrected decision is:

> Named handoff collects no context or note. A return that leaves another
> current responsible recipient for every selected Source-action scope also
> collects no context or note. Only an explicit recipient-initiated return
> whose fresh source preview and authoritative expected-head commit would leave
> one or more exact scopes in source-owned **Needs assignment** requires one
> **Return recovery context**.
>
> Website v1 offers exactly one unselected code-owned choice:
>
> - `responsibility_mismatch` — **This work belongs with someone else**;
> - `cannot_take_current_work` — **I can't take this work**; or
> - `other` — **Something else**.
>
> **Something else** reveals no text field. Core collects no explanation,
> note, attachment, mention, copied D30 feedback, second reason, default,
> remembered value, Tenant customization, or AI classification.
>
> The code proves only what the actor selected. It is not the source-derived
> transition reason and does not prove cause, capability, availability,
> eligibility, fault, source state, or a correct successor. It may change only
> permission-safe guidance on the currently authorized Website recovery
> surface. It never changes destination, routing, scopes, permission,
> priority, urgency, date, reminder, escalation, notification, automation,
> completion, publication, Giving, finance, HR, member care, or person
> analytics.
>
> One short expected-head source transaction derives the trusted actor and
> exact resulting gap scopes, validates the code/version, and atomically
> appends the complete responsibility generation, immutable receipt, context,
> and identifier-only projection intent. Context is null for every other
> transition/result. Code, version, and gap-scope digest participate in
> canonical idempotency; exact replay returns the receipt and changed meaning
> conflicts.
>
> The operational source owns context, visibility, and schedule. Tasks Hub
> references the receipt and safe outcome but does not store or interpret the
> code. Payload, task comments/reasons, Support Hub move reasons,
> notifications, workflow events, logs, search, AI, generic exports, caches,
> external analytics, and later sources are not owners or automatic consumers.
>
> Future sources such as Mobilize may reuse only the source-owned safe envelope
> after their own evidence-backed contract; Website labels and meanings are
> never inferred. If representative evidence shows that the choices do not
> improve recovery or cannot be understood reliably without personal detail,
> Core removes the prompt and collects nothing rather than adding prose,
> categories, Tenant configuration, or automation.

The interaction remains inside D33's one responsive Base Maia panel. Named
handoff and covered return do not render the group. A qualifying return first
shows the exact ownerless scopes and **Website > Changes requested > Needs
assignment**, then one unselected RadioGroup headed **What is the main reason
you're returning this work?** The choices use concise helper text; missing
selection produces a persistent inline, programmatically associated error;
the final action says **Return for reassignment** and the safe alternative says
**Keep assigned to me**. No nested dialog, disabled-button-only validation, or
toast-only result exists.

The data contract structurally enforces the operation/result/context matrix,
trusted server attribution, current source authorization, same-scope
relationships, code/version immutability, and append-only history. Two-last-
recipient, recipient-add/remove, source-terminal, authorization, catalog,
lost-response, changed-code replay, mixed-scope, old-client, and projection-
failure races fail without mutation or converge from the source receipt.

All 22 requested adversarial categories have material concerns because the
field touches personal attribution and an authoritative responsibility
transition, although scalability risk is modest. The required disposition is
not alarmist: three constant-size codes add little runtime cost; the material
risks come from invalid state combinations, false semantics, copied sinks,
employee monitoring, and reason-driven coupling. Detailed eight-field findings,
30 normative rules, 120 acceptance criteria, 26 named monitors, primary-source
research, and the ordered rollout are in:

- [`phase-24-d34-conditional-return-recovery-context-adversarial-review.md`](./phase-24-d34-conditional-return-recovery-context-adversarial-review.md)
- [`phase-24-d34-conditional-recovery-context-primary-research.md`](./phase-24-d34-conditional-recovery-context-primary-research.md)

The exploratory primary-research four-code set is retained as evidence but is
explicitly superseded by this three-code disposition. Support Hub's accepted
5–500-character move reason remains a different purpose-owned contract and is
not changed or generalized.

## D35 — Who receives attention when Website work needs assignment?

### Why this needs your decision

D34 gives an authorized recovery user a small, source-owned hint, but it does
not decide who is responsible for noticing and resolving an ownerless action.
The Website source lane is safe and authoritative but may be missed. Sending a
personal item to every manager/editor would confuse capability with
responsibility and create noise. Requiring a new coordinator roster everywhere
would create setup burden unless it produces real accountability.

### Hope Ministries example

Maria returns the final French Page correction and selects **This work belongs
with someone else**. Website now shows **Needs assignment**. Should Ana receive
a personal **Assign returned Website work** item because Hope Ministries named
her for recovery, should authorized staff discover one shared lane, or should
Core alert everyone who can manage Website work?

### Option 1 — shared lane plus optional bounded personal recovery — recommended

Website always shows one source-owned **Needs assignment** row to currently
authorized recovery staff. A Tenant may additionally name one to three
**Website work-recovery coordinators** for the distinct action **Assign
returned Website work**. Only their current authorized intersection receives
one shared source-backed task/attention projection; the first successful source
assignment ends every projection. The roster grants no edit access and is
separate from D29 Review coordinators. No email or recurring reminder is sent
by default.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** zero required setup for a safe discoverable lane; small
teams may opt into clear personal accountability; the same person may be chosen
for both coordinator purposes only by deliberate separate selection.

**Impact:** one source truth and one shared recovery action, bounded noise, no
capability broadcast, and modest optional configuration.

### Option 2 — source recovery lane only

Website shows the one authorized **Needs assignment** lane, but no personal
task or attention projection is created.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** simplest and quietest. It depends on somebody habitually
checking the lane, so ownerless work may wait without individual
accountability.

**Impact:** least configuration and projection work; greatest discovery risk.

### Option 3 — broadcast every Website manager or capable editor

Every currently authorized Website manager/editor receives personal attention
for each ownerless action.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** no setup, but duplicate attention, unclear ownership, and
alert fatigue; capability is misrepresented as responsibility.

**Impact:** easiest to implement superficially and least safe/scalable. Reject.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — shared lane plus optional bounded personal
recovery.** It makes the safe no-configuration path complete while letting a
Tenant add explicit accountability without broadcasts, guessed recipients, or
another source of truth.

Do you choose **Option 1 — shared lane plus optional 1–3 work-recovery
coordinators**, **Option 2 — source recovery lane only**, or **Option 3 —
broadcast all authorized Website managers/editors**? You may amend any option.

### D35 resolution

**Founder direction:** Option 1 — one shared lane plus optional one to three
recovery coordinators, with current modern-practice and Core-consistent UX/UI
review.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

> Website owns one permission-filtered **Needs assignment lane** over current
> authoritative source-work heads. One row exists for each compatible recovery
> occurrence in which one or more exact Source-action scopes remain required
> and have no responsible recipient. The lane is a Website source view—not a
> Mission Control queue, task assignee, shared notification/read state, claim,
> or second lifecycle—and independently authorized staff may assign from it.
>
> The lane cannot be disabled, dismissed, archived, snoozed, claimed,
> completed, or mutated through a task. It remains available when coordinator
> policy, authorization resolution, Tasks Hub, notification, Realtime, worker,
> or Inngest is absent, delayed, or failed.
>
> D35 has one closed, versioned Tenant policy with exactly two postures:
> code-owned source_lane_only@1, the missing-row and zero-setup default; or
> named_coordinators, exactly one to three unique, unordered, co-equal stable
> same-Tenant Parties. Named zero, duplicates, cross-scope members, or a fourth
> member are invalid. Removing the final member explicitly selects **Use Needs
> assignment only**. D35 adds no Site override; current exact Site/source
> authorization narrows the Tenant route for every occurrence.
>
> The D35 route has a distinct purpose, head, immutable revisions/members,
> recipient role, action, presentation, audit, and retention from D21 Website
> review responsibility and D29 external-review follow-up. Core never copies,
> aliases, synchronizes, defaults, suggests, unions, or falls back between
> them. Selecting the same person for more than one purpose requires separate
> deliberate saves.
>
> Coordinator membership records responsibility intent only. It grants no
> Tenant assignment, Website capability, Site/source visibility, protected
> detail, correction eligibility, edit/review/publication, Giving, finance, or
> other access. Policy management, coordinator responsibility, lane/detail
> visibility, assignment authority, and destination eligibility are separate
> current predicates.
>
> For each recovery occurrence, the server resolves the complete configured
> one-to-three-person set against current Tenant/environment, identity, Active
> Tenant Assignment, exact Site/source/detail visibility, **Assign returned
> Website work** authority, governance, and current expected heads. A complete
> result may release its qualified subset. Proved zero releases nobody.
> Partial, stale, contradictory, corrupt, timed-out, over-limit, or
> indeterminate proof releases nobody. There is no broadcast or guessed
> fallback; the source lane remains.
>
> One recovery occurrence/action has one stable source-work identity and at
> most one shared source-backed recovery-task identity. Tasks Hub may create
> one recipient-specific assignment and personal engagement projection for
> each admitted coordinator; it never creates copied tasks, a group assignee,
> shared unread, or a generic queue row. Source/team counts count the occurrence
> once; each coordinator's My tasks count and engagement are personal.
>
> **Assign returned Website work** assigns correction responsibility through
> the D33 current expected-head source command. It does not edit, approve,
> publish, complete, cancel, claim, or satisfy correction work. Generic task
> Complete, Reopen, Reassign, Delete, Dismiss, Suppress, Archive, Snooze,
> Comment, date, reminder, bulk, drag, claim, or acceptance operations reject.
> The first successful source assignment/end receipt alone ends assigned scopes
> in the lane and every applicable coordinator projection. Partial assignment
> leaves remaining gaps; self-assignment creates a separate performer lineage.
>
> D30 explanations and D34 Return recovery context remain protected source
> references and never enter lane/task lists, channels, workflow events, logs,
> search, analytics, AI, exports, caches, Inngest, or route policy. Protected
> detail loads only after current purpose-specific authorization.
>
> D35 creates no second bell item, email, SMS, push, digest, recurring reminder,
> target date, SLA, age escalation, sound, Site override, group/team, automatic
> fallback, order, round robin, schedule, workload/AI routing, Tenant rules DSL,
> or Mobilize behavior. Inngest is optional identifier-only post-commit task
> projection/reconciliation; it owns no source, lane, policy, recipient,
> authorization, task truth, durable idempotency, or human wait.

The Core-consistent settings IA is **Settings → Websites → Reviews** with
**Review responsibilities** for **Review notifications** and **External review
follow-up**, then a separate **Correction responsibilities** section containing
**Returned Website work**. The card summary says **Needs assignment only**.
Its editor uses two explanatory radios—**Keep it in Needs assignment only** or
**Also give specific people a task**—and reveals the one-to-three-person Base
UI combobox only for the second choice. It states that choosing people grants
no Website access and exposes no roster copy, order, availability, schedule,
workload, or channel controls.

The source lane is **Website → Changes requested → Needs assignment**. It uses
safe action-led Site/locale rows, deterministic source ordering, safe filters,
cursor pagination, one **Assign work** action, lazy protected detail, and
distinct empty/loading/no-access/failure/stale states. Coordinator Tasks Hub
rows use one **Assign Website work** source action, explain that the recipient
is choosing an owner rather than becoming one, preserve personal unread, and
have no generic task controls. Both surfaces use Base Maia/Base UI, semantic
tokens, visible focus/status, 44px important targets, 320px/400% reflow,
forced colors, keyboard/screen-reader operation, localization, and source-
truth recovery after weak-network or lost-response cases.

## D36 — How should a coordinator-policy save affect work already in Needs assignment?

### Why this needs your decision

Hope Ministries currently has four authorized Website rows in **Needs
assignment**. Ana changes **Returned Website work** from **Needs assignment
only** to **Also give specific people a task** and selects Ana and Joel.

The ordinary save can safely govern future occurrences. Existing rows are
different: automatically applying it could create an unexpected burst of
personal tasks or disclose work a selected person did not expect; never
applying it could leave the four current rows without the accountability Ana
was trying to add. Any current-work operation must also preserve unchanged
recipients' read state, re-prove every source/policy/authorization head, and
avoid counting hidden work.

### Option 1 — prospective save plus explicit current-work action — recommended

Saving changes future occurrences. When current work exists, Core shows a
permission-safe impact summary and a separate **Apply coordinators to current
work** action. That command reloads current heads, resolves the complete route,
preserves unchanged engagement, creates fresh personal assignments only for
newly admitted recipients, handles removed recipients through a typed
differential transition, and reports applied/skipped/changed outcomes without
exposing hidden work.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** no surprise fan-out; one obvious follow-up only when a
backlog exists; canceling it does not undo the prospective setting.

**Impact:** one additional deliberate action buys clear consequences,
authorization safety, idempotent recovery, and truthful engagement history.

### Option 2 — automatically apply every save to all current work

Every successful save recomputes and changes personal projections for all
current qualifying Needs-assignment occurrences.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** one click, but a simple roster edit can silently create or
remove many private tasks and change several people's apparent workload.

**Impact:** lowest clicks, highest privacy, concurrency, lost-response,
rollback, and support risk.

### Option 3 — future occurrences only

Coordinator changes never affect current Needs-assignment work.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** quiet and simple, but a Tenant configuring coordinators to
repair today's backlog must open and handle every row separately.

**Impact:** smallest mutation surface, greatest manual recovery friction.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — prospective save plus an explicit current-
work action.** It follows Phase 24's least-surprise, impact-previewed,
differential-transition pattern and gives staff one clear way to address a
current backlog without hidden fan-out.

Do you choose **Option 1 — prospective plus explicit apply-to-current**,
**Option 2 — automatically apply to all current work**, or **Option 3 — future
work only**? You may amend any option.

### D36 resolution

**Founder direction:** Option 1 — prospective save plus a separate explicit
current-work action, provided it fits the repository and cannot break current
work.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

> Saving **Returned Website work** appends one immutable D35 Tenant policy
> revision, advances its expected current head, establishes one authoritative
> cutover, and returns one durable policy receipt. It is complete and
> prospective by itself. Work entering Needs assignment after the cutover uses
> the saved setting; work already current keeps its applied policy/routing basis
> until a separate authorized current-work application.
>
> Save changes no current routing, Tasks Hub assignment, personal engagement,
> source state, correction owner, content, public Website, Giving, or finance.
> Its result says: **The setting was saved for new returned work. Existing work
> has not changed.** Preview/apply failure or cancellation never rolls back or
> makes ambiguous the completed save.
>
> Before save, helper copy explains that current work changes only through a
> later explicit action. When relevant and separately authorized, the settings
> surface shows **Update current work → Review current-work impact**. It does
> not auto-open, hide current effects in Save, preselect application, block
> saving, or create nag/unread/reminder state.
>
> Preview is a fresh, permission-safe server result bound to the target policy
> head, cutover, current source/routing/authorization heads, resolver versions,
> and D37’s code-owned cohort contract. It is explanatory evidence, not
> mutation authority. It distinguishes Website-item units from personal-
> assignment additions, preserved/no-new-unread assignments, and ended
> coordinator responsibility. Hidden work, counts, Sites, source detail,
> D30/D34 content, qualification, and sibling engagement are non-enumerating.
>
> The review title is **Apply this setting to current Needs assignment work?**
> Named-target confirmation uses **Apply setting to current work**. Lane-only
> confirmation uses **Use Needs assignment only for current work** and says
> personal coordinator assignments end while the source lane remains. The
> review is the single confirmation; there is no nested dialog, typed phrase,
> remembered consent, countdown, or approximate consequence label.
>
> Confirmation invokes one trusted server command that recomputes impact and
> trusts no client cohort, recipient list, count, actor, Tenant, occurrence, or
> preview body. Materially changed policy, authority, cohort, source/routing
> head, or recipient impact writes nothing and returns **Nothing was applied.
> Review the updated impact.**
>
> Acceptance creates one immutable product-owned **Current-work policy
> application** plus normalized occurrence members/results. One user operation
> may be chunked but is not one giant transaction or browser loop. Each
> occurrence re-proves its exact source, Needs-assignment, routing, policy,
> authorization, action-scope, and complete/zero/indeterminate recipient result
> and commits one differential routing successor atomically.
>
> Every accepted member reaches exactly one durable outcome: applied, already
> current, source changed, target policy superseded, not current, not
> authorized, recipient resolution indeterminate, or execution failed. Totals
> conserve the cohort and progress is never reported as applied.
>
> Continuing recipients preserve assignment and engagement lineage, including
> read state, with no new unread. Newly admitted currently authorized
> recipients alone receive one fresh assignment/unread. Removed recipients end
> as **Coordinator responsibility changed** under typed code
> `coordinator_policy_changed`, never Completed, Read, Dismissed, Access
> revoked, correction Reassigned, or Source resolved.
>
> Applying lane-only ends applicable personal coordinator assignments but never
> removes Needs assignment or source actions. Work already prospectively using
> the target policy is unchanged and never duplicated. Ended/assigned/recurrent
> source work receives no stale projection.
>
> A newer policy stops every uncommitted older-target member. Already committed
> generations remain immutable history and are corrected only by the newer
> saved policy plus another explicit current-work application. Retry is bounded
> to the exact immutable application/member/heads; a terminal failed or
> indeterminate member cannot release delayed work. Exact replay returns the
> receipt; changed meaning conflicts.
>
> Progress/result is route-addressable, resumable after navigation or lost
> response, persistently visible and programmatically announced. A toast is
> supplementary; no blind resubmit or misleading Undo is offered. Source lane
> remains available through projection/executor failure.
>
> Browser writes are revoked. Same-scope constraints, immutable attribution,
> operation-correct RLS `USING`/`WITH CHECK`, owner/service/RPC/worker/support/
> repair parity, minimized identifier-only events, and source-safe
> reconciliation preserve Tenant/privacy boundaries. Inngest may only claim and
> process accepted member IDs through the same product command; it owns no
> cutover, cohort, policy, authorization, result, idempotency, or source truth.
>
> D36 creates no Site override, correction/source/public/Giving/finance effect,
> generic task mutation/bulk API, email, bell item, SMS, push, digest, reminder,
> due date, target date, SLA, escalation, claim, staff score, or automatic
> Mobilize behavior. The D37 resolution below defines the exact current-work
> cohort/capability; D38 grant governance and implementation proof remain
> before activation.

## D37 — Which current Needs-assignment work should one application cover?

### Why this needs your decision

Hope Ministries has twelve current ownerless Website items across three Sites.
Ana may manage the Tenant recovery policy and inspect one ordinary Site; a
restricted Site’s source detail is not visible to her. D35 intentionally has
one Tenant policy and no Site override.

D36 separates the prospective save from current adoption, but the application
still needs one exact cohort and authorization rule. Applying only what Ana can
see may leave hidden current work permanently on older settings. Requiring row
selection turns policy settings into a second task-management grid. Applying
Tenant-wide requires a stronger capability and strict non-enumerating preview.

### Option 1 — complete Tenant cohort under a separate Tenant-wide capability — recommended

Core derives the complete compatible current Tenant cohort server-side,
discloses only authorized safe aggregates/details, re-proves every source and
recipient, and starts nothing unless the cohort can be determined completely.
Policy editors without this additional capability can save prospectively but
cannot apply current work.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** one coherent Tenant policy, one deliberate backlog action,
and no need to grant content visibility merely to administer recovery policy.

**Impact:** strongest consistency and least repeated work, with the strictest
capability, cohort-conservation, and non-enumeration requirements.

### Option 2 — only work the initiating person can individually view

The operation applies only to current occurrences whose source detail the actor
may inspect.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** narrower immediate blast radius, but hidden work remains on
older policy bases and several administrators may need to repeat the action.

**Impact:** simpler disclosure, weaker completeness and harder-to-explain mixed
current state.

### Option 3 — manually select Sites, filters, or rows

Staff choose a subset from a bulk-work interface.

**Staff/Tenant UX:** granular control, but more decisions, omission/stale-
selection risk, hidden-work leakage, mobile/accessibility burden, and confusion
about why excluded work retains older settings.

**Impact:** highest complexity and effectively introduces temporary Site/
filter policy exceptions. Reject without strong future evidence.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — complete compatible Tenant scope behind a
distinct Tenant-wide current-work-application capability.** It keeps D35’s one
Tenant policy coherent while permission-safe presentation protects restricted
work. Exceptional individual correction assignment remains available from the
source lane.

Which cohort should D37 record?

### D37 resolution

**Founder direction:** Option 1 — complete compatible Tenant cohort under a
separate Tenant-wide application capability, provided it is current modern best
practice and produces an excellent, quiet, repository-consistent UX.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

> One D36 application covers one **Website recovery current-work cohort**:
> every authoritative occurrence in the exact Tenant, environment, and
> **Assign returned Website work** purpose that entered Needs assignment before
> the target D35 policy's trusted cutover, remains current at the prepared
> cohort seal, and is classified compatible by a complete code-owned
> producer/version catalog.
>
> A known incompatible producer/version is outside the setting's scope. An
> unknown producer/version, missing catalog/partition/page/head, duplicate or
> corrupt occurrence identity, contradictory census fence, truncation,
> timeout, or other inability to prove the complete compatible universe makes
> preparation indeterminate. Core offers no confirmation, accepts no
> application, changes no current work, and never falls back to actor-visible
> rows.
>
> Authoritative Website occurrence/head truth and the closed catalog alone own
> membership. Site, locale, actor visibility, filter, page, row selection,
> Tasks Hub, notification, CMS, cache, search, analytics, recipient
> qualification, and client-supplied IDs/counts never include or exclude a
> member. Trusted cutover/source sequence—not wall-clock/display/task time—
> distinguishes pre-cutover current work from post-cutover work already
> governed prospectively. Recurrence is a new occurrence identity.
>
> Core prepares normalized no-effect cohort/impact evidence before review. One
> atomic seal binds exact Tenant/environment/purpose, policy/cutover, catalog/
> cohort versions, census fence, immutable normalized members, count/digest,
> actor Party, current capability generation, semantic command identity, and
> reviewed consequence bounds before any member claim. Staging/seal failure
> creates no accepted or executable application.
>
> Confirmation trusts no caller actor, Tenant, Site, member, recipient, count,
> filter, preview body, result, or attribution. Any change that could add a
> member, add/end an assignment, change selected Parties, broaden disclosure,
> or otherwise exceed the reviewed impact writes nothing and requires a fresh
> review. A sealed member that merely ended, became already current, or can
> receive only a no-effect D36 result remains conserved; execution never
> substitutes a wider recipient result.
>
> One separate **Tenant-wide Website recovery current-work application
> capability** authorizes only preparation, review, acceptance, and safe result
> of this exact operation. Policy editing, Tenant/Site administration, Website
> content access, Tasks Hub access, coordinator membership, source visibility,
> and ordinary assignment authority neither imply nor are implied by it.
>
> The capability intentionally includes the minimum complete aggregate
> disclosure needed for informed consent: target mode and selected coordinator
> identities, exact Website-item count, and exact aggregate assignment add/
> preserve/end/already-current/proved-zero/currently-unverifiable counts. It
> grants no member identity, Site, locale, title, source body, D30/D34 context,
> visible/restricted split, qualification reason, per-person workload, sibling
> engagement, source action, task administration, or correction authority.
> Core creates no second partial-count mode. A Tenant that cannot trust someone
> with the complete aggregate blast radius does not grant the mutating
> capability.
>
> In the existing **Update current work** section, the trigger remains
> **Review current-work impact** and the title remains **Apply this setting to
> current Needs assignment work?** A scope block says **Across [organization] —
> all current Needs assignment work covered by this setting**, including work
> whose source detail the actor cannot open. A compact semantic summary keeps
> Website items separate from personal assignment additions, preserved/no-new-
> unread assignments, ended **Coordinator responsibility changed** assignments,
> already-current work, proved-zero work, and unverifiable no-effect work.
>
> The ordinary primary action remains **Apply setting to current work** and
> lane-only remains **Use Needs assignment only for current work**. The review
> is the single confirmation: no row grid, Site/locale filter, checkbox,
> selection, nested modal, typed phrase, remembered consent, destructive
> styling by default, or approximate count.
>
> Policy editors without application authority see only the quiet successful
> truth: **The setting was saved for new returned work. Existing work has not
> changed.** They see no disabled action, backlog existence/count, alert,
> badge, unread, role roster, or request-access dead end. Authorized holders
> receive a calm secondary action; **Not now** writes nothing and creates no
> nag.
>
> Complete empty/aligned says **Current work already uses this setting** with
> no confirmation. Indeterminate says **We couldn't check all current work.
> Nothing was started. The saved setting still applies to new work.** It offers
> **Check again**, never **Continue with visible work**. Accepted progress and
> aggregate result are persistent, route-addressable, resumable, accessible,
> and safe after navigation/lost response. The terminal heading is
> **Current-work update finished**, never task/source **Completed**; delayed
> Tasks Hub projection is reported separately.
>
> Application authority never qualifies a coordinator. Every member still
> re-proves D35's complete/zero/indeterminate route against each selected
> Party's active Tenant Assignment, exact Site/source visibility, and
> **Assign returned Website work** authority. Proved zero adopts the target
> basis without personal tasks and preserves the source lane. Indeterminate or
> materially changed impact releases nobody and changes no prior routing basis.
>
> Cohort acceptance is complete while D36 execution stays independently atomic
> per occurrence. Every sealed member reaches one durable terminal outcome and
> totals conserve the seal. One member failure cannot corrupt or roll back a
> sibling. Policy supersession or application-capability revocation stops
> uncommitted effects; committed routing remains immutable and correction uses
> a fresh policy/application.
>
> Browser writes are revoked. Composite same-scope relationships, immutable
> trusted attribution, member/effect uniqueness, terminal checks,
> operation-correct RLS `USING`/`WITH CHECK`, `ENABLE` plus `FORCE RLS`, least
> grants, hardened functions, and owner/service/RPC/worker/support/repair/
> export/cache/Realtime/AI parity preserve the same boundary. Inngest may page
> product-owned preparation or sealed identifier-only claims through the same
> commands; it owns no catalog, cohort, seal, authorization, routing, result,
> idempotency, or source truth.
>
> D37 adds no Site/locale/row subset, policy exception, coordinator fallback,
> source/correction/task-completion/content/public/Giving/finance effect,
> channel, reminder, date, SLA, employee score, generic bulk-task API, or
> automatic Mobilize behavior.
