## D52 — How late may an otherwise-current reminder occurrence remain useful?

### Why this needs your decision

Hope Mission's admitted request reaches its immutable D50 eligibility instant
on Monday. The policy stays On and the D43 request remains current, but a worker
outage or indeterminate D49 coordinator proof prevents source seal. Service
recovers Friday. D51 tells us exactly what happens if Off or another source end
wins, but neither occurred. Core still needs a terminal answer for whether this
same one occurrence may seal and release days late.

This is a usefulness boundary, not a due date, SLA, retry count, provider
timeout, task reminder, or delivery promise. It determines whether recovery
quietly omits a stale courtesy reminder or produces an outage catch-up burst.
D52 does not choose the numeric cadence/usefulness values, content, channels,
quiet hours, or activation. Those values must later come from the same finite,
code-owned activated-profile registry—not Tenant free text.

### Option 1 — finite code-owned usefulness window — recommended

Each admitted cadence choice also names one finite elapsed usefulness window
anchored to the immutable D50 eligibility instant. The same occurrence may seal
and cross a registered irreversible-effect boundary only before that window
ends and while every current source/recipient/authorization gate passes. At the
end it terminally skips; an indeterminate occurrence closes without guessing
zero, and no replay, restore, re-enable, route repair, or worker recovery can
catch it up. A boundary admitted in time may still finish/reconcile afterward
under D51.

**UX/impact:** avoids both exact-instant fragility and indefinite surprise.
Ordinary staff see no countdown or failure badge; the request and task remain
usable. The eventual timing disclosure can say **If Asym cannot create the
reminder soon enough, it skips it instead of sending it late.** Authorized audit
may show the precise source disposition.

### Option 2 — remain useful until the D43 request ends

The same occurrence may seal at any later time while the request remains
current, regardless of outage length.

**UX/impact:** minimizes omissions but can send a courtesy reminder weeks or
months after its intended moment and create a large recovery burst. It turns
request lifetime into an unbounded reminder retry window without evidence.

### Option 3 — exact-instant execution only

The occurrence must seal at the D50 instant (or an implementation-minimal
transaction boundary); any delay terminally skips it.

**UX/impact:** prevents stale attention but makes ordinary queueing, locks,
deploys, and brief outages silently eliminate reminders. It is operationally
brittle and would make scheduler precision a hidden product promise.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — a finite code-owned usefulness window.** It
keeps courtesy attention timely without making exact scheduling reliable or
allowing unbounded catch-up. It composes with D50's immutable elapsed clock,
D51's Off fence, D49's single occurrence, product-owned claims, and replaceable
Inngest execution while leaving evidence-based numeric values for the finite
cadence registry.

Which D52 usefulness model should Core record: **Option 1 — one finite code-
owned window then terminal skip/no catch-up**, **Option 2 — remain eligible
until the request ends**, or **Option 3 — exact-instant only**? You may amend any
option.

### D52 resolution

**Founder direction:** select the best current option after deep repository,
modern-practice, reliability, technical-debt, brittleness, and UX/UI review.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept Option 1 with required
amendments.**

The bounded model is the only proportionate choice. Request-lifetime
eligibility permits arbitrarily stale outage catch-up; exact-instant execution
makes ordinary queueing, locking, deploys, and brief outages silently erase a
valid courtesy occurrence. The unqualified option still needed a precise source
clock, a terminal outcome for indeterminate D49 proof, per-effect race rules,
provider-boundary treatment, and a deliberately quiet user experience.

The corrected decision is **one source-owned bounded usefulness interval**:

> Every later activated non-Off cadence profile is one closed,
> versioned code-owned pair of strictly positive finite whole-second values:
> `wait_for_seconds` and `useful_for_seconds`. D48/D50 pin the profile identity,
> revision, both values, and one immutable finite UTC
> `useful_until = not_before + useful_for_seconds` in the same successful D43
> source-creation transaction. The authoritative admission interval is
> half-open: `not_before <= claim_instant < useful_until`. The lower boundary is
> inclusive; at exact equality with `useful_until`, expiry wins. If a profile is
> expressed as days, one day is exactly 86,400 elapsed seconds. Missing,
> unsupported, nonpositive, nonfinite, contradictory, or overflowing optional
> evidence follows D48's typed safe non-admission path without blocking the
> valid D43 request.
>
> `claim_instant` is a fresh trusted primary-database instant captured after
> the relevant locks and proofs and immediately before the guarded source or
> effect transition. It is not a browser, application, worker, task, provider,
> analytics, Inngest, transaction-start, or optional physical-commit clock.
> Exact replay returns the original profile, instants, disposition, and semantic
> receipt. A later policy edit, time-zone change, restore, deployment, or retry
> never recomputes them.
>
> D49 source seal and every still-unreleased member/channel irreversible-effect
> admission must independently re-prove the interval, current D43 actionability,
> D48 admission, the pinned D51 cancellation epoch, the sealed D49 member, and
> all current assignment, authorization, privacy, consent, destination,
> readiness, suppression, and channel gates. D43 terminality and D51 Off are
> earlier independent source fences and remain decisive even while useful time
> remains. Expiry, Off, seal, release, and attempt races use one product-owned
> locked/CAS order; a losing whole command conflicts or returns the committed
> semantic result rather than guessing from timestamps.
>
> If D49 remains indeterminate when usefulness ends, the one occurrence closes
> terminally as **usefulness expired / no release**; that does not rewrite the
> historical proof as proved zero. A sealed proved-zero occurrence remains
> proved zero. A cohort sealed before expiry remains immutable source history,
> but every still-unreleased member/channel descendant must cross its own
> boundary before the same source ceiling. One released descendant never
> authorizes another, and no replay, restore, re-enable, route repair, later
> eligibility, or worker recovery can reopen, replace, or catch up expired work.
>
> An in-product reminder released before expiry remains truthful and follows
> ADR-0027's current D43 source-actionability presentation rules; D52 is an
> admission ceiling, not an automatic read, archive, retention, or presentation-
> end time. For email, **Prepared definitely unsubmitted** work is suppressible
> at expiry and protected material becomes unavailable under its existing
> Phase 17/6 deadline. If the pre-I/O **Submission may have begun** fence wins
> before expiry, that one admitted initial provider call may start, finish, or
> reconcile later only as the immediate bounded continuation of the same pre-
> I/O critical section with its envelope already prepared. A stalled or
> restarted process performs no call or retry. The independent outcome remains
> **None**, **Accepted**, **Definitely rejected**, or **Indeterminate**. After
> expiry, Core may reduce evidence from
> reconciliation/webhooks but may admit no new attempt, follow-up call, same-key
> follow-up, retry, replacement attempt, rekey, blind resend, recall claim, or
> changed-envelope replay.
>
> A future provider TTL or channel expiration can only narrow delivery further;
> it cannot own, extend, or prove the source usefulness boundary. Inngest may
> wake or reconcile identifiers, but owns no clock, transition, terminal state,
> uniqueness, idempotency, or business audit fact. The product database and
> source command remain authoritative.

The future complete Base Maia editor exposes no separate grace-period control
and no second hidden duration. Each visible cadence choice is one complete,
versioned timing profile; the selected outcome is described in the same compact
field help:

> **If Asym cannot create the reminder soon enough, it skips it instead of
> sending it late.**

Ordinary administrators and recipients see no countdown, expiry timestamp,
Due/Overdue or missed badge, catch-up button, task date, failure notification,
provider status, worker status, or terminal-state jargon. Expiry changes no D43
request, access, D44 responsibility, source-backed task, read state, or
permission. It creates no second task, task reminder, cancellation message,
successor occurrence, digest, escalation, or unread reset. A D42-authorized
audit/recovery view may distinguish localized source-created, eligible,
useful-until, cohort-sealed, release, terminal-skip, submission, and provider-
evidence facts without exposing protected prose or peer recipients.

This is modern practice without importing vendor defaults. FCM and Web Push
make message usefulness finite; APNs may still deliver after a provider
expiration; AWS bounds retry age; Microsoft Entra and Okta use explicit review
lifetimes but choose very different policies. Those systems support the need
for an explicit freshness fence, not a Core duration. Provider TTL remains an
optimization because it cannot retract or author product truth. Core's own
ADR-0016 already requires a missed reminder window to be skipped, never caught
up. D52 therefore defines the invariant and defers exact profile values to D53
and the existing D47 representative-evidence gate.

D52 is documentation only. It creates no runtime, schema, migration, OpenSpec
delta, profile, value, policy row, message key, plan, channel, provider request,
Inngest function, feature flag, telemetry, or UI now. Current Core still has no
D47–D52 access-review cadence runtime; existing task `remind_at`, contribution
age scans, scheduled jobs, and provider defaults remain migration evidence, not
authority or precedent.

## D53 — Which exact complete timing profiles may the future policy offer?

### Why this needs your decision

D52 makes a profile one indivisible pair: when the one courtesy reminder first
becomes eligible and how much longer it may still be created. It deliberately
does not provide numbers. If Hope Mission selects **After 7 days**, a hidden or
indefinite retry window would make that label misleading; exposing two separate
duration controls would be noisy and permit unresearched combinations.

Cross-product research does not supply a defensible universal number. Current
identity-governance products range from midway reminders inside a configured
review period to inactivity-based expiration, while transport products expose
TTL values from immediate discard to weeks. Those are different domains. The
existing D47 gate requires representative nonprofit/missions evidence before
any non-Off profile exists, so D53 must decide how exact pairs enter the closed
registry—not invent a popular-looking default.

### Option 1 — evidence qualifies each complete candidate pair; remain Off with no UI until one passes — recommended

The code registry initially contains only Off. Preregistered representative
research evaluates complete candidate pairs such as `(7 elapsed days,
7 elapsed days useful)`; a pair is added only after need, comprehension,
fatigue, accessibility, privacy, low-bandwidth, operational, and harm thresholds
pass. No Off-only placeholder setting ships. The first UI release may expose
one proven non-Off card plus Off; later evidence may add at most a small set
without changing old pinned revisions.

**UX/impact:** no speculative interval, no hidden grace choice, and the least
noisy editor. Users see only outcome-meaningful cards backed by evidence. The
trade-off is that the feature remains Off-only until research proves an exact
pair—which is already required by D47.

### Option 2 — standardize one pair now from cross-product convention

Choose one fixed pair now—for example reminder eligibility after seven elapsed
days with seven further elapsed days of usefulness—and validate it during
rollout.

**UX/impact:** fastest path to a simple two-card editor, but no reviewed Core or
representative ministry evidence currently supports those numbers. Production
would become the experiment, and the default could either nag too soon or
silently skip before part-time/international staff rhythms make action useful.

### Option 3 — let each Tenant choose wait and usefulness durations

Expose separate bounded duration selectors or custom numeric fields.

**UX/impact:** maximizes local control but creates a two-dimensional timing
matrix, invalid combinations, weak comparability, support burden, migration
debt, and a high chance that administrators mistake usefulness for a deadline
or delivery guarantee. It conflicts with D47's small code-owned choice set.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — evidence-qualify only complete timing-pair candidates that pass the
existing evidence gate, beginning with Off only.** This does not postpone a
known product answer; it prevents us from presenting an unsupported number as
one. Research evaluates a complete user-visible outcome, and the implementation
stays simple: one closed profile identity/revision, two immutable elapsed values,
one concise card only after later activation, and no free-form scheduler.

Which D53 registry rule should Core record: **Option 1 — remain Off until each
complete pair independently passes the D47 evidence gate**, **Option 2 — choose
one conventional pair now and validate in rollout**, or **Option 3 — Tenant-
configurable wait and usefulness durations**? You may amend any option.

### D53 resolution

**Founder direction:** Option 1 — remain Off until each complete pair passes
the D47 evidence gate, with deliberate resistance to overengineering and an
excellent, quiet Core-consistent UX/UI.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

The evidence-first direction is correct, but “the registry initially contains
only Off” would itself create the placeholder artifact D46/D47 prohibit, and
“passing research adds the pair” would collapse evidence qualification into
product activation. D53 therefore adopts the following minimal two-stage
boundary:

> **Current state is Off by absence.** Until at least one exact complete
> `(wait_for_seconds, useful_for_seconds)` pair passes D47 and then earns a
> separate complete activation decision, Core has no cadence registry entry,
> enum, table, row, policy head, message key, manifest row, Delivery Step,
> executor, schedule, feature flag, telemetry, setting, route, card, disabled
> option, empty state, documentation link, “coming soon” copy, beta badge, or
> other user-visible/programmatic placeholder. D43 requests, D44 routing/tasks/
> required initial attention, and D45 optional initial email remain unchanged.
>
> **The existing D47 gate is reused, not rebuilt.** D53 creates no research
> workflow engine, approval service, database evidence registry, committee role,
> admin console, periodic recertification job, scoring model, analytics product,
> or external research-vendor dependency. A candidate pair and its evidence
> live as version-controlled, privacy-minimized research/decision/release
> artifacts reviewed through the existing repository and product-governance
> process. Runtime never reads research files or computes whether evidence
> passed. D53 reuses D47's Access Product, UX Research, IAM/Security, Privacy,
> Accessibility, and Architecture review domains without creating a larger
> standing committee.
> Initial qualification and any deliberately opened rereview require the
> protocol's available source evidence. A lawful scheduled deletion of raw
> research data or an external source-link outage does not silently deactivate
> an activated profile or make release network-dependent: the durable local,
> privacy-minimized decision record and provenance are the release authority.
>
> **Evidence qualification is pair-specific and produces a proposal only.**
> Shared baseline evidence may be referenced when it remains current, in scope,
> and methodologically compatible, but every exact pair independently proves
> the full D47 root problem/no-build comparison, task-based behavioral outcome,
> meaning comprehension, fatigue/fairness/harm, accessibility, localization,
> international/mobile/low-bandwidth use, omission-versus-staleness trade-off,
> and D48–D52 technical feasibility under preregistered method-appropriate
> criteria. Every study candidate uses an immutable `research_candidate_id`,
> preregistered protocol version, exact pair, and tested semantic/interaction
> context—not a product profile identifier. A changed second, protocol version,
> material semantic/interaction meaning, source clock, or usefulness outcome is a new pair proposal. Meaning-preserving editorial,
> accessibility, and localization corrections follow ordinary content/a11y
> review and do not mint a candidate or profile. One pair's evidence cannot
> qualify another.
>
> Vendor defaults, founder or Tenant preference alone, support anecdotes,
> request-age distributions, opens/clicks, completion correlations, current
> staff response times, feature popularity, or a production A/B test cannot
> qualify a pair. Any critical deadline/access/automatic-decision misconception,
> material unmitigated fatigue/fairness/privacy/accessibility harm, missing
> cohort, contradictory evidence, or failed preregistered outcome keeps the pair
> absent. Thresholds may not be weakened after results are known. Research may
> observe authorized existing behavior and accessible prototypes; it may not
> send live reminders or create person-level performance surveillance.
>
> Passing D47 creates only one **evidence-qualified timing-pair proposal** for
> founder/product ratification. It does not create product truth, reserve a code
> profile identity, establish Tenant availability/rollout state, or grant
> permission to send. The exact qualified pair and tested semantic/interaction
> contract become the basis for an **activated access-review timing profile** only in a later
> reviewed activation package that also closes D46–D55-plus stable meaning,
> content, channel, authorization/RLS, privacy/retention, concurrency,
> idempotency, load, migration, mixed-version, kill/repair, OpenSpec, manifest,
> test, and release-evidence gates. That activation package assigns an immutable
> code-owned profile identity/revision and links it to the qualified research
> candidate. An evidence approval, code merge, feature
> flag, provider setting, or executor deployment cannot independently activate
> it.
>
> A future activated profile is an immutable code-owned identity/revision and
> exact whole-second pair. A Tenant policy command accepts only that identifier/
> revision; trusted Phase 12 code resolves the pair and D48/D50/D52 pin the
> exact profile identity/revision, pair values, and derived source facts—never
> the research artifact. Browser, API caller, import, support, database row, provider,
> worker, feature flag, experiment, or Tenant cannot submit or rewrite seconds.
> An activated profile is never silently edited, automatically expired, or
> reinterpreted because research ages. Material contrary evidence triggers a
> new reviewed ordinary-retirement or governed urgent-safety-withdrawal
> decision. Historical decoders and pinned
> source tuples remain; no deployment or rollback may mutate history or catch up
> excluded requests. Exact withdrawal and mixed-version sequencing must be
> proved in the later activation package before the first profile can ship.
> A governed urgent-safety withdrawal blocks new offering, selection, and source admission while
> preserving required compatibility decoders and truthful historical reads.
> Ordinary profile retirement is different: it blocks new selection/reselection
> only. A Tenant whose current selected policy head references that profile
> continues prospective D43 source admission until an authorized deliberate
> policy change, and the UI shows it in a separate read-only **Current setting**
> summary outside the selectable radio choices. Only a
> separately governed urgent safety withdrawal may stop current-head/new-request
> admission. Its authority, threshold, mixed-version sequencing, and Tenant UX
> must be resolved explicitly before the first profile activates; D53 does not
> smuggle that emergency policy into ordinary retirement.
>
> A later activation may use a temporary, owner-named release/kill control only
> after the pair and feature have already passed every product gate. That
> control may narrow availability, never qualify/select a pair or become source
> truth, and its creation must include removal criteria and an owner. D53 adds
> no dormant beta/experiment flag now.

The UX has two deliberately different states:

1. **Before activation:** nothing appears. People & access → Access requests
   remains complete without a reminder section, empty state, unavailable card,
   tooltip, upsell, or explanation of internal research. Hiding a nonexistent
   capability is intentional product clarity, not permission-by-obscurity;
   server/API/schema surfaces are equally absent.
2. **After at least one profile is fully activated:** the D44/D47-governed
   future route-addressable Base Maia **People & access → Access requests → Settings** form
   may add one compact **Courtesy reminders** fieldset containing only the
   Tenant's current effective **Off** choice—whether represented by absence or
   an explicit later policy revision—and fully activated profiles. Rendering Off
   does not seed a placeholder. Off may appear selected because it is the Tenant's actual effective state, not as a manipulative
   recommendation. Unqualified, unsupported, and experimental pairs are absent
   rather than disabled. A retired profile is absent from new choices and new
   selection APIs but remains truthfully visible in a separate read-only
   **Current setting** summary outside the selectable radio choices wherever the
   Tenant's policy head still references it.

The future fieldset uses the shared Base UI radio group/Field/Label primitives,
Maia/Zinc semantic tokens, and a vertical one-column layout. Each profile is one
plain-language choice such as **After [activated interval]**; the second
duration is not a second control. Persistent helper copy says:

> **This creates one courtesy reminder only if the request is still waiting. It
> does not set a due date or change access. If Asym cannot create the reminder
> soon enough, it skips it instead of sending it late.**

One available, collapsed-by-default **How timing works** disclosure contains
D48–D52 details and renders the selected exact pair in plain language, for
example: **Eligible after 7 elapsed days; if it cannot be created within the next
7 days, it is skipped.** It never exposes `wait_for_seconds`,
`useful_for_seconds`, or other internal field names. Opening it is optional;
its availability and exact-policy content are required. First
enable, re-enable, or non-Off profile change retains **Applies only to access
review requests created after you save. Requests already waiting aren't
included.** Selecting Off uses D51's inline consequence review. The form uses
an explicit Save/Cancel flow, fresh expected-head server validation, durable
semantic receipt, persistent programmatically announced success, and safe lost-
response recovery—never autosave, save-on-blur, a nested modal, toast-only
success, a current-work count/list, provider status, or evidence score.

Keyboard, fieldset/legend/label semantics, focus visibility and recovery,
programmatic errors/status, 320-CSS-pixel and 400-percent reflow, target size,
forced colors, reduced motion, long localization, RTL/CJK, mobile touch, and
low-bandwidth reconnect remain release gates. D53 selects no component
implementation and adds no UI now; the later implementation must reuse Core's
existing `base-maia`/Base UI primitives rather than introduce another library
or bespoke timing control.

Current official guidance supports this restrained shape without becoming Core
authority: GOV.UK recommends turning assumptions into research questions,
inclusive iterative rounds, and one clearly labelled choice at a time; USWDS
warns that defaults need evidence and that tile radios can create clutter;
WCAG requires visible labels/instructions without excessive information. Even
feature-flag vendors warn that unnecessary/stale flags create testing and
maintenance debt. These support D53's evidence, absence, and simple future
fieldset; they do not qualify a number, profile, component, or live experiment.

D53 is documentation only. It changes no runtime, schema, migration, OpenSpec,
profile, policy, request, grant, EffectiveAccess, D44 responsibility, task,
notification, message key, channel, provider object, workflow, feature flag,
telemetry, analytics, research store, or UI. Current Core still has no D43–D53
cadence runtime; existing finance/task reminders and current “coming soon” UI
are nonprecedents, not reusable admission or design patterns.

All 22 adversarial categories contain a material concern under an unqualified
“evidence first” rule. The corrected decision resolves them through 30
normative requirements, 120 continuous acceptance criteria, 120 classified
research assertions, 60 research acceptance criteria, explicit source/owner/
invariant/state/race/failure/authorization/privacy/UX/rollout matrices, and
named monitors with signal, threshold, owner, and response in:

## D54 — What in-product attention should the one courtesy occurrence create?

### Why this needs your decision

Suppose Hope Mission later activates one timing profile. A D44
coordinator already received and read the initial **Access review needs
attention** item and still has the same source-backed task. The request remains
pending when the separate courtesy occurrence crosses D50/D52. Core must decide
whether that occurrence creates new local attention, remains source-only for
possible external delivery, or mutates earlier engagement/task state.

This is not the content/channel decision yet. It decides the local presentation
identity and whether one request looks like duplicate work. ADR-0027 forbids
fabricating read/unread history, and ADR-0183 keeps Tasks Hub work separate from
reminder attention, but a separately admitted source occurrence could still
legitimately create one new notification item.

### Option 1 — one distinct reminder item, perceptually and programmatically grouped — recommended

Create one recipient-specific in-product reminder occurrence with its own
stable meaning/key and unread state, then group/correlate it with the existing
access-request attention so the Notification Center shows one coherent request
thread rather than duplicate work. Visual layout, reading order, accessible
names/descriptions, and programmatic relationships must convey the same grouping;
color or proximity alone is insufficient. Its safe title can be **Access review
is still waiting** and its action opens the exact currently authorized request.
Only the new occurrence may be unread. The original item's engagement/history
and the one Tasks Hub task remain unchanged.

**UX/impact:** provides dependable local attention even when every external
channel is Off or unavailable, preserves honest occurrence/engagement history,
and avoids a second task. It adds one real notification occurrence, so grouping,
copy, current authorization, and no-duplicate perceptual/programmatic treatment
must be exact.

### Option 2 — no new in-product item

Record the source occurrence but create no local notification. It could feed
only separately admitted future external steps.

**UX/impact:** minimizes Notification Center noise, but an optional external
channel could become the only reminder path. Tenants or recipients with email
Off/unready would receive no personal courtesy attention despite the qualified
source occurrence.

### Ruled out by governing decisions

Resetting/reopening the original item's unread state, changing its timestamp, or
adding priority/due/reminder state to the Tasks Hub task is not a viable D54
choice. It rewrites engagement/history and conflicts with ADR-0027 and ADR-0183.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — a distinct recipient-specific reminder item
that is perceptually and programmatically grouped with the existing request
attention and never creates or mutates a task.** This keeps in-product attention reliable, provenance
truthful, and the experience coherent without making external delivery a
fallback requirement.

Which D54 local-presentation rule should Core record: **Option 1 — one distinct,
perceptually and programmatically grouped reminder item**, or **Option 2 — no new
in-product item**? You may amend either option.

### D54 resolution

**Founder direction:** Option 1 — create one distinct reminder item and group it
coherently with the request's existing attention, with modern, dependable,
accessible UX and no brittle or duplicate-work model.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

The core direction is right, but the original phrase **grouped with the existing
request attention** assumed every recipient has a per-request initial item. D44
proves otherwise: a coordinator newly admitted to several already-pending
requests receives one multi-request
`access_request_responsibility_updated_v1` occurrence, not one hidden
`holder_access_review_requested_v1` child per request. Treating that aggregate
as a request thread would cross source episodes and contract meanings. D54
therefore records this narrower permanent rule:

> After—and only after—an exact timing profile passes D47/D53 and the complete
> D46–D55-plus activation package, one admitted D49 reminder occurrence may
> create at most one required local in-product item for each exact sealed member
> who still passes the current D43, D44, D48, D49, D51, D52, same-Tenant,
> assignment, Party, role/surface, source-visibility, authorization, and privacy
> gates at one atomic release boundary. It is a distinct recipient item with
> its own immutable occurrence and engagement—not a resend or mutation of the
> initial item, the responsibility aggregate, the D43 request, an access source,
> or the one ADR-0183 source-backed task.
>
> The future activation generation assigns and registers the stable reminder
> key and one reminder-specific source-applicability/end rule. D54 names or
> reserves neither. Product-database uniqueness binds the exact reminder source
> occurrence, sealed member, future registered local step/key, recipient Party/
> role/surface, and contract revision. Replay returns the same item; changed
> immutable meaning conflicts. Event, task, group, worker, realtime, and
> provider identifiers never own the business effect.
>
> Phase 17 derives one deterministic, rebuildable **Access-review attention
> group** from the exact Tenant, D43 request episode, recipient Party and Active
> Tenant Assignment, role/surface, privacy class, uninterrupted D44
> responsibility lineage, and grouping-contract revision. An eligible matching
> `holder_access_review_requested_v1` item may be its other child. The multi-
> request `access_request_responsibility_updated_v1` aggregate, another request,
> another responsibility lineage, recipient, role, surface, privacy boundary,
> or Tenant never joins. If no eligible initial child exists, the reminder is a
> complete one-child group; Core never fabricates, revives, clones, or backfills
> an initial item merely to make grouping appear complete.
>
> Children keep independent immutable availability, applicability, engagement,
> timestamps, and history. Only the new reminder child receives fresh unread
> state; every older child remains exactly as read or unread as it already was.
> The group stores no independent read, archive, source, request, task, grant,
> or access truth. Its badge contribution is the Boolean OR of currently
> authorized visible unread children and therefore at most one. Needs-attention
> membership derives from current actionable children even after they are read.
> Expanding, scrolling, sorting, viewport exposure, and realtime invalidation
> mark nothing read. Selecting the reminder's exact Review action may
> idempotently mark only that reminder child read; any broader explicit group
> operation must resolve to item-level expected-set writes so a concurrently
> arriving child remains unread or yields a truthful stale result.
>
> The future reminder uses ordinary **Attention** and
> `presentation.source_actionable_then_recent_90d@1`. Its protected meaning is
> only **this exact current access review is still waiting at the admitted
> courtesy point**. Safe presentation is **Access review is still waiting**,
> category **Access requests**, supporting copy **Review this request in People
> & access.**, and one typed authenticated action that reauthorizes the exact
> request. It makes no Due, Overdue, deadline, SLA, urgency, escalation, blame,
> ignored/no-response, awareness, delivery, access-change, or completion claim
> and reveals no holder/requester identity, reason, capability, group/grant/
> provenance, authority evidence, decision, location, ministry, or member-care
> fact.
>
> D43 resolution ends applicable initial and reminder children under their own
> source rules. D51 Off after a lawful local release ends only the reminder
> child's active/unread contribution; it does not end or rewrite the still-
> actionable initial item, request, task, responsibility, grant, or access.
> D52 bounds first release and does not shorten truthful released Recent
> history. Current assignment/authorization loss removes active and recent
> presentation immediately, and later restoration or re-admission never revives
> an old projection. A failed atomic item/group release publishes no orphan;
> repair retries only the same durable occurrence while every gate remains
> useful and current.
>
> D54 reuses ADR-0027's existing item/Attention Group model and Core's Base
> Maia/Base UI primitives. It creates no generic thread, conversation, grouping
> DSL, shared group-engagement row, custom feed/tree/listbox keyboard system,
> second notification system, or task feature. Visual grouping, DOM reading
> order, accessible names/descriptions, count, and state must agree through
> semantic list/section/heading/disclosure structure; color, proximity, avatar,
> dot, or timestamp alone is insufficient. Arrival is quiet: no focus theft,
> auto-open, modal, sound, vibration, urgent styling, assertive announcement, or
> toast-only history. Keyboard, visible focus, target size, screen reader,
> forced colors, 320-CSS-pixel/400-percent reflow, text spacing, reduced motion,
> localization/RTL/CJK, mobile touch, time-zone display, and low-bandwidth/
> reconnect behavior are release gates.
>
> D45's `profile.access_governance_attention@1` applies only to the two D44
> initial-email slots. The reminder does not inherit that Tenant switch or
> recipient preference. Its local item is required; every external reminder
> channel is absent/not-applicable until separately admitted and proved.

This is documentation only. Current Core still has no D43–D54 runtime, access-
request schema, reminder key, manifest/census row, profile, plan/step, renderer,
preference, group table, source-end registration, OpenSpec requirement, route,
worker, telemetry, or production notification UI. The hardcoded bell demo and
current contribution reminder code are migration inputs, not authority. D54
adds none of those artifacts now, and the Phase 17 census remains exactly 20
Target Live candidates and 20 Reserved keys.

The corrected decision is a modern pattern for Core because it combines
explicit semantic grouping with complete independent children, source-owned
actionability, derived rather than shared engagement, quiet arrival, and native
accessible relationships. Android's official grouping guidance likewise treats
children as complete notifications and recommends explicit rather than
automatic grouping; WAI requires visually conveyed relationships to be
programmatically determinable and disclosures to use ordinary button semantics.
Those sources support the interaction shape but do not override ADR-0027's
stricter Tenant/recipient/source/privacy boundaries.

All 22 adversarial categories contain a material concern under the unqualified
Option 1 wording. The amendments above resolve them through 30 normative
requirements, 120 continuous acceptance criteria, 120 classified research

## D55 — What should urgent safety withdrawal do to Tenant timing-policy heads?

### Why this needs your decision

Suppose one timing profile is fully activated and selected by many Tenants, but
new reviewed evidence later finds a material privacy, accessibility, fatigue, or
safety harm that cannot wait for ordinary retirement. D53 deliberately says no
profile may activate until urgent-withdrawal authority, mixed-version behavior,
history compatibility, and Tenant UX are settled. Core must now choose whether
the platform blocks the unsafe profile while preserving each Tenant's authored
selection or automatically writes Off for every affected Tenant.

This is different from ordinary retirement. Retirement removes a profile from
new choices while a Tenant's current selection continues; urgent withdrawal is
a harm-containment boundary. It must stop new effects immediately without
falsifying who changed Tenant policy or corrupting already truthful history.

### Option 1 — one monotonic platform safety fence; preserve Tenant heads — recommended

Publish one immutable, exact-profile safety-withdrawal generation that
immediately blocks new offering/selection, current-head D43 admission,
uncommitted D49 seal, and every unreleased local/external descendant. Do not
rewrite Tenant policy heads or silently select a replacement. Existing requests,
tasks, access, pinned decoders, source evidence, and lawfully released history
remain truthful. A released local reminder ends active/unread contribution
through its registered withdrawal rule and may retain authorized Recent/audit
history; external submission that may already have begun is reconciled and
never recalled or retried.

The settings surface shows the preserved current selection in a calm read-only
state such as **Unavailable for safety**, with concise impact text and the
ordinary explicit Save flow to keep Off or choose another independently
activated profile. It creates no Tenant-wide fanout, task, notification, inbox
alert, automatic substitute, or mass policy write.

**UX/impact:** fastest fail-safe containment with honest attribution and a clear
next action. Tenants can see what they had selected and deliberately choose the
replacement, while ordinary users simply stop receiving new reminder effects.

### Option 2 — automatically publish Off successor heads for every affected Tenant

Run a platform-authorized bulk mutation that writes a new Off policy head for
each Tenant selecting the withdrawn profile.

**UX/impact:** the stored Tenant state immediately says Off, but the platform
appears to have made a Tenant policy choice. It introduces O(Tenant) writes,
partial-batch recovery, races with concurrent Tenant saves, synthetic actor/
reason attribution, duplicate receipts, mixed-version ordering, and difficult
rollback if the safety determination changes. It also risks notification noise
if those mass changes are surfaced.

### Recommendation and exact question

**My recommendation is Option 1 — a monotonic exact-profile platform safety
fence that preserves Tenant heads and truthful history.** It makes the unsafe
behavior impossible immediately without impersonating Tenant intent, mass-
mutating rows, or choosing a substitute. The UI remains calm: explain the
unavailable current setting and let an authorized person deliberately save Off
or another proven profile.

When an activated timing profile must be withdrawn urgently for safety, should
Core choose **Option 1 — preserve each Tenant's selected head under one platform
safety fence**, or **Option 2 — automatically publish Off for every affected
Tenant**? You may amend either option.

### D55 resolution

**Founder direction:** Option 1 — use one platform safety fence while preserving
every Tenant-selected head.

**Disposition after adversarial review: Accept with required amendments.**

The permanent direction is correct, but the original wording left four
material gaps. First, the glossary incorrectly called the Tenant-selected head
the effective policy; D55 makes those separate facts. Second, **paused** or
**safety review** would falsely imply the exact revision may resume. Third, the
actuation authority/evidence contract is a separate blocking decision and cannot
be guessed. Fourth, released Recent presentation remains permissible only while
its independent decoder/renderer/privacy contract is still safe. D55 therefore
records this exact model:

> One future D56-qualified trusted platform command may append one immutable,
> globally applicable **Access-review timing-profile safety withdrawal** for one
> exact activated profile identity/revision. The primary product database owns
> the decision and linearization order. The future decision binds the exact
> revision, durable semantic operation identity, trusted commit generation,
> server-derived attribution, stable safe cause class, restricted incident/
> evidence reference and digest, privacy-safe rationale, and contract revision.
> Duplicate replay returns the same decision; changed target, cause/evidence, or
> authority conflicts.
>
> Withdrawal is subtract-only, append-only, and terminal. It cannot be updated,
> deleted, cleared, bypassed for one Tenant, imported, retargeted, or treated as
> a feature flag, ordinary retirement, Tenant Off, provider pause, workflow, or
> fallback selector. It cannot define, qualify, activate, select, or alter a
> profile. The exact revision never becomes executable again. A safe return
> requires a separately evidenced and fully activated successor revision plus
> each Tenant's deliberate selection; even identical elapsed values do not
> silently rehabilitate the withdrawn revision or old requests.
>
> The **Selected access-review timing-policy head** remains the Tenant-authored
> truth. The **Effective access-review cadence disposition** is derived:
>
> `effective = selected activated profile only when supported and not safety-withdrawn; otherwise Off`
>
> The platform does not publish Tenant Off successors, change actor attribution,
> choose a replacement, perform an affected-Tenant census, or fan out writes.
> Saving Off from a preserved withdrawn head is still a real D51 Tenant policy
> transition and advances its cancellation epoch even though effective behavior
> was already Off. Saving a successor uses the ordinary expected-head and
> prospective-only non-Off rules. Neither action is collapsed into a no-op.
>
> Every selection/reselection API, D43 cadence admission, D49 seal, plan compile,
> local release, and external irreversible-effect boundary must atomically
> re-prove that the exact profile revision is not withdrawn using current
> primary-product-database state after the relevant locks. Missing, stale,
> unreadable, malformed, contradictory, unknown, or mixed-version-unsupported
> safety proof fails closed for the optional reminder effect. The valid D43
> request, Access requests lane, initial D44 attention, and one source-backed
> task remain usable. Cache, client, Realtime, workflow, provider, support,
> feature-flag, and process-memory state can only invalidate, execute, or narrow;
> none authorizes.
>
> Fence-versus-selection and fence-versus-D43 each have two safe serialized
> outcomes. Fence-first rejects the profile or creates the valid request without
> cadence admission. Selection/admission-first preserves the selected head or
> pinned source tuple, but the committed withdrawal immediately derives
> effective Off and blocks D49 and every descendant that has not crossed its own
> registered irreversible boundary. A save receipt reports both selected and
> effective truth. No retry, successor, cache repair, restore, rollback, or
> policy edit catches up an old episode.
>
> Uncommitted D49 and every unreleased local/external descendant close under a
> stable safety-withdrawn/no-release result—not D49 proved zero, D52 expired,
> D51 Tenant Off, or D43 resolved. No request, access source, selected head,
> pinned source tuple, sealed-recipient evidence, task, engagement, or provider
> evidence is rewritten. A locally released D54 reminder immediately loses
> active/unread contribution without fabricated read/archive/dismissal or sibling/
> task/source mutation. Its immutable evidence remains; authorized non-unread
> Recent presentation is allowed only while the independent decoder/renderer/
> privacy contract remains safe. A shared presentation defect uses its own Phase
> 17 containment rather than being inferred from the timing fence.
>
> External work **Prepared definitely unsubmitted** is suppressed. If
> **Submission may have begun** committed first, the one already admitted frozen
> provider call may only complete/reconcile as the immediate continuation of that
> boundary. D55 authorizes no new call, retry, rekey, resend, replacement,
> fallback, follow-up, or recall claim.
>
> The future settings surface omits the withdrawn profile from new choices and
> save APIs but preserves one read-only **Current setting** summary:
>
> - **Selected:** `[profile label]`
> - **Status:** **Unavailable for safety**
> - **Effective:** **Off**
> - **Explanation:** **Courtesy reminders are off. Existing access requests,
>   tasks, and access are unchanged. This setting will not restart.**
>
> A secondary **Choose a new setting** action opens the ordinary fieldset with
> Off and other currently available activated profiles. Nothing is preselected;
> Save remains disabled until the authorized user deliberately chooses, and
> Cancel preserves the selected head. The withdrawn profile never appears as a
> disabled radio. There is no autosave, forced replacement, warning modal,
> incident detail, internal fence/head/revision jargon, affected-request list,
> task, bell item, email, banner, toast, mass Tenant alert, or claim that earlier
> provider submission was recalled.
>
> Visible and programmatic selected/effective facts, fieldset labels, errors,
> status, focus, keyboard, forced colors, 320-CSS-pixel/400-percent reflow, text
> spacing, screen reader, localization/RTL/CJK, mobile, and low-bandwidth/lost-
> response behavior must agree. Tenant-visible safe status is distinct from the
> restricted actor, reporter, evidence, incident, affected-Tenant count, and
> person-level research facts available only through D42-governed purpose.
>
> Future persistence denies Tenant/browser mutation, uses exact-profile
> uniqueness and restrictive deletion, derives attribution from trusted server
> context, and proves application authorization, database grants/RLS `USING`
> and `WITH CHECK`, functions/views, owner/`BYPASSRLS`/service/support/worker/
> restore parity, and no clear/bypass path. The O(1) withdrawal commit takes
> effect before asynchronous cleanup; every query/effect gate enforces it
> immediately. Compatible readers and fail-closed writers deploy before any
> profile becomes selectable, and rollback preserves the withdrawal and decoder.

The exact D56 authorization/evidence contract remains a pre-activation blocker.
D55 permits only the future command that D56 authorizes; it does not preselect a
role, quorum, automation trigger, or service principal. Tenant administrators,
`permissions.manage_grants`, support/impersonation, a `super_admin` role string,
workers, providers, feature flags, and possession of service-role credentials
alone do not satisfy it.

D55 is documentation only. Current Core has no D43–D55 cadence profile,
withdrawal state, selected/effective resolver, API, capability, key, plan/step,
schema/RLS, OpenSpec requirement, manifest/census entry, route, UI, flag, worker,
telemetry, automatic trigger, or reminder runtime. The current Web Studio
environment flags are deployment fallbacks; Eve's clearable global automation
switch is a separate bounded context whose persisted restriction/audit/fail-
closed principles—but not schema, JSON state, capabilities, actor-input RPC, or
control surface—are relevant. Counts remain exactly 20 Target Live candidates
and 20 Reserved keys.

This is consistent with current official practice without importing a conflicting
control plane. AWS recommends known, tested emergency levers with deterministic
criteria and graceful preservation of critical functions; D55 keeps the full
access-request workflow alive while disabling only optional reminder effects.
Google SRE emphasizes clear ownership, versioned change history, safe stop/
rollback behavior, and purpose-built configuration UX. Azure demonstrates why a
feature flag is useful for fast reversible operational toggles; D55 deliberately
uses a terminal product disposition instead because profile identity, history,
and Tenant authorship must not be reinterpreted by a mutable flag. NIST's current
incident-response guidance supports preparation, containment, evidence, and
recovery, while Core's source and privacy owners remain authoritative.

All 22 adversarial categories contain a material concern under the unqualified
Option 1 wording. The corrected decision resolves them through 30 normative
requirements, 120 continuous acceptance criteria, 120 classified research
assertions, 60 research acceptance criteria, complete source/owner/invariant/
lifecycle/race/failure/authorization/privacy/UX/rollout matrices, and named
monitors with signal, threshold, owner, and response in:
