### Ruthless synthesis and required order

Before recording D59, the corrected decision must separate brand from content,
Navigation, media, renderer, money/account, and release authority; define
explicit-copy/no-inheritance behavior; state that no-code means no staff runtime
code; and preserve the Phase 23 proposal as unmerged evidence with an explicit
Base Maia reconciliation gate. R1-R16 now do so.

The later consolidated Phase 24 spec/design must next define the exact complete
candidate compatibility rules, authorized commands/relationships, Site-aware
Web Studio journey, preview/public closure, locale/accessibility/asset proof,
cache and failure behavior, and global-config migration. It must consume—never
duplicate—whatever Phase 23 release contract is accepted first. Only after that
alignment may OpenSpec deltas and implementation tickets issue.

Implementation safeguards are one qualified resolver/projection; exact scope
and authority derived by the server; semantic values only; immutable qualified
assets; one pinned closure per response; preserved current public output on every
failed or ambiguous release; no private CMS/operational data in presentation; and shared
Base Maia/Base UI for the editor and standard interaction layer unless a
governing amendment explicitly says otherwise.

D59 deliberately does not freeze physical tables/collections/RPCs, DTCG or
other token serialization, exact fonts/colors/variants/limits, cross-Site copy,
scheduled design release, A/B testing/personalization, asset/CDN provider, cache
TTL, certified-package SDK/partner program, or a new approval workflow. Those
are either implementation evidence or separate decisions, not omissions in the
brand model.

### Release proof and justified operational signals

Release is blocked until production-shaped evidence proves two Tenants with at
least two Sites each; exact cross-scope denial; draft/preview/failure no-effect;
concurrent publish/restore/content/locale races; one complete old or new response
without mixed versions; unchanged Navigation/content/legal/payment/account/
message truth; safe asset/revocation/retirement paths; no platform/foreign
fallback; full keyboard/screen-reader/contrast/reflow/zoom/forced-colors/
reduced-motion/no-JS/images-disabled/long/RTL/CJK/mobile behavior; recognizable
giving and exact checkout/account handoffs; hostile input/CSP/preview/cache
tests; and measured performance on representative routes/devices/networks.

| Signal                                                | Threshold                                                                                           | Owner                          | Required response                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `site_brand_scope_mismatch_total`                     | Any event                                                                                           | Security + Public Runtime      | P0 contain the affected scope, preserve/restore the last proved generation, inspect resolver/cache/assets, and re-prove affected Sites.         |
| `site_presentation_unknown_or_mixed_generation_total` | Any event                                                                                           | Public Site Release            | Stop rollout/activation, preserve current heads, reconcile exact receipts/generations, and repair only through a proved successor.              |
| `site_presentation_required_asset_missing_total`      | Any current-generation event                                                                        | Public Media + Site Runtime    | Contain affected presentation, use only the prequalified safe path, and replace through an immutable successor after retained-reference review. |
| Public Site Core Web Vitals                           | Mobile or desktop p75 exceeds LCP 2.5 s, INP 200 ms, or CLS 0.1 over the release observation window | Web Platform + Site Experience | Stop cohort expansion, attribute to the exact version/package/generation/assets, then optimize or restore by successor.                         |

The performance threshold uses the current
[Core Web Vitals](https://web.dev/articles/vitals) “good” p75 boundaries; the
implementation must reverify them before freezing release evidence.

Accessibility, tenant isolation, legal/payment truth, and release correctness are
release gates, not monitor-and-tolerate risks.

### Modern evidence and repository reconciliation

- [Shopify theme design guidance](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/best-practices/design)
  recommends minimum necessary settings, predictable flexibility, robust
  content handling, mobile-first performance, and variations rather than
  duplicate components. Its
  [color guidance](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/best-practices/design/color-system)
  favors small purpose-named palettes and accessible foreground/background
  relationships.
- [Payload Versions](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/overview),
  [Drafts](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/drafts), and
  [Preview](https://payloadcms.com/docs/admin/preview) provide useful private
  authoring mechanisms without making drafts public; Core still owns the
  release and authorization contract.
- [WordPress Site Editor](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/site-editor/)
  demonstrates whole-Site identity/styles, preview, fan-out explanation,
  revisions, and reset. Its custom-CSS capability is not imported because it
  conflicts with Core's safety and upgrade boundaries.
- [Shopify accessibility guidance](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/best-practices/accessibility)
  and [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) support logical structure,
  keyboard/focus, contrast, non-color meaning, reflow, resizing, alternatives,
  and mobile proof.
- [OWASP File Upload guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html)
  supports allowlisted decoded types/signatures, generated names, safe storage,
  size limits, and image rewriting rather than trusting filenames or MIME
  claims.
- [USWDS role-based theme tokens](https://designsystem.digital.gov/design-tokens/color/theme-tokens/)
  and the stable
  [DTCG 2025.10 format](https://www.w3.org/community/reports/design-tokens/CG-FINAL-format-20251028/)
  validate semantic roles/typed values but do not justify a new token-format
  dependency in D59.
- Repository OpenSpec says CMS owns public presentation, public websites are
  Tenant-branded/highly customizable, and public/authenticated surfaces remain
  separate. Merged UI rules require Base Maia/Base UI and prohibit app-local
  palettes/component forks. Current `siteId: null`, hard-coded GiveHope config,
  global navbar/metadata, visible Asymmetric.al footer, and legacy **Global
  Branding** prototype are current migration facts, not desired behavior.
- [Phase 23 PR #1340](https://github.com/Asymmetric-al/core/pull/1340) was
  verified open, unmerged, and blocked on 2026-08-30. Its D9/D10 proposal is
  carefully bounded but not governing, and its custom Presentation Package lane
  must be reconciled with the merged UI constitution before adoption.

### Documentation and implementation status

D59 is recorded in the glossary, ADR-0030, ADR-0186, Phase 2, Phase 5, Phase
17, the Web Studio living spec, the roadmap, and this decision log. It changes
no runtime, schema, migration, provider, deployment, Phase 23 proposal, or
OpenSpec in this grooming step. R1-R16 are the exact future spec language; the
consolidated Phase 24 OpenSpec delta and cross-PR reconciliation are mandatory
before implementation tickets.

## D60 — Compact read-only message readiness in the Site workspace

### Founder direction

**Option 1 — compact read-only readiness in the Site workspace.** The founder
selected contextual readiness inside the Site journey while requiring modern,
low-noise UX and no duplicate message configuration, brittle status logic, or
new technical debt.

### Adversarial disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The placement is correct, but the raw
three-label proposal would flatten Phase 17's approved-fallback result, hide
asynchronous observation and unavailable-source conditions, and tempt future
code to treat a cached badge as activation authority. D60 must be a disposable,
role-filtered presentation of Phase 17 truth—not a new Site readiness concept.

Record this corrected decision:

> **D60-R1 — Scope and authority.** Each exact Tenant × environment × Site
> setup/readiness view may show one quiet, read-only **Messages** summary for
> currently applicable Site capabilities and Site Locales. It is a disposable
> projection of Phase 17's authoritative Tenant message readiness, not a
> message setting, catalog, publication, provider source, readiness source,
> task, audit record, or activation authority. Phase 24 stores and edits none
> of the underlying facts.
>
> **D60-R2 — One owner and one derivation.** Phase 17 remains the sole owner of
> message contracts and lifecycle, publications and compatible fallback,
> locale activation/readiness, Brand Kits and Role Layouts, Delivery Plans,
> Tenant-owned Resend connection and proof, Sender Profiles, reply
> destinations, repair, delivery evidence, and provider reconciliation. Phase
> 17 derives one provider-neutral safe projection. Phase 24 never reconstructs
> it from current compatibility fields such as `connected`, `sendReady`,
> scalar verification flags, a deliverability score, template publication,
> provider-domain state, test-send success, or historical delivery outcome.
>
> **D60-R3 — Applicable set and account boundary.** Phase 17 includes only Live
> contracts that the exact Site's current or candidate capabilities can invoke
> and only the relevant Site Locales. Reserved, Retired, optional-disabled,
> unrelated Tenant-wide, platform-owned, other-Site, and speculative future
> contracts are omitted rather than counted as Site setup debt. Tenant-wide
> sign-in, claim, verification, recovery, and donor-account messages remain in
> the Tenant Donor Portal/System Messages context established by D57-D58. An
> organization-wide prerequisite appears in a Site summary only when an exact
> Site capability genuinely depends on it, and is labelled **Organization-wide**.
>
> **D60-R4 — Preserve source truth; add only honest presentation states.** Each
> applicable requirement preserves Phase 17's source-owned `Ready`, `Uses
compatible fallback`, or `Needs attention` result. The Site presentation
> adds **Status unavailable** only when it cannot prove one current complete
> projection. **Checking** may describe an active verification or rebuild, and
> **Setup needed** may explain a known `Needs attention` cause, but neither is
> a competing domain lifecycle. Missing, stale, partial, source-mismatched,
> unavailable, incompatible, or unknown evidence never renders `Ready`.
>
> `Ready` never means submitted, provider-accepted, delivered, inboxed, read,
> understood, legally complete, permanently deliverable, or that every Tenant
> message is translated. `Uses compatible fallback` is a truthful usable
> outcome, not silently green exact-locale coverage and not automatically a
> repair incident.
>
> **D60-R5 — Compact roll-up and exact consequence.** The healthy summary is
> one subdued line, for example **Messages · Ready — Receipts and other system
> messages required by this Site are ready.** Exceptions are grouped by cause
> and progressively disclosed; D60 creates no Site × locale × contract matrix.
> Each non-Ready item names the human outcome, Site/organization and locale
> scope, exact affected capability, responsible owner, whether that capability
> is blocked, evidence age where useful, and one safe next action. It uses
> human language such as **French giving receipts**, not template keys,
> provider objects, internal tables, or dependency-graph jargon.
>
> Example: **French giving receipts · Uses fallback — Currently sends the
> approved English receipt. French Giving remains available under this
> contract.** A blocker says **French giving receipts · Needs attention —
> French Giving cannot activate until the protected receipt is ready.** A
> source failure says **Message status · Unavailable — Current readiness could
> not be confirmed; no settings changed.**
>
> **D60-R6 — Freshness, completeness, and concurrency.** Every projection
> carries exact Tenant, environment, Site/applicability scope, capability and
> locale/purpose, Phase 17 catalog/activation generation, observed readiness-
> evidence generation or version, stable reason/owner codes, trusted evaluated
> time, and a code-owned typed destination when allowed. It is rebuildable and
> non-authoritative. A newer owner generation, incomplete member set, expired
> proof, event gap, source disagreement, unknown schema, or failed rebuild
> invalidates the favorable presentation. An older or late response can never
> overwrite a newer result or restore `Ready`.
>
> Exact numerical freshness limits belong to Phase 17 provider/design evidence,
> not a magic duration frozen by D60. The implementation must nevertheless
> define and prove a bounded self-healing read/reconciliation path. Loading
> says **Checking message status** rather than presenting an unqualified old
> green badge.
>
> **D60-R7 — Activation independence.** D6 remains controlling: core public
> Site activation proves core public readiness only. The summary never blocks
> or activates the Site, a Site Locale, Giving, donor account, or any other
> capability. Each capability owner declares its exact Phase 17 dependency and
> re-proves current source evidence inside its own authorized activation
> command. A badge, cache entry, projection, deep link, task, provider status,
> or prior `Ready` result is never accepted as that proof. A core Site may stay
> live while an exact message-dependent optional action is omitted, replaced
> honestly, or unavailable.
>
> Public-Site-locale and Phase 17 message-locale activation stay separate
> authorities. The Site journey may show current coverage, safe fallback, and
> exact blockers and then hand off to the separately authorized System Messages
> action; it never silently activates a message locale or blocks public content
> for unrelated, optional, future, or compatible-fallback messages.
>
> **D60-R8 — Typed navigation and reauthorization.** An actionable item may
> carry one allowlisted, server-resolved destination descriptor for the exact
> current System Messages context. It is not an arbitrary URL and never carries
> authority. Phase 17 independently derives Tenant/scope, reauthorizes, and
> reloads current truth. If the issue was resolved, replaced, or became
> inapplicable, the destination shows that current state rather than reviving
> stale work. A viewer without the needed Phase 17 permission sees a safe
> existing handoff such as **Ask an organization administrator**, not restricted
> detail, a disabled control, a 403 dead end, or a newly invented approval flow.
>
> **D60-R9 — Tenant, authorization, and privacy safety.** The server derives
> active Tenant, environment, Site, viewer, and authorization epoch from trusted
> context on every read. Browser filters, Site/locale ids, cache keys, deep-link
> parameters, or provider metadata cannot select ownership or authorization.
> Authenticated responses/client state are scoped by current Tenant, viewer
> authority, environment, Site, applicability, and source generation and are
> never public or shared across viewers.
>
> The safe projection contains no message body/subject, recipient or Party/
> contact fact, credential/API-key hint, sender or reply mailbox where
> restricted, DNS record/challenge, provider account/message id or payload,
> complaint/bounce identity, suppression evidence, private Site/locale, hidden
> contract inventory, or sensitive missionary/member-care information.
>
> **D60-R10 — Database and privileged-path parity.** D60 does not require a new
> table. If later design persists a rebuildable projection, relationships and
> keys are tenant-aware; source evidence is immutable/versioned; current-scope
> reads are indexed; Tenant/Site/actor attribution is server-derived; deletes
> are restrictive; and browser mutation is absent. Every view, function, RPC,
> realtime subscription, cache, background rebuild, and service-role path
> enforces the same scope and permission boundary, including equivalent `USING`
> and `WITH CHECK` protection wherever a Tenant-scoped mutation exists. An
> allowed write cannot move a row into a forbidden Tenant/Site state.
>
> **D60-R11 — Provider and failure distinction.** Phase 17 decides whether
> domain/credential/webhook/provider evidence represents incomplete Tenant
> setup, a Tenant repair, platform/provider disruption, protection pause, or an
> indeterminate outcome. A provider outage is never mislabeled as **Connect
> Resend**, and provider verification is evidence rather than permanent
> business readiness. The summary names the accountable owner and may say **No
> action needed from you**. Timeout, partial response, authorization loss,
> incompatible schema, missed invalidation, or source outage yields **Status
> unavailable** with a safe retry/current destination; it does not mutate Phase
> 17, take down the public Site, or retain false green.
>
> **D60-R12 — UX and accessibility.** The card follows the shared Mission
> Control/Web Studio Base Maia/Base UI shell. Status text and an icon carry
> meaning in addition to color; the status tag is noninteractive and visually
> distinct from its descriptive action. Healthy detail is collapsed, problems
> are exception-first, and there is one next action rather than a checklist or
> provider console. The experience proves keyboard/touch, visible focus,
> screen-reader name/description, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 200% zoom/text spacing,
> long localized language/capability names, RTL/CJK/bidi, slow/offline/loading/
> empty/not-applicable/error/permission-restricted states, and stable focus.
> User-initiated or relevant in-session status changes use polite status
> semantics; unchanged background refreshes do not repeatedly announce or
> steal focus. Repair persists after refresh and never relies on a toast alone.
>
> **D60-R13 — Operations and observability.** Phase 17 retains durable
> readiness, publication, connection, provider, and repair history. D60 records
> only safe projection diagnostics and ordinary view/navigation audit where
> repository policy requires it. Metrics/logs are low-cardinality and keyed to
> environment, scope kind, capability/contract class, result, reason class,
> source generation, and lag—not Tenant/site names, domains, addresses,
> message content, recipients, provider payloads, or sensitive ministry facts.
> Rebuild and invalidation are scoped; the Site page never calls Resend or
> recomputes every contract synchronously.
>
> **D60-R14 — Migration and decision boundary.** Current `connected`,
> `sendReady`, scalar verification flags, and percentage deliverability score
> are transitional migration evidence, never backfilled as Phase 17 `Ready`.
> Mixed readers accept an understood complete projection version or show
> **Status unavailable**; rollout shadow-compares by Tenant cohort before legacy
> readers retire.
>
> D60 authorizes no duplicate System Messages page, message/editor setting,
> sender/domain credential field, provider integration/poller/webhook, test
> send, manual override, activation gate, mutable readiness Boolean, database
> technology, event bus, cache technology, task, notification, reminder,
> escalation, or implementation. The consolidated Phase 24 design must consume
> Phase 17's safe generated projection and carry D60's exact proof before
> implementation tickets issue.

### Current behavior, intended behavior, and permanent path

| Layer               | Verified current/proposed state                                                                                                                                    | D60 intended behavior                                                                                 | Permanent path                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Staff product       | Current admin routes expose a separate Email Studio and Resend integration; the complete System Messages workspace is planned, not shipped.                        | One quiet Site summary with one current owner action.                                                 | Phase 17 ships the authoritative workspace/projection first; Phase 24 consumes it.                                |
| Connection source   | `tenant_email_settings.validation_snapshot` is the preferred current source, while legacy scalar fields remain synchronized compatibility data.                    | No current scalar becomes contract/Site/locale readiness.                                             | Complete Phase 17's generated provider-neutral readiness projection and retire legacy readers after shadow proof. |
| Current UI          | The Resend settings UI can say **Connection Active**, expose `sendReady`, and show a synthetic percentage deliverability score.                                    | Plain exact result, impact, responsible owner, freshness, and action; no score or vague Active badge. | Do not adapt the current card into D60 by renaming its coarse fields.                                             |
| Readiness semantics | Phase 17 already separates contract readiness (`Ready`, `Uses compatible fallback`, `Needs attention`) from connection posture, publication, and delivery outcome. | Preserve those distinctions and add only an unavailable presentation for an unprovable projection.    | Phase 17 owns one current versioned derivation; the Site owns placement only.                                     |
| Site workspace      | No shipped `cms.sites` or Site setup/readiness product exists.                                                                                                     | Future Phase 24 Site setup consumes a small safe projection.                                          | Build after the Site model and Phase 17 contract exist; no temporary duplicate schema.                            |
| Activation          | D6 already keeps core website activation separate from Giving, messages, aliases, and additional locales.                                                          | Message issues affect only an exact declaring capability.                                             | The capability command re-proves Phase 17 directly; the Site card never authorizes.                               |

Current behavior is migration evidence, not a reusable message-readiness model.
The permanent path is one source-derived read projection, not a renamed
`sendReady` Boolean.

### Staff journeys

1. **Healthy.** Nina opens **Hope Relief · relief.hope.org**. Site setup shows
   one quiet **Messages · Ready** line. Details stay collapsed; **Open System
   Messages** appears only if her current role permits it.
2. **Approved fallback.** French public content is enabled. The summary says
   **Uses fallback** and explains **French giving receipts currently use the
   approved English receipt**, including whether French Giving is allowed.
3. **Exact blocker.** A protected French receipt is required and missing. The
   row says **Needs attention · Blocks French Giving** and offers **Review
   French receipt message**. The public French website can still publish under
   D6; Phase 17 reauthorizes the action.
4. **Checking or unavailable.** During active verification the copy says
   **Checking** without pretending success. A stale, incomplete, or unavailable
   source says **Status unavailable — Current readiness could not be
   confirmed; no settings changed**, and never leaves old green in place.
5. **No message permission.** A Site manager sees only the safe local
   consequence and **Ask an organization administrator**. They do not see
   sender/domain details, hidden contracts, provider evidence, or a broken
   privileged link.

### Twenty-two-category adversarial result

Every category has a material concern under the unqualified option. D60-R1-R14
retain the selected contextual UX while preventing a second message product or
an unsafe green badge.

Phase 17 already owns a complete System Messages workspace. Option 2 hides relevant blockers; Option 3 duplicates authority. | **Narrows, does not invalidate.** R1-R3 and R5: one exception-first contextual projection containing only current applicable dependencies; no second catalog/editor.                                |

### Ruthless synthesis and required order

Before D60 can be recorded, the decision must preserve Phase 17's compatible-
fallback result, distinguish a known adverse result from an unprovable read,
exclude nonapplicable and Tenant-account contracts, keep D6 activation
independence, and define current-source/authorization behavior. R1-R14 now do
so; no further founder choice is needed for those safety consequences.

The consolidated Phase 24 spec/design must next define the exact safe projection
schema and version negotiation; Phase 17-owned applicability and reason/owner
vocabulary; generation closure, invalidation, bounded freshness, current-state
reconciliation, and rebuild; role-filtered Site summary and typed destinations;
capability activation reproof; migration away from coarse connection readers;
and the complete release matrix. OpenSpec updates and implementation tickets
must wait for that coherent design rather than implement the current
`sendReady` surface as an interim shortcut.

Implementation safeguards are one source-derived provider-neutral projection;
trusted exact scope; current authorization on every read and destination;
newer-generation-wins; unavailable-on-unprovable; no cross-viewer cache; no
message/provider mutation in Site; no Site activation authority; and one quiet
exception-first Base Maia/Base UI presentation. These are requirements, not a
new platform.

D60 deliberately does not freeze a table/view/RPC, event or cache technology,
route component, freshness duration, provider polling interval, exact visual
layout, new permission taxonomy, campaigns/newsletters/support replies, future
channels, task/notification/reminder/escalation behavior, or provider health
dashboard. Those are either owned elsewhere or require evidence, not missing
pieces of this decision.

### Release proof and justified operational signals

Release is blocked until production-shaped evidence proves all of the
following:

- exact `Ready`, `Uses compatible fallback`, `Needs attention`, active
  **Checking**, and **Status unavailable** presentation without inventing a
  second readiness lifecycle;
- zero/one/many applicable contracts; required/optional-disabled;
  Reserved/Live/Retired; Site/organization/platform scope; exact and partial
  locale coverage; and changed applicability during the read;
- Tenant-wide donor-account contracts absent from Site rows, with a genuine
  organization-wide Site dependency safely grouped and labelled;
- core Site/public-locale activation succeeding with unrelated message issues,
  exact capability activation rejecting missing current Phase 17 proof, and no
  activation command trusting the Site projection;
- source generation change, incomplete member set, event loss/reorder/
  duplication, rebuild, stale and partial responses, late older response,
  cache eviction, Tenant switch, permission loss, Site reassignment/retirement,
  provider outage/recovery, and mixed reader versions;
- authorized exact destination, unauthorized safe handoff, already-resolved or
  inapplicable destination, wrong-Tenant/Site denial, IDOR, and open-redirect
  negatives;
- no body, subject, recipient, address, credential hint, DNS record/challenge,
  provider id/payload, suppression identity, hidden contract, private locale,
  or sensitive ministry fact through UI, API, cache, realtime, logs, telemetry,
  exports, or support tooling;
- no Site-owned message mutation, provider poll, readiness reducer, manual
  override, duplicate configuration column, task, or notification;
- keyboard, touch, visible focus, screen reader, non-color status, stable
  announcements, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 200% zoom/text spacing, long localized
  labels, RTL/CJK/bidi, slow/offline/loading/empty/error/permission states, and
  refresh-persistent recovery; and
- representative multi-Tenant, multi-Site, multi-locale load proving bounded
  latency, scoped invalidation, and no provider call or full contract graph on
  Site-page reads.

| Signal                                                               | Threshold                                                                               | Owner                                 | Required response                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `site_message_readiness_false_ready_total`                           | Any `Ready` rendered from stale, incomplete, mismatched, or source-disagreeing evidence | Phase 17 + Site Experience + Security | P0 disable the affected projection path, show **Status unavailable**, inspect affected capability activations, repair generation/invalidation, and re-prove before restoring. |
| `site_message_readiness_cross_scope_disclosure_total`                | Any event                                                                               | Security                              | P0 revoke the response/cache path, evict affected data, assess disclosure, repair Tenant/Site/viewer scoping, and restore only after negative proof.                          |
| `capability_activation_used_readiness_projection_as_authority_total` | Any event                                                                               | Owning capability + Architecture      | P0 stop the activation path, reconcile affected activations from Phase 17 source evidence, replace projection trust with direct reproof, and add a permanent guard.           |
| `site_message_readiness_generation_gap_total`                        | Any missing/conflicting generation or incomplete applicability closure                  | Phase 17 Projection Operations        | Mark affected scopes **Status unavailable**, rebuild from source, inspect event delivery/versioning, and prevent `Ready` until closure matches.                               |
| `site_message_readiness_wrong_destination_total`                     | Any destination resolving another Tenant/Site, arbitrary URL, or unauthorized detail    | Security + Phase 17 UX                | Disable the producer, inspect safe diagnostics, repair typed binding/authorization, and re-prove every destination class.                                                     |

Phase 17 provider/domain drift, preparation failures, webhook lag, suppression,
and delivery incidents remain Phase 17 monitors. D60 consumes their safe
reason/owner consequences and does not duplicate them.

### Modern evidence and repository reconciliation

- Repository Phase 17 already defines scope-aware **Tenant message readiness**
  and exact contract-locale results of `Ready`, `Uses compatible fallback`, or
  `Needs attention`; it separately defines six connection postures and forbids
  deliverability scores. D60 therefore preserves those meanings instead of
  importing a competing external enum.
- Current [Resend domain verification](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/domains/verify-domain)
  is asynchronous and begins at `pending`; its
  [domain-verification events UX](https://resend.com/changelog/domain-verification-events)
  uses a timeline, specific record/failure/fix, and capability-aware partial
  states. That supports explicit checking and one precise owner action, not an
  indefinite spinner or aggregate green badge.
- [AWS SES email-identity evidence](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/APIReference-V2/API_GetEmailIdentity.html)
  separates verification status from sending readiness and exposes current
  check/success evidence and failure reasons. Provider proof is therefore only
  one input to business readiness.
- [Shopify localization status](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/localization-and-translation)
  distinguishes translated, outdated after the source changes, and
  untranslated content, including notifications. A previously favorable
  locale result cannot remain green across a source revision.
- The official [Kubernetes API conventions](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md)
  establish the useful modern read-model precedent: the owner writes observed
  status, `Unknown` is explicit, and observed generation identifies stale
  results. Core adopts the invariant, not Kubernetes' wire format or
  infrastructure.
- [Microsoft's materialized-view pattern](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/architecture/patterns/materialized-view)
  supports a rebuildable read projection while warning that it may lag its
  source. D60 therefore requires explicit freshness and never makes the view a
  write authority.
- [GOV.UK status-tag guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/tag/)
  says tags are noninteractive, descriptive, visually distinct from buttons,
  and should use the smallest useful status set. D60 keeps the status separate
  from its action and hides nonapplicable/healthy detail.
- [WCAG status-message guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/status-messages)
  and [WCAG 2.2 use of color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)
  require programmatically determinable status changes without focus movement
  and meaning beyond color. D60 applies those requirements without creating a
  chatty live region.
- [Vercel custom-domain setup](https://vercel.com/docs/domains/set-up-custom-domain)
  shows the broader Core-consistent pattern of current status, exact required
  action, and asynchronous readiness; provider diagnostics stay with the owner
  rather than being copied into every consumer surface.

External practice strengthens the selected contextual read projection, but it
does not override Phase 17's governing vocabulary, D6 activation boundary, or
Core's Base Maia/Base UI constitution.

### Documentation and implementation status

D60 is recorded in the glossary boundary, Phase 17, the Web Studio living spec,
the Phase 24 roadmap, and this decision log. It changes no runtime, schema,
migration, provider configuration, message publication, activation, task,
notification, or OpenSpec in this grooming step. R1-R14 are the exact future
spec language; the consolidated Phase 24 OpenSpec delta and implementation
design must carry the projection, authorization, freshness, activation, UX,
migration, and proof contracts before tickets issue.

## D61 — Eligible local-currency suggestion with donor control

### Founder direction

**Option 1 — eligible local suggestion with donor control.** The founder
selected local-first presentment for a multi-currency Site while requiring the
best donor and staff UX, modern practice, reliable Stripe behavior, and no
brittle provider coupling or technical debt.

### Adversarial disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The interaction pattern is modern and
useful, but it is unsafe as a thin currency selector. The current runtime
hardcodes USD, accepts arbitrary caller currency, multiplies every amount by
100, uses USD-specific fee/formatting logic, has no Site or exact connected-
account qualification, and has no implemented cart. D61 must become a server-
authorized, exponent-correct, provider-neutral selection contract with a hard
rollout fence.

Record this corrected decision:

> **D61-R1 — Selection only.** D61 selects the initial donor-facing **Donor
> Presentment Currency** for one current gift intent. It does not activate a
> currency, choose Tenant/Legal Entity/merchant/Settlement Account Binding,
> calculate or guarantee FX, select settlement/payout/bank/accounting/Field
> Account currency, retain a foreign balance, change Stripe topology, or
> establish donor residence, tax, receipt, sanctions, or legal jurisdiction.
>
> **D61-R2 — Deterministic precedence.** For one pristine valid giving intent,
> resolution is: an explicit choice already recorded on that intent; one
> current eligible **Donor Currency Suggestion**; the Site's explicit default
> when currently qualified; otherwise an explicit choice from remaining
> qualified currencies. Core never chooses arbitrary or implicit USD. When no
> currency qualifies, Giving is unavailable with a truthful Tenant-branded
> state while the public Site remains available.
>
> If the Site default is unavailable but other qualified currencies exist,
> Core shows **Choose a currency to continue** rather than silently promoting
> another default. The current nonempty cart's frozen currency outranks every
> new Site/location suggestion and is revalidated, not replaced.
>
> **D61-R3 — Location is a disposable suggestion.** Use at most one trusted,
> request-scoped ISO country hint supplied through the deployment ingress and a
> versioned platform-owned current-tender mapping. It returns at most one
> candidate. Missing, unknown, disputed, multi-currency, unsupported, stale, or
> untrusted input produces no suggestion and falls through R2. Staff do not
> maintain country rules.
>
> D61 requests no device/GPS location, makes no third-party geolocation call,
> trusts no browser language/locale/query/header as authority, and adds no raw-
> IP/country donor profile, cookie, durable preference, marketing segment, or
> location record. Existing separately governed fraud/security logging is not
> widened. Location never changes Site, locale, content, currency eligibility,
> merchant, payment route, or compliance decision.
>
> **D61-R4 — Exact payment qualification.** A currency is donor-visible only
> when it is both Site-enabled and the payments owner currently proves it for
> the complete exact context: Tenant, environment/mode, Site/giving entry,
> selected designations and resulting Legal Entity/payment groups, effective
> Settlement Account Binding and connected account/charge topology, cart
> currency intersection, one-time or recurring cadence, amount/minimum/maximum,
> canonical exponent/provider representation, and at least one admissible
> payment rail. Stripe's global currency list, Site default, client input,
> provider Dashboard toggle, or prior success is never enough.
>
> Payments supplies one source-labelled, freshness-bounded, provider-neutral
> qualification projection. Site/checkout does not call Stripe account/config
> APIs on page render or selector open. Final acceptance re-proves current
> qualification before any provider object; unknown, stale, contradictory, or
> incomplete proof is not eligible. D62 below ratifies that activation/proof
> lifecycle; both decisions remain launch gates.
>
> **D61-R5 — One cart, one donor choice.** Explicit donor selection always wins
> while it remains qualified and belongs only to the current gift intent. It
> survives refresh/navigation and authenticated cross-device continuity for
> that intent but never becomes an account/profile default. A new empty cart
> may receive a new suggestion. Guest persistence stays tenant-namespaced;
> authenticated persistence remains owner-scoped.
>
> Currency belongs authoritatively to the cart/gift-intent aggregate. Every
> line and compatible payment group must equal it through structural integrity,
> not UI convention. Guest merge, login, cross-device resume, another Site,
> location change, policy refresh, and two tabs never silently mix or replace
> currency. A recurring agreement freezes the accepted currency for future
> occurrences; renewals never consult location.
>
> **D61-R6 — Currency-transition boundary.** Automatic suggestion occurs only
> before amount/cart state. Once a line, amount, accepted command, or provider
> attempt exists, D61 never silently converts, preserves digits under another
> currency, clears donor work, or changes currency. A later donor-requested
> transition requires its own ratified consequence/confirmation contract, a
> successor cart/attempt revision where needed, and a distinct idempotency
> identity. D63 below ratifies that deliberately narrow transition; every other
> post-entry currency mutation remains forbidden.
>
> **D61-R7 — Donor control and placement.** On a current context with two or
> more qualified currencies, show one compact, visibly labelled **Currency**
> control immediately before presets/custom amount and above any Express
> Checkout or Payment Element that could authorize money. With one qualified
> currency, show the same information as static text rather than a disabled
> selector. With none, show the R2 unavailable state. Currency choice is not a
> global header/footer preference, banner, modal, redirect, or Site/locale URL.
>
> Use `CAD — Canadian dollar`, not a flag, country, raw provider code, or
> ambiguous `$`. A local candidate may receive a quiet **Suggested** annotation
> inside the control; no splash message or location permission prompt appears.
> Repeat the ISO code wherever commitment matters: amount, recurring terms,
> fee/FX disclosure, sticky total, payment-method area, review, submit action,
> processing, confirmation, receipt, refund, donor history, staff operations,
> reporting, and accounting handoff.
>
> **D61-R8 — International money correctness.** Every amount is a checked
> integer in the authoritative ISO currency's minor units. Parsing and
> formatting use one canonical, version-qualified currency/CLDR seam with an
> explicit presentation locale; locale never selects currency. Bare floating
> major units, universal cents, `×100`, `toFixed(2)`, implicit USD, hard-coded
> symbols, and scattered formatters are forbidden. JPY, BHD, ISK, HUF, TWD,
> locale decimal/grouping, currency minimum/maximum, rounding, and lossless
> provider round-trip are release gates.
>
> **D61-R9 — Amount, fee, recurring, and method coherence.** Currency resolves
> before presets and amount entry. Every preset, custom amount, minimum,
> maximum, fee-cover estimate/policy, total, schedule/recurring disclosure, and
> provider method is recalculated or qualified for the selected currency. D61
> authorizes no hidden preset conversion, Asym FX rate, copied flat Stripe fee,
> or claim that a bank will not charge conversion. Before authorization, Core
> states the exact charge amount/currency and truthfully warns where a donor's
> bank may apply its own exchange rate or fee.
>
> Currency/mode changes may alter available methods; unavailable methods are
> removed with one polite accessible update, never left selectable or used to
> change currency. External advice to put a Stripe Currency Selector beside the
> Payment Element is adopted only as a clarity principle: Core's current
> PaymentIntent path resolves currency before provider creation and repeats it
> read-only at payment, rather than importing Checkout Sessions behavior.
>
> **D61-R10 — Server-owned financial acceptance.** Client currency, country,
> amount, Site, designation, and payment-method fields are untrusted intent.
> Before accepting money state or creating a provider attempt, the server
> resolves trusted host → Site → Tenant, revalidates every designation and
> complete cart, proves current financial routes, parses checked minor units,
> proves same-currency conservation, and pins exact currency, amounts, Site/
> attribution, cart revision, policy/qualification generation, Legal Entity,
> Settlement Account Binding, provider account, and environment. Site and
> location never select those financial owners.
>
> **D61-R11 — Concurrency, idempotency, and attempt immutability.** Currency
> participates in cart revision/CAS, accepted-command semantic fingerprint,
> outbox identity, and provider-operation idempotency. Competing first-line/
> currency writes have one atomic winner. Reusing a key with a different
> currency conflicts or returns its exact existing meaning; it never mutates or
> provisions a different-currency charge. Staff configuration drift races with
> submit through final reproof. Once provider submission may have begun, Core
> retrieves/reconciles the exact attempt after ambiguity and never blindly
> retries, changes its currency, or reuses its client secret.
>
> **D61-R12 — Provider execution and reconciliation.** D61 remains compatible
> with Core's existing PaymentIntent seam and current pinned Stripe API version,
> but cannot use the current unsafe wrapper unchanged. Stripe receives only the
> already accepted explicit currency and integer minor amount for the exact
> connected account/route. Automatic payment methods are an execution feature,
> not qualification authority. Provider amount, currency, account, mode,
> binding, and eventual Balance Transaction must reconcile with frozen Core
> intent; disagreement is quarantined, never normalized or overwritten.
>
> Stripe may convert presentment into settlement and owns exact provider
> execution/conversion evidence. Phase 20 preserves that evidence; neither
> Stripe nor Phase 20 chooses donor currency. D61 does not enable Adaptive
> Pricing, Checkout Sessions, FX Quotes, provider-side irreversible settings,
> another account, or automatic foreign settlement.
>
> **D61-R13 — Site policy and staff authority.** Operational Postgres—not CMS—
> owns one Site default and bounded enabled presentment-currency ceiling.
> Authorized staff save the complete set atomically under expected revision.
> Invariants are `enabled ≠ ∅` and `default ∈ enabled`; removing the default
> requires selecting its replacement in the same command. Tenant, Site, actor,
> audit attribution, and current Phase 12 EffectiveAccess derive from trusted
> server context. D61 grants no permission and no direct browser/provider write.
>
> Provider drift does not erase Tenant intent. It removes the affected currency
> from current donor eligibility, shows staff the source-labelled reason/owner,
> and preserves history. Site policy changes are prospective: accepted gifts,
> recurring agreements, provider events, refunds, receipts, and accounting
> evidence never change. A nonempty cart preserves its stated intent and must be
> explicitly repaired before submission if no longer qualified.
>
> **D61-R14 — Quiet staff UX.** The Site workspace shows one **Currencies** card:
> **Default when no eligible suggestion applies**, **Donors can give in**, one
> current status per selected currency, prospective impact, and one cause-owned
> next action. Plain copy explains local suggestion and the ordinary settlement
> consequence, for example **Donor pays CAD · Stripe currently settles in USD ·
> conversion costs may apply**. Staff preview the standard donor control through
> the existing Site preview.
>
> Staff never configure country mappings, FX rates, Stripe charge topology,
> provider method matrices, bank accounts, retained settlement, QBO/Xero
> multicurrency, per-country overrides, or duplicate Sites here. No giant
> country × currency grid, new simulator, global score, or provider enum appears.
> Ordinary local-settlement tenants see no multicurrency-accounting wizard.
>
> **D61-R15 — Tenant, database, RLS, cache, and privacy safety.** Public reads
> expose only the exact safe current qualified currency projection after trusted
> host/Site resolution. Site-policy relations use same-Tenant scope integrity,
> canonical currency validation, restrictive deletion/history, unique current
> identity, indexed reads, server-derived attribution, and equivalent `USING`
> and `WITH CHECK` wherever Tenant writes exist. Owner-scoped cart RLS remains
> owner-only; service-role/background paths reassert owner plus every exact
> financial scope. An allowed update cannot move a policy/cart/line into a
> foreign Tenant, Site, owner, or currency.
>
> Country/suggestion is request-specific checkout context outside cached public
> CMS/Site output. Cache identity includes exact Tenant, environment, Site,
> policy/qualification generation, cart/viewer scope where applicable, and any
> trusted coarse-country variant; raw IP is never a key. One location's
> suggestion cannot leak through a shared response, and D61 creates no country-
> sized full-page cache or external lookup latency.
>
> **D61-R16 — Failure, lifecycle, and rollout.** Missing location uses R2;
> missing qualification does not. Policy/provider drift, incompatible method,
> unsupported amount/currency, stale cart, permission loss, cache mismatch,
> provider outage, lost response, or mixed-version projection preserves
> inspectable donor intent and fails before a wrong charge. Core never silently
> falls back, converts, deletes, or claims success. A suggestion-only kill
> switch leaves explicit choice/Site-default giving available where proved;
> a currency safety fence stops only new affected attempts and preserves event,
> refund, receipt, history, and accounting handling.
>
> Rollout is server-first: canonical currency/exponent seam and downstream
> renderers; exact connected-account/binding and qualification; structural cart
> and idempotency; safe projection; default-only compatibility; donor UI; staff
> enablement; one additional currency per proved Site/account/environment; then
> broader cohorts. Existing Sites seed their current currency as sole enabled
> and default, so D61 initially changes no donor behavior. No non-USD cohort
> launches while current arbitrary-string, `×100`, USD formatter/fee, platform-
> key fallback, or incomplete downstream behavior remains reachable.
>
> **D61-R17 — History and observability.** Durable business history records Site
> policy revision, authorized actor/time/reason, qualification reference,
> accepted cart/command revision, exact presentment amount/currency, financial
> pins, provider attempt/evidence, and prospective successor/retirement. It does
> not store suggestion location as money evidence. Technical telemetry uses
> safe low-cardinality scope/result/reason/generation/lag and aggregate country-
> currency suggestion outcomes; no raw IP, donor/cart identity, sensitive Site/
> ministry fact, or cross-Tenant label enters logs/metrics.
>
> **D61-R18 — Decision boundary.** D61 authorizes no currency-specific URL or
> redirect, language/currency coupling, donor preference service, precise
> geolocation, external geocoder, staff-authored country rules, provider matrix
> clone, FX/conversion engine, cross-currency cart, preset-conversion policy,
> any post-entry currency behavior outside D63, new payment architecture, Adaptive
> Pricing/Checkout Sessions/FX Quotes, multi-settlement, bank/accounting setup,
> or implementation. It freezes no physical Site-policy/projection table, cache
> technology, provider-poll interval, exact visual component, currency catalog
> package, or freshness duration. D62 below defines exact qualification/
> activation before implementation tickets may issue.

### Current behavior, intended behavior, and permanent path

| Layer            | Verified current/proposed state                                                                                                                                                                        | D61 intended behavior                                                                                              | Permanent path                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Site policy      | No runtime `public.sites`, Site default/enabled currency model, or staff Site-currency product exists; Phase 2/24 are planned.                                                                         | One operational Site default and enabled ceiling, separate from qualification.                                     | Build only through the Phase 2 Site owner and Phase 24 staff product; CMS never owns money eligibility.                               |
| Donor UI         | Checkout hardcodes `usd`, `$`, USD presets/fee assumptions, and a USD request fingerprint.                                                                                                             | One local suggestion/explicit control before amounts, exact ISO currency throughout.                               | Replace—not wrap—the USD-only presentation with the shared exponent/locale-aware money seam.                                          |
| Server input     | `donatePostSchema` accepts any nonempty caller currency; the API computes `Math.round(amount * 100)` and the RPC stores unconstrained text.                                                            | Client currency is untrusted intent; the server accepts only exact qualified ISO currency and checked minor units. | Land server authorization and database constraints before showing another currency.                                                   |
| Cart             | Current runtime has one charge and no cart. Phase 13 plans one-currency cart behavior but previously repeated currency on lines without a structural cart owner.                                       | One authoritative cart currency with line equality, revision, merge, resume, and concurrency rules.                | Reconcile Phase 13 schema/commands first; never implement D61 as component-only state.                                                |
| Stripe route     | Current PaymentIntent wrapper is idempotent but receives no exact Settlement Account Binding/account context; tenant keys may fall back to an environment key.                                         | Explicit currency executes only on the exact qualified connected-account route.                                    | Gate D61 behind the exact Connect/binding vertical slice; keep PaymentIntents unless separately changed.                              |
| Payment methods  | `automatic_payment_methods` is enabled, but current UI/config has no currency/mode qualification.                                                                                                      | Methods derive after currency/mode and may narrow without changing currency.                                       | Payments owns current safe qualification; Site consumes a projection and final command re-proves.                                     |
| Downstream money | Many receipt/history/admin/report formatters remain USD-specific; Phase 20 already separates presentment, settlement, payout, accounting, and reporting.                                               | Exact presentment currency survives every downstream projection while settlement stays separate.                   | Inventory and convert every money-bearing seam before foreign presentment; Phase 20 consumes provider evidence only.                  |
| Provider feature | Stripe's live 2026 docs confirm Adaptive Pricing is Checkout Sessions-only and unavailable on PaymentIntents. The older indexed custom-amount exclusion is no longer in today's live restriction list. | Provider-neutral D61 on explicit PaymentIntent currency.                                                           | Do not freeze the stale custom-amount claim or import Adaptive Pricing; re-prove provider contracts on any future integration change. |

The current route has a critical/high-likelihood money defect if another
currency becomes caller-selectable: JPY/BHD and Stripe special cases cannot be
represented safely, and an arbitrary client currency can reach provider
creation. D61 is therefore a forward contract and release fence, not permission
to extend current behavior.

### Donor and staff journeys

1. **Eligible local suggestion.** A Canadian donor reaches a valid Hope Relief
   giving entry. CAD is Site-enabled and qualified for the complete route, so
   the amount area starts **Currency · CAD — Canadian dollar** with a quiet
   **Suggested** annotation. No redirect, modal, location prompt, or delay
   occurs.
2. **Donor correction.** Before entering an amount, the donor selects EUR. EUR
   becomes the current intent currency; presets/methods re-resolve, the ISO code
   appears through review and receipt, and later location changes do nothing.
3. **One choice.** When only USD qualifies, checkout shows **USD — US dollar**
   as static labelled text, not a disabled one-item dropdown.
4. **No suggestion.** Missing/ambiguous country uses the qualified Site default
   immediately. If that default is unavailable but CAD/EUR remain qualified,
   the donor explicitly chooses one. If none qualify, the Giving panel explains
   current unavailability while the Site continues to work.
5. **Resumed work.** A donor who began a CAD cart in Canada opens it from France.
   The cart stays CAD. Core revalidates CAD; it neither suggests EUR nor changes
   existing amounts. If CAD is no longer qualified, work is preserved and
   submission pauses for the separately governed recovery choice.
6. **Staff setup.** Nina opens **Web Studio → Hope Relief → Currencies**, selects
   default USD and enables CAD/EUR in one reviewable save. She sees only current
   donor availability, prospective consequence, ordinary settlement summary,
   and one owner action—never country rules, Stripe tables, FX rates, banks, or
   accounting configuration.

### Twenty-two-category adversarial result

Every category has a material concern under the unqualified option. D61-R1-R18
preserve the selected local-first donor UX while making invalid money states,
provider coupling, cross-scope configuration, and staff complexity structurally
or procedurally impossible.
