### Ruthless synthesis and required order

Before D61 can be recorded, **suggested**, **enabled**, **qualified**,
**selected**, **accepted**, **presented**, and **settled** currency must remain
separate. The donor may receive one convenient empty-intent recommendation, but
only the payment owner can qualify it and only the accepted money command can
freeze it. R1-R18 now encode that distinction.

The current runtime is not a shortcut candidate. Its caller-authorized currency,
floating major units, `×100`, USD formatting/fees, environment-key fallback,
and missing Site/Connect/cart contracts are release blockers. Adding a dropdown
first would create a critical money defect, not an incremental UX improvement.

Required implementation order is:

1. carry D62's exact payment-qualification/activation contract into the
   consolidated specification;
2. land the Phase 2 canonical currency/exponent seam and remove implicit USD,
   arbitrary-string, floating/two-decimal, and scattered formatter authority;
3. prove exact Tenant/Legal Entity/Settlement Account Binding/connected account
   execution and Phase 20 provider settlement-evidence continuity;
4. reconcile Phase 13 cart ownership, structural same-currency integrity,
   guest/account merge, accepted intent, idempotency, and provider mismatch;
5. expose one safe versioned qualification/public checkout projection with
   cache and final-reproof behavior;
6. add the Base Maia/Base UI donor control and complete accessible states;
7. add the quiet Site staff policy/readiness card; and
8. roll out default-only, then one foreign currency per exact proved cohort,
   while retaining all historical readers/workers on rollback.

Implementation safeguards are a nonauthoritative country hint; one platform-
owned versioned map; exact server-derived qualification; one cart currency;
checked integer minor units; current financial pins; currency-bearing
idempotency; provider mismatch quarantine; no per-render Stripe call; no
country-varying Site cache; and explicit unavailable/recovery states. That is a
small set of deep boundaries, not a new FX or geolocation platform.

D61 deliberately does not freeze the physical Site-policy/qualification schema,
country-header vendor, cache/event technology, qualification duration,
supported launch currencies/methods/cadences, exact component, preset/amount
transition semantics, FX quote/fee model, conversion-copy details, or retained
settlement. These require source evidence or later decisions; guessing now
would create the technical debt the option is intended to avoid.

### Release proof and justified operational signals

Release is blocked until production-shaped evidence proves all of the
following:

- Site default, one/many/no qualified choices, unavailable default with other
  choices, missing/invalid/spoofed/ambiguous/VPN country hints, unsupported
  local currency, and no location-service network dependency;
- local suggestion, explicit donor override, new cart, resumed cart, travel/
  later hint, refresh/back/forward, shared device, guest→account merge,
  authenticated cross-device resume, cross-Site entry, and two-tab cart CAS;
- trusted host → Site → Tenant, exact Legal Entity/payment groups, Settlement
  Account Binding, connected account/environment/mode, direct-charge topology,
  current currency/method/cadence/amount qualification, and negative forged/
  stale/cross-scope cases;
- server rejection of disabled, unqualified, cross-Tenant, malformed, and
  client-authorized currency before any provider object;
- structural one-cart currency, all-line/group conservation, first-line/
  currency atomicity, semantic idempotency conflict, no old-client-secret reuse,
  lost-response readback, duplicate/reordered provider evidence, and provider
  amount/currency/account mismatch quarantine;
- JPY, BHD, ISK, HUF, TWD, every supported exponent/special case, locale decimal
  input, minimum/maximum, rounding, overflow, and provider-lossless round trip;
- one-time, recurring, mixed cadence/designation, fee cover, presets, Express
  Checkout, Payment Element, method narrowing, SCA, processing, failure,
  confirmation, refund/dispute, receipt, donor history, staff operations,
  reports, messages/documents, ledger, and settlement/accounting evidence;
- staff atomic default/enabled save, default removal/replacement, stale
  revision, permission loss, provider drift, policy change before/after cart/
  provider attempt/accepted gift, and source-owned repair;
- tenant/cache/RLS `USING` and `WITH CHECK`, service-role/background parity,
  request-country isolation, no country-varying full public cache, no raw-IP/
  location persistence, and safe aggregate telemetry;
- Base Maia/Base UI keyboard/touch/focus, screen-reader naming, non-color
  meaning, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 200% zoom/text spacing, long currency names,
  RTL/CJK/bidi, reduced motion, low bandwidth, offline/loading/stale/error, no
  initial currency flash, no layout shift, and one polite method/amount update;
  and
- old-code/new-schema and new-code/old-schema behavior, default-only migration,
  per-cohort feature/safety fences, and rollback after foreign-currency gifts
  that stops new attempts but preserves event/refund/receipt/history/accounting
  processing.

| Signal                                          | Threshold                                                                                   | Owner                           | Required response                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkout_presentment_currency_mismatch_total`  | Any provider amount/currency/account/mode differing from frozen Core intent                 | Payments + Finance Integrity    | P0 quarantine the occurrence, stop the affected currency/account path, reconcile provider/ledger evidence, and restore only after exact proof.                                    |
| `checkout_unqualified_currency_admitted_total`  | Any accepted attempt whose currency lacked current complete qualification                   | Payments on-call + Architecture | P0 stop new affected attempts, preserve/reconcile existing evidence, repair qualification/acceptance, and re-prove the full cohort.                                               |
| `checkout_currency_cross_scope_total`           | Any wrong-Tenant/Site/owner/environment/account policy, projection, cart, or attempt        | Security + Payments             | P0 disable the read/command/cache path, assess disclosure and money effects, purge unsafe cache, repair scope, and pass the negative matrix before restore.                       |
| `checkout_currency_silent_change_total`         | Any non-pristine intent whose currency changed without the separately authorized transition | Donor Experience + Payments     | Disable suggestion/transition for the cohort, preserve carts/attempts, repair precedence/revision logic, and rerun journey/idempotency proof. Treat a submitted-money case as P0. |
| `checkout_currency_qualification_reject_ratio`  | Above 1% for one enabled currency over 15 minutes with at least 100 attempts                | Payments Operations             | Pause new attempts for that exact currency/scope, compare projection with current account/provider evidence, repair or mark unavailable, and never fall back silently.            |
| `checkout_currency_suggestion_correction_ratio` | Above 20% for one country→currency candidate over 30 days with at least 100 suggestions     | Product + Donor Experience      | Review mapping/copy and qualitative evidence; adjust only through a reviewed mapping successor, never by silently overriding donor control.                                       |

Currency-specific provider/settlement/accounting exceptions remain with their
Phase 20 owners. D61 monitors selection and exact acceptance; it does not clone
provider or finance operations.

### Modern evidence and repository reconciliation

- Stripe's current [PaymentIntent creation contract](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create)
  accepts one explicit currency and integer minor-unit amount. Core can keep its
  provider seam after its own server authorization, exact Connect binding,
  idempotency, and money correctness are repaired; D61 does not require a
  checkout-stack rewrite.
- Today's [Stripe Adaptive Pricing documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/currencies/localize-prices/adaptive-pricing?payment-ui=embedded-components)
  states that the feature and Currency Selector require Elements with Checkout
  Sessions and are not supported on the Payment Intents API. Core therefore
  adopts local-first clarity, not that provider product. The live restriction
  list no longer includes the older indexed **custom amounts unsupported**
  bullet; D61 deliberately records neither stale claim and requires fresh proof
  for any future provider change.
- Stripe's current [currency documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies)
  defines presentment separately from payment-method and settlement currency,
  requires currency-specific integer minor units, documents zero-/three-decimal
  and special cases, and exposes currency-dependent minimums/maximums.
- [Stripe payment-method support](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/payment-method-support)
  varies by currency, business/customer country, product, API flow, and
  connected-account eligibility. A global supported list cannot be D61
  qualification.
- [Stripe Connect multicurrency guidance](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/currencies)
  confirms that presentment/settlement differences create FX and that connected
  accounts add route-specific considerations. ADR-0061 and Phase 20 therefore
  remain the settlement/accounting owners.
- [Fundraise Up](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/checkout-currencies/) recommends
  geolocation plus donor choice, keeps one selected currency for the
  [whole gift cart](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/gift-catalog/), and now repeats
  ISO codes where symbols are ambiguous in its
  [currency-visibility update](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/changelog/better-currency-visibility-in-checkout/).
- [GoFundMe Pro](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288800980123-Multi-currency-support)
  shows local currency first with correction and carries it across giving and
  receipt surfaces. Its distinct display/processed/settlement meanings reinforce
  Core's refusal to collapse those authorities.
- [Shopify selector guidance](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/markets/country-language-ux)
  supports code-plus-name/symbol, product-consistent controls, and a compact
  popover rather than an excessive modal. Core keeps currency independent from
  language and omits flags.
- [Unicode CLDR/UTS 35](https://unicode.org/reports/tr35/tr35-numbers.html)
  defines localized currency formatting, ambiguous narrow symbols, currency-
  code independence from locale, and versioned territory/current-tender data.
  Core uses the standards data, not a handwritten mapping or locale guess.
- [W3C Geolocation](https://www.w3.org/TR/geolocation/) classifies device
  location as a permission-gated privacy-sensitive feature. D61 does not ask
  for it; a trusted optional country-level ingress hint is sufficient.
- [Vercel request-header documentation](https://vercel.com/docs/headers/request-headers.rsc)
  exposes a possible country adapter. D61 does not hard-code Vercel as domain
  authority: every supported ingress must prove header overwrite/trust, and
  absence falls back without another request.
- Repository facts resolve external conflicts: Phase 2 owns currency/exponent
  correctness; Phase 13 owns cart/accepted intent; payment owners qualify and
  execute; Phase 20/ADR-0061 own settlement evidence; locale never selects
  currency; Base Maia/Base UI remains exact. External products supply evidence,
  not governing ownership.

### Documentation and implementation status

D61 is recorded in the glossary, ADR-0061, Phase 2, Phase 5, Phase 13, the Web
Studio living spec, the Phase 24 roadmap, and this decision log. No new ADR is
justified: the local suggestion is reversible, while the hard-to-reverse
presentment/settlement and money-ownership trade-off already lives in ADR-0061.
This grooming step changes no runtime, schema, Stripe configuration, provider
object, Site policy, money, migration, cache, or OpenSpec.

R1-R18 are the exact future spec language. The consolidated Phase 24 OpenSpec
delta and design must carry the selection, qualification dependency, cart/
money/idempotency, authorization/RLS/cache/privacy, donor/staff UX, provider,
migration, rollback, proof, and monitoring contracts before implementation
tickets issue.

## D62 — Inline proof before offering a presentment currency

### Founder direction

**Option 1 — prove before offering CAD.** The founder required the check to be
part of ordinary setup, kept simple and straightforward, while retaining modern
payment safety, excellent staff and donor UX, reliability, and a permanent
architecture rather than a brittle Stripe-specific workaround.

### Adversarial disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** Proving known readiness before donors see
CAD is the right answer. The raw wording overstates what setup can prove,
however: before a donor exists, Core does not know the final designations,
amount, cadence, method, device, issuer, authentication, Radar outcome, or
provider response. D62 therefore requires two deliberate proof levels: one
side-effect-free setup qualification for the stable offering envelope, followed
by complete server revalidation at checkout before any provider object.

Record this corrected decision:

> **D62-R1 — Purpose and authority.** D62 governs when a staff-selected **Donor
> Presentment Currency** may become available for new gifts. Site policy owns
> the Tenant's desired default and enabled-currency ceiling. Payments alone
> owns **Donor Presentment Currency Qualification**. Effective donor
> availability is always:
>
> `Site-enabled currency ∩ current exact route qualification`
>
> D62 does not execute or guarantee a payment; choose settlement, payout, bank,
> accounting, Field Account, or Legal Entity; calculate FX; activate retained
> currency; or make CMS/provider state a financial authority.
>
> **D62-R2 — One ordinary setup flow.** Adding CAD happens in the existing
> **Site → Currencies** card. Staff choose `CAD — Canadian dollar`; that selection
> automatically starts the check. There is no separate test, wizard, checklist,
> certification screen, task, score, provider table, or second dashboard.
> Healthy completion requires one explicit **Add CAD** action only.
>
> **D62-R3 — Two proof levels.** Setup qualification proves the stable current
> offering envelope for each named public Site route and giving-mode cohort
> before a donor exists. Checkout acceptance separately re-proves the complete
> donor-specific gift context immediately before the first provider effect.
> Setup **Ready** means **Core found no current known setup blocker for this
> named scope**. It never promises issuer approval, donor-specific method
> eligibility, authentication, fraud acceptance, network availability, a future
> renewal, or payment success.
>
> **D62-R4 — Exact setup grain.** Each immutable, source-labelled qualification
> generation binds Tenant, live/sandbox environment, Site financial route,
> Legal Entity, effective Settlement Account Binding and version, connected
> account, charge topology, ISO currency, giving mode/cadence family, at least
> one admissible payment rail, canonical currency/exponent and amount-bound
> implementation, fee/preset/downstream certification, pinned provider/API and
> payment-configuration contract, evaluator generation, observation time, and
> expiry. A provider-neutral Payments adapter normalizes those facts; Site/CMS
> code never stores or interprets raw Stripe fields as product truth.
>
> **D62-R5 — Declarative evidence, no synthetic transaction.** Setup may inspect
> Core deployment/certification, exact binding/account/environment, provider
> `charges_enabled`, active required capabilities, unresolved requirements,
> effective payment-method configuration, country/currency/product compatibility,
> recurring-adapter readiness, and ordinary settlement-conversion compatibility.
> It creates no PaymentIntent, SetupIntent, Customer, Price, subscription,
> mandate, charge, refund, payout, ledger, or accounting object and changes no
> provider configuration. Test/sandbox success is never live qualification; a
> prior successful gift and Stripe's global currency list are never sufficient.
>
> **D62-R6 — Small, honest result vocabulary.** The Payments boundary returns
> semantic `qualified`, `not_qualified`, or `unknown` per exact cohort, with a
> source-owned safe reason. The staff card renders only concrete text:
> **Checking CAD availability…**; **Ready for one-time and recurring gifts**;
> **Ready for one-time gifts · Recurring needs setup**; **Payment setup needed**;
> **CAD isn’t available for this Site**; **Couldn’t check right now**; or, after
> drift, **Paused for new gifts**. Do not use vague **Limited**, percentage
> readiness, stale green, provider enum, or **Ready** without its scope.
> Timeout, `429`, `5xx`, lost response, missing source, and contradictory or
> expired evidence are **unknown**, never **not supported** and never **Ready**.
>
> **D62-R7 — Initial activation and default coverage.** A newly selected
> currency changes durable Site policy only when at least one intended current
> route qualifies. A partial result may activate only the named donor contexts
> and must state that consequence before save. A new Site default must qualify
> across every current Site entry and giving mode that relies on that default;
> a partially qualified currency may remain additional but cannot become a
> misleading fallback. If no route qualifies, the existing live policy stays
> unchanged and the card offers the one owner action needed to continue setup.
>
> **D62-R8 — Broad but bounded Site intent.** Adding CAD means **offer CAD
> wherever this Site's payment routes currently qualify**, not **create a staff-
> managed route/method matrix**. The consequence review names what is available
> now and makes this prospective intent clear. A later Payments qualification
> may add or remove an effective route without another per-route toggle, while
> the complete Site enabled ceiling remains unchanged until an authorized staff
> command changes it. Staff never configure methods, provider capabilities,
> country rules, charge topology, or qualification expiry here.
>
> **D62-R9 — Authorization and atomic save.** Phase 24 registers the Site-scoped
> `sites.manage_presentment_currencies` capability in the existing Phase 12
> EffectiveAccess model. It grants no provider, binding, settlement, bank,
> accounting, FX, cart, or accepted-money authority. After all provider reads
> finish outside the database transaction, the server reauthorizes the actor and
> atomically compares the complete Site-policy revision, exact qualification
> fingerprints/generations, default/enabled invariants, and current Tenant/Site
> scope. A changed result returns the refreshed consequence and writes nothing.
> Retry after an ambiguous response reads back the command's durable business
> effect; duplicate submission yields one policy revision and one audit effect.
>
> **D62-R10 — Final acceptance remains money authority.** Before any provider
> object, checkout re-resolves trusted host → Site → Tenant and revalidates every
> selected designation/payment group, Legal Entity, effective binding/account/
> environment/topology, actual amount and provider minimum/maximum, cadence,
> selected method, ISO currency/exponent, current Site policy, qualification
> generation, one-cart conservation, and currency-bearing command/idempotency
> fingerprint. Client state and setup projection express no acceptance
> authority. A final mismatch preserves the cart and provides one explicit
> recovery; it never silently converts, substitutes, retries, or charges.
>
> **D62-R11 — Freshness, invalidation, and drift.** Qualification expires at the
> earliest declared source boundary and is invalidated narrowly by binding
> succession, account deauthorization, current account/capability/requirement or
> payment-configuration change, provider-contract/catalog change, recurring-
> adapter change, or Core money-ruleset deployment. Signed provider events are
> hints to fetch current state, not arrival-ordered truth. Missing, duplicated,
> delayed, or out-of-order events cannot extend green evidence. Source-owned
> reconciliation refreshes bounded cohorts; public render and selector use do
> not poll providers.
>
> **D62-R12 — Safe lifecycle and existing obligations.** Drift or a safety fence
> removes only the affected currency/route/mode from **new** donor availability
> and labels it truthfully for staff. It preserves the Site's selected intent,
> public Site, other currencies/routes, nonempty carts, accepted gifts, recurring
> agreements and their Phase 16 execution/recovery authority, provider events,
> refunds/disputes, receipts, donor/staff history, ledger, reporting, settlement,
> and accounting evidence. One donor decline never pauses a currency globally.
> Availability resumes only from a current successor qualification.
>
> **D62-R13 — Tenant, database, RLS, and privileged-path safety.** Policy and
> qualification storage uses non-null immutable Tenant and scope keys, canonical
> currency checks, same-Tenant composite foreign keys, append-only qualification
> generations with one current head, restrictive deletion, and indexed current
> reads. Tenant, Site, actor, Legal Entity, binding, account, environment, result,
> and audit attribution derive from trusted server context. Direct DML is
> revoked; RLS is enabled and forced where applicable; mutation policies enforce
> equivalent `USING` and `WITH CHECK`; an allowed update cannot move a row or
> current head across scope. Service-role/workflow/cache paths reassert every
> scope and never accept caller-authored readiness.
>
> **D62-R14 — Efficient, idempotent provider interaction.** Refresh provider
> account/capability/configuration evidence once per exact reusable account
> scope, coalesce concurrent checks, cache only within a declared freshness
> bound, use bounded timeouts, and handle provider `429` with exponential
> backoff and jitter. Never call Stripe per currency row, public
> page render, donor selector open, checkout field change, or cached projection
> read. Job/retry identity is tied to the durable qualification effect and source
> generation, not one HTTP request; stale results cannot overwrite successors.
> D62 freezes no queue, cache, polling vendor, or arbitrary universal TTL.
>
> **D62-R15 — Money, settlement, and integration boundary.** A qualification
> does not assert that every amount/method succeeds, calculate a conversion rate
> or fee, promise settlement, or require a CAD bank account. Ordinary Stripe
> conversion from CAD presentment into the existing settlement currency remains
> compatible without retained foreign balance, QBO/Xero multicurrency, Adaptive
> Pricing, Checkout Sessions, or FX Quotes. Phase 2 currency/exponent and Phase
> 13 amount/cart/provider correctness, Phase 16 recurring authority, and Phase
> 20 settlement/accounting evidence remain separate release gates. The current
> Core PaymentIntent seam and pinned SDK/API contract may evolve only through
> their owning design; D62 hard-codes neither Accounts v1/v2 nor raw provider
> shapes and does not reopen the governing direct-charge topology.
>
> **D62-R16 — Calm, accessible staff UX.** The chosen currency row reserves
> space while checking, never moves focus, and announces the final status once
> through polite programmatic status semantics. Status uses text and meaning in
> addition to color, is visually distinct from its action, and works with
> keyboard, 44×44 CSS-pixel touch targets, visible focus, 320-CSS-pixel reflow,
> 200% zoom/text spacing, long localized currency names, RTL/CJK/bidi, reduced
> motion, low bandwidth, and failure/retry. A qualified row shows one concise
> settlement sentence, for example **Donors can use CAD for one-time gifts.
> Stripe currently settles in USD; conversion costs may apply.** An exception
> exposes one secondary **Finish payment setup** or **Try again** action and
> returns to this same card.
>
> **D62-R17 — Donor UX.** Donors see CAD only where the current exact giving
> context qualifies. A one-time-only currency does not appear as a valid
> recurring choice. A later cadence, destination, amount, method, or provider
> change never silently switches currency, preserves digits under another
> currency, or discards work. D63 alone permits a donor-confirmed currency
> transition that preserves revalidated non-money intent while explicitly
> clearing disclosed money/payment state. D61's labelled currency-before-money control,
> ISO-code repetition, explicit donor control, unavailable state, cart
> preservation, and final reproof remain binding. D62 adds no donor spinner,
> setup status, provider terminology, or provider-call latency.
>
> **D62-R18 — Source of truth and durable audit.** Operational Postgres owns
> Site requested/default/enabled policy; the Payments domain owns normalized
> qualification generations; Stripe owns current provider account, capability,
> requirement, configuration, and execution facts; Phase 13 owns accepted gift
> intent/money; Phase 16 owns recurring obligations; Phase 20 owns settlement/
> accounting evidence. CMS, the staff projection, cache, and provider are never
> competing write authorities. Durable history records Site-policy revision,
> trusted actor/time/reason, exact qualification scope/fingerprint/result/time,
> accepted command references, invalidation/successor, and safe reason. Technical
> logs do not replace business history.
>
> **D62-R19 — Security and privacy.** Staff and public projections expose the
> minimum safe outcome and cause-owned action. They reveal no API secret,
> client secret, bank detail, provider account/binding identifier, raw capability
> or requirement payload, identity/KYC detail, provider response body, internal
> request ID, another Tenant's status, donor fact, or sensitive ministry fact.
> Detailed provider diagnostics remain authorization-gated with redacted logs,
> retention, export, backup, and support-access controls. Repair destinations
> are server-generated and same-scope validated.
>
> **D62-R20 — Migration, rollout, and rollback.** Ship server-first: canonical
> currency/exponent and all downstream money readers; exact Connect binding and
> provider adapter; versioned qualification and final-acceptance enforcement;
> tenant-safe projection/cache; Site setup UI; donor UI; then one exact Tenant/
> account/currency/mode cohort. Existing Sites seed only their proven current
> currency. UI cannot activate CAD while arbitrary currency strings, floating
> major units, `×100`, implicit/two-decimal USD, environment-key fallback,
> incomplete recurring/refund/receipt/reporting/accounting readers, or old code/
> new schema incompatibility remains reachable. Rollback stops only new affected
> attempts and retains all historical handlers.
>
> **D62-R21 — Proof and observability.** Production-shaped positive, negative,
> boundary, authorization, concurrency, drift, provider, accessibility,
> migration, and rollback tests below are release gates. Low-cardinality
> telemetry carries safe cohort/result/reason/generation/age, never Tenant names,
> account IDs, donor/cart IDs, raw provider errors, or high-cardinality ministry
> data. Any effective scope without current proof, cross-scope result, synthetic
> setup object, or stale admission is a hard incident, not a tolerated metric.
>
> **D62-R22 — Deliberate non-goals.** D62 creates no generalized certification
> platform, rules-language, provider plugin marketplace, provider Dashboard
> clone, currency × route × method editor, durable staff workflow, new task or
> notification system, country matrix, test-charge/refund harness, FX engine,
> Adaptive Pricing/Checkout Sessions/FX Quotes migration, retained settlement,
> bank/accounting wizard, manual readiness override, physical schema mandate,
> arbitrary freshness number, or supported-currency launch list. Those require
> their own owner and evidence; none is necessary to make this setup safe.

### Current behavior, intended behavior, and permanent path

**Current behavior is not D62-ready.** The public checkout hardcodes USD, the
API accepts arbitrary nonempty currency text, server code calculates
`Math.round(amount * 100)`, legacy storage has unconstrained currency text,
receipt/statement paths assume two-decimal `en-US`, the Tenant Stripe resolver
can fall back to an environment key, and the repository has no implemented
Site, Legal Entity, Settlement Account Binding, Connect direct-charge wrapper,
cart, or recurring target path. Creating only the Currencies card would expose
foreign-currency intent to a USD-shaped money pipeline and is therefore a
critical defect, not an incremental launch.

**Intended behavior** is the R1-R22 two-level model: one automatic, declarative
setup preflight in the existing card; one atomic authorized save; a fast safe
read projection for donor choice; and complete final acceptance revalidation.

**The permanent path** is provider-neutral at the domain seam but deliberately
not a speculative plugin framework. The current pinned Stripe adapter supplies
normalized evidence; a future API/account-model upgrade replaces that adapter
without changing Site policy, donor availability, or audit meanings. Stripe's
latest external recommendation to prefer Accounts v2 or Checkout Sessions does
not silently override Core's governing Phase 13 direct-charge/PaymentIntent
decisions. The owning payment design must explicitly reconcile any migration;
D62 neither blocks it nor smuggles it into Site setup.

### Twenty-two-category adversarial review

Every requested category is assessed independently against the founder's raw
choice. Every category has a material concern until the cited D62 requirement
is applied; no category is silently treated as safe merely because the option
is directionally correct.

| Category                                                      | Material concern, failure, importance, severity/likelihood, and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                           | Effect on answer and permanent prevention / exact spec language                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Problem validity, necessity, and alternatives                 | **Yes — High/High.** Donors benefit from local presentment, but global provider support does not prove this account/route. Checkout-only validation is the strongest simpler alternative, yet knowingly moves deterministic setup failures to donors after effort. | **Narrows, does not invalidate.** R1-R3 and R10 keep preflight plus final reproof; no-build is acceptable only while one currency remains enabled.              |
| Brittleness                                                   | **Yes — High/High.** Bindings, account capabilities, provider requirements/configurations, recurring adapters, currency rules, and Core deployments drift independently. A timeless green Boolean breaks immediately.                                              | R4, R11, R14, and R18 require scoped generations, expiry, invalidation, current-state reconciliation, and no stale overwrite.                                   |
| Technical debt                                                | **Yes — High/High.** `cad_ready`, copied Stripe matrices, synthetic charges, or raw provider enums would become shadow payment infrastructure and make another processor/API migration expensive.                                                                  | R1, R4-R5, R14-R15, and R22 require one Payments evaluator/projection, normalized evidence, and no provider clone.                                              |
| Edge cases                                                    | **Yes — High/High collectively.** One-time-only readiness, multi-entity Sites, method/country limits, amount minima, JPY/BHD/ISK/HUF/TWD rules, deauthorization, `429`, delayed events, and mid-cart drift are ordinary realities.                                 | R3-R7, R10-R17, and the release matrix require explicit cohort results, final context proof, and safe preservation.                                             |

| Overengineering                                               | **Yes — High/Medium.** A universal certification engine, matrix editor, staff workflow, polling console, or synthetic transaction harness solves speculative cases and burdens every Tenant.                                                                       | R2, R6, R14, R16, and R22 reduce the product to one evaluator, one row, one result, one action, and implementation-neutral internals.                           |

| Source of truth, ownership, and domain invariants             | **Yes — Critical/High.** Site intent, payment qualification, provider facts/execution, accepted money, recurring obligations, and settlement can collapse into one mutable **enabled** flag.                                                                       | R1, R3-R4, R10, R12, and R18 name each owner and make the qualified intersection and historical immutability explicit.                                          |

| Failure modes                                                 | **Yes — Critical/Medium-high.** Provider timeout/lost response, stale cache, partial save, missing webhook, or rejection after object creation can show false green, duplicate effects, or leave half-enabled policy.                                              | R5-R6, R9-R11, and R14-R15 require no setup effect, unknown-safe outcomes, transactional CAS, readback, expiry, and no blind retry/fallback.                    |
| Lifecycle, temporal correctness, concurrency, and idempotency | **Yes — Critical/High.** Evidence can change between check/save and save/checkout; concurrent staff edits and reordered events can regress the current head or overwrite policy.                                                                                   | R9-R12 and R14 require generation-aware CAS, final reproof, append-only successors, durable-effect idempotency, and current-state reconciliation.               |

| Security and privacy risks                                    | **Yes — High/Medium.** Provider requirements may expose KYC identity, bank/account, internal IDs, credentials, or business-sensitive data; broad cache/log labels can leak cross-Tenant status.                                                                    | R13 and R19-R21 require least-data projections, trusted repair links, gated redacted diagnostics, retention controls, and safe telemetry.                       |
| Scalability and performance risks                             | **Yes — High/High at scale.** Tenant × Site × currency × route × method provider reads and per-render polling multiply quickly, contend with payment traffic, and hit account/endpoint/read-allocation limits.                                                     | R14 requires account-scope reuse, coalescing, bounded freshness, queue/backoff where needed, and zero provider calls on public/donor renders.                   |

| Observability and auditability gaps                           | **Yes — High/High.** Without scope/fingerprint/generation, safe cause, policy revision, and successor history, teams cannot explain why CAD appeared, disappeared, or failed or distinguish ordinary decline from evaluator drift.                                 | R11, R18, R20-R21 and the signals below separate durable business audit from low-cardinality technical diagnostics.                                             |
