### Modern evidence and repository reconciliation

- Fundraise Up's current [donation amount settings](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/suggested-amounts/)
  separate enabled frequencies and support staff-authored suggestions. Its
  approach supports the UX pattern; its AI option is intentionally not imported.
- Givebutter's current [suggested amount settings](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/2859751-how-to-customize-suggested-donation-amounts)
  also separate frequency sets and preserve Other amount. Its eighteen-choice
  maximum is rejected as too noisy for Core's ordinary giving surface.
- Donorbox's current [giving-level guidance](https://donorbox.org/nonprofit-blog/donation-tiers-to-boost-online-donations)
  recommends a small set, commonly four to six, with a custom option. D64 caps
  six and recommends three/four rather than treating vendor advice as authority.
- Stripe's current [currency contract](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies)
  requires minor-unit integer amounts and documents currency/route-specific
  minimums, maximums, zero-decimal and special-case currencies. Its
  [local-pricing comparison](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/currencies/localize-prices)
  distinguishes manually set native values from FX-derived options; D64 chooses
  no provider pricing or FX path.
- W3C's current [labels and instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html),
  [status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html),
  [target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html),
  and [radio-group pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/)
  support the explicit, quiet, operable editor/donor contract without excessive
  instructional noise.
- Repository authority wins where external patterns diverge: D61 says Site
  giving policy is Operational Postgres truth and CMS stores neither it nor
  payment qualification; Phase 13 owns cart/accepted Money; Phase 16 owns
  cadences; ADR-0061 rejects Core-authored FX. D64 therefore does not use
  Payload drafts, Stripe Prices, or vendor personalization despite their
  availability elsewhere.

### Documentation and implementation status

D64 is now recorded in the glossary, ADR-0061, Phases 2, 5, 12, 13 and 16, the
Web Studio living spec, the Phase 24 roadmap, and this log. No new ADR is needed:
ADR-0061 already owns the difficult presentment/FX boundary. This grooming step
changes no runtime, schema, migration, provider object, currency, cart, Site
policy, capability grant, cache, or current OpenSpec. R1-R22 are the exact
future requirement language; the consolidated Phase 24 OpenSpec delta must
carry it before tickets or implementation issue.

## D65 — What should happen if a donor changes a gift's frequency after entering details?

Hope Relief has reviewed **CAD 100 one-time** and **CAD 25 monthly** suggestions.
A donor selects CAD 100 for one line, then changes that line to **Monthly**.
Keeping `100` silently turns one charge into CAD 100 every month; mapping “the
second one-time button” to “the second monthly button” silently changes value.
The same problem exists for monthly→annual or quarterly→monthly, and schedule
details can become invalid even before payment entry.

This question covers every transition between two distinct Phase 16 schedule
identities, including one-time↔recurring and recurring-cadence↔recurring-
cadence. It is line-scoped: changing one gift must not clear unrelated cart-line
amounts.

### Option 1 — preserve purpose, clear the affected money/schedule, and show the target set (recommended)

If the affected line has no selected/prefilled/custom amount, nonempty or
incomplete amount input, fee choice,
entered schedule/anchor/start/end state, amount/schedule-derived claim,
payment-method/mandate/future-use state, or provider session, the schedule
switches immediately and its reviewed target suggestions appear unselected.

Otherwise Core first proves that the same destination is available for the
target schedule and keeps the entire current cart untouched. If incompatible,
the choice is unavailable with one clear explanation. If compatible, one
accessible confirmation says:

**Change this gift to monthly?**  
**Your gift amount will be cleared. Where this gift goes will stay.**

Only when applicable, append **Your schedule details, fee coverage choice, and
selected payment method will also be cleared**, naming only the state that
actually exists. Actions are **Keep one-time** and **Change to monthly**;
initial focus is **Keep one-time**, and Escape/cancel changes nothing.
After success, only the affected line's amount/schedule state and the exact
dependent fee/payment-group state clear. Other lines and every revalidated non-
money purpose stay. The monthly set appears unselected. Failure says the
original one-time gift is unchanged.

No frequency changes are available during confirmation, authentication, wallet
approval, redirect, processing, capture, cancellation/reconciliation, success,
or unknown provider outcome. This reuses D63's preserve/clear/CAS/idempotency
kernel at the affected line/payment-group grain rather than clearing the cart.

**Pros:** no accidental recurring commitment, no invented equivalence, and one
consistent safety model. **Cons:** a donor who intended the same amount must
select or enter it again.

### Option 2 — keep the same exact numeric amount

CAD 100 remains CAD 100, but the interface relabels it unmistakably as **CAD 100
each month** and final review repeats the schedule.

**Pros:** fastest and preserves the donor's typed digits. **Cons:** a schedule
toggle can multiply the commitment with no explicit money re-entry, a dangerous
default for donor trust; existing schedule details may still be incompatible.

### Option 3 — map preset position to the target frequency

The second one-time suggestion becomes the second monthly suggestion.

**Pros:** quickly lands on a staff-reviewed monthly amount. **Cons:** invents an
ordinal equivalence nobody authorized, fails for custom/unequal sets, and hides
the actual value change.

**Recommendation:** Option 1. It is the clearest extension of D63-D64 and uses
one bounded transition contract. Untouched browsing remains immediate and
unselected; consequential donor work receives one exact confirmation.

Which D65 frequency-change rule should Core record?

### Founder answer

> Preserve purpose, clear the affected money and schedule. Think about the best
> UX and UI for all users (staff and donors).

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The answer is the safest modern product
rule, but “affected” must mean the smallest **complete dependency closure**, not
only fields visibly inside one line. Applying D63 cart-wide would destroy
unrelated donor work; applying D65 only in the browser would strand stale fee,
payment, mandate, review, grouping, provider, or authorization meaning. The
corrected decision below preserves the founder's intent while closing those
gaps.

### Current behavior, intended behavior, and best permanent path

- **Current repository behavior:** the production donor checkout still coerces
  every submitted frequency to `one-time`, displays a static **One-time gift**,
  and holds one flat client amount/payment state rather than the Phase 13 cart.
  Its fingerprint includes frequency/schedule/payment/fee dimensions, but the
  full Phase 13/16 schedule-transition product does not exist. Existing code is
  migration evidence, not approval to layer D65 onto the current form.
- **Intended Phase 13/16 behavior:** a cart line owns one-time or one exact
  recurring cadence; amount is per occurrence; multiple lines may share
  payment groups or compatible recurring cohorts; twice-monthly creates two
  execution legs. Accepted term versions and schedule epochs are append-only.
- **Best permanent path:** add one typed pre-acceptance line-schedule command
  after the real cart, D64 target sets, Phase 16 kernel, compatibility planner,
  and provider fences exist. Reuse D63's revision/CAS/idempotency and explicit
  preserve/clear primitives, but do not reuse its cart-wide grain and do not
  create a generalized transition engine.

### Corrected decision — normative requirements

**D65-R1 — bounded pre-acceptance scope.** A **Donor Gift-Schedule
Transition** changes exactly one unaccepted, editable cart line between two
distinct currently offered Phase 16 schedule identities. It never edits an
accepted contribution, recurring agreement, term version, schedule epoch,
occurrence, mandate, invoice, receipt, refund, ledger fact, settlement, or
accounting history. Accepted-plan changes use Phase 16's separately authorized,
effective-dated, append-only supersession path.

**D65-R2 — closed schedule identity.** A schedule identity is `one_time`, or
`recurring + exact cadence_code`. One-time is not a cadence. Weekly, every two
weeks, twice monthly on the 1st and 15th, every four weeks, monthly, quarterly,
semiannual, and annual retain Phase 16's exact meanings. Core never maps human
labels, provider Prices, interval counts, or suggestion positions.

**D65-R3 — exact pristine predicate.** A line may switch immediately without
confirmation only when neither it nor its dependency closure contains a
selected, typed, prefilled, custom, allocated, nonempty, or incomplete amount;
D64/CTA provenance; donor-entered anchor/start/end/final date; fee election or
estimate; amount/schedule-derived disclosure or review; payment selection/input;
future-use or mandate acceptance; wallet/authentication state; exposed client
secret; provider object/session; or submitted operation. Merely rendering
unselected choices or an untouched kernel-derived draft default is not material.

**D65-R4 — fast projection, authoritative target reproof.** The selector and
dialog may use the current sanitized projection with no provider roundtrip. The
line's frequency control precedes its amount, uses plain localized donor
language, and includes a safe purpose in its accessible name for multi-line
carts. A line with only one available schedule shows static text rather than a
disabled selector; an ineligible alternative is not selectable and has one
plain reason. Immediately before any clear, the server derives and re-proves
the exact owner, Tenant, Site, designation/purpose, Legal Entity/route, cart
currency, target cadence and policy generation, D61/D62 qualification, giving
timezone, schedule kernel/planner, amount-entry availability, and at least one
eventual admissible payment path. Every proposed preserved fact is independently
revalidated. A stale or incompatible target writes nothing and receives one
cause-specific explanation; Core never redesignates the gift.

**D65-R5 — consequence-specific accessible confirmation.** Material state
keeps the complete source cart authoritative while the shared Base UI
AlertDialog asks once:

> **Change this gift to monthly?**  
> **Your gift amount will be cleared. Where this gift goes will stay. You'll
> choose a new amount for each month.**

Only when applicable it adds **Your scheduled dates will also be cleared**,
**Your fee coverage choice will also be cleared**, and/or **You'll choose a
payment method again for this checkout**. Multi-line dialogs use a safe purpose
label. Actions are **Keep one-time** and **Change to monthly**, adapted to the
real source/target labels. Initial focus is the least-destructive action;
Escape, cancel, outside press, focus loss, browser back, or dismissal never
confirms. Ordinary styling—not red danger styling—is required.

**D65-R6 — server-owned preservation allowlist.** Preserve the affected line's
stable display lineage, order, currency, Tenant/Site/source/locale/entry
attribution, and currently target-valid designation/purpose. Preserve donor
identity/contact, tribute, anonymity, comments, and communication consent only
under their existing owners and only when their meaning remains valid. Preserve
every unrelated line's donor-entered amount, purpose, and schedule exactly. The
caller supplies no replacement copy; new fields clear until classified and
proved schedule-independent.

**D65-R7 — clear source money and schedule meaning.** On success, set the
chosen target schedule identity and clear the affected amount, raw/partial
input, D64/CTA provenance, allocation-derived amount, source cadence anchor,
start/end/final date, occurrence/leg preview, amount-per-occurrence and
combined-period totals, and every schedule-dependent impact, match, benefit,
tax, fee, disclosure, acknowledgement, or review projection. The target amount
is null and **Amount needed**, never zero, source digits, a target minimum,
ordinal-mapped suggestion, or inferred equivalent.

**D65-R8 — fresh target schedule.** Phase 16's current kernel derives the
target schedule under the current giving timezone: ordinary recurring cadences
start from the current civil-date default; twice monthly uses today when the
current civil date is the 1st or 15th and otherwise the next 1st/15th slot; and
no end date remains the default. No source date survives. Before acceptance the
donor sees the new **Today / Next / Then** result, exact per-occurrence amount,
count, and—when twice monthly—both slots and the combined monthly face amount.

**D65-R9 — smallest complete dependency closure.** Rerun the authoritative
Phase 13/16 compatibility planner. Supersede every draft one-time payment group,
recurring cohort preview, execution plan, total, fee estimate, authorization
hash, and review token whose membership or complete meaning changes. A sibling
line's intent survives even when its shared execution projection must rebuild.
A group may survive only when its complete authoritative fingerprint is
identical and no submitted or ambiguous operation exists.

**D65-R10 — fee semantics.** If the cart-header fee-cover election or any fee
basis/estimate applies to the changed line or affected group, clear the election
and all dependent estimates; do not carry one-time consent into repeated
installments. The confirmation names this consequence. A policy default may be
presented later only as a new suggestion/election, never as preserved donor
consent. D65 does not invent per-line fee settings to hide the dependency.

**D65-R11 — payment method, mandate, and consent isolation.** Clear every
selected/saved method, collected payment detail, wallet, future-use choice,
mandate/terms acceptance, mounted payment UI, client secret, and provider
binding attached to an affected group. A reusable provider PaymentMethod may
remain provider-owned, but is neither selected nor authorized for the target
until current terms are shown and fresh applicable consent is received.

**D65-R12 — target-native amount experience.** After authoritative success,
render the exact D64 target Site/currency/schedule set unselected plus **Other
amount**. A missing or intentionally empty set remains a clean custom-only flow
while qualified. Neither source digits nor suggestion position initializes the
target. No provider object is created until the donor chooses a currently valid
target amount.

**D65-R13 — one successor revision.** Success advances one cart revision with
cause `donor_schedule_change`, retains stable line lineage for display, and
creates a new semantic line fingerprint, execution plan, and provider
idempotency namespace. Browser history, BFCache, service workers, stale tabs,
guest merge, cache, analytics replay, or retry cannot revive predecessor
meaning. D65 does not require a generalized event-sourced cart.

**D65-R14 — provider-attempt and stale-secret fence.** An exposed, attempted,
authenticated, processing, mandate-bound, submitted, or outcome-ambiguous
provider object/session never authorizes the successor. Every predecessor
client secret or confirmation token must be unable to submit before target
payment becomes available. A provably unattempted, unexposed object may be
updated or replaced only through the pinned Payments adapter when its lifecycle
contract proves stale execution impossible; otherwise use a fenced,
reconcilable retirement.

**D65-R15 — closed in-flight states.** Disable schedule changes during
submission, confirmation, wallet approval, redirect, authentication,
`requires_action`, processing, capture pending, provider cancellation, webhook
reconciliation, success, or lost-response/outcome-unknown state for any affected
group. Say **We're checking your payment. This gift's frequency can't be
changed yet.** Reconcile first. A definitive terminal failure may return to a
new editable successor; success remains immutable.

**D65-R16 — atomicity, concurrency, and idempotency.** An authenticated command
binds owner, cart and expected revision, exact line, source/target schedule
identities, complete line/group fingerprint, current cadence and Site/currency
qualification generations, planner version, and one semantic idempotency
identity; without provider state, one transaction commits the complete
successor or nothing. A guest cart remains client-only: the request binds its
expiring guest session, minimal untrusted local revision/fingerprint, exact
line/source/target, current generations/planner, and semantic identity; the
server derives and validates one successor result, and local state changes only
after success or bounded readback. Core may retain an expiring non-PII command
outcome for retry/readback, not the guest cart or permanent donor history.
Provider retirement uses a fenced saga: source remains visible and target
payment remains disabled until proved. Duplicate delivery returns one effect;
reused identity with different meaning, concurrent edits, acceptance, or stale
policy conflict without silent merge.

**D65-R17 — failure preserves work.** Never optimistically clear browser or
payment UI. Offline state, timeout, `429`, `5xx`, authorization loss, stale
policy, conflict, provider ambiguity, or lost response leave the source cart
visible and authoritative. Read back the command/revision before retry. Known
failure says **We couldn't change this gift to monthly. Your one-time gift is
unchanged.** Incompatibility says **Monthly giving is no longer available for
this fund. Your one-time gift is unchanged.**

**D65-R18 — guest, authenticated, Tenant, and RLS safety.** Guest changes
modify only the minimal expiring Tenant-namespaced local cart after the server's
revalidated successor result and remain untrusted until later checkout
acceptance; they create no server cart, pre-identity Party, CRM, or payment
record. If a guest checkout already has server/provider state, only the
server-issued checkout-operation token can identify it and the server reasserts
its binding; caller-supplied group/provider IDs have no authority.
Authenticated carts remain owner-scoped, not tenant-membership-scoped.
Same-scope keys, immutable per-line scope, owner RLS `USING` and `WITH CHECK`,
direct-DML revocation, and privileged-path reauthorization prevent cross-owner,
cross-Tenant, cross-Site, or sibling-line mutation. The caller never supplies
group, cohort, provider, actor, or audit authority.

**D65-R19 — structural invariants and post-success UX.** One-time structurally
requires recurring cadence/schedule/mandate fields to be null. An editable
recurring draft may hold target cadence with unanswered amount/schedule input;
review, provider creation, acceptance, and activation require a positive current
amount and complete valid schedule. Only after success does Core destroy
affected payment UI, keep siblings visible, mark the line **Amount needed**,
focus its first amount control, and announce politely **This gift is now
monthly. Choose an amount for each month.** Totals show incomplete—not zero.

**D65-R20 — ownership, privacy, and evidence.** Phase 13 owns mutable line
intent/revision; Phase 16 owns schedule meaning/policy and accepted recurring
truth; D64 owns suggestions; Payments owns provider grouping/execution. URLs,
components, analytics, and provider objects own none. Normal guest exploration
does not create permanent audit history. Bounded authenticated command evidence
uses safe IDs/fingerprints, from/to schedule classes, affected dependency
classes, actor/session, cause, outcome, and timestamps—never exact draft amount,
client secret, mandate content, contact/tribute/comment, or sensitive ministry
label.

**D65-R21 — bounded implementation, rollout, and proof.** The ordinary path is
one O(lines + planned groups) operation under Phase 13's 50-line cap, using
batched current projections and pure existing kernels; it performs no FX,
geolocation, CMS, Stripe subscription update, or provider call when no provider
state exists. Land nullable unanswered draft amounts, exact schedule identity,
D64, the Phase 16 kernel/planner, CAS, preserve/clear classification, provider
fences, and old/new compatibility before enabling. Roll out pristine first,
then one non-pristine cohort, then every cadence pair. Rollback disables new
transitions but retains successor readers and never revives predecessor state.

**D65-R22 — deliberate non-goals.** No same-digit carryover, suggestion-position
mapping, amount conversion, equivalence table, proration engine, Stripe Price or
subscription amendment, accepted-plan editor, hidden undo store, permanent guest
journal, cart-wide reset, donor checklist, staff setting/capability/task,
approval workflow, or generalized transition/rules engine is created.

### Staff, missionary, and support UX

- Ordinary draft exploration creates no CRM record, task, staff notification,
  donor history, or Site-setting change. Missionaries neither see nor control a
  donor's unsubmitted frequency exploration.
- The D64 Site preview exercises the same shared donor frequency/amount
  component so staff can verify one-time and recurring presentation without a
  second implementation. Changing a preview frequency never edits the saved
  amount sets.
- Staff may see privacy-bounded aggregate selection/completion metrics. Support
  receives a correlated safe trace only for command failure, provider
  retirement, lost response, or reconciliation; it shows the line ID, from/to
  schedule classes, cleared dependency classes, result, and timestamps—not
  exact draft money, contact data, secret, mandate text, or sensitive purpose.
- Accepted recurring-plan changes appear only in Phase 16's durable plan
  history. D65's draft exploration never impersonates that authoritative
  history.

### Ruthless synthesis — strongest path forward

**Required before recording:** define D65 as pre-acceptance and line-scoped;
define the material-state predicate, safe preservation allowlist, source clear
set, target reproof, fresh schedule default, shared dependency closure,
provider/stale-secret fence, and exact confirmation/success/failure language.
Those amendments are now part of D65.

**Required in the consolidated spec/design:** model schedule identity and null
draft amount structurally; specify the one command, owner/RLS rules,
CAS/idempotency binding, dependency fingerprint, planner invalidation, provider
retirement/readback, and D64 target projection. Add scenarios to the governing
`donation-lifecycle` spec and active recurring delta before tickets or runtime
implementation. Physical tables may remain design-owned; invariants may not.

**Required implementation order:** (1) land the real typed Phase 13 cart,
currency-safe amount, Phase 16 schedule kernel/planner, and D64 projection;
(2) land the authenticated server transaction, guest validation/result/readback
path, and database/RLS/idempotency/provider fences behind a disabled feature;
(3) build the shared frequency/amount UI and accessible confirmation; (4) prove
pristine transitions; (5) enable one non-pristine cohort; (6) prove and enable
every remaining cadence pair; (7) retain successor readers on rollback. Staff
receive no configuration, notification, task, or CRM record for ordinary draft
exploration.

### Required proof

- All **72 distinct directed transitions** among one-time plus eight recurring
  cadences, plus the **nine same-identity no-op cases**; target-disabled,
  incompatible and stale cases; short month, leap year, DST, and twice-monthly
  1st/15th behavior.
- Pristine transition and each material trigger independently: selected,
  prefilled, custom, partial amount; D64/CTA source; every schedule input; fee;
  derived review; method; saved method; future use; mandate; wallet; exposed
  secret; provider object; and submitted state.
- Cancel, Escape, outside press, browser back, focus loss, offline, timeout,
  lost response, and command failure preserve the exact source cart.
- One-line, mixed one-time/recurring, cross-Tenant, group split/merge, shared
  one-time PI, recurring cohort, twice-monthly two-leg, and 50-line carts;
  unrelated line intent is byte-for-byte unchanged while exact shared state
  invalidates.
- Target D64 configured, reviewed-empty, missing, removed, and stale sets; no
  automatic selection; target amount null cannot review, create a provider
  object, accept, or render as zero.
- Cart-header fee election and selected method/mandate clearing with exact
  conditional copy; fresh current policy default cannot masquerade as consent.
- Every provider lifecycle state, stale secret/token refusal, retirement
  success/failure/replay, webhook reordering, and no provider call/object on the
  clean path.
- Duplicate request, same identity/different target, two tabs, line removal,
  acceptance race, guest-to-login merge, cache/BFCache/service-worker restore,
  and rollout/rollback mixed versions.
- Guest/authenticated ownership; cross-owner, cross-Tenant/Site/designation,
  forged group/provider IDs; RLS `USING` and `WITH CHECK`; direct DML and
  privileged-service negative tests.
- Keyboard and screen reader AlertDialog behavior, cancel-first focus, visible
  focus, status announcements, 44×44 targets, 320px reflow, 200% zoom/text
  spacing, long localization, CJK, RTL/bidi, reduced motion, mobile, low
  bandwidth, and no full-page reset.
- Removal of current one-time coercion/static frequency/flat-state assumptions
  before release, plus trace from D65 through glossary, ADRs, PRDs, consolidated
  OpenSpec, design, tickets, implementation, tests, and release evidence.

### Modern evidence and repository reconciliation

- Fundraise Up's current [suggested amount settings](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/suggested-amounts/)
  and [checkout frequencies](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/checkout-frequencies/)
  keep frequency-specific money and schedule behavior distinct; its
  [designation rules](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/designations-overview/) show
  why target purpose compatibility must be re-proved.
- Givebutter's current [suggested amount settings](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/2859751-how-to-customize-suggested-donation-amounts)
  independently support frequency-specific suggestions and Other amount.
- Stripe's current [SetupIntent guidance](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/setup-intents)
  requires future-use terms to cover anticipated frequency and amount
  determination; its [PaymentIntent lifecycle](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paymentintents/lifecycle)
  and [payment-method support matrix](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/payment-method-support)
  justify closed in-flight/provider fences. Stripe's
  [subscription-update API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/update)
  can change billing/proration; Core deliberately keeps that outside D65.
- W3C's current [redundant-entry guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/redundant-entry.html)
  supports preserving still-valid donor input; [error prevention](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-prevention-legal-financial-data.html)
  and the [alert-dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/)
  support one precise confirmation for consequential financial state.
- These sources support the constraints, not the exact clear-versus-carry rule.
  Clearing one affected amount is a Core product judgment because a schedule
  change changes per-occurrence commitment, target policy, consent, and payment
  eligibility. Repository authority wins over Stripe's newer preference for
  Checkout Sessions: D65 preserves Core's governed Payments adapter and does not
  reopen provider architecture.

### Documentation and implementation status

D65 is now recorded in the glossary, ADR-0013, ADR-0017, ADR-0061, Phases 5,
13, and 16, the Phase 24 roadmap, and this log. No new ADR is required: the
difficult boundaries remain owned by existing cart/cohort, schedule, and
currency ADRs. This grooming step changes no runtime, schema, provider object,
cart, Site policy, money, staff capability, or current OpenSpec. R1-R22 are the
exact future requirement language; the consolidated Phase 24 OpenSpec delta
must carry them before ticketing or implementation.

## D66 — When may a newly enabled Site locale become public?

Hope Relief adds **French (Canada)**. Navigation, giving controls, consent and
legal text, errors, and confirmations are translated, but several ordinary
stories still exist only in English. Staff need to prepare and preview the
locale without exposing a broken mixed-language giving journey. Donors need a
clear language choice and truthful fallback—not an indefinite launch blocker.

### Option 1 — explicit publish after a small critical-path gate; reviewed fallback for ordinary content (recommended)

Staff can add the locale, translate, and preview immediately. It becomes a
public selector/URL only after one explicit **Publish French (Canada)** action
proves a bounded critical path: navigation and global chrome; identity/account
and giving controls; money/schedule/fee/payment disclosures; consent, privacy,
tax/legal text; validation/errors; confirmations/receipts; accessibility names;
and required Phase 17 system messages. Ordinary CMS content may use the Site's
declared reviewed fallback locale, and the workspace keeps missing/outdated
items visible after launch.

Example: `hope.org/lang/fr-ca` is not public until its core French website is
ready. The adversarial review below determines whether an English-only story
may appear at `hope.org/lang/fr-ca/stories/wells` or must remain an explicit
link to its independently current English address.

**Pros:** protects consequential journeys without making one old story block a
locale forever; separates preparation from public activation; gives staff one
clear readiness summary and explicit action. **Cons:** requires Core to define
and maintain a small critical-path inventory and show fallback honestly.

### Option 2 — publish immediately and fallback for everything

Adding the locale immediately exposes its URL and selector; every missing value
falls back.

**Pros:** fastest and simplest activation. **Cons:** can expose mixed-language
payment, consent, error, legal, and confirmation experiences; staff can mistake
“locale added” for “donor journey ready.”

### Option 3 — require 100% of every Site item before publication

The locale stays private until every localized field and historical content
item is translated and current.

**Pros:** minimizes visible fallback. **Cons:** one obsolete story, optional
field, or constantly edited page can block launch indefinitely; encourages
placeholder translations and recurring cleanup rather than better donor safety.

**Recommendation:** Option 1. Shopify separates adding from publishing a
language, recommends translations be ready, and reports translated/outdated/
untranslated states. Contentful supports locale-specific publication, and
Payload supports field localization and fallback, while its independent
localized status is experimental/default-off. W3C supports explicit user-
selectable language links and correct page/part language metadata. D16's
repository-governing root behavior deliberately rejects browser-language
negotiation, so external negotiation advice is not imported.

Which D66 locale-publication rule should Core record?

### Founder answer

> Option 1 — critical-path readiness plus explicit publication. Really examine
> the UX and UI cleanly and clearly, make sure there will be no Supabase/
> database or Vercel issues, and make a clean note if Core must maintain a
> small, well-defined critical-path inventory.

### Final disposition

**Reject and replace.** Private preparation plus explicit proof-gated
publication is correct, but the Option 1 wording bundled three incompatible
requirements: it used routes outside D15's `/lang/{exact-locale}` grammar; it
made independently owned Giving, account, payment, receipt, and message
capabilities universal website blockers; and it proposed English rendering at
a French URL despite D15-D16's exact-locale invariant. External Shopify,
Contentful, and Payload fallback patterns cannot silently override those
governing repository decisions.

The corrected decision retains the valuable core and replaces the conflicting
parts: a small core-website publication contract, exact-locale public serving,
ordinary missing content omitted with optional explicit cross-language links,
and separate nonblocking capability summaries.

### Current behavior, intended behavior, and best permanent path

- **Current repository behavior:** there is no `public.sites` or Site Locale
  runtime table, `PublicRequestContext.siteId` remains `null`, the public reader
  accepts no locale, and Payload has no localization configuration or localized
  Site/Navigation model. The donor root emits one static GiveHope/English brand,
  canonical, OpenGraph locale, Latin font set, and `<html lang="en">`; the CMS
  catch-all treats `/lang/fr-ca/...` as ordinary slug text. Current cache policy
  keys by host/descriptor, while the reserved locale tag is invalidation-only
  and globally broad. There is no generated locale sitemap route despite static
  24-hour sitemap headers. These are migration blockers, not partial D66.
- **Intended repository behavior:** D15 owns stable explicit
  `/lang/{lowercase-exact-locale}` bases; D16 alone owns the locale-neutral root
  default; D14 independently owns exact-locale Giving addresses; D57-D58 keep
  authenticated accounts Tenant-wide; D60 keeps message readiness Phase 17-
  owned. One immutable locale-exact Public Site Generation is public serving
  truth.
- **Best permanent path:** normalize stable Site Locale identity under Phase 2
  A1a, add one code-owned Site Locale Publication Contract to the existing
  generation compiler, build the compact Languages workspace over source-owned
  evidence, and enable one authorized CAS publication only after compatible
  readers/cache/routing land. Do not build a readiness database, translation
  engine, fallback graph, or second serving head.

### Corrected decision — normative requirements

**D66-R1 — private preparation is not publication.** Adding a canonical Site
Locale creates one stable same-Site private context for authoring, review, and
production-faithful preview. It allocates or reserves no favorable public route,
language-menu entry, canonical, alternate, sitemap/search result, cache entry,
Giving address, message locale, account behavior, currency, payment behavior,
or default. Private, unknown, withdrawn, and preview requests remain
privacy-safe non-success.

**D66-R2 — Core must maintain one small publication contract.** This statement
is true and mandatory: Site Platform owns one code-reviewed, versioned **Site
Locale Publication Contract** in a typed exhaustive registry. It is not Tenant
configuration, database checklist rows, a translation percentage, or copied
source status. The current contract version and deterministic digest are pinned
in every candidate/release. A new universal core-website dependency must be
classified in the same change or CI fails; source owners review their adapters.

**D66-R3 — version 1 has exactly five core-website families.** The bounded
inventory is:

1. trusted Tenant/environment/Site/verified-host/stable-locale/route/release
   identity;
2. exact-locale homepage, complete Site frame and Brand Version, same-locale
   Navigation/footer/language control, and support/privacy/legal destinations
   actually invoked by that core frame;
3. known-Site not-found, error, unavailable, and recovery presentation;
4. complete exact-locale presentation of every applicable member of families 2
   and 3, plus correct `lang`/`dir`, script/font/bidi, responsive, keyboard,
   nonvisual, and accessibility behavior; and
5. canonical, reciprocal locale-equivalence, sitemap/robots eligibility,
   public serializer, immutable generation, and cache-serving closure.

Ordinary stories, archives, updates, campaigns, optional Pages, staff UI, and
independently activated capabilities are explicitly outside the inventory.
Adding a sixth family requires a reviewed successor contract version, never a
Tenant row or silent code path.

**D66-R4 — readiness composes source-owned evidence.** Each family adapter
returns owner contract/version, applicability and complete-member digests,
exact immutable source versions, evidence digest, and `ready | blocked |
unknown`. Publication accepts only a complete current `ready` closure. Missing,
partial, stale, unsupported, contradictory, or unknown evidence fails closed.
The Site card is a disposable permission-filtered projection with `checked_at`;
the command always reloads and re-proves sources. New drafts and ordinary edits
do not mutate a current release.

**D66-R5 — optional capability independence.** Site Locale publication does
not enable Giving, issue a D14 address, activate Tenant account localization,
publish a Phase 17 message locale, generate receipts, configure currencies, or
change payment/provider behavior. Giving, Messages, account, currency, and
payment summaries may appear separately as **Available**, **Needs setup**,
**Uses compatible fallback**, or **Status unavailable**, exactly as their owners
provide. They neither satisfy nor block the D66 core contract. If one becomes
public later, its own activation command proves its exact locale dependencies.

**D66-R6 — exact-locale serving; no Site-wide content fallback.** A public
`/lang/fr-ca/...` route always resolves as the stable French (Canada) Site
Locale and never substitutes, redirects, negotiates, or aliases another Site
Locale or uses it as field, fragment, resource, or Page fallback. Deliberately
authored quotations, names, titles, and multilingual passages remain permitted
when the source owner includes them and the renderer marks their actual
`lang`/`dir`. Public Payload reads set provider fallback off.
This explicitly preserves D15-D16 and rejects Shopify/Payload transparent
fallback as a Core public-runtime behavior. Message fallback remains the
separate Phase 17 whole-publication contract.

**D66-R7 — ordinary missing content stays honest and nonblocking.** An ordinary
French resource with no exact French publication never blocks the locale. It
remains absent from French Navigation, site search, sitemap, `hreflang`, and
favorable route projection. A source-owned component or placement may store a
typed same-resource alternative relation. The runtime may resolve and render
that authorized relation only when its target is present in its current
authorized public generation and is not source-revoked; D67 translation
freshness is a separate editorial fact. It never invents placement, label, or
equivalence. The French UI may then
say **Read this story in English** and link to the literal English URL; it never
silently redirects. Translation statuses are **Current**, **Out of date**,
**No public translation**, and **Could not be checked**—not quality scores. D66 does
not decide whether an already-published exact French resource remains public
after its source later changes; D67 owns that temporal policy.

**D66-R8 — compact Languages workspace.** **Site → Languages** is one responsive
list, not a matrix, wizard, or percentage dashboard. A row shows native locale
name, canonical code, generated prefix, one honest state—**Not public**,
**Needs attention**, **Ready to publish**, **Publishing**, **Published**,
**Published · changes to review**, D67 **Published · needs attention**, or
**Status unavailable**—one short exception count, and at most the next two
actions. **Checking** is temporary status text,
not lifecycle. No flags, raw message keys, Payload fields, route IDs, hashes,
provider objects, cache tags, or internal roles appear.
Every generated blocker, success, and handoff label uses the complete Site
Locale display label, such as **French (Canada)**, never ambiguous **French**.

**D66-R9 — exception-first detail and production preview.** The locale detail
shows `hope.org/lang/fr-ca`, one **Website essentials** summary, and only current
blockers by default. Each blocker explains what visitors cannot safely do,
names the human source owner, and provides one permitted action. Ordinary
content shows counts and one **Manage French (Canada) content** handoff into Web Studio.
Preview uses the real public renderer with exact staff/Tenant/Site/locale/path
authorization, signed short-lived Draft Mode, `noindex`, `no-store`, a visible
Preview banner, and Exit; it never populates the published cache or uses donor
data.

**D66-R10 — one proportionate publication action.** During Site Setup, the
first default locale is included in D6's one **Go live** review; Core does not
ask staff to publish the locale and then publish the Site. On an already-live
Site, a ready additional locale shows **Publish French (Canada)**. The concise
ordinary confirmation says: **Publish French (Canada)? This makes
hope.org/lang/fr-ca public and adds French (Canada) to this Site's language
menu. It does not enable Giving or change financial settings.** When the
safe aggregate is complete and nonzero for the viewer, interpolate the actual
count—for example: **8 ordinary pages will remain unavailable in French
(Canada) until translated. English equivalents appear only where an authorized
placement provides a labelled link.** If omitted items exist, say **Some
ordinary pages will remain unavailable in French (Canada) until translated**
and do not imply a complete total. Hidden content is never revealed. Actions
are **Keep private** and **Publish French
(Canada)**. No reason, typed phrase, separate approval queue, or new reviewer is
created.

**D66-R11 — one server-owned publication command.** `sites.publish_locales`
authorizes one packages/api command. The caller supplies only stable candidate,
expected-head/policy references, and a semantic idempotency key. Tenant, Site,
environment, locale identity, actor, capability, profile, evidence, target,
timestamps, and audit attribution derive from trusted server context. Outside
the lock it batch-compiles exact immutable source versions and Preview. Inside
one short stable-order transaction it reauthorizes current EffectiveAccess,
Site lifecycle, expected heads, route allocation, source vector, contract/
renderer compatibility, and candidate digest; then inserts the immutable
generation/proof, receipt, audit, and deduplicated outbox and CAS-advances the
sole public head—or rolls back all effects. No network call occurs under lock.

**D66-R12 — normalized relational identity without a second head.** Phase 2's
`default_locale` and `allowed_locales[]` become migration inputs/compatibility
projections, never dual write authorities. A bounded repeated `site_locales`
aggregate carries non-null Tenant, Site, stable ID, canonical locale under a
pinned standards profile, and immutable route identity after first use.
Deployment environment is structurally isolated per Supabase project/database
for this aggregate; it remains trusted command/cache/audit context rather than
a partially persisted Site key. A future shared multi-environment database must
first add a non-null environment discriminator across `sites` and every
dependent unique key/FK in one expand-and-cut-over migration. Full-scope unique
keys/FKs bind the locale to Site. Public Site Generation
and its exact-scope one-row head remain the only serving authority; there is no
`is_ready`, `is_public`, `translation_percent`, current flag, checklist table,
or second release head. New relational writers remain disabled while any old
array writer can serve. After source-proved backfill and shadow reads, one
cohort cutover fences every old array mutation before enabling relational
writers; retained arrays are one-way derived projections whose direct writes
reject. No bidirectional dual-write bridge is permitted.

**D66-R13 — Supabase, RLS, and privileged-path safety.** Operational relations
use primary keys, positive revisions, `timestamptz`, fixed-length checked
digests, same-scope composite FKs, indexed FKs/RLS predicates, one exact-scope
head key, immutable history, and `ON DELETE RESTRICT`. Enable and FORCE RLS;
revoke default `anon` access. Phase 12's central PDP/PEP alone enforces
`sites.manage_locales` and `sites.publish_locales`; RLS remains coarse defense-
in-depth for the one trusted Tenant and structural same-Site/locale boundary
and contains no role or capability predicates. Any permitted structural
mutation has equivalent old-row `USING` and new-row `WITH CHECK` so scope cannot
move. Views exposed to browser roles are security-invoker. Security-definer
functions use an empty search path, fully qualified objects, and minimal
execute grants. Because Supabase secret/service roles bypass RLS, revoke direct
DML from `anon`, `authenticated`, `service_role`, and secret-key application
paths on locale identity, generation, head, proof, receipt, audit, and outbox
authority tables. Mutation is possible only through the registered command
function/role. First locale activation, whole-locale withdrawal/restoration, and
locale-wide contract transitions require fresh human `sites.publish_locales`
EffectiveAccess and one sealed command binding request hash, expected heads, and
commit-time proof. After activation, later resource publications follow the
Tenant's source-owned manual, automatic, or scheduled publication policy and add
no second locale approval; they still bind source policy, locale admission,
expected heads, and safety. A registered single-Tenant NHI may compile,
reconcile, dispatch outbox work, or mechanically commit only an unchanged
command already authorized by the applicable source/locale policy under its live
owner ceiling; it may never supply a missing human decision or alter the command.
Caller IDs never become authority.

**D66-R14 — Payload/CMS boundary.** Payload owns localized content fields,
drafts, versions, Navigation, and editor provenance in `cms`; it does not own
operational locale identity, readiness, route allocation, or public head. Core
canonical locale IDs map explicitly to adapter codes. Public reads require
Tenant/Site/exact locale/published version and `fallbackLocale:false` through
the sole reader with `overrideAccess:false`; access hooks and negative tests
carry CMS isolation because Payload's role bypasses RLS. Navigation and every
critical CMS dependency require immutable/versioned publication before D66.
Payload's experimental/default-off localized status may later improve editing
only behind pinned-version proof; it never authorizes publication.

**D66-R15 — one generation prevents partial public activation.** Selector
membership, exact route, frame, content, canonical, reciprocal alternatives,
sitemap/robots, search inputs, renderer, and cache identity all derive from the
same immutable Public Site Generation. A committed release first shows
**Publishing French (Canada)… You can leave this page.** It becomes
**Published** only after readback proves the same generation in the exact
public URL, language menu, canonical/alternate metadata, and Core-generated
sitemap response. Search-engine crawl or indexing is external observation and
never holds the staff state in **Publishing**. Failed invalidation retries the
same outbox effect; staff never republish manually or create another head. The
committed Public Site Generation head becomes sole authority atomically. During
the bounded convergence window, lagging edges may return only privacy-safe
absence or prior output that a fresh authoritative-head check explicitly proves
still authorized; they never act as another head, rely on a stale favorable
check, or authorize favorable output independently.
Favorable publication is head-first and admission-allow second, so propagation
delay yields safe absence rather than premature public serving.

**D66-R16 — Vercel/Next routing and cache safety.** Locale publication is data-
driven and makes no Vercel Domain API call, consumes no Domains API quota,
requires no deployment, and never uses `generateStaticParams` as locale truth.
Next 16 Proxy performs no database/content readiness query, browser-language
negotiation, or sole authorization. Resolve request host/preview outside `use
cache`; pass Tenant, environment, Site, trusted host, stable Site Locale, public
generation, resource, audience, and renderer as cache arguments. Tags are
bounded stable-ID invalidation handles; bare `locale:fr-ca` is prohibited.
The admission adapter stores only a compact host/Site/locale/generation/status
tuple, never content, per-Page keys, or five-family evidence, and reuses A6's
one bounded request lookup. Its Edge Config implementation must prove current
read/write/size limits and cost; partitioning or provider replacement stays
behind the adapter. Exhaustion or unavailability denies admission and never
falls back to a database scan or broad allow.
Private/unknown/withdrawn/preview/adverse responses are `no-store`; favorable
authorization/current-head checks never rely on stale-while-revalidate.
Pre-stream host/Site/locale/public-head admission uses Phase 5 A6's generation-
bound, adverse-first Edge Config projection in Proxy, or an equivalently proved
non-React route boundary. It performs no database/content scan and is never
sole authorization; it is a deny gate and never grants authority, and the
runtime rechecks the authoritative head. Missing, stale, unknown, or
incompatible admission produces the privacy-safe non-success before React
streaming begins. Exact resource existence likewise resolves
before the first Suspense boundary where a true HTTP 404 is required. One
helper emits the complete metadata/alternate object; metadata and sitemap
consume the same generation.

**D66-R17 — lifecycle and drift.** Private preparation never auto-publishes.
Publishing does not make the locale default. A normal critical-source draft,
ordinary edit, new contract version, cache event, elapsed time, task completion,
or provider observation never unpublishes or mutates the current immutable
release. Only a current authoritative translation-input publication may derive
D67 **Out of date**/**changes to review**. Draft impact may appear only inside
the owning source's preview, and an unproved/incompatible profile transition is
**Could not be checked**, not freshness. Every favorable-to-adverse transition,
including withdrawal, Site suspension, and source-safety revocation, is
admission-fence first: persist and acknowledge the generation-bound adverse
Edge Config state before committing the authoritative adverse head. Unknown
fence outcomes reconcile before that transition continues; direct mutations
that bypass the order are prohibited. Once the adverse fence is acknowledged,
a failed, conflicted, timed-out, or unknown head transition keeps the fence
adverse, records **Needs attention** against the same durable command, and
retries/reconciles that exact transition forward. Core never silently restores
admission. Restoration requires an explicit cancellation/recovery result that
reauthorizes the actor and proves the current head, every affected source owner,
and the previously served generation remain safe. Staff see **French (Canada)
is unavailable while we finish applying this safety change.** When an authoritative source owner
explicitly revokes prior output as no longer true, lawful, private, secure, or
safe to present, Core fences the smallest complete affected dependency closure
and reuses last-known-good output only while still authorized. Withdrawal is a
separate explicit lifecycle command; it is blocked while the locale is the
D16 default or has unresolved source-owned public dependencies, preserves
route/release/history, removes favorable discovery through one successor, and
never redirects or selects another default.

**D66-R18 — concurrency, idempotency, and failure.** The command binds expected
Site/locale/public/profile/source/route heads and one request hash. Duplicate
same-meaning delivery returns the original receipt; the same key with changed
meaning conflicts. Concurrent publish/publish, publish/source edit, publish/
access revocation, publish/default change, Site suspension, or withdrawal has
one CAS winner and no mixed generation. Stale favorable-publication proof says
**Readiness changed—review the new item before publishing.** A known pre-commit
publication failure says **Couldn't publish—nothing changed.**
That copy is forbidden after an adverse fence; the unavailable safety-change
state and forward-recovery contract in R17 apply. Unknown outcomes reconcile
receipt/head before retry. Staff input and prior authorized public output remain.

**D66-R19 — visitor and accessibility contract.** Only current public Site
Locales appear in the language menu, using native names plus meaningful script/
region and no flags. Alternatives are trusted semantic links, never path-string
replacement, and work without JavaScript. Every public page server-renders
correct `lang`/`dir`, logical CSS, bidi isolation for dynamic names/codes,
script-capable fonts/line breaking, tenant-native brand, and accessible status/
failure behavior. Staff and public flows prove keyboard, screen reader, visible
focus, touch, forced colors, reduced motion, long/CJK/RTL copy, 320-CSS-pixel
reflow, 400% zoom, and weak-network behavior without downloading a locale
matrix.

**D66-R20 — bounded scale, observability, and evidence.** The five-family gate
is constant-size and evaluates adapters in parallel/batches. Ordinary status is
indexed aggregate counts plus paginated details, never Site × locale × field
scans on each view or public request. No build enumerates every Tenant/Site/
locale/Page. Release evidence records safe scope IDs, contract/profile/
renderer, exact source vector/digests, actor, receipt, head change, and
convergence—not translated bodies, preview tokens, sensitive ministry titles,
credentials, provider IDs, or PII. Technical traces correlate to durable
business receipts but never replace them.

**D66-R21 — migration, rollout, and rollback.** First land stable Site/Site
Locale relations, constraints/RLS/generated types, exact-locale Payload fields/
versions/access, additive public-reader/context/cache interfaces, and compatible
generation readers with all writers disabled. Evidence-inventory current
English output; never infer translation/publication from English copy, default
locale, `_status`, `siteId=null`, host traffic, or browser language. Backfill
only source-proved private locale identities; shadow-compile and diff complete
generations. Land readers before writers. While any old array writer can serve,
relational writers remain off; one cohort cutover then fences every legacy
array mutation before enabling relational writes. Retained arrays become
one-way derived compatibility projections with rejected direct writes—never a
bidirectional bridge. Then prove D6 first-Site behavior and one additional-
locale cohort. Activation requires every serving runtime to support the
contract/generation. Rollback stops relational writers without re-enabling
legacy array writes and retains compatible readers, relational history, current
heads, route allocation, receipts, and history; recover forward.
Prove PostgreSQL 15 and 17 plus the exact pinned preview Next/Payload adapters.

**D66-R22 — deliberate non-goals.** D66 creates no automatic translation,
machine-translation authority, linguistic-quality score, completion percentage,
per-field public fallback, Site-wide fallback chain, locale negotiation,
geolocation, flags, bulk publish, scheduled/automatic publish, translation
vendor abstraction, generic workflow/checklist/rules engine, duplicate content
editor, new approval queue, Giving/address/account/message/payment activation,
new serving head, Vercel domain/deployment workflow, or implementation in this
grooming step.

### Ruthless adversarial category review

Every required category has a material concern. Each row states the failure,
importance, severity/likelihood, evidence, answer effect, and permanent
requirement.

Current Shopify/Contentful patterns separate preparation/publication, while Core already requires immutable release generations. | **Narrows and replaces.** Keep a bounded core gate and explicit action; ordinary missing content is nonblocking but absent, not cross-language rendering; R1-R7.                               |
| Brittleness                                                   | **Yes — High/High.** Hand-maintained strings/routes drift when the shell changes; a one-time checklist goes stale.                                                                                                                                                                     | Five typed owner adapters, contract version/digest, same-change classification CI, and generation-by-generation affected closure; R2-R4/R17.                                                   |
| Technical debt                                                | **Yes — Critical/High.** A readiness table, Payload status, `allowed_locales[]`, cache flag, and public generation could become five competing truths.                                                                                                                                 | Normalize stable Site Locale, retain one Public Site Generation head, keep readiness derived, and disable Payload fallback/status authority; R4/R12/R14-R15.                                   |
| Edge cases                                                    | **Yes — High/High.** First default versus additional locale, single-locale Site, current default withdrawal, Site suspension, missing Page, unsupported script, source revocation, stale Preview, and existing D14 addresses change the outcome.                                       | Closed lifecycle, D6 integration, dependency-aware withdrawal, exact absent behavior, and complete proof matrix; R1/R10/R17-R21.                                                               |

| Failure modes                                                 | **Yes — Critical/Medium.** DB commit, outbox, CDN invalidation, selector, route, metadata, and sitemap can partially succeed; streaming can turn missing locale into a soft 200.                                                                                                       | One generation/receipt/outbox, prior-safe serving, convergence readback, no-store adverse path, true-status pre-stream admission, reconcile-before-retry; R11/R15-R18.                         |

### Ruthless synthesis — strongest path forward

**Required before recording:** correct the route grammar; explicitly preserve
D15-D16 no-fallback behavior; remove optional capabilities from the core gate;
define the five-family Core-maintained contract and its owner/maintenance rule;
separate first Site Go-live from additional-locale publication; and make
**Publishing** an honest convergence state. Those corrections are now part of
D66.

**Required in the consolidated spec/design:** normalize stable Site Locales;
define the Public Site Generation manifest/head, exact five adapters, command,
receipt/outbox, capabilities, RLS/grants/privileged path, Payload exact-locale
adapter, public request/metadata/cache interface, states/copy, and withdrawal
preconditions. Add a dedicated Phase 24 Site-management OpenSpec delta rather
than hiding D66 inside the broad parity change. No physical model may create a
second serving head or mutable readiness authority.

**Required implementation order:** (1) land accepted Phase 2 Site/Site Locale
and Phase 12 EffectiveAccess foundations; (2) localize/version Payload content
and Navigation with fallback disabled at the public reader; (3) land exact-
locale request context, route grammar, server-rendered shell/error/metadata/
sitemap and generation-compatible readers; (4) land schema/RLS/constraints and
the five-family shadow compiler with writers disabled; (5) prove current English
output and D6 first-Site activation; (6) build the compact Languages UX and real
Preview; (7) enable one additional-locale cohort; (8) expand only after
Supabase, Next, Vercel, accessibility, cache, SEO, and rollback proof.

### Required proof

- Adding a locale creates no public route, language-menu/search/sitemap entry,
  favorable cache, Giving/message/account/payment change, or default change.
- All five families: complete, missing, extra, duplicate, stale, unknown,
  unsupported contract/renderer, and a new unclassified universal dependency.
- Any number of ordinary untranslated Pages does not block; those Pages have no
  French favorable route/navigation/search/sitemap/`hreflang`; an explicit
  English equivalent link is exact, labelled, safe, and never a redirect/render
  fallback. Already-published out-of-date behavior is tested under D67, not D66.
- D6 first default Go-live versus a later Site Locale; publishing a locale does
  not invoke D14 Giving issuance, D16 default activation, D17 Plan, D57-D58
  account behavior, D60 message activation, currency, or Payments.
- Staff state/copy/action permissions for manage-only, publish, content-only,
  unauthorized, revoked-between-preview-and-confirm, and assistant paths;
  every generated label uses the complete Site Locale name; zero/one/many
  ordinary-page consequences use a number only for a complete safe aggregate
  and otherwise say **Some**, without revealing hidden items.
- Production Preview tenant/site/locale/path scoping, expiry, no token leakage,
  `noindex`, `no-store`, cache bypass, banner/Exit, and no donor data.
- PostgreSQL 15 and 17: duplicate locale/head/digest, cross-Tenant/Site/locale
  FKs, restrictive delete, referenced-FK indexes, direct DML denial,
  `anon`, authorized/unauthorized authenticated, old-row `USING`, new-row `WITH
CHECK`, table-owner, security-definer, and service/secret-role poisoning.
- RLS-introspection proves no role/capability predicate; Phase 12 PDP/PEP denies
  missing manage/publish capability, while direct authority-table DML is denied
  to `anon`, `authenticated`, service-role, and secret-key application paths.
- An NHI cannot initiate first locale activation, whole-locale lifecycle, or a
  source publication whose applicable Tenant policy requires a human decision.
  NHI compile/reconcile/outbox/mechanical-commit replays cannot alter request
  hash, expected heads, proof, or the already-satisfied source/locale policy.
- Deployment-environment isolation proves project/database binding, cache/audit
  coordinate separation, and no partial row-level environment discriminator;
  a simulated shared-environment design fails until Site and every dependent
  key/FK migrate together.
- Two publish attempts, source/default/access/Site-state/withdraw races,
  same-key replay, changed-key meaning, lost response, receipt/head readback,
  outbox duplication/failure/recovery, head-first favorable admission,
  fence-first adverse admission, unknown fence outcome, direct-sequence bypass,
  and one old-or-new complete generation.
- Adverse-fence success followed by head failure, conflict, timeout, lost
  response, forward retry/reconciliation, and explicitly reauthorized safe
  restoration preserve the adverse fence and exact honest staff state.
- Payload exact-locale reads with fallback off; draft/unpublished/cross-scope/
  versionless Navigation rejection; experimental localized status never affects
  authority.
- Alternative-language placement without its source-owned typed relation, an
  invented equivalence/label, or an unsafe/stale target is absent. Deliberately
  authored quotations/names/multilingual passages render with truthful nested
  `lang`/`dir` and are not misclassified as fallback.
- `/lang/{locale}` allocation/collisions, unknown/private/withdrawn/adverse true
  HTTP status before streaming, no soft favorable 200, no browser negotiation,
  no Proxy DB/content scan, no cross-locale alias/redirect/substitution; stale
  or missing Edge Config admission fails safely and runtime head recheck remains
  authoritative.
- Edge Config/alternative-adapter maximum item/config size, write/read budget,
  partition boundary, update propagation/readback, outage, rate-limit, and
  malformed/stale tuple tests prove one bounded lookup, no per-Page inventory,
  and deny-on-exhaustion behavior.
- Cache keys/tags include every D15 dimension; bare locale tags fail CI; cached
  404/410/redirect/adverse responses cannot delay launch or survive withdrawal;
  same-generation selector/page/metadata/sitemap; missed invalidation backstop.
- Canonical, self-inclusive reciprocal supported `hreflang`, provider-unsupported
  locale omission, sitemap splitting at D15 limits, no stale 24-hour static
  assumptions, and one complete metadata helper.
- Server-rendered tenant-native brand, `lang`/`dir`, fonts, logical properties,
  bidi isolation, native locale names/no flags, JavaScript-off links, keyboard,
  screen reader/status, touch, forced colors, reduced motion, CJK/RTL, 320px,
  400% zoom, mobile/desktop weak-network paths and production Core Web Vitals.
- Current global-English/static metadata/catch-all/cache migration inventory,
  source-proved private backfill only, shadow diff, mixed versions, reader-first
  enablement, legacy-array writer fence before relational writers, rejected
  direct array writes, no bidirectional bridge, kill switch, retained-reader/
  relational-history rollback, and forward recovery.
- Publication stays **Publishing** only for Core-controlled URL/menu/metadata/
  sitemap convergence; simulated search-engine crawl/indexing delay never holds
  the state or creates a second authority.
- Trace from D66 into glossary, ADR-0187, public-runtime ADRs, Phases 2/5/12/17/
  23/24, consolidated OpenSpec, design, tickets, implementation, tests, and
  release evidence with identical terms, five families, states, and owners.
