### Modern evidence and repository reconciliation

- Shopify's current [localization management](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/localization-and-translation)
  separates adding from publishing a language and exposes translated/outdated/
  untranslated status. Core adopts that preparation/publication separation but
  rejects Shopify's transparent primary-language fallback and browser redirect.
- Contentful's current [locale-based publishing](https://www.contentful.com/help/localization/locale-based-publishing/)
  supports independently published locales and exposes important fallback/
  workflow limitations. Core keeps provider mechanics behind its own immutable
  generation rather than depending on vendor plan/status behavior.
- Payload's current [localization contract](https://payloadcms.com/docs/configuration/localization)
  supports localized fields and fallback, but locale codes are provider input,
  fallback defaults on, and localized status requires an experimental flag.
  Core therefore disables public fallback and treats localized status only as a
  future editor convenience.
- Google recommends separate localized URLs and reciprocal/self-inclusive
  alternatives in its [localized-version guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions).
  Core emits only exact current equivalents and omits unsupported search codes
  rather than changing Site Locale identity.
- W3C requires truthful [page language](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page.html)
  and [language of parts](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-parts.html),
  and its [status-message guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
  supports quiet programmatic publication progress without focus theft. Core's
  deterministic D16 root decision outranks generic negotiation guidance.
- Next.js documents localized route/server rendering and
  [localized sitemaps](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/sitemap),
  while streaming can return 200 after `notFound`; D66 therefore resolves locale
  admission before streaming. Vercel's [CDN model](https://vercel.com/docs/how-vercel-cdn-works)
  and Next's [Cache Components revalidation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating)
  support generation-keyed caching and scoped invalidation, not cache authority.
- Supabase's current [RLS guidance](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)
  confirms grants and policies are separate, updates need old/new scope checks,
  views and service roles need special care, and secret roles bypass RLS.
  PostgreSQL's [constraint contract](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html)
  supports full-scope keys/FKs; referencing columns still require explicit
  indexes.

### Documentation and implementation status

D66 is now recorded in the glossary, new ADR-0187, the four public-runtime
ADRs, Phases 2, 5, 12, and 17, Web Studio's living spec, the Phase 23/24
roadmap, and this log. It explicitly supersedes Phase 2's scalar/array locale
authority and the roadmap's generic Site fallback-chain wording. No runtime,
schema, migration, route, cache, Payload configuration, Site Locale, capability
grant, Vercel resource, or current OpenSpec changed during grooming. R1-R22 are
the future normative language; a dedicated consolidated Phase 24 OpenSpec delta
must carry them before ticketing or implementation.

## D67 — What should happen when an already-published translation becomes out of date?

Hope Relief has a reviewed French water-project story public at
`hope.org/lang/fr-ca/stories/eau`. Staff then update the English source with new
ordinary program details. Separately, imagine the Legal owner replaces a
required giving disclosure because the old wording is no longer safe. These are
not the same kind of change.

### Option 1 — two-lane, source-governed disposition (recommended)

For ordinary source drift, Core keeps the last reviewed exact-locale publication
and derives staff-only **Out of date**. For a registered safety-governed source
successor, the authoritative source owner explicitly chooses whether prior
translation-dependent public use may continue or must be revoked. An adverse
choice fences the smallest complete affected dependency closure—which may be one
resource, one finite code-owned public dependency family, or, only for a
universal frame dependency, the Site
Locale—until an authorized current successor exists.

**Pros:** preserves stable donor-visible French content, avoids needless Site
outages, and gives authoritative owners immediate narrow safety control. **Cons:**
staff must understand that **Out of date** ordinary copy can remain public and
prioritize it appropriately.

### Option 2 — automatically withdraw centrally classified critical translations

A central Phase 24 classification identifies “critical” content and removes
linked translations whenever that source changes; ordinary content stays public.

**Pros:** narrower than withdrawing every changed translation and gives one
predictable platform rule. **Cons:** duplicates domain safety judgment, becomes a
generic risk taxonomy, and can still turn irrelevant changes or
misclassification into broad outages.

### Option 3 — automatically show the updated source language

The French URL immediately shows current English until French catches up.

**Pros:** visitors always receive the newest facts. **Cons:** violates D15-D16
exact-locale identity, surprises visitors, creates SEO/accessibility ambiguity,
and imports the fallback behavior D66 just rejected.

**Recommendation:** Option 1. It separates ordinary editorial freshness from a
source-authoritative safety revocation, keeps the smallest affected scope, and
uses immutable reviewed publications rather than timestamps or automatic
language substitution.

Which D67 staleness rule should Core record?

### Founder answer

> Option 1 — two-lane, source-governed disposition, but don't over-engineer it.
> Think about the best possible UX/UI that is consistent with our repo/product.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The two-lane direction is correct, but the
short option text did not define a source relation, distinguish an authoritative
publication from autosave, correct D66's overbroad human gate, prevent a central
safety engine, or specify the source-owned consequence review and race-safe
adverse transition. The binding decision is
[ADR-0188](../../adr/0188-retain-reviewed-translations-across-source-drift.md)
and the complete
[D67 adversarial review](./phase-24-d67-two-lane-source-governed-disposition-adversarial-review.md).

### Exact corrected decision

> Every exact target revision owns one immutable **Translation Provenance**:
> **Translated** pins exactly one explicit **Translation Basis**;
> **Independently authored** pins none and is not compared with a source;
> **Legacy · source unclassified** pins none and is **Could not be checked**.
> For D66 reporting, a currently public Independently authored target is
> **Current** (no translation follow-up), while its detail always says
> **Independently authored** and never claims a comparison. The basis binds the
> same Tenant/Site/stable resource inside the current deployment's structurally
> isolated environment, a distinct exact source
> locale, exact authoritative translation-input revision, and versioned source-
> owner canonicalization profile plus digest. A successor may deliberately
> classify legacy content; history never mutates. Core never infers provenance or
> basis from English, Default Site Locale, matching identity/path/text,
> timestamps, authoring order, provider fallback, or mutable provider status.
>
> Translation freshness and public-use safety are separate. Only a new current
> authoritative source translation-input publication may change freshness;
> drafts, autosaves, rejected or future-effective candidates, unrelated source
> facts, cache age, elapsed time, task state, and notifications do not. A
> mismatch under the same or explicitly compatible canonicalization profile/
> version derives **Out of date** and the locale presents **Published · changes
> to review**. A bare digest is never compared across unproved profile versions;
> incompatible, missing, or unreadable evidence is **Could not be checked**,
> never **Current**. A profile change alone does not invent freshness. Neither
> fact is a stored serving state.
>
> Ordinary drift leaves the last reviewed exact-locale version in the current
> authorized generation, including its existing route, Navigation, search,
> sitemap, reciprocal alternatives, and explicit authorized language-labelled
> links. Core does not edit, auto-translate, substitute, redirect, relabel,
> withdraw, or show a donor-facing stale warning. An authorized translator who
> can read the complete exact source comparison and authorize target review may
> publish an edited successor or **Confirm translation is still current**;
> either creates an immutable target successor review/revision, Translation
> Basis, and compatible generation against the exact current source—even when
> rendered bytes are unchanged—and conflicts safely if source or target changes
> during review. Without both permissions, Core exposes neither comparison nor
> Confirm and offers an existing permission-safe editor/admin handoff, not a new
> task.
>
> A registered source contract may classify a successor as safety-governed. Its
> existing source publication review then requires one unselected source-owned
> public-use choice: **Keep reviewed translations public** or **Make affected
> translations unavailable**. The first means only that prior source meaning
> remains authorized for public use; it does not attest translation quality or
> clear ordinary **Out of date**. The second appends a typed immutable revocation
> for the exact server-derived dependency set. The review names complete Site
> Locales and the smallest complete effect, reuses any reason already owned by
> that source, and creates no D67 reason, second approver, queue, task, timer,
> notification, or generic workflow/policy engine.
>
> The same registered source owner may also use its existing explicit adverse-
> only revocation command when containment cannot wait for a successor. That path
> needs no keep-public choice because the selected source command is already
> adverse, but it uses the same typed reason, exact server-derived closure,
> authorization, receipt, and recovery. Unsafe source meaning never waits for
> replacement copy.
>
> Every registered safety-governed unpublish, retire, tombstone, or delete intent
> must likewise resolve prior public use or complete adverse fencing before the
> transition. Referenced source/basis/disposition/dependency/receipt/audit
> evidence cannot be hard-deleted.
>
> An adverse disposition reuses D66's fence-first transition. The compiler—not
> the caller—derives the smallest complete resource, finite code-owned public
> dependency family, or universal Site Locale closure from exact generation
> dependencies. The family is not a Phase 12 authorization capability or Tenant-
> configurable taxonomy. A resource revocation
> creates a successor generation omitting that resource; the compact generation-
> level fence may temporarily deny the containing locale during cutover. D67
> creates no per-Page Edge Config truth. Unknown, incomplete, stale, ambiguous,
> or cross-scope closure remains adverse at its registered containing scope and
> reconciles the same durable command forward. The generation head remains sole
> favorable serving authority; a fence only subtracts and never selects another
> language or resource.
>
> Receipt-backed staff status is exact: **Publishing and applying the public-use
> restriction… You can leave this page**; after fence-before-head, **Public
> access is blocked while Core finishes the update**; after convergence,
> **Published** plus a permission-safe consequence; unknown result, **We're
> checking the result. Do not publish again.** **Couldn't publish—nothing
> changed** appears only after proof that neither fence nor head changed.
>
> Source owners retain source truth/revocation, target owners retain translation
> review, Phase 12 retains authorization, and Public Site Generation retains
> serving. Giving, payment, messages, privacy, security, and operational owners
> remain separate. A revoked dependency is not restored in place; recovery uses
> newly authorized source/target evidence and normal successor commands.
>
> `sites.publish_locales` governs first locale activation, whole-locale
> withdrawal/restoration, and locale-wide contract transitions. After activation,
> ordinary resource successors follow their Tenant-controlled source publication
> policy—including allowed automatic or scheduled release—and do not require a
> second locale-manager approval. Every transition still re-proves locale
> admission, source authority, expected heads, and safety.

### D67 staff and public UX

**Site → Languages** remains the D66 compact responsive list. A complete,
permitted aggregate may say **French (Canada) · Published · 3 translations to
review**, with localized pluralization;
otherwise it says **Published · changes to review** without a misleading count.
Partial safety closure takes precedence as **Published · needs attention** with a
permission-safe unavailable count; a universal locale fence uses **Needs
attention**. For a complete permitted ordinary-resource population, the four D66
buckets are evaluated in order and counted once: no current public target is
**No public translation** regardless of private draft; otherwise a public
Independently authored target is **Current**; otherwise legacy/unclassified or
missing/incompatible/unreadable required evidence is **Could not be checked**;
otherwise a public Translated target is **Current** for matching compatible input
or **Out of date** for drift. At one current watermark, `ordinary_total` equals
the sum of **Current**, **Out of date**, **No public translation**, and **Could
not be checked**. When authorized, **No public translation**
detail says **Draft exists** or **Not started**; otherwise it remains generic and
does not reveal a hidden draft. Independent detail remains **Independently
authored**. The locale detail opens on **Changes to review** and
explains: **These French (Canada) translations were reviewed before their source
content changed. Their current French (Canada) versions are still public.** Each
row/card names the resource,
type/path, exact source locale, and authoritative source-publication effective
time localized for display—not Payload `updatedAt`, autosave, or audit-log
time—and offers at most **Review changes** and **View public page**.

Web Studio keeps Payload's existing editor and version seam. A calm **Source
changes to review** banner loads an authorized comparison only on request. A
no-edit **Confirm translation is still current** action explains: **Keeps the
public page unchanged and records that you reviewed the latest source.** Success
uses a polite status message. Source-only, target-only, and combined/indeterminate
races preserve the draft and identify the actual permitted next review—for
example, **This French (Canada) translation changed while you were reviewing it.
Review the latest translation before confirming.** No modal, confirmation,
reason, or task is added to an ordinary source edit. Comparison and Confirm are
absent without complete source-comparison and target-review authority.

The rare safety choice stays in the authoritative source's existing publication
review, not Languages. Its unselected fieldset asks **What should happen to
existing translations when this update is published?** The Keep hint says the
previous source meaning must still be safe and translators still see changes to
review; the unavailable hint says public use does not return automatically and a
newly authorized replacement is required. The compiler/receipt always binds the
complete closure. Full labels/counts render only when the viewer may receive the
complete set; otherwise copy and action are non-enumerating, and detail permission
never blocks containment. The final action derives from visible closure—resource
count, public dependency family, whole locale, or **Publish and apply the required public-use
restriction**—and says Core will not substitute a language or withdraw unrelated
content. Translators, locale managers, callers, and AI cannot supply or waive it.

Ordinary out-of-date content has no visitor-facing status. An adversely contained
route is tenant-brand-native, privacy-safe, and server-rendered. Source-owned
typed presentation maps concealment to 404, permanent gone to 410, and transient/
unknown safety to `no-store` 503. It includes bounded `Retry-After` only when the
owning source/runtime proves a truthful interval; otherwise the header is
omitted. Soft 200 is forbidden. A resource result links to the same exact-locale
Site home only when independently current; public-dependency-family/locale
closure offers only an independently safe contact/status action and no cross-
locale link. It never exposes the reason or Asym branding and never substitutes
another locale.

All controls use Core Base Maia/Base UI primitives and exact Site Locale labels,
semantic HTML, visible focus, non-color status/diff semantics, WCAG 2.2 24×24
minimum targets or spacing exception with 44×44 primary-action target, and
complete keyboard/screen-reader/forced-colors/reduced-motion,
320 CSS pixel, 400% zoom, long-label, CJK/RTL/bidi, weak-network, permission-loss,
and no-JavaScript public proof. Progress/success uses polite `role="status"`;
blocking conflict uses a focus-linked error summary/one `role="alert"`; persistent
badges never repeatedly announce. Web Studio shows an honest unavailable state
when required JavaScript/network is absent and preserves work. D67 adds no locale matrix, percentage, dashboard,
eager all-locale/diff download, or second editor.

### D67 source of truth and invariants

- Source owner: current translation-input revision/digest and any safety-governed
  public-use disposition.
- Target content owner: immutable exact-locale revisions, three-way Translation
  Provenance, Translation Basis, review, and ordinary publication decision.
- Public Site Generation: sole favorable public selection and dependency
  manifest/head.
- D66 admission fence: deny-only projection during adverse cutover; never a head.
- Content Health/Languages projection: permission-filtered explanation and
  counts with evaluated source/target-head watermark; never freshness/
  publication/revocation authority. Current/zero/complete renders only when that
  watermark covers the current authoritative heads; otherwise Checking becomes
  Status unavailable/Could not be checked.
- Payload: qualified authoring/version/diff adapter with exact locale and fallback
  disabled; provider status is not Core truth.
- Vercel/Next caches and Edge Config: derived delivery/admission mechanics;
  ordinary freshness creates no Vercel write and revocation creates no Domain API
  call, deployment, or per-resource Edge Config inventory.

Current deployment environment isolation is one Supabase project/database, not a
partially persisted relational discriminator. Within that database, Tenant,
Site, resource, and locale keys/FKs enforce scope while trusted command/cache/
audit context pins the environment. Before any future shared multi-environment
database stores D67 data, one atomic expand-and-cut-over migration must add a
non-null environment discriminator to Site and every dependent unique key/FK.

Invalid states are prevented through immutable exact-scope records, same-scope
keys/FKs or typed versioned cross-owner references, restrictive deletion,
positive revisions, fixed checked digests, indexed FK/RLS/reverse-dependency
paths, provenance cardinality/distinct-locale checks, command-only writes, and
expected-head/set-digest compare-and-set. Phase 12 current EffectiveAccess is
commit-time authority. Applicable operational relations enable/FORCE RLS with
old-row `USING`/new-row `WITH CHECK`; views are security-invoker; hardened
functions use empty search path/qualified objects/minimum execute. Direct
`anon`, `authenticated`, service/secret-role application, Payload-bypass,
generic-worker, caller, and AI authority writes are prohibited. Actor, scope,
effective time, and audit derive from trusted context. Safety-governed unpublish/
retire/tombstone/delete cannot bypass disposition/fencing or hard-delete
referenced evidence.

### Adversarial result and proof

All 22 required categories have material concerns. None rejects the corrected
two-lane direction; together they require explicit provenance, separate axes,
source-owned rare disposition, generation-only adverse closure, D66 authority
correction, exact scope/authorization, semantic idempotency, proof-only
migration, accessible UX, and provider-neutral delivery. The complete category-
by-category failure, severity, likelihood, evidence, decision effect, permanent
fix, exact requirement, AC1–AC25 suite, and eight signal/threshold/owner/response
monitors are recorded in the linked D67 adversarial review.

Current runtime remains explicitly different: it has no Payload localization,
Site Locale resource context, Translation Basis, public generation dependency
manifest, source disposition, derived freshness, locale-prefixed donor route, or
durable CMS publication audit; Navigation is versionless. Phase 23 PR #1340 is
open and blocked, so D67 consumes only an accepted compatible future lineage/
generation/health contract. Migration must never infer source relation or
revocation from default locale, timestamps, equal text, `_status`, provider
versions, deletion, or logs.

D67 is now recorded in the glossary, ADR-0188, ADR-0187, ADR-0028, Phases 5, 12,
17, Phase 23/24 roadmap, Web Studio living spec, and this decision log. No
runtime, schema, migration, route, cache, Payload/Vercel configuration, OpenSpec,
ticket, task, or notification changed. A consolidated Phase 24 OpenSpec delta
carrying D67-R1–R16 and AC1–AC25 is mandatory before design, ticketing, or
implementation.

## D68 — What should “fallback-chain configuration” mean after Core's exact-locale no-substitution decisions?

### Why this needs your decision

The original Phase 24 outline promises fallback-chain configuration, but D15,
D16, proposed Phase 23 D22, D66, and now D67 deliberately prohibit silently
rendering or redirecting another language at an exact-locale URL. We should
either redefine “fallback” as an authoring/visitor-assistance preference or
remove the global setting before it becomes a misleading, brittle promise.

Example: Hope Relief's French (Canada) editor starts a story while French
(France) and English (United States) versions already exist. Later a visitor
opens a French (Canada) URL for a story that has no French (Canada) version. The
system needs to know which conveniences are legitimate without pretending those
locales are equivalent.

### Option 1 — authoring-source preference; public alternatives stay explicit (recommended)

Each Site may order enabled locales as **suggested translation sources** for
**Copy from…** and comparison. It affects only staff convenience. Public runtime
never follows that order; a visitor sees another-language link only when the
resource/placement owner explicitly records the D66 typed alternative relation.
Rename the setting **Suggested translation sources**, not fallback chain.

**Why this is strong:** it delivers the highest-frequency staff benefit, keeps
public meaning source-owned, works for independently authored regional variants,
and adds only a small ordered Site preference over existing exact-locale
lineages. **Tradeoff:** staff still make resource-level public-alternative choices
where helpful; a missing visitor page does not automatically gain a link.

### Option 2 — explicit visitor-alternative order with no substitution

Each Site orders enabled locales for a missing-resource assistance panel. Core
checks actual same-resource, current authorized versions in order and presents up
to a small bounded number of language-labelled links; the visitor chooses and the
URL changes. It never renders or redirects automatically.

**Why this is strong:** visitors get consistent recovery without hidden
substitution, and staff manage one Site-level preference. **Tradeoff:** a global
order may imply equivalence the content owner never intended, needs careful
privacy/SEO/safety filtering, and adds more public-runtime logic than Option 1.

### Option 3 — no global order; resource-owned alternatives only

Core stores no Site-level fallback/source order. Translation authors can choose
any currently permitted source when starting work, and each resource/placement
explicitly owns any public alternate link.

**Why this is strong:** smallest and most semantically accurate model, with no
global assumption across content families or regional variants. **Tradeoff:** the
authoring UI cannot prioritize likely sources and staff may repeat choices; Sites
with a consistent language hierarchy receive less convenience.

### Recommendation

**Option 1.** It turns a dangerous runtime-fallback promise into a clear staff
preference, preserves D66's explicit resource-owned public links, and adds useful
convenience without a new public resolver or translation workflow. Option 3 is
best if representative ministry research finds no repeated authoring-source
order. Option 2 remains honest but should be selected only if tested visitor
recovery value outweighs the semantic and runtime cost.

Which D68 direction should Core record: **Option 1 — Suggested translation
sources**, **Option 2 — explicit visitor-alternative order**, or **Option 3 — no
global order**? You may amend any option.

### Founder answer

> **Option 1.** It converts a dangerous runtime-fallback promise into a clear
> staff convenience while preserving explicit public meaning and avoiding
> another resolver or workflow.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The direction is correct, but the original
wording could still create a mandatory total order, automatic first-source
selection, hidden Translation Basis, authorization leak, or Payload/public
fallback. The binding decision is
[ADR-0189](../../adr/0189-site-suggested-translation-sources-are-authoring-only.md)
and the complete
[D68 adversarial review](./phase-24-d68-suggested-translation-sources-adversarial-review.md).

### D68 staff UX

**Site → Languages → Authoring preferences** contains one secondary section:

A Site with fewer than two authoring-eligible locales shows no source-order
control. The second authoring-eligible locale reveals the empty section without
adding a source.

- **Suggested translation sources**
- **Choose which Site languages editors see first when they copy or compare
  translations. This does not publish, replace, or show another language to
  visitors.**
- Empty: **No sources suggested. Editors can still choose any available
  source.** plus **Add source**.
- One item: full locale identity and **Remove**, without meaningless reorder
  controls.
- Several: semantic ordered list with visible position, **Move up**, **Move
  down**, **Remove**, explicit **Save changes**/**Cancel**, and optional drag as
  enhancement only.
- **Add source** remains visible in empty/one/many states while an unlisted
  authoring-eligible locale remains. Its unselected chooser appends to the
  unsaved order; it never silently inserts first.
- Success: **Suggested translation sources updated.**

Locale identity uses autonym, staff-UI display name, and canonical code—for
example **français (France)** / **French (France) · fr-FR**—with correct
`lang`/`dir`/bidi isolation and no flags or ambiguous **French**.

For every authorized missing target, a quiet **Start French (Canada)** sheet
offers two unselected paths whenever Copy is available: **Start blank — Create
an empty private French (Canada) draft** and **Copy from… — Choose an existing
language/version to create a private draft**. Start blank remains available when
no Copy source exists; its success says **French (Canada) draft started. It is
not public.** Choosing Copy opens **Copy into French (Canada)** and says: **Choose
the version to copy. This creates a new French (Canada) draft. It does not publish
or create a visitor-facing language link.** Sources begin unselected under
**Suggested for this Site** and **Other available sources**. The final action is
**Create French (Canada) draft**. Success says **French (Canada) draft created
from French (France). Review it before publishing.** Existing targets show
read-only Compare instead of overwrite.

Reorder is never drag-only: locale-qualified Move controls work by keyboard and
single pointer, retain focus on the moved row, update DOM and visual order
together, and politely announce **French (France) moved to position 1 of 3**.
Add focuses and announces the appended row. Remove uses a locale-qualified name,
focuses next, previous, or Add source in that order, and announces removal. The
complete setting/chooser passes Core Base Maia/Base UI, visible focus, 24×24
minimum/spacing and
44×44 primary touch targets, screen reader, forced colors, reduced motion,
320px/400%, long/CJK/RTL, weak-network, permission-loss, conflict, and truthful
staff JavaScript-failure proof. Source body/diff loads only after selection.

Weak-network copy is exact: ranking failure shows the ordinary unranked chooser;
only an authoritative empty set says no source exists; an unknown candidate
query says **We couldn't load translation sources. Try again.**; selected-source
fetch failure keeps selection and says **We couldn't load [locale]. Try again or
choose another source.**; save-network failure keeps the order and says
**Couldn't save suggested sources. Your changes are still here. Try again.**

On a save conflict, Core retains the user's unsaved order, fetches and displays
the latest saved order separately, never auto-merges, and says **Suggested
sources changed while you were editing. Your changes were not saved.** Staff
explicitly review and retry against the new revision or reset to the saved order.

### D68 source of truth and invariants

- Site Locale identity/lifecycle: Phase 2/24 operational Site Locale owner.
- Suggested source order: Phase 24 Site authoring preference in Operational
  Postgres.
- Exact source revision and eligibility: Phase 23/content source owner.
- Actual source used by a target: D67 Translation Basis.
- Public alternate link: resource/placement owner under D66.
- Public serving: Public Site Generation.
- Whole-message fallback: Phase 17.
- Payload, staff projection, cache, and UI: replaceable readers/adapters only.

Current environment isolation remains one Supabase project/database; D68 does
not invent a partial environment column. A future shared-environment database
must first scope Site and every dependent key/FK atomically.

### Adversarial result and proof

All 22 required categories have material concerns. None rejects the corrected
staff-only direction; together they require optional/partial order, explicit
unselected choice, provenance/public nonauthority, exact authorization,
structural storage, atomic CAS/idempotency, safe degradation, accessible UX, and

decision effect, permanent fix, D68-R1–R16 language, AC1–AC25 suite, and seven

## D69 — May **Copy from…** use a private saved draft?

### Why this needs your decision

D68 decides how eligible source languages are ranked, but not which saved
version of a language may be copied. Core can have both a current published
version and a newer private saved draft. This choice decides whether staff may
start the target from that draft instead of waiting for publication. It neither
publishes a version nor creates public fallback.

Example: Hope Relief is preparing an English (United States) campaign update and
a French (Canada) version for the same launch. English has a current public
version plus a newer server-confirmed private draft. May the French editor copy
the private draft now, or must they begin from the current public version?

### Option 1 — latest saved draft plus current published version (recommended)

For each eligible source locale, offer at most the latest server-confirmed,
copy-eligible private draft and the current published version. Group both under
one locale, label them **Saved draft · not public** and **Published**, select
nothing by default, and pin the exact chosen revision. Never offer unsaved browser
text, a save whose result Core cannot yet confirm, a version in unresolved
conflict, superseded recovery/autosave checkpoints, release candidates, or
arbitrary history. The current server-confirmed Working Revision may be eligible
whether it was saved automatically or with **Save now**. The copied draft stays
private. Before it can be published, Core rechecks the exact source and target;
if the source changed, the editor reviews those changes first.

**Why this is strong:** it lets translation proceed in parallel without
publishing early, bounds the chooser to two meaningful heads rather than version
history, and matches Phase 23's server-acknowledged revision model. **Tradeoff:**
staff must distinguish private from public source truth, and later source change
still requires the D67 review before target publication.

### Option 2 — published source versions only

Only the current authorized published revision appears for each source locale.
Private drafts never enter the chooser.

**Why this is strong:** simplest mental model and provenance; the source is
stable public truth before translation begins. **Tradeoff:** forces serial work,
delays coordinated launches, and may tempt staff to publish source content early
merely to unblock translation.

### Option 3 — bounded per-Site source-visibility policy

Each Site chooses **Published only** or **Latest saved draft and current
published** for future Copy choosers. Every displayed and selected revision still
passes the Option 1 bounds and authorization rules.

**Why this is strong:** supports both conservative and parallel editorial teams
without a per-resource rule. **Tradeoff:** adds another Site setting, makes the
same action behave differently across Sites, and still requires all Option 1
safety/status mechanics when drafts are enabled.

### Recommendation

**Option 1.** Parallel localization is a meaningful editorial advantage, and a
server-confirmed saved revision can be copied safely without treating it as
public or current. The essential protections are a two-head maximum, visible
**Saved draft · not public** status, exact revision pinning, no target publication
from an unproved basis, and source/target recheck—not forcing the source public
prematurely. Option 2 is the strongest simplicity alternative if tenant research
shows parallel translation is rare. Option 3 is valid but should require evidence
that organizations need different policies.

Should **Copy from…** use **Option 1 — latest saved draft plus current published
version**, **Option 2 — current published version only**, or **Option 3 — a
per-Site policy**?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — latest saved draft plus current published version.** The founder
asked Core to identify issues, produce an excellent repo-native UX, and prove the
choice against modern practice, database/authorization safety, reliability, and
technical-debt risk.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The two-head product direction is correct,
but the phrase **latest saved draft** is unsafe unless it means Core's exact
current server-acknowledged Working Revision rather than Payload/provider latest.
A rolling autosave row also cannot serve as durable provenance, and private
source meaning cannot become public through a translated target before D67's
public-source proof.

### Exact corrected decision

> For each source locale already eligible for the exact D68 action/viewer, Core
> projects at most two distinct versioned copy-manifest input identities:
> **Latest saved draft** is the exact current server-acknowledged D12 Working
> Revision when ADR-0191-qualified; **Current published version** is the exact
> immutable source revision pinned by D1's current authorized public generation
> when it also passes ADR-0191 qualification. Each exact head qualifies before
> enabled-candidate deduplication.
> Provider `draft: true`, `_status`, row order, timestamps, unsaved/debounced/
> in-flight/outcome-unknown/conflicted work, superseded autosaves, schedules,
> releases, restored history, prior publications, and arbitrary versions are not
> candidates. A schedule never creates a third choice. Equal compatible copy
> input collapses to one Current published version row only when the public head
> also qualifies, with **The saved draft has no newer copyable changes.** An
> unknown/unqualified public head never hides a qualified private sibling.
>
> D68 ranks eligible locale groups only. One Base Maia **Copy into French
> (Canada)** Sheet uses a single unselected **Source version** RadioGroup. A
> private row beside a current public sibling says **Latest saved draft — Not
> public · Has unpublished changes**; a never-published private-only row says
> **Latest saved draft — Not public · Never published**. Both use localized
> absolute saved time/timezone and explain that only work saved to Core copies; a
> public row says **Current published version — Published** and explains that
> visitors currently receive it. Nothing is recommended or preselected,
> including a one-row set. Opening focuses the Sheet title with
> `tabIndex="-1"`; Tab enters the first unchecked radio without selecting it, and
> closing restores **Copy from…**. The footer has Back, Cancel, and disabled-
> until-selected **Create French (Canada) draft**; there is no second
> confirmation. Success opens the target editor and leaves a persistent exact-
> source, not-public receipt. ADR-0190 owns complete loading, empty, offline,
> failure, stale-head, access-loss, target-race, unknown-outcome, focus,
> accessibility, mobile, RTL, zoom, and weak-network copy.
>
> One purpose-shaped private `no-store` read filters exact source-version and
> target-start authority before revealing candidates. One trusted resource
> command treats the selected reference/head as untrusted, derives scope/actor/
> time, reauthorizes source read and target create, and rechecks lifecycle,
> safety, copy manifest/profile/references, the selected source-lane head and
> eligibility, and target absence/head. It never substitutes a changed selected
> head; an unrelated change confined to the unselected source lane does not
> invalidate an exact selection. Concurrent starts have one structural winner;
> semantic idempotency reconciles lost acknowledgement.
>
> For private Copy, the source owner freezes or reuses one immutable, retention-
> protected Copy Source Checkpoint for the exact acknowledged Working Revision.
> Exactly one checkpoint exists for each complete same-scope immutable copy-input
> identity, so concurrent target locales reuse it. A rolling autosave row is never
> Basis evidence. The accepted adapter atomically
> commits checkpoint if needed, one private target Working Revision, Translated
> provenance, exact D67 Translation Basis, content-free audit, receipt, and
> result—or none. If physical owners cannot prove that boundary, private Copy
> stays off; Core adds no saga or repair workflow. Copy includes only the finite
> versioned source manifest and transfers no public, review, schedule, route,
> safety, assignment, lease, capability, validation, or provider state.
>
> A private checkpoint is not an authoritative source publication. Its target
> cannot first publish as Translated until D1's current authoritative source
> publication pins the same exact source revision represented by the checkpoint
> under the same compatible copy-manifest/canonicalization identity, or D67
> compare/update/**Confirm translation is still current** creates a reviewed

> state, second approval, setting,
> version browser, workflow, task, notification, public fallback/resolver,

>

### Ownership and proof

D12 owns Working Revision, acknowledgement, lease, checkpoints, and retention;

## D70 — How complete must **Latest saved draft** be before Copy offers it?

### Why this needs your decision

D69 proves that a private source can be copied safely, but acknowledgement only
means Core saved the revision. Payload drafts may intentionally be incomplete.
D70 decides whether Copy should allow useful in-progress content with visible
issues, require the source to satisfy every publication rule, or add a separate
staff readiness action.

Example: Hope Relief's English campaign draft has its final story and call to
action, so the French editor could start useful work today. The English image is
missing alt text and one required publication field still has a warning. Should
the draft appear as a Copy source?

### Option 1 — structurally safe draft with visible issues (recommended)

Offer an acknowledged private draft when the source owner's finite copy manifest
can be read and copied safely and every copied reference is currently permitted.
Publication-only completeness, review, alt text, SEO, route, Giving readiness,
and schedule may remain incomplete. The row says **Source draft has issues** and
explains **Some source publication requirements are unfinished. The new target
will be checked separately.** Core never copies validation approval, carries
source issue state into the target, or claims publication readiness.

**Why this is strong:** it preserves D69's parallel-work benefit, avoids forcing
premature publication completeness, and keeps validation owned by each exact
target. **Tradeoff:** translators may begin from source content that later
changes, which D67 already handles, and the UI must distinguish safe-to-copy from
ready-to-publish without dumping a long error list into the chooser.

### Option 2 — publication-ready private drafts only

Offer the private candidate only when it currently passes every source
publication-contract requirement except the final publish decision.

**Why this is strong:** the copied source is close to public and staff see fewer
known issues. **Tradeoff:** unrelated source-only blockers serialize translation,
duplicate a publication-readiness gate inside Copy, and can make the private lane
little better than waiting for publication.

### Option 3 — explicit **Ready for translation** checkpoint

Require an authorized source editor to mark an acknowledged revision **Ready for
translation** before it appears. Later edits clear or supersede that readiness.

**Why this is strong:** source editors deliberately signal semantic stability
without publishing. **Tradeoff:** it adds a new lifecycle state, action,
permission/audit/concurrency path, and coordination step with no demonstrated
tenant need; staff can mistake it for review or publication approval.

### Recommendation

**Option 1.** Copy should require structural and authorization safety, not full
publication readiness. It gives staff the parallel authoring value D69 was
chosen for while keeping the permanent architecture bounded to source
acknowledgement, finite-manifest qualification, target-owned validation, and D67
review of later source changes. Option 2 is the strongest conservative
alternative if Core cannot separate copy-safety validation from publication
validation. Option 3 is a good workflow only if tenant evidence later proves
editors need a deliberate handoff; adding it now would be overengineering.

Should **Latest saved draft** use **Option 1 — structurally safe with visible
issues**, **Option 2 — publication-ready only**, or **Option 3 — explicit Ready
for translation checkpoint**?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — structurally safe with visible source issues.** The founder required
current modern-practice proof and the same complete adversarial review before the
answer could enter the developing specification.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** Incomplete drafts are normal and should not
serialize localization, but Saved, Payload-valid, and Published are not Copy
proof. The accepted answer replaces vague “structurally safe” with exact,
revision-bound **Copy Qualification** and replaces generic issue inheritance with
a viewer-authorized, non-gating **Source Finding Summary**.

### Exact corrected decision

> Every private or public D69 source head must pass one purpose-specific Copy
> Qualification for its exact revision/digest and current compatible versioned
> resource/copy profile, manifest, canonicalization, qualifier, block/node/
> package versions, and declared count/depth/byte limits. The complete present
> input must be recognized and every value/reference must have one exhaustive
> treatment: copy the value, preserve a currently authorized target-compatible
> stable reference, create an owner-defined deterministic target repair, use an
> explicit meaning-preserving safe omission, or never copy. Unknown, corrupt,
> ambiguous, over-limit, executable, lossy, coerced, inferred, fallback-derived,
> unauthorized, cross-scope, silently omitted, unclassified, or zero-effect
> input cannot create a Translated target.
>
> After D12 side-effect-dark acknowledgement of an exact canonical revision, its
> source owner asynchronously starts or reuses a pure, bounded evaluation of the
> exact source content that emits content-free Copy Qualification Evidence,
> without delaying Save or changing D12's
> domain effect. A legacy D1 exact
> current publication may receive evidence only after retained-reader/digest
> proof; future D1 publication reuses evidence carried by the exact D12 revision.
> At most one durable immutable completed evidence result exists per complete
> same-scope revision/digest/source-contract-digest identity; that versioned
> collision-resistant contract digest covers retained schema/profile/manifest/
> canonicalizer/qualifier/block/node/package versions and declared limits. The
> complete identity is the idempotency/uniqueness key. Missing, in-progress,
> failed, or timed-out work is retryable unknown, not evidence. Bounded automatic
> reconciliation or authorized **Check again** idempotently requests the same
> identity through source-owned durable work rather than storing attempt history
> on the revision. Evidence records only source-input-qualified/source-input-not-
> qualified, material-effect presence, transferred-reference identities, and at
> most one bounded safe reason class. It never proves a future target locale/
> profile, actor, authority, lifecycle, or reference admission. Failure never
> blocks Save/autosave/recovery/Preview and the evidence is not a mutable
> `copy_safe` status, candidate, workflow, issue, approval, or publication result.
> Pending work coalesces to the useful current D12/private, current D1/public, and
> revisions referenced by retained D69 Copy Source Checkpoint/Basis frontier;
> superseded unretained autosaves do not create an
> unbounded queue or mutate completed evidence.
>
> The picker independently composes each exact private/public head's compatible
> source evidence with the exact target locale/profile plus one batched live scope,
> authorization, lifecycle, safety, and reference query without candidate body/
> diff/history reads. It deduplicates only enabled qualified heads; equal input
> prefers public only when public also qualifies. Missing/unknown/mismatched/
> incompatible evidence is not favorable and never hides a qualified sibling.
> After selection, the D69 command reads the exact body, verifies its
> digest/versions/limits, reruns complete qualification and reference proof, and
> only then enters the atomic write. Evidence alone grants nothing.
>
> Missing release values, incomplete editorial details, untranslated prose,
> accessibility details/suggestions, review, approval, paths, SEO, schedules,
> public dependencies, and D1/D66 closure do not block Copy when qualification
> independently succeeds. Accepted source/D32 **Details to finish**,
> **Suggestion**, and **Technical issue** classes remain Copyable; stale or
> unavailable checks remain separately unknown. A Technical issue blocks only
> when the independent Copy contract cannot be proved, not because of its label.
>
> D70 consumes a viewer-authorized Source Finding Summary bound to exact revision/
> digest, current compatible validator/rule generation, evaluated coverage
> watermark, `complete | partial | unavailable`, and authorized classes. Old or
> incomplete coverage never looks clear. D70
> creates no issue catalog/ledger, severity mapping, task, notification, waiver,
> approval, workflow, or issue viewer. Finding changes alone are display-only and
> never stale selection, alter idempotency, qualify Copy, enter Basis/receipt/
> audit, or transfer to the target. The target structurally validates during
> creation and independently derives exact-locale findings afterward. Target-
> check outage says **Target checks are unavailable right now. Your draft is
> saved and private**, with authorized bounded **Check again** composed beside—not
> replacing—any D67 blocker/action. The outage neither satisfies nor independently
> blocks later publication; D1/D66 alone validate it.

### Staff UX

The D69 unselected RadioGroup remains. A qualified source row may add **Has
details to finish**, **Has suggestions**, or both. Partial coverage retains known
classes and adds **Some source editing checks are unavailable**; complete outage
says **Source editing checks are unavailable**. Every such state explains:
**You can still copy this source version. The new French (Canada) draft will be
checked separately.** No state says Ready, Passed, No issues, or Ready to
publish.

Finding text is associated description, not the radio's entire accessible name.
No link/button/disclosure nests inside the complete 44-pixel row. Optional lazy
category detail and an independently authorized source-owner/head-accurate handoff appear
separately after selection. Finding loading/failure neither blocks qualified
Copy nor moves focus; later finding refresh scopes busy/status to its own summary
and leaves the RadioGroup operable. Target success keeps ADR-0190's immutable source receipt,
adds **Copied content needs review in French (Canada)**, derives only target
findings, and keeps D67's publication blocker separate.

Implementation must fix deficient shared Sheet/radio close/hit-target behavior
rather than fork local controls, use the full-width single-column mobile Sheet
with reachable safe-area footer, never line-clamp essential identity/finding/
time/recovery copy, and prove keyboard, screen-reader, touch, forced-colors,
reduced-motion, 320px/400%, long/CJK/RTL/bidi, and weak-network behavior. D71
decides how a structurally unqualified head appears; it is never a disabled radio.

### Ownership and proof

D12 owns acknowledged revision and exact revision attachment; D22/resource
owners own retained readers and finite profiles/manifests; D32/source validators
own findings; D70 owns qualification semantics and summary use; D69 owns the
projection/atomic command; D67 owns Basis/public-source review; D1/D66 own
publication/generation. Payload remains adapter only. D70 adds no capability,
standalone candidate/status/issue table, Site/locale state, setting, workflow,
public runtime, Vercel, Giving, currency, Stripe, message, receipt, or payment
behavior. This decision freezes no physical source-owner evidence table shape.

All 22 required categories contain material concerns. The complete failure,
impact, severity, likelihood, evidence, decision effect, permanent fix,
D70-R1–R18 requirements, AC1–AC30 suite, and twelve signal/threshold/owner/response
monitors are in the
[D70 adversarial review](./phase-24-d70-revision-bound-copy-qualification-adversarial-review.md).
ADR-0191, ADR-0187/0190, CONTEXT, Phases 2/5/12, Web Studio living spec, roadmap,
and this log record the corrected boundary. No runtime, schema, migration,
Supabase policy, Payload/Vercel setting, merged OpenSpec, ticket, or deployment
changed. Accepted D12/D22/D32 equivalents, D67-D71, consolidated Phase 24
OpenSpec, exact provider/profile coverage, and production-shaped proof gate
implementation.

## D71 — How should unavailable or unchecked source heads appear?

### Why this needs your decision

D70 independently evaluates both **Latest saved draft** and **Current published
version**. A head can be proved unavailable for Copy, or its availability can be
temporarily unknown because qualification could not finish. Simply hiding an
authorized head can make staff think work disappeared; showing it as a disabled
radio harms chooser semantics and implies it is almost selectable.

Example: Hope Relief's latest English (United States) draft contains a legacy
Impact Carousel block that the French (Canada) copy profile cannot safely
interpret. Its current published English version qualifies. Separately, a Spanish
published head could not be checked during a brief qualifier outage. **Start
blank** remains available. What should an authorized source reader see?

Every option below keeps these safeguards: one Base UI RadioGroup contains only
enabled qualified heads; an unavailable/unknown head and its action are never a
RadioGroup descendant and have no radio role, glyph, `aria-disabled`, or roving-
focus membership; no enabled head means no empty
RadioGroup; unauthorized heads are omitted without count/timing/error leakage;
proved unavailable and unknown never share the same explanation; automatic refresh
of non-gating finding/status metadata never autoselects or moves focus; gating
loss of a selected/focused head follows D69/D70's persistent cause-focus recovery;
and every qualified sibling plus **Start blank** remains available. User-triggered recovery keeps focus when possible; if
its action disappears, focus moves to the persistent candidate-results heading/
status and announces the result once while every radio stays unselected. From the
Sheet title, Tab reaches the first enabled radio when one exists, otherwise the
first truthful recovery or Back action.

### Option 1 — visible source-status list after the choices (recommended)

Immediately after the one RadioGroup, show an always-visible, nonselectable
authorized unavailable-head semantic list in the same locale/head order. Each row retains
its locale grouping visually, but no status/action is interleaved into or nested
inside the RadioGroup. Rows are ordinary list/description items—never disabled,
`role="status"`, alert, or live regions. Any recovery is a separate control
associated with its row; only one aggregate polite status announces load or
user-triggered retry results:

> **English (United States) · Latest saved draft — Not public · Unavailable to copy**  
> Saved August 30, 2026 at 10:42 AM ICT  
> Copy cannot transfer this content without losing information.

For unknown/outage, use distinct copy:

> **Spanish (Mexico) · Current published version — Published · Copy availability couldn't be checked**  
> Published August 29, 2026 at 4:18 PM ICT

The full locale, version kind, public/private state, and localized absolute saved/
published time plus timezone match D69's authorized identity cues; time is
associated description, never the only state. Author remains absent by default.
Without exact-head-detail authority, the entire row is omitted.

Offer a separate 44-pixel, source-owner/head-accurate action only when the bounded
plain-language cause is source-repairable and the viewer can act—for example,
**Open source draft** for the private head, or **Open source editor** to create a
successor to an immutable public head. Never imply the published revision itself
can be edited. A platform/profile cause keeps repair platform-owned and shows no
misleading editor action. Unknown offers authorized, bounded **Check again**.
Opening the source preserves exact head context plus a permission-safe return to
the same target Copy intent; return refreshes fresh and unselected.

If no enabled head remains, omit the RadioGroup and disabled Create action; say
**No source versions can be copied right now**, retain every authorized status/
recovery row, and provide D69's existing **Start blank**/Back path without another
confirmation. This state remains distinct from true empty, unauthorized omission,
and query failure.

**Why this is strong:** exact head, cause class, and valid recovery stay at the
decision point; staff do not confuse a platform outage with bad content; and APG
Tab/arrow semantics remain clean. **Tradeoff:** status rows follow rather than sit
inside their locale's radio subgroup, so locale identity must remain explicit.

### Option 2 — collapsed source-status summary

Show enabled candidates normally, then a permission-shaped summary such as **1
source version is unavailable** or **Copy availability couldn't be checked for 1
source version**. A Base UI Collapsible reveals exact authorized head identities,
distinct safe cause/status, and only cause-owned actions. A numeric count appears
only when the projection proves the complete viewer-authorized set; partial or
unknown coverage uses nonnumeric wording.

**Why this is strong:** keeps the common chooser visually quiet and can scale
across several source locales. **Tradeoff:** staff need another action and may
miss why their latest draft is absent.

### Option 3 — source-status notice before the version chooser

On **Start French (Canada)**, summarize each authorized unavailable/unknown head
with distinct wording and safe actions before the Sheet opens. The Sheet then
contains only enabled candidates; if none exist, it goes directly to **Start
blank** plus the same truthful status/recovery context. The notice consumes the
same purpose-shaped D69/D70 projection—no second resolver, cache, or body read—and
the chooser rechecks it on open rather than treating the notice as authority.

**Why this is strong:** produces the cleanest RadioGroup and presents all safe
alternatives before entering it. **Tradeoff:** separates the unavailable version
from exact source-version selection and adds copy to the prior step.

### Recommendation

**Option 1.** D69 admits at most two heads per locale, and the list remains inside
D68's existing bounded/page/search projection rather than expanding every locale
eagerly. This gives occasional ministry staff the clearest head-specific truth and
cause-owned recovery at the point of choice, without a new workflow or disabled-
control footgun. It also handles the harder case correctly: one equal-input public
head can be unknown while its private sibling remains a valid choice. Activation
must prove maximum-catalog usability/performance; Option 2 is the strongest
alternative if compact density is preferred. If Option 1 is accepted, failure of
its D68 bounded/page/search maximum-catalog proof blocks activation and requires a
governed spec revision; implementation cannot silently switch options or invent
another cap/pagination model.

Should D71 use **Option 1 — visible status list after choices**, **Option 2 —
collapsed status summary**, or **Option 3 — notice before the chooser**?

### Founder answer

**Option 1: one visible unavailable-head list immediately after the qualified
RadioGroup.** The choice must produce the best practical UX/UI consistent with
Core and the repository, and every later grill question must include a title,
plain-language context, a concrete example, well-considered options, and a clear
recommendation.

### Adversarial disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The visible list is the strongest choice,
but the informal answer was not safe or testable enough. The accepted design is
the corrected decision below. All 22 required review categories contain a
material concern under an unqualified implementation; none requires rejecting
the direction after the amendments. The complete failure, impact, severity,
likelihood, evidence, decision effect, permanent prevention, D71-R1–R16,
AC1–AC28, and named monitors are in the
[D71 adversarial review](./phase-24-d71-qualified-choices-visible-unavailable-list-adversarial-review.md).

### Corrected decision

For one exact authorized viewer, target, Copy action, and D69 private/public
head, the D68–D70 server projection derives exactly one rebuildable **Copy Source
Disposition**: qualified, proved unavailable, qualification unknown, or not
disclosable. Whole-query loading/offline/failure remains D69 chooser state and
never fabricates head-level unknowns.

Only qualified heads enter candidate deduplication and the unselected
**Source version** RadioGroup. Immediately afterward, one neutral **Unavailable
source versions** section shows authorized proved-unavailable and unknown heads
as ordinary semantic `ul`/`li` content in canonical locale/head order. A status
row is never a radio, disabled control, selectable card, row-click target, alert,
or live region. V1 displays no unavailable count. Unauthorized or otherwise
nondisclosable heads leave no row, count, placeholder, timestamp, reason, action,
response distinction, or avoidable timing distinction.

Each row repeats the permitted full locale, **Latest saved draft** or **Current
published version**, private/public state, semantic localized absolute time and
timezone, one bounded content-free explanation, and at most one independently
authorized cause-owned action. Locale text uses the accepted `lang`, `dir`, and
bidi-isolation contract; essential text never clamps. Repeated controls include
their locale and head kind in the accessible name. Static rows do not announce.
One initially empty aggregate polite/atomic status announces only user-triggered
recovery outcomes.

Check again reuses D70's exact evidence-work identity, coalescing, rate/backoff,
and lost-response reconciliation. Every recovery or source handoff reauthorizes
the displayed exact revision and proves it is still the applicable current
D12/D1 lane head; Core never silently substitutes a successor. A newly qualified
radio remains unselected. If a focused action disappears, focus moves to the
persistent **Source version** heading and announces one neutral result.

With zero qualified heads, Core omits the RadioGroup and disabled Create control,
keeps permitted status/recovery rows, and makes **Start {target locale} blank
draft** the direct primary Sheet-footer action beside Back/Cancel. Candidate and
status response members are additive, separately typed, and derived from one
authorization/head snapshot and cursor; paging retains a locale group that has
only authorized status heads. Compatible older readers see qualified candidates
only.

Copy Source Disposition is presentation truth, not durable truth. D71 creates no
table, Boolean, status row, grant, RLS policy, view, function, RPC, query, job,
poller, retry ledger, task, notification, workflow, provider call, Vercel/Stripe
behavior, public resolver, or publication authority. It remains one batched read
inside D69's p95 300 ms metadata budget. Activation must prove the Site Locale
owner's maximum supported catalog, including the worst case of two authorized
unavailable/unknown heads for every visible locale. If that maximum is not
governed or the proof fails, D71 remains off rather than inventing a cap or
silently collapsing the list.

### Why this survived the review

- It tells authorized staff why recent work is absent without contaminating a
  mutually exclusive choice control with nonchoices.
- It uses Core's installed Base Maia/Base UI Radio, Field, Item, Sheet, Button,
  semantic-token, focus, and responsive conventions instead of an app-local
  primitive or workflow.
- It preserves D12/D1 source heads, D70 evidence, live authorization, D69 Copy,
  D67 provenance, and D1/D66 publication as separate authorities.
- It fails closed for private-head disclosure and stale actions while keeping
  Start blank available.
- It adds no Supabase schema or Vercel dependency, and therefore introduces no
  new RLS, migration, provider-rate, rollback, or repair burden.

### Current behavior and proof boundary

Current `develop` has Payload draft/autosave behavior but no D69–D71 Copy heads,
qualification projection, or unavailable-source UI. Phase 23 PR #1340 was
verified open and blocked on 2026-08-30. This ruling is intended product behavior,
not shipped runtime. Implementation remains gated on accepted D12/D22/D32
equivalents, D67–D71, consolidated Phase 24 OpenSpec, exact installed-dependency
conformance, hostile authorization/concurrency/mixed-client evidence,
maximum-catalog performance/accessibility proof, and representative staff
usability evidence.

## D72 — When a Site has several verified domains, which one is its public address?

### Plain-language context

Phase 24 lets staff add and verify custom domains, but verification only proves
that a hostname is configured; it does not decide how visitors, search engines,
links, analytics, locale URLs, or Giving addresses should treat several verified
hostnames for the same Site. We need one simple product rule before designing the
domain workspace or its activation confirmation.

This is a domain-_role_ decision, not a Vercel setting. Vercel can attach several
domains and configure domain redirects, and currently recommends a `www` primary
with an apex redirect for CDN control. Google recommends choosing one
representative URL for duplicate pages and consistently aligning redirects,
canonical markup, sitemaps, and internal links. Provider capability is evidence;
Core remains the authority for which host serves or redirects.

Primary evidence:

- [Vercel — Deploying and redirecting domains](https://vercel.com/docs/domains/working-with-domains/deploying-and-redirecting)
- [Vercel — Adding and configuring a custom domain](https://vercel.com/docs/domains/working-with-domains/add-a-domain)
- [Google — Canonicalization methods and best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls)
- [Google — Multi-regional and multilingual Sites](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/advanced/crawling/managing-multi-regional-sites)

### Concrete example

Hope Relief has verified all three hostnames for one Site:

- `www.hoperelief.org` — the address on current campaigns;
- `hoperelief.org` — the apex form people often type; and
- `supporthope.org` — an older memorable campaign domain.

A visitor opens `https://supporthope.org/lang/fr-CA/stories/water-project`.
Should that hostname remain in the browser while serving the same Site, redirect
to the matching path on one primary hostname, or be unsupported except for the
usual apex/`www` pair?

### Safeguards every option keeps

- No Asym or `asymmetric.al` hostname or branding is exposed on Tenant public
  surfaces.
- Verification, DNS, TLS, and Vercel project assignment are evidence only; D6's
  explicit Core activation remains the sole favorable public authority.
- A hostname belongs to at most one Tenant/environment/Site role at a time;
  unknown, stale, transferred, conflicting, or unproved hosts fail closed.
- Canonical links, internal links, sitemaps, `hreflang`, Open Graph URLs, feeds,
  and generated public URLs use one server-owned effective origin—not request-
  header inference or CMS-authored absolute URLs.
- Redirect destinations are server-derived, same-Site, allowlisted origins with
  path/query handling proved against open redirects, loops, header spoofing, and
  locale loss.
- Domain roles never reinterpret, reactivate, or transfer retired or issued
  Giving-address meaning; D9–D15 remain authoritative.
- Staff see plain states—**Primary**, **Redirects to primary**, **Needs DNS**,
  **Ready to activate**, **Active**, **Needs attention**—with Preview/Activate/
  Change-primary consequences; they never edit Vercel IDs or canonical tags.

### Option 1 — one primary Site domain plus explicit redirect-only aliases (recommended)

Each live Site has exactly one current **Primary domain**. Any other verified and
explicitly activated hostname is a **Redirect domain**: it permanently redirects
the same valid path and permitted query to the primary host and never serves a
second copy of the Site. Staff may choose either apex or `www`; the UI can suggest
Vercel's `www` recommendation and an apex companion, but never activates either
silently. A deliberate primary-domain change previews the new public origin and
lets staff keep the former primary as a redirect when safe.

**Why this is strong:** visitors converge on one clearly branded address; links,
SEO signals, analytics, caching, cookies, locale alternates, and support all have
one origin; legacy campaign domains can continue working; and the model needs
only two public roles rather than a routing rules engine.

**Tradeoff:** the browser changes to the primary hostname after an alias visit,
and a primary-domain migration needs explicit impact review and redirect
continuity.

### Option 2 — one primary domain plus only its apex/`www` companion

Each Site has one primary hostname and may optionally activate only the matching
apex or `www` form as a redirect. Other campaign or legacy domains cannot attach
to the Site; staff keep them outside Core or migrate them once.

**Why this is strong:** it is the smallest domain model, easiest to explain,
secure, test, and operate, and it handles the most common typing variation.

**Tradeoff:** a ministry cannot preserve an older branded or campaign domain in
Core, which can break known links or force separate registrar/provider work.

### Option 3 — several serving domains with one declared canonical domain

Several activated hostnames may serve the same paths directly. One is declared
canonical for generated links, sitemap entries, and canonical metadata; every
serving alias emits the same canonical target. This is viable for organizations
that intentionally need several visible public brands to reach identical
content.

**Why this is strong:** visitors keep the hostname they entered, and campaign
domains can remain visibly branded without redirects.

**Tradeoff:** it materially expands origin, cache, cookie, analytics, security-
header, SEO, locale-alternate, support, and migration proof. Canonical markup is
a signal rather than a guarantee, so duplicate public origins remain real.

### Recommendation

**Option 1 — one primary Site domain plus explicit redirect-only aliases.** It
best matches Core's existing one-canonical-host language, produces the clearest
staff and visitor mental model, preserves useful legacy domains, and avoids the
duplicate-origin debt of Option 3 without the unnecessary restriction of Option 2. It also gives the later activation UX one honest question: **Will this domain
be the Site's primary address, or redirect to it?**

This recommendation does not freeze a table shape, Vercel endpoint, redirect
implementation, alias count, or `www` choice. Those remain design and measured-
limit decisions after the role invariant is accepted.

### Exact question

For each live Site, should Core use **Option 1 — one primary domain plus explicit
redirect-only aliases**, **Option 2 — one primary plus only its apex/`www`
companion**, or **Option 3 — several serving domains with one declared
canonical domain**?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — one primary domain plus explicit redirect-only aliases**, but only
if current evidence proves that it is modern best practice.

### Adversarial disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The one-primary direction is current,
proven practice. Vercel recommends a primary apex/`www` choice with the other
redirecting; Shopify, WordPress.com, and Squarespace use one primary plus
redirecting secondary domains; Google treats server redirects as a strong
canonical signal and recommends direct final destinations with aligned internal
links, canonicals, and sitemaps.

The informal answer is not accepted literally. **Alias domain** commonly means a
second serving origin, while Core is rejecting duplicate serving. A blanket
Vercel domain redirect would also run before D9–D15 Giving, D16 root, auth,
callbacks, APIs, and other route owners. The corrected roles are **Primary Site
Domain** and **Redirect Site Domain**; staff-facing copy says **Redirects website
visits**.

All 22 required categories contain a material concern under the unqualified
answer. None invalidates the corrected direction. The complete failure, impact,
severity, likelihood, evidence, decision effect, permanent prevention,
D72-R1–R18, AC1–AC40, ten signals, synthesis, and release gates are in the
[D72 adversarial review](./phase-24-d72-primary-and-redirect-site-domains-adversarial-review.md).

### Corrected decision

Each publicly activated, nonretired Site retains exactly one current **Primary
Site Domain**, including while D7 suspends website serving. It is one proved
Tenant-controlled HTTPS hostname that alone may serve the Site's favorable
website content and supplies the origin for newly generated internal, canonical,
`hreflang`, sitemap, feed, social/share, cache, and Public Site Generation
output. A private Site in Setup may have no public domain role; retirement keeps
immutable history without a favorable role.

A Site may have zero or more explicit **Redirect Site Domains**. Such a hostname
never serves duplicate website content or becomes another website origin. For
one exact current same-Site route-owner-qualified `GET`/`HEAD` navigation, Core
may return one server-derived redirect to the final equivalent destination on
the current Primary Site Domain. Arbitrary destinations, serving aliases,
rewrites, proxying, fallback Sites/homepages, chains, loops, automatic apex/`www`
activation, and Tenant routing rules are prohibited.

Website redirect is not every-route redirect. D9–D15 Giving/checkout, issued
addresses, protected actions, auth, preview, API, callback/return, webhook,
provider-result, control, and every other source-owned route run first and keep
their accepted behavior. A separately authorized existing Giving address may
continue directly on the hostname; that authority comes from Giving, never the
Redirect Site Domain role. D72 grants no new direct-route allocation.

The route owner builds the final target. A request to Redirect Domain `/`
composes D16 and points directly to the current explicit default-locale homepage
rather than chaining through Primary `/`. Only an owner-allowlisted navigation
query may survive. `Location` uses the approved explicit empty-fragment form and
must pass real-browser fragment-inheritance proof. Missing/retired/withdrawn/
restricted routes retain their privacy-safe `404`; authority failure is neutral
no-store `503`. Non-navigation methods never replay through the website role.

Vercel whole-domain redirects cannot implement D72. Vercel terminates TLS and
delivers the proved hostname, while Core's trusted pre-content/pre-cache
host/router projection evaluates the role and registered route owner. The public
request hostname comes only from a proved hosting-adapter request-target
contract; caller-set or cross-app `Host`, `Forwarded`, or `X-Forwarded-Host`
values cannot select Tenant, Site, role, or target.

No publicly activated Tenant website uses `asymmetric.al`, `vercel.app`, or
another platform-branded primary, redirect, canonical, or fallback. Platform/
provider hosts are private access-controlled preview infrastructure. V1 custom
public roles are production-only while environments use isolated Supabase
databases; a second public environment requires one platform-wide current-host
claim authority first. Exact Tenant wildcard public domains are outside D72.

Operational Domain authority owns canonical WHATWG/IDNA hostname identity,
complete Tenant/environment/Site binding, public-role generation, sole current
head, immutable history, authorization receipt/audit, and provider-evidence
references. One immutable complete Site-domain role generation contains exactly
one non-null primary plus its redirect membership. Current custom-host occupancy
is globally unique. CMS `primaryDomain`, proposed `primary_domain` and
`alias_domains[]`, DNS, TLS, Vercel, request headers, Edge projections, search,
cache, UI, imports, or AI cannot create public role authority.

Tenant-bearing Domain relations require complete same-scope keys/FKs, restrictive
delete, minimum grants, enabled/FORCE RLS, operation-correct `USING` and
`WITH CHECK`, command-only current-head mutation, and service/owner/function/
RPC/worker/Payload/import/support/AI poison parity. Any platform-global hostname
claim authority remains private/no-Data-API. Public role commands derive actor,
scope, capability, role, and audit attribution from trusted server context.

Phase 12 registers `sites.manage_domains` for never-public candidates, protected
setup details, and provider-proof requests; it grants no public effect.
`sites.activate_domains` governs D6 domain participation, Redirect activation/
deactivation, and D73 Primary successors; it grants no arbitrary target,
provider force-transfer, Site publication, Giving/address, callback/auth, cache,
or cross-Tenant authority.

Provider calls run outside authoritative transactions. Work coalesces, uses live
rate/reset headers and `429` backoff, and reconciles ambiguous outcomes. Local
role changes use expected heads, bounded locks, one semantic idempotency identity,
immutable receipt/audit/outbox, and original-result retry. Favorable activation
requires current complete ownership/DNS/TLS/provider/Site/route/public-generation
proof. Adverse authority fences Core first. No failure promotes another domain.

A Primary change cannot flip a domain string alone. It prepares compatible D1/
D66 Public Site Generation successors for every current public Site Locale and
atomically advances the host/origin/canonical/alternate/sitemap/feed/cache cohort
or nothing. ADR-0194/D73 requires the explicit former-primary website role and
route-specific redirect/cache consequence.

### Staff and visitor experience

**Site → Domains** is one Base Maia vertical workspace—not a provider dashboard
or matrix. **Primary website address** appears first; D7 website availability is
shown separately as **Website live**, **Website offline**, or its current state.
Redirect and Not-used-for-website/setup sections follow with plain states:
**Needs DNS**, **Securing domain**, **Ready to activate**, **Redirects website
visits**, and **Needs attention**. **Not public** requires complete current owner
proof that no favorable Core public route remains.

Each row shows one truthful next action, last checked absolute time/timezone, and
source-labelled provider evidence without raw IDs/errors, fixed rate limits,
canonical controls, or routing rules. Redirect rows disclose a bounded owner-
derived exception such as **Existing Giving links keep their current address**;
numeric counts require a complete authorized inventory. D72 adds no route scanner.

IDNs show safe readable Unicode plus canonical ASCII when different, with bidi
isolation and LTR technical rendering. Apex/`www` companion guidance is optional
and source-labelled; Core never creates, selects, activates, or promotes it
silently.

Visitors receive a direct HTTPS website redirect without an interstitial,
content flash, Asym branding, duplicate client analytics, or Redirect-domain
application cookie. The role grants no parent-domain cookie, CORS/CSP/auth/
callback/service-worker, or HSTS `includeSubDomains`/preload authority.
