## D82 — What should happen to a never-public draft path during the handoff?

### Decision title

**Disposition of the exact source-candidate D2 path claim**

### Plain-language context

D80 asks staff to review the new Page's parent and full web address. D81 then
creates the new Page and cleans the original Page in one transaction. A real
collision appears when the original Page's saved draft already staged the exact
address intended for the new Page.

The current D80 rule treats every source-owned draft path as occupied. That is
safe, but it can force staff to choose a worse address even though D81 will
release the exact never-public claim at the same commit. The opposite shortcut—
free the path first and claim it later—creates a race and a confusing two-step
workflow. D82 must decide the smallest safe ownership rule.

This question is only about one exact D2 candidate claim whose complete Core
route-effect history proves it has **never been selected by an activated public
generation or any public, redirected, or protected route effect and has no
platform-reserved, specialized source-owned, scheduled, safety, migration, or
Trash-retained owner other than the exact current private candidate claim**. Its immutable
private Placement Revision may remain in authorized History; that evidence is
not a current route claim. The question does not reopen the source live
`/about` URL, any historical public address, D78/D79, domain ownership,
redirects, or Vercel.

### Concrete Hope Relief example

Luis changed About's saved draft address from:

`https://hoperelief.org/about`

to:

`https://hoperelief.org/serve/short-term-teams`

He then correctly says the content now serves a different purpose. D80 creates
a new **Short-term team application** Page and D81 returns About's sealed Page-
owned Working heads to the `/about` release pins while separately managed
content stays unchanged. Should the new private Page take the already-reviewed,
never-public `/serve/short-term-teams` claim in that same commit, require a
different path, or begin without a final public-path claim?

### Safeguards every option keeps

- The source live `/about` route and every current/historical public address
  remain unchanged.
- Public, historical, redirected, platform-reserved, protected, root/Home, system,
  safety-withdrawn, or Trash-retained claims never transfer through D82.
- Staff see and review the complete tenant-branded proposed URL; no silent
  suffix such as `-2` is added.
- Database constraints and one D2 owner transaction decide uniqueness; UI
  preflight is never a reservation.
- Target creation remains private, `no-store`, `noindex`, and has no public D1
  route or canonical.
- Source and target must be the exact same Tenant, environment, Site, and
  locale; actor/scope/claim facts are server-derived and reauthorized.
- A stale claim, competing claimant, public/head/lease drift, or any failure
  preserves the source and creates no target.
- A later source **Restore as a new draft** never reclaims or overwrites a path
  now owned by the target. Editorial and Placement history remain independently
  comparable; authorized axes may restore separately, and a colliding old
  Placement requires an explicit new D2 source placement or returns the exact
  collision.
- D82 does not silently transfer the source Placement identity, descendants,
  Navigation, or sibling-order authority. Descendant and create-time sibling-
  position consequences require their own decisions.
- No option calls Vercel, DNS/TLS, redirect, deployment, search/cache, Stripe,
  or money systems.

### Option 1 — Atomically adopt the exact never-public candidate path (recommended)

The **Web address** field is prefilled with the source candidate's path and
labels it **From About's saved draft**. Staff can keep or edit it before the
review. If they keep it, the D2 owner verifies that the claim belongs only to
the exact sealed source Placement candidate and has never had public or
protected history. D2's D82 disposition inside the D80-D84 transaction
supersedes that source draft claim and creates the fresh target Placement claim
with no unowned interval.

Example:

> **Web address**  
> `/serve/short-term-teams`  
> **From About's saved draft**  
> Core has not published this address. It will be reserved for the new private
> Page after the move and will not be live yet.

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** it preserves the staff member's
already-reviewed intent, avoids a fake collision and extra step, and remains
race-safe because one D2 transaction changes ownership. The field is already
editable, so this adds no extra decision control or workflow.

**Cost:** D2 needs a narrow atomic supersession rule and proof that the exact
claim was never public/protected. That is more precise than a blanket “all
claims are occupied” rule and needs hostile concurrency tests.

### Option 2 — Always require a different target path

D80 never transfers any source Placement claim, even one that was only a draft.
Staff choose a different available target address. D81 still cleans the source
candidate and preserves its original path in protected source history.

Example:

> `/serve/short-term-teams` is part of About's saved draft and cannot be used
> during this move. Choose another address, such as
> `/get-involved/short-term-teams`.

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** it is the simplest ownership rule,
eliminates claim-transfer code, and makes the fresh Page/fresh path boundary
absolute.

**Cost:** it creates avoidable staff friction, can produce a worse public URL,
and makes a safe never-public claim unusable solely because the system cleans
it and creates the target atomically.

### Option 3 — Create an unplaced private Page and choose its path later

D80 creates the independent Page content and source clean result without a
final D2 Placement/path claim. The target editor clearly shows **Address not set
· Not ready to publish**. Staff later use the ordinary D2 placement review to
choose any then-available parent and path, including the old candidate path if
it remains available.

Example:

> **New Page · Private draft**  
> Address not set  
> Choose an address before previewing or publishing.

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** content preservation never blocks on a
route decision, and D2 remains a completely ordinary later action. It is useful
for teams that intentionally separate content creation from information
architecture.

**Cost:** it weakens D80's “review the whole new Page now” experience, creates a
new incomplete target state and later task, prevents production-faithful route
preview, and leaves the desired path open to another claimant.

### Recommendation

**Option 1 — atomically adopt the exact Draft-only Path Claim.** It gives
the best staff experience and the strongest ownership result without another
screen, state, or workflow. Modern transactional content systems support
compare-and-set document/claim changes, but the exact never-public eligibility
is a Core/D2 rule: verify it from immutable route history and database facts,
not staff memory or analytics. The existing editable Web-address field still
lets staff choose a fresh path when that is better.

Option 2 is the strongest minimal-implementation alternative: safest to explain
and easiest to prove, at the cost of needless path churn. Option 3 is the
strongest content-first alternative when route decisions genuinely should be
deferred, but it adds an incomplete state and later work that Phase 24 has not
otherwise needed.

### Exact question

When the sealed source candidate owns one exact path that Core has never
published or protected, should Core use **Option 1 — atomically adopt that reviewed path
for the new private Page**, **Option 2 — always require a different target
path**, or **Option 3 — create the new Page unplaced and choose its path later**?

### Founder answer (2026-08-31)

> Option 1 — Atomically adopt the exact never-public path, but make sure this
> is modern best practice, current, excellent for tenant/staff UX, deeply
> researched, and does not add overengineering, technical debt, or brittleness.

### Adversarial disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** Current Payload, Sanity, PostgreSQL,
Supabase, Vercel, Next.js, Google, and W3C primary sources support the component
practices—private drafts, configurable version history, transaction/CAS,
structural uniqueness, least authority, public/private routing separation, no
SEO work for a URL that did not move publicly, redundant-entry avoidance,
predictable inputs, and persistent status. Core's D12—not a vendor default—owns
immutable append-only meaningful checkpoints. No reviewed vendor defines this
exact command as a universal CMS feature. The permanent answer is therefore a narrow Core/D2
composition, not a generic slug-transfer feature.

The adversarial review corrected five dangerous ambiguities:

1. **“Never public” is Core-scoped and “never historical” is false.** The
   precise **Draft-only Path Claim** has never participated in an activated or
   public/protected Core route effect under any claimant. Its immutable private
   Placement Revision remains in authorized source History but is not a current
   claim.
2. **Prove the canonical key, not one row.** D2's sole compiler and complete
   route-effect history cover case, slash, percent-encoding, Unicode, locale,
   parent, framework/platform-reserved paths, every prior owner, and current policy
   generations. Unknown legacy/import history is ineligible; analytics, logs,
   provider checks, Vercel, and current-row absence prove nothing.
3. **Append/supersede; never reassign.** The immutable source Placement/claim
   identity does not move. D2's D82 disposition inside the D80-D84 transaction
   supersedes the exact current source private claim and appends a fresh target
   Placement plus claimant-ownership occurrence/version; a stable canonical-
   key namespace row may retain its identity. The result has one database-
   enforced current owner and no observable gap or dual owner.
4. **Reuse the existing product.** D82 extends the existing D2/D80-D84 plan,
   transaction, receipt, History, and PageShell review. It reuses D2's
   authoritative route namespace/provenance and adds no reservation, generic
   transfer API, second D82 route ledger, unplaced lifecycle, workflow, queue,
   saga, redirect, suffix, Vercel dependency, or money path.
5. **Do not hide hierarchy effects.** D82 changes no descendants, Navigation,
   or sibling authority. At D82's decision boundary, a dependent descendant
   path closure remained blocked for D83; ADR-0204 below now admits only its
   completely qualified D2-derived source closure. Create-time sibling position
   remains D84.

### Corrected decision recorded

When the exact sealed same-scope source Placement candidate is the sole current
private owner of the reviewed D2 canonical key, the placement group shows
source provenance and lets staff retain or edit it. Keeping the values is
eligible only after complete positive proof that Core has never activated,
served, redirected, or protected any canonical equivalent and that no
platform-reserved, specialized source-owned, scheduled, safety-withdrawn,
migrated, or Trash-retained owner exists other than that exact current private
source candidate claim.

Commit reauthorizes the source Placement-supersede and target Placement-create
effects; fences every D79-D81 head, lease, public pin, source claim, parent
chain, public base, canonicalizer, and route-policy generation; and first
reconciles any existing semantic receipt. The D82 disposition inside the same
D80-D84 transaction appends the fresh target Placement plus claimant-ownership
occurrence/version, supersedes the source current private claim,
retains source private History, and completes every target/source/checkpoint/
head/lease/receipt/audit/outbox effect or none. Same-input replay returns the
one result even though the target now owns the key; changed input conflicts.

Public and protected keys, unknown provenance, descendant-dependent closure,
scope/policy/permission drift, and any race fail closed. No source Revision or
claimant-ownership-occurrence identity is relabelled; a stable namespace row
may advance its current-owner version. No path is released first, overwritten, silently
suffixed, redirected, published, or sent to Vercel/Stripe/another provider.
Later source restore runs ordinary D2 and never reclaims the target key.

### Final staff experience

D82 adds no new step. The existing handoff placement group shows:

> **Parent Page**  
> Serve
>
> **Web address**  
> `/short-term-teams`
>
> **Full address**  
> `https://hoperelief.org/serve/short-term-teams`
>
> **From About's saved draft**  
> Core has not published this address. If you keep it, it will be reserved for
> the new private Page when these changes move. It will not be live yet.

Changing the parent or segment removes that provenance and returns to ordinary
D2 validation. Selection/checking never mutates, navigates, or moves focus.
The one action remains **Move saved changes to new Page draft**.

Late errors distinguish address conflict, source drift, invalid current route
rules, invalid parent, temporarily unavailable proof, permission loss, and
unknown response; all preserve input and say **Nothing was moved** only after
authoritative rollback proof. Competitor details are permission-safe. An
unknown response says **Checking whether the changes were moved...** and
reconciles the receipt before retry.

Success focuses the authorized target editor and persistently says:

> **Saved changes moved**  
> `/serve/short-term-teams` is reserved for **Short-term team application**.
> It is not live. About remains live at `/about`. Nothing was published.

The target header still shows exact Site, tenant domain, locale, and **Draft —
not live**. The review uses existing PageShell/Base UI/base-maia/Zinc Field and
status patterns, visible focus, 44-pixel targets, 320-CSS-pixel/400-percent
reflow, forced colors, reduced motion, keyboard/screen-reader operation, bidi-
isolated wrapping URLs, CJK/RTL/long labels, persistent errors, and weak-
network receipt recovery. Donors see no D82 state or route change.

### Required repository reconciliation

- ADR-0201/D80 has one sole exception to unrelated draft collisions: the exact
  ADR-0203-qualified source Draft-only Path Claim.
- ADR-0202/D81 includes D2 source-claim supersession plus a fresh target
  claimant-ownership occurrence/version in its one transaction while retaining
  private source Placement History.
- Proposed ADR-0146 and the `add-web-studio-cms` OpenSpec need an explicit
  atomic private-claim succession scenario without weakening namespace
  uniqueness.
- Phase 12 requires source Placement supersede plus target Placement create
  effects; target authority alone remains insufficient.
- D23 Copy-to-Site remains source-unchanged and treats its source path only as
  a suggestion; D82 cannot widen it.
- D1/D2/D3/D12/D33, migration, RLS/grants/functions, privileged/Payload paths,
  glossary, living spec, roadmap, OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets/tests/release
  evidence carry D82-R1-R25, I1-I24, AC1-AC60, monitors, and zero-public/
  Vercel/money proof.

The permanent decision is
[ADR-0203](../../adr/0203-atomic-adoption-of-exact-draft-only-page-path-claims.md),
and the complete 22-category review, 25 requirements, 24 invariants, 60
acceptance criteria, proof suite, named monitors, and synthesis are in the
[D82 adversarial review](./phase-24-d82-atomic-draft-path-adoption-adversarial-review.md).

## D83 — What should happen to descendant draft addresses when the source parent is cleaned?

### Decision title

**Disposition of source-tree descendant draft paths during a material-purpose
handoff**

### Plain-language context

D82 safely moves one exact private address claim from the source candidate to
the new private Page. D2, however, derives a child Page's full address from its
parent Page. If the source candidate staged a different parent or web-address
segment, that one change may also have produced draft-only address changes for
children that still belong to the source Page tree.

D81 cleans the source Page back to its current public Placement. The new Page
must not silently inherit the source's children, and the children must not lose
or keep misleading draft paths. D83 decides whether Core should deterministically
re-derive those source-only descendant addresses, require staff to resolve the
tree first, or make the handoff pause for a full descendant impact review.

This question changes no public URL, Page identity, parent relationship,
Navigation item, donor result, or Vercel state. It is about private D2 candidate
paths only. Create-time sibling position is a separate later question.

### Concrete Hope Relief example

About is live at:

`https://hoperelief.org/about`

Its child **Our team** is live at:

`https://hoperelief.org/about/our-team`

Luis's saved About candidate changed About's planned address to:

`https://hoperelief.org/serve/short-term-teams`

Because D2 derives child paths, the same candidate closure temporarily planned:

`https://hoperelief.org/serve/short-term-teams/our-team`

D80-D82 now create the independent **Short-term team application** draft at
`/serve/short-term-teams` and clean About back to `/about`. **Our team** still
belongs under About and Navigation does not move. What should happen to its
private planned address?

### Safeguards every option keeps

- About, Our team, and every other source child retain their stable Page
  identities, source parent relationships, locale, Site, permissions, History,
  and Navigation ownership. Nothing transfers to the new Page.
- The currently activated source tree and donor-visible URLs remain unchanged;
  no option publishes or creates redirects/canonicals.
- D2's existing canonical compiler, affected-descendant closure, route-policy,
  expected-head/CAS, database constraints, and D33 capacity profile remain the
  only path authority. No second tree or route engine is added.
- The review shows the exact affected count and permission-safe examples. It
  never calls an ancestor change “one Page” when other private addresses are
  affected.
- A descendant with incompatible/unacknowledged Placement work, a relevant
  Placement lease/head that cannot be preserved under D12, a schedule,
  permission gap, incompatible public/protected route obligation, or stale head
  blocks or uses its existing D2 owner action; nothing is overwritten or
  silently discarded. Unrelated Editorial leases do not block. The same Page's
  unchanged active route at the restored source-derived path is expected and
  does not itself block.
- Same-input replay has one result; any failure preserves the entire source
  candidate/closure and creates no target.
- No option calls Vercel, DNS/TLS, deployment, search/cache, Stripe, or money
  systems.

### Option 1 — Re-derive source descendants in place through D2 (recommended)

D2 seals the complete affected source-only closure. When D81 restores About's
private Placement head to the `/about` public pin, D2 deterministically derives
each unchanged child's private address from that clean source ancestor. In the
same atomic boundary, D2 supersedes every obsolete descendant draft-claim
ownership occurrence and records the qualified source-only successor claim
result for each newly derived key. Equality with the same child's exact current
public path is **public-pin convergence**, not a duplicate private claim. Its
old-to-new draft address still counts once when the keys differ. Existing child
immutable
Placement/closure History, parent identity, and existing sibling relationships
stay with About; no history row is rewritten. The compact handoff summary shows
the affected count and can expand to exact old/new draft mappings.

Example:

> **2 source Page addresses will return with About**  
> **Our team · Current saved address:** `/serve/short-term-teams/our-team`  
> **After the handoff:** `/about/our-team`  
> These Pages stay under About. Navigation and the live website do not change.

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** proposed D2 already requires one
complete affected-descendant closure and says unchanged descendants should not
need manual approval. This preserves source-tree meaning, avoids a separate
cleanup trip, and adds no new workflow or owner.

**Cost:** the sealed D80-D82 plan and transaction must fence the exact D2
closure, descendant head/dependency digests, and route-policy generation. Any
independent descendant conflict blocks instead of being auto-merged.

### Option 2 — Require staff to resolve the source tree before handoff

D80-D82 remains available only when the source path effect is a singleton. If
children are affected, staff use the existing D2 Page-tree/Move Page review to
cancel or settle the source ancestor and descendant candidate paths, then
return to the material-purpose handoff.

Example:

> **Resolve 2 Page addresses first**  
> About's saved move also changes Our team and Contact. Review those Page
> addresses, then return here. Nothing was moved.

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** it is the smallest implementation and
keeps D80-D82 strictly one-Page. Every tree consequence is resolved in D2's
ordinary dedicated surface before the higher-consequence handoff.

**Cost:** staff leave the flow and perform another review. On mobile or weak
networks this is slower and easier to abandon. If the required D2 action cleans
the source root, its private claim is released and D82 adoption ends; the target
address becomes an unreserved ordinary suggestion, must be checked again, and
may be taken before the handoff.

### Option 3 — Require a full descendant impact confirmation inside the handoff

D2 prepares the same atomic source-only claim succession as Option 1,
with the same existing immutable child History and same-Page public-pin
convergence rule, but the
handoff cannot proceed until staff open and confirm the complete affected list.
No per-child transfer or new parent choice is added; a child requiring an
actual decision still uses its existing D2 action.

Example:

> **Review 2 affected Page addresses**  
> Open the list and confirm that Our team and Contact stay under About before
> moving the saved changes.

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** it gives maximum transparency for
information-architecture-heavy teams and makes the complete private closure
unmissable without inventing subtree transfer.

**Cost:** it adds mandatory ceremony even when the outcome is mechanically
derived and publicly inert. Larger trees make a rare recovery flow feel like a
release workflow.

### Recommendation

**Option 1 — re-derive source descendants in place through the existing D2
closure.** It is the cleanest permanent behavior because it follows D2's
already-governing deterministic hierarchy, keeps every child with the source,
shows the exact impact, and avoids both hidden mutation and a second workflow.
It remains bounded: an unchanged descendant needs no manual approval, while
any independently edited, scheduled, protected, inaccessible, or stale
descendant blocks through its existing owner.

Selecting Option 1 or Option 3 would narrow D82's temporary singleton blocker
and I21 only for a completely sealed, source-only, qualified closure with these
claim/history semantics. Every cross-owner, stale, inaccessible, scheduled, or
otherwise incompatible descendant closure remains blocked. Neither option
authorizes subtree transfer.

Option 2 is the strongest minimal-implementation alternative and should remain
the safe fallback until the D2 closure can participate in the proven atomic
boundary. Option 3 is the strongest high-control alternative, but its mandatory
review cost is not justified for deterministic, private-only descendant
results without evidence that ministry staff need it.

### Exact question

When cleaning the source Page also changes private derived addresses for child
Pages that stay with the source, should Core use **Option 1 — re-derive those
source descendants through D2 in the same handoff**, **Option 2 — require staff
to resolve the source tree first**, or **Option 3 — require a full descendant
impact confirmation inside the handoff**?

### Founder answer (2026-08-31)

**Option 1**, provided current best practice, Core-consistent excellent staff
UX, atomicity, scalability, and the absence of avoidable brittleness/technical
debt survive a full adversarial review.

### Adversarial disposition

**Accept with required amendments.** The outcome is modern and proportionate,
but **re-derive in place** must not be implemented as recursive child Page
mutation. Payload's current Nested Docs behavior confirms that ancestor-derived
breadcrumbs/URLs normally cascade to descendants, while Payload transaction
guidance and a current reported nested-doc rollback/false-success issue show why
Core must not make provider child resaves its domain boundary. Sanity's current
Hierarchy **Public Beta** only corroborates direct-parent patterns; its stable
transaction docs, PostgreSQL's tree/constraint/locking primitives, and proposed
D2's bounded preparation support the architecture. WCAG Redundant Entry applies
to not retyping parent/path fields—not confirmation policy—while status/reflow/
error guidance governs accessible presentation.

### Corrected decision recorded

**D83 — Atomic Source-tree Draft-path Re-derivation.** When a qualified
D80-D82 handoff cleans the source ancestor and changes private derived paths or
breadcrumbs for same-Tenant/environment/Site/locale descendants that remain
source-owned, D2 server-computes and seals the complete exact closure.

D2 preserves every descendant's stable Page identity, direct parent, authored
local segment, sibling order, every existing immutable History row, Editorial
content, Navigation, permissions, schedules, references, public state, and every
other owner fact.
It recomputes only D2-owned private derived paths, breadcrumbs, route delta, and
current claim outcomes. Existing revisions are never mutated. If the accepted
D2 storage model requires a materialized descendant successor, it is one D12-
fenced cause-labelled immutable revision with identical authored inputs. It is
appended only when the accepted representation/monotonic Working contract
requires it; a redundant revision and a true old-key-equals-new-key no-effect
are never created.

Every old derived effect has exactly one result:

1. a qualified new private claim for the same descendant;
2. same-Page public-pin convergence with no duplicate private claimant or
   redundant revision; one qualified clean successor may append only when the
   accepted representation requires it, and a differing old private address
   remains exactly once in the sealed plan, receipt, mapping, and affected
   count; or
3. an unchanged-current-private-effect result when old/new derived address and
   corresponding breadcrumb output are identical—retaining the same claimant,
   appearing only in closure conservation, and creating no revision, claim
   occurrence, audit noise, or staff mapping; or
4. a complete pre-mutation blocker.

Every old/new key, exact Placement/dependency head, relevant lease/schedule,
permission/effect epoch, public pin, structural membership, and compiler/policy
generation must remain current. Another owner, protected or unknown history,
stale/inaccessible scope, independently incompatible Placement work, or an
over-capacity closure blocks the whole handoff and uses the exact D2 owner
action. If that action cleans/releases the source root claim, D82 adoption ends:
the target address is an unreserved ordinary suggestion, must win fresh
validation, and may be lost to a competitor.

High fan-out reuses one sealed, digest-bound D2 plan/impact artifact, bounded/
resumable preparation, and the active D33 Production Capacity Profile; D83
creates no private closure head. One short PostgreSQL transaction atomically
applies the admitted complete plan through existing Placement/claim boundaries,
performs D82's root claim succession,
creates the D80 target, cleans/checkpoints the D81 source, and appends the one
receipt/audit/outbox result—or changes nothing. There is no recursive child
Payload resave, one-write-per-child HTTP loop, authoritative partial batch,
D83-specific saga/queue, workflow, capability, second route engine, or
background compensation. An existing D2 executor may distribute inert prep;
skipped prep never defines closure membership or commit outcome.

The plan and receipt bind `closure_member_count` for conservation/capacity and
`changed_address_count` for staff-visible old-to-new changes; public-pin
convergence is included in the latter when the old private address differs.

Unrelated descendant Editorial drafts and leases remain untouched. Relevant
Placement work is preserved through exact dependency fencing or blocks; D83
never silently takes over or merges another editor's work. Stable Page-identity
references remain stable, literal path strings do not auto-rewrite, and old
preview credentials never retarget. Every preview use reauthorizes current
exact scope; tokens are routing context, not bearer authority. Any sealed-plan
artifact needed to render committed History or an authorized old preview is
retained under D2/D12 owner policy rather than reduced to a digest.

D83 changes no public generation, public canonical, public breadcrumb,
Navigation, redirect, search/cache/sitemap, donor result, Vercel/DNS/TLS,
Stripe, currency, gift,
recurring, ledger, CRM, email, or other external-provider/money fact. Qualified
same-database Payload persistence, the internal outbox, and private Web Studio
projection recovery remain allowed. D83 remains unavailable on current `develop`
because its Tenant-only scalar-slug Payload Page lacks the accepted D1/D2/D12/
D80-D83 substrate.

### Final staff, Tenant, and donor experience

The existing PageShell handoff review adds one always-visible consequence
summary only when at least one effective descendant address changes:

> **2 related draft addresses will update**  
> These Pages stay under About. Their private addresses will be recalculated
> from About's current `/about` location. Their live addresses and Navigation
> will not change.

**Review 2 address changes** uses the existing accessible disclosure for a
small exact list or D2's searchable/resumable impact view for high fan-out. The
count and public/non-public meaning are never hidden. Opening every mapping is
not mandatory because no qualified child needs a semantic choice. The existing
**Move saved changes to new Page draft** action is the one closure-level
confirmation; no checkbox, RadioGroup, modal, wizard, per-child approval, or
second CTA is added.

One exact row reads:

> **Our team · Draft address change**  
> **Current saved address:**  
> `https://hoperelief.org/serve/short-term-teams/our-team`  
> **After the handoff:** `https://hoperelief.org/about/our-team`  
> **Live address stays:** `https://hoperelief.org/about/our-team`

Preparation, descendant Placement work, permission-safe blocker, route
collision/protection, stale tree, capacity fallback, proof unavailable,
committing, unknown outcome, and success remain persistent cause-owned states.
At 320 CSS pixels/400 percent, mappings stack and wrap; URLs remain selectable
and bidi-isolated. Native disclosure/button semantics, visible focus, linked
errors, complete polite status, forced colors, reduced motion, keyboard/screen-
reader, RTL/CJK/long-title, weak-network, and reauthentication cases are release
gates.

There is no donor or visitor UI. The best public experience is proven non-
change.

The durable decision is

The full review records all 22 required categories, D83-R1-R29, 28 invariants,

No runtime, schema, migration, Supabase policy, OpenSpec delta, ticket, Vercel/

## D84 — Where should the new target Page appear among its siblings?

### Decision title

**Initial sibling position for the fresh material-purpose target Page**

### Plain-language context

D80-D83 now create one independent private target Page with a reviewed Parent
Page and web address. D2 also stores the Page's order among other children of
that parent. This order controls how staff see the Page tree and any future
explicit hierarchy-based listing. It does **not** automatically place the Page
in Navigation, change its URL, or publish it.

The source candidate may already contain a deliberate position because staff
previously moved it under the selected parent. Sometimes it contains no
meaningful position at all. D84 decides whether Core should preserve a proved
position, always append the new Page after existing siblings, or ask staff to
choose every time.

Modern CMSs support explicit sibling ordering, but there is no universal
default worth importing blindly. Payload currently uses fractional indexing
and supports generating an order key at the start, end, or between stable
neighbors. WordPress exposes Page order separately from hierarchy and
Navigation. The sound Core decision is therefore behavioral: preserve explicit
reviewed intent when it exists, use a calm deterministic default when it does
not, and keep Navigation independent.

This is target design only. Current `develop` has no accepted Site/locale D2
sibling-order model, stable-neighbor intent, or D80-D84 command substrate, so no
scalar/provider-order shortcut may implement the decision.

### Concrete Hope Relief example

Under **Serve**, Hope Relief currently has:

1. Volunteer
2. Mission trips
3. Resources

Luis's acknowledged About candidate was deliberately placed between **Mission
trips** and **Resources** while staging `/serve/short-term-teams`. D80-D83 now
create **Short-term team application** as the fresh private target. Should it
retain that reviewed neighbor position, appear last under Serve, or require a
new position choice in the handoff?

### Safeguards every option keeps

- D2, not Payload's opaque order key or the browser, owns the exact sibling
  order and final concurrency-safe insertion.
- The target stays private; no option publishes, changes its URL, or adds/
  reorders a Navigation item.
- D84 adds no source/descendant parent/order mutation. Only sealed D81/D82/D83
  owner effects may advance affected heads/change source-clean or derived state;
  D84 preserves the pre-existing relative order in their final cohort.
- Position is scoped to the selected same-Site/locale Parent Page or trusted
  server-resolved Top-level/root placement owner and uses a tagged start,
  between, end, or only boundary, never null or a copied provider value.
- A stored order value alone is not proof of deliberate intent. Option 1 applies
  only when the acknowledged D2 candidate links to immutable command provenance
  for an explicit tagged closed boundary, with stable neighbor IDs where
  applicable. The append-last branch likewise
  requires positive D2 provenance for the ordinary default/no explicit choice.
  Missing, unreadable, legacy, contradictory, or corrupt provenance requires
  ordinary D2 position review and is never silently classified as append-last.
  D84 adds no standalone intent flag/table, History axis, or second ordering
  system.
- A stale/deleted/reparented neighbor or changed parent triggers re-review; Core
  never silently inserts somewhere other than the reviewed outcome.
- Keyboard-accessible controls are required anywhere drag-and-drop is offered;
  mobile and assistive-technology users never depend on dragging.
- No option adds a general Navigation-order coupling, public resolver, workflow,
  capability, Vercel call, donor UI, or money effect.

### Option 1 — preserve an explicit valid position; otherwise append last (recommended)

If the exact acknowledged source candidate included a closed explicit start,
between, end, or only boundary under the same trusted Parent Page/Top-level
cohort and that boundary remains current, the new target takes that position.
Core generates its own D2 order value; it never copies/reassigns the source
Page's opaque order key. If D2 provenance positively records the ordinary
default/no explicit position, the target appends after the tail of the locked
post-D81/D82/D83 final cohort. If a reviewed boundary becomes stale, staff use
the ordinary D2 review before commit rather than silently falling back. Unknown
provenance also requires review.

Example:

> **Page tree position**  
> After Mission trips · Before Resources  
> The new Page will not be added to Navigation.

Default branch:

> **Page tree position**  
> No reviewed position was saved.  
> **Result:** Last under Serve  
> Navigation will not change.

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** it preserves already-reviewed
information-architecture intent, gives a predictable zero-question default,
and avoids another control in a rare handoff. Stable neighbor anchors plus D2
CAS are provider-neutral and survive fractional-order implementations.

**Cost:** D2's existing immutable command provenance must positively distinguish
explicit intent, a known append default, and unknown state, then fence the exact
semantic gap. That is a bounded general D2 responsibility, but it needs exact
semantics and concurrency tests.

### Option 2 — always append the new target last

Every target receives a D2-generated position after the current last Page in
the selected Parent Page/Top-level cohort. Staff can later use the ordinary
Page-tree reorder action if desired.

Example:

> **Page tree position**  
> Last under Serve  
> You can reorder it later. Navigation will not change.

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** it is maximally simple, predictable,
and easy to prove. It never implies that a position belonging to the source
Page transferred to the target.

**Cost:** it discards deliberate staged ordering and can create a second cleanup
task immediately after a handoff. For large sibling sets, “fix it later” is
needless friction and easier to forget.

### Option 3 — require an explicit position choice in the handoff

The placement group always includes an accessible **Position under Serve**
control using stable before/after labels. Drag-and-drop may supplement it but
never replace it. The handoff cannot proceed until staff review the position.

Example:

> **Position under Serve**  
> After: Mission trips  
> Before: Resources

**Why this is a genuinely good option:** it provides maximum conscious control
for tightly curated Page trees and never infers whether the source position was
intentional.

**Cost:** every handoff adds a decision even when staff never care about tree
order. The control is more complex on mobile, in long/translated sibling lists,
and under concurrent reorder; it risks making Page-tree order look like
Navigation order despite repeated copy.

### Recommendation

**Option 1 — preserve an explicit valid position; otherwise append last.** It
best respects acknowledged staff intent while retaining a simple deterministic
default and no extra question for the common case. The critical amendment is
that “preserve” means re-create one tagged closed boundary, using stable
neighbor identities where applicable, through D2; it never means copy the
source Page's order value or move that source Page. A stale explicit boundary
blocks for a refreshed review rather than silently appending. Unknown
provenance also blocks; append-last is a positively recorded default resolved
at commit, not a guess.

Option 2 is the strongest minimal alternative if Core cannot reliably
distinguish explicit position intent in the accepted D2 model. Option 3 is
appropriate only if usability evidence shows staff routinely need to choose
tree order during this already-rare handoff; current evidence does not justify
making it mandatory.

### Exact question

When D80-D83 creates the fresh private target Page, should Core use **Option 1
— preserve an explicit still-valid sibling position and otherwise append
last**, **Option 2 — always append last**, or **Option 3 — require staff to
choose a position in the handoff**?

### Founder answer

**Option 1 — Preserve an explicit valid position; otherwise append last.** The
answer was accepted with the required amendments below after current primary-
source research, canonical-repository review, and an independent adversarial
pass.

### Final disposition

**Accept with required amendments.**

Option 1 is the strongest product choice only when “explicit” and “otherwise”
are proved rather than inferred. Proposed D2 currently owns sibling order but
does not distinguish a deliberate staff choice from its ordinary default,
imported/migrated order, or a provider rank. Therefore:

- preserve only immutable D2 placement-command provenance proving a tagged
  start/between/end/only boundary under the exact selected Parent Page or
  trusted server-resolved Top-level/root placement owner;
- use append-last only when D2 provenance positively records the ordinary
  default or no explicit sibling-position choice;
- make missing, legacy, unreadable, contradictory, or corrupt provenance
  review-required rather than silently append;
- derive one locked post-D81/D82/D83-clean, pre-target-insert baseline for both
  an explicit boundary and append-last;
- make append-last semantic at commit rather than binding an incidental tail;
- generate a fresh target order representation, mutate no immutable prior
  revision, permit only sealed owner-qualified predecessor effects, and add no
  D84-caused collateral Page parent/order write; and
- retain boundaries only as minimized, tombstonable `material_page_handoff`
  evidence, never a continuing placement relationship or purge-blocking FK.

Without this general D2 provenance contract, the explicit-preservation branch
is unavailable. A positively known default may still append last; unknown state
must use ordinary D2 review.

### Exact corrected decision

> **D84 — Reviewed sibling placement with append-last default.** The D80-D84
> handoff shall create the fresh private target using D2's general new-Page
> placement command. The visible choice is an eligible Parent Page or **Top
> level**; D2 resolves Top level from trusted Site context to the existing Site-
> root placement owner/root Page, never from null or caller input.
>
> A reviewed position may be preserved only when the exact current acknowledged
> source Placement candidate is linked to immutable D2 command provenance that
> positively proves staff selected one tagged closed boundary:
> `start(successor)`, `between(predecessor, successor)`, `end(predecessor)`, or
> `only(empty cohort)`. Stable Page identities are required where applicable;
> null means none of these things. Under lock, D2 shall determine the exact
> qualified D81/D82/D83 effect manifest, derive its post-clean/pre-target final
> sibling cohort, validate the explicit boundary against that cohort, and
> generate a fresh target order value in the one transaction. It shall infer
> nothing from a rank, array index, provider row, import, migration, or UI state.
>
> Append-last is available only when D2 provenance positively records the
> ordinary default or no explicit sibling position. D2 resolves the tail from
> that same final baseline at commit. Missing, legacy, unreadable,
> contradictory, corrupt, or unrecognized provenance requires ordinary D2
> review. A stale explicit boundary also requires review and never silently
> appends. Unrelated changes that preserve the exact closed-boundary semantics
> need not force re-review.
>
> The target receives one fresh Placement revision/head/order representation.
> No immutable prior revision is mutated. Only sealed owner-qualified D81/D82/
> D83 effects may advance affected heads or change source-clean/derived state;
> D84 causes no additional pre-existing Page write and preserves the relative
> order of the final cohort while inserting only the target. Boundary identities
> are minimized, tombstonable `material_page_handoff` evidence with no
> continuing placement authority or purge-blocking FK. Exact replay returns the
> original result.
>
> D84 adds no capability, order engine, mandatory selector, Navigation/public
> route/generation change, external provider/control-plane call or effect,
> Vercel call, donor UI, schedule, designation, currency, recurring,
> contribution, Stripe, or ledger effect. The qualified same-database Payload
> persistence adapter may participate; Payload's native reorder endpoint is not
> authority.

### Final staff experience

Qualified explicit gap:

> **Page tree position**  
> **After:** Mission trips  
> **Before:** Resources  
> Uses the position reviewed in the saved Page change. Navigation and the live
> website will not change.

Reviewed start/end states use **First under Serve** plus **Before**, or **Last
under Serve** plus **After**, followed by the same “Uses the position reviewed”
sentence. An explicitly reviewed empty cohort shows **Only Page under Serve**
and **Uses the only position reviewed in the saved Page change**. These remain
distinct from the default through the explanatory text.

Known default:

> **Page tree position**  
> **Result:** Last under Serve  
> No sibling position was chosen in the saved Page change. The new Page will be
> added at the end when this handoff finishes. Navigation and the live website
> will not change.

An empty parent shows:

> **Page tree position**  
> **Result:** Only Page under Serve  
> No sibling position was chosen in the saved Page change. The new Page will be
> the only Page under Serve when this handoff finishes. Navigation and the live
> website will not change.

For D80's **Top level** choice the equivalent results are **First at top
level**, **Last at top level**, and **Only Page at top level**. Staff never see
the internal root/Home Page presented as their parent choice.

A stale boundary with authorized detail says **Page order changed**. Unknown
provenance says **Review the Page tree position before continuing** and “We
couldn't verify whether this Page's position was deliberately chosen. Your
saved work is safe.” When aggregate placement is allowed but anchor/specific-
cause detail is not, the same status shape and timing uses **Position needs
review** and “Review the current Page tree position. Nothing was moved or
published. Your saved work is safe.” All route to the existing D2 **Review
position** action. The existing **Move saved changes to new Page draft** action
remains the only handoff CTA.

The row uses description-list/native semantics and explicit After/Before/Last/
Only labels rather than an arrow, indentation, or color. It wraps at 320 CSS
pixels/400% zoom, handles long/CJK/RTL/bidi names, forced colors, reduced
motion, keyboard, screen reader, touch, weak network, and permission-safe
detail. Any ordinary tree drag has a named non-drag single-pointer and keyboard/
AT equivalent.

### Current evidence and repository status

Payload's current documentation supports fractional start/end/between keys, but
does not prove Core scope, staff intent, immutable Placement, or handoff
concurrency. The pinned `4.0.0-internal.1f9ae9a` native implementation is a
generic mutable provider feature and is not D2 authority. Figma's ordering
research confirms same-gap concurrent insertion needs authoritative server
assignment; Umbraco confirms append-last is a proven calm new-Page default;
WordPress/Craft keep hierarchy/order explicit; W3C requires a non-drag pointer
alternative as well as keyboard access.

The permanent architecture and the complete 22-category review are recorded in
[ADR-0205](../../adr/0205-reviewed-sibling-placement-with-append-last-default.md)
and the
[D84 adversarial review](./phase-24-d84-reviewed-sibling-placement-adversarial-review.md),
including D84-R1-R28, I1-I24, AC1-AC53, lifecycle, data ownership, rollout, and
eight named monitors.

At the review snapshot, local `HEAD` and fetched `origin/develop` remained
`7abd2c11ffd4ed70c6775c4fd6f51c996e4350dd`. Phase 22 PR #1323 remained
`OPEN/BLOCKED` at `70c50e8c97556c43be5543332fb0993b468b90ab`; Phase 23 PR
#1340 remained `OPEN/BLOCKED` at
`9069dcad67f9630323474ca5ee8bcc85ca7bf0f6`.

No runtime, schema, migration, Supabase policy, OpenSpec delta, ticket, Vercel/
DNS/TLS/Stripe/Resend request, deployment, public route, donor state, money
truth, or production behavior changed. D84 remains unavailable until its owner,
authorization, transaction, migration, capacity, UX/accessibility, mixed-
version, and zero-effect proofs pass.

### Phase 24 coverage disposition

D84 closes the remaining target-Placement facet of D80-D84. A dependency scan
found no legitimate D85 inside this material-purpose handoff: folders, Topics,

separate handoff questions for them would be over-grooming.

The next correct step is a complete Phase 24 decision-to-spec coverage audit
and consolidated OpenSpec/PRD synthesis. The former D56 question remains
explicitly deferred to the Phase 12/17 activation boundary; it is not silently
treated as resolved Phase 24 work. A new founder question should be asked only
if the coverage audit proves another real unresolved product choice.
